seg.4fea7db714b7.src: Chimmili is a small Telugu sweet of roasted sesame and jaggery, ground coarsely and rolled into balls. It is one of the offerings made on Nagula Chavithi in Karthika masam, along with chalimidi and the milk poured at the snake anthill (putta). Sesame and jaggery sweets like it are made again at Sankranti.
seg.4fea7db714b7.t: ꯆꯤꯝꯃꯤꯂꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ꯫ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯊꯤꯀ ꯃꯥꯁꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯥꯒꯨꯂꯥ ꯆꯕꯤꯊꯤꯗꯥ ꯀꯠꯊꯣꯀꯄ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ, ꯆꯂꯤꯃꯤꯗꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯤꯜꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ (ꯄꯨꯠꯇꯥ)ꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫ ꯁꯪꯛꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤꯗꯁꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.4fea7db714b7.back: Chimmili is a small Telugu sweet food. Roasted sesame and jaggery, ground without grinding too fine, are made into laddu. It is one among the things offered on Nagula Chavithi in the month of Karthika, together with chalimidi and milk poured into the snake's house (putta). At Sankranti too a sesame and jaggery sweet food like this is made.

seg.6e104d560e56.src: Roasted sesame gives it a nutty, toasty taste, and cane jaggery a caramel sweetness. The texture is soft and a little crumbly, and each ball is gone in two bites. This recipe makes about 12.
seg.6e104d560e56.t: ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ, ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤꯔꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤꯔꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯃꯃꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯑꯅꯤꯗꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ 12 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯏ꯫
seg.6e104d560e56.back: Roasted sesame gives a nut-like, roasted taste, and sugarcane jaggery gives a caramel-like sweet taste. It is soft and a little crumbly, and each laddu is finished in two bites. This recipe gives about 12.

seg.9e72f273d4f2.src: Total includes 5 minutes for the roasted sesame to cool.
seg.9e72f273d4f2.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.9e72f273d4f2.back: The total includes 5 minutes for cooling the roasted sesame.

seg.df9373d040ca.src: ⟦1⟧The recipe card⟦/1⟧Save it or send it to family. ⟦2⟧Open full size⟦/2⟧
seg.df9373d040ca.t: ⟦1⟧ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ⟦/1⟧ꯃꯁꯤ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯃꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ⟦2⟧ꯐꯨꯜ ꯁꯥꯏꯖꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ⟦/2⟧

seg.2097a0e593c6.src: Make chimmili at home: roast sesame till it crackles, grind coarsely, pulse with grated cane jaggery and cardamom, shape into balls.
seg.2097a0e593c6.t: ꯌꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯝꯃꯤꯂꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2097a0e593c6.back: Make chimmili at home: roast the sesame until it makes a crackling sound, grind it without grinding too fine, run it briefly in the mixie with grated sugarcane jaggery and cardamom, and make laddus.

seg.ac56800c5ad4.src: ¾ cup grated cane jaggery ⟦1⟧lightly packed; soft jaggery binds best⟦/1⟧
seg.ac56800c5ad4.t: ꯀꯞ ¾ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯥ; ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯍꯜꯂꯤ⟦/1⟧
seg.ac56800c5ad4.back: ¾ cup grated sugarcane jaggery ⟦1⟧to put in without pressing too much; soft jaggery binds best⟦/1⟧

seg.39c46fb56757.src: 1 tsp ghee, for greasing your palms
seg.39c46fb56757.back: 1 small spoon ghee (milk-oil), to put on the hands

seg.ed775cba4fcf.src: Grate the jaggery and measure out the sesame before you start; once the sesame is roasted, the rest moves quickly.
seg.ed775cba4fcf.t: ꯍꯧꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯊꯕꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯠꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.ed775cba4fcf.back: Before starting, grate the jaggery and keep the sesame measured; after the sesame is roasted the other work goes fast.

seg.cfb9d281b47f.src: Heat a heavy kadai or pan on low heat for a minute. Add the sesame; no oil or ghee is needed.
seg.cfb9d281b47f.t: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯊꯥꯎ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯗꯦ꯫
seg.cfb9d281b47f.back: Heat a heavy kadai on low fire for one minute. Add the sesame; oil or ghee is not needed.

seg.89a51ce5355c.src: Dry-roast the sesame on a low flame till it crackles and turns light golden. Stir all the time; the seeds start to pop and smell nutty after 4–6 minutes. Do not let them turn brown.
seg.89a51ce5355c.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 4–6 ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯣꯡꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯍꯧꯏ꯫ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯒꯅꯨ꯫
seg.89a51ce5355c.back: Roast the sesame on low fire without oil until it makes a crackling sound and becomes a little golden colour. Stir it gently all the time; after 4–6 minutes the seeds start to jump (pop) and give a nut-like smell. Do not let it become brown.

seg.999792547560.src: Tip the sesame onto a wide plate straight away so it stops browning. Cool it for about 5 minutes, until it is just warm to the touch.
seg.999792547560.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫ ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯁꯣꯛꯂꯕꯗꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.999792547560.back: Immediately pour the sesame onto a wide plate, otherwise it will keep turning brown. Cool it for about 5 minutes, until it is only a little warm when touched by hand.

seg.77b614ea2f92.src: Grind the sesame coarsely in short pulses. Use the small jar of the mixer and pulse 3–4 times, a second or two at a time; stop while you can still see broken seeds.
seg.77b614ea2f92.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ 3–4 ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯃꯃꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯅꯤ; ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯕ ꯐꯪꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.77b614ea2f92.back: Grind the sesame in the mixie, running it in short bursts, without grinding too fine. Use the small jar of the mixie and run it 3–4 times, each time one or two seconds; stop while broken seeds can still be seen.

seg.175aeced5810.src: Add the jaggery and cardamom; pulse till it comes together. This takes 4–6 more short pulses; scrape down the sides once. A pinch pressed between your fingers should hold its shape.
seg.175aeced5810.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ 4–6 ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ; ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯤꯕꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯅꯝꯂꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯩꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.175aeced5810.back: Add the jaggery and cardamom; run until it binds. For this, running 4–6 more short times is needed; once, push down with a spoon what has stuck to the sides. When pressed a little between the fingers it should hold its shape.

seg.6f94cb46b9ab.src: If the mixture is too dry to hold, add 1–2 tsp more grated jaggery and pulse once or twice again.
seg.6f94cb46b9ab.t: ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1–2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6f94cb46b9ab.back: If it is too dry to bind, add 1–2 more small spoons of grated jaggery and run once or twice more.

seg.226f137c9449.src: Tip the mixture into a bowl and grease your palms lightly with ghee.
seg.226f137c9449.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.226f137c9449.back: Pour the mixture into a bowl and put a little ghee on your hands.

seg.ff3eb71729c2.src: Shape into small balls. Take a heaped tablespoon at a time, press it firmly in your fist, then roll it smooth. Work quickly while the mixture is still warm, as it turns crumbly when it cools.
seg.ff3eb71729c2.t: ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯂꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯈꯨꯠ ꯈꯨꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯁꯥꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯏꯪꯂꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.ff3eb71729c2.back: Make small laddus. Each time take one full big spoon, close it in the fist and press hard, then make it round gently. Work fast while the mixture is warm, because when it cools it becomes crumbly.

seg.ee9e027268aa.src: Leave the balls on a plate until they cool completely, about 15 minutes, then store them in an airtight jar.
seg.ee9e027268aa.t: ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ee9e027268aa.back: Keep the laddus on a plate until they cool completely, about 15 minutes, then keep them in an airtight jar.

seg.7fe633314020.src: Roast on a low flame and keep stirring; sesame goes from golden to burnt quickly, and burnt sesame tastes bitter.
seg.7fe633314020.t: ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯦꯞꯇꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯈꯥꯏ꯫
seg.7fe633314020.back: Roast on low fire and keep stirring without stopping; sesame burns quickly from golden colour, and burnt sesame is bitter.

seg.d50b37351252.src: Grind in short pulses only; long runs turn sesame into an oily paste.
seg.d50b37351252.t: ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.d50b37351252.back: Grind only in short bursts; if run for a long time, the sesame becomes an oily paste.

seg.75f5428655c4.src: Shape while the mixture is warm. If it turns crumbly, pulse it once more with a teaspoon of grated jaggery.
seg.75f5428655c4.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯁꯥꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.75f5428655c4.back: Make the laddus while the mixture is warm. If it has become crumbly, add one small spoon of grated jaggery and run once more.

seg.1d42a24453d2.src: Soft jaggery binds best. If yours is hard, grate it finely so it blends in evenly.
seg.1d42a24453d2.t: ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯀꯟꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯆꯞ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1d42a24453d2.back: Soft jaggery binds best. If your jaggery is hard, grate it finely so that it melts evenly.

seg.5a7ed16f4810.src: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for darker chimmili with a smoky sweetness.
seg.5a7ed16f4810.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯆꯤꯝꯃꯤꯂꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5a7ed16f4810.back: Palm jaggery: for a chimmili that is darker and has a smoke-like sweet taste, use the same amount of grated palm jaggery.

seg.569a63f3cd17.src: Black sesame (nalla nuvvulu): roast and grind it the same way for darker, stronger-tasting balls.
seg.569a63f3cd17.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯨꯕ (ꯅꯜꯂ ꯅꯨꯕ꯭ꯕꯨꯂꯨ): ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.569a63f3cd17.back: Black sesame (nalla nuvvulu): for a laddu that is darker and stronger in taste, roast and grind in the same way.

seg.da0d1a9b6378.src: Peanut or coconut: pulse in 2 tbsp roasted peanuts or grated dry coconut with the jaggery.
seg.da0d1a9b6378.t: ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ: ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.da0d1a9b6378.back: Peanut or coconut: together with the jaggery add 2 big spoons of roasted peanuts or grated dry coconut and run.

seg.32d41fc0994e.src: Without a mixer: pound the warm sesame and jaggery together in a stone mortar (rolu) until the mixture holds, then shape.
seg.32d41fc0994e.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ: ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯝꯕꯜ (ꯔꯣꯂꯨ) ꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.32d41fc0994e.back: Without a mixie: pound the warm sesame and jaggery together in a stone mortar (rolu) until it binds, then make laddus.

seg.2fa9aaef4425.src: On Nagula Chavithi morning, offer chimmili with milk at the snake anthill (putta) or in your puja, then share them as prasadam. They also go well with evening tea.
seg.2fa9aaef4425.t: ꯅꯥꯒꯨꯂꯥ ꯆꯕꯤꯊꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯇꯥ, ꯆꯤꯝꯃꯤꯂꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯂꯤꯜꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ (ꯄꯨꯠꯇꯥ)ꯗꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯁꯥꯗꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯈꯥꯌꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯁꯨ ꯐꯩ꯫
seg.2fa9aaef4425.back: On the day of Nagula Chavithi, offer the chimmili with milk at the snake's house (putta) or in your puja, then distribute it as prasadam. It is also good to eat with afternoon tea.

seg.bd50831bbb3f.src: Keeps a week in an airtight jar. Store the jar at room temperature, in a dry place.
seg.bd50831bbb3f.t: ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bd50831bbb3f.back: It keeps well for one week in an airtight jar. Keep the jar inside the home, without heating or cooling it, in a dry place.

seg.4023b0de08bd.src: Why is my chimmili not holding together?
seg.4023b0de08bd.back: Why does my chimmili not bind?

seg.7fed90d1ebe0.src: The sesame may be under-ground, or the mixture may have cooled. Pulse it once more with 1–2 tsp extra grated jaggery and shape it while it is still warm.
seg.7fed90d1ebe0.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯏꯪꯂꯛꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1–2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7fed90d1ebe0.back: The sesame may not have been ground well, or the mixture may have cooled. Add 1–2 more small spoons of grated jaggery, run once more and make the laddus while it is warm.

seg.694d2b416f39.src: Why does my chimmili taste bitter?

seg.d0ee77d0957e.src: The sesame was roasted too dark. Roast it on a low flame only until it crackles and turns light golden, then tip it onto a plate at once so it stops browning.
seg.d0ee77d0957e.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯈꯤ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯅꯕꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d0ee77d0957e.back: The sesame was roasted until it became very dark. On low fire roast only until it makes a crackling sound and becomes a little golden, then pour it onto a plate immediately so that it stops turning brown.

seg.30d31a37acfa.src: Can I use palm jaggery instead of cane jaggery?
seg.30d31a37acfa.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.30d31a37acfa.back: Can palm jaggery be used instead of sugarcane jaggery?

seg.77afe99f558c.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The chimmili will be darker, with a deeper, slightly smoky sweetness.
seg.77afe99f558c.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯆꯤꯝꯃꯤꯂꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯒꯅꯤ, ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫
seg.77afe99f558c.back: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (tati bellam). The chimmili will be darker, with a stronger taste and a little smoke-like sweet taste.

seg.bae4fc214e74.src: Nagula Chavithi falls on Friday, 13 November 2026, in Karthika masam, a few days after Deepavali. Chimmili, chalimidi and milk are among the offerings made at the snake anthill (putta) that morning.
seg.bae4fc214e74.t: ꯅꯥꯒꯨꯂꯥ ꯆꯕꯤꯊꯤ ꯏꯔꯥꯏ, 13 ꯅꯣꯚꯦꯝꯕꯔ 2026ꯗꯥ ꯂꯩ, ꯀꯥꯔꯊꯤꯀ ꯃꯥꯁꯃꯗꯥ, ꯗꯤꯄꯥꯕꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ꯫ ꯑꯌꯨꯛ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯂꯤꯜꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ (ꯄꯨꯠꯇꯥ)ꯗꯥ ꯀꯠꯊꯣꯀꯄ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯝꯃꯤꯂꯤ, ꯆꯂꯤꯃꯤꯗꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ꯫
seg.bae4fc214e74.back: Nagula Chavithi is on Friday, 13 November 2026, in the month of Karthika, a few days after Dipavali. On that day, among the things offered at the snake's house (putta) are chimmili, chalimidi and milk.

seg.eb6e42bdf428.t: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ · ꯇꯥꯗ ꯀꯦ ꯒꯨꯗ ꯋꯥꯂꯤ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ
seg.eb6e42bdf428.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · tati bellam coffee · taad ke gud wali coffee [Hindi words in Meetei script]

seg.4b090c2ce3d3.src: Filter coffee is how many Telugu homes start the day: a strong decoction dripped through a steel filter, topped up with hot milk and frothed between a tumbler and davara. This version is sweetened with grated palm jaggery (thati bellam) in place of sugar.
seg.4b090c2ce3d3.t: ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯀꯣꯐꯤꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯏ: ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯂꯒꯤ ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯊꯔꯀꯄ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ, ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯕꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐꯣꯝ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ꯫ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯟꯏ꯫
seg.4b090c2ce3d3.back: In many Telugu homes the morning starts with filter coffee: strong decoction dripped slowly from a steel filter, hot milk added on top, and froth made by pouring between a tumbler and a davara. In this way, instead of sugar, grated palm jaggery (tati bellam) is added to sweeten it.

seg.cff6d2079da1.src: Palm jaggery gives the cup a deep, slightly smoky caramel sweetness that sits well with the bitterness of the decoction. Once the decoction is ready it takes about 5 minutes, and it suits a slow morning as much as an evening break.
seg.cff6d2079da1.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤꯔꯤ, ꯃꯁꯤ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯈꯥꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ꯫ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯆꯪꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯆꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛꯁꯨ, ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯡꯉꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄ ꯃꯇꯝꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯁꯨ ꯐꯩ꯫
seg.cff6d2079da1.back: Palm jaggery gives the cup a strong, slightly smoke-like caramel sweet taste, which goes well with the bitter taste of the decoction. After the decoction is ready it takes about 5 minutes, and it is good for slow-going days and also for afternoon resting time.

seg.814efc526088.src: 5 minutes if your decoction is already made.
seg.814efc526088.t: ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ꯍꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯔꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5꯫
seg.814efc526088.back: 5 minutes if the decoction is already made.

seg.9ad0a1e24d76.src: Boil the milk, add it to the decoction, then stir in grated palm jaggery off the heat. Froth it between tumbler and davara.
seg.9ad0a1e24d76.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯅꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯕꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐꯣꯝ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9ad0a1e24d76.back: Boil the milk, add it to the decoction, then taking it off the fire add grated palm jaggery and stir gently. Make froth by pouring between the tumbler and the davara.

seg.927b924ff51d.src: 2 tbsp filter coffee powder ⟦1⟧enough decoction for 2–3 cups⟦/1⟧
seg.927b924ff51d.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯞ 2–3ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ⟦/1⟧
seg.927b924ff51d.back: 2 big spoons filter coffee powder ⟦1⟧decoction enough for 2–3 cups⟦/1⟧

seg.8aa60818ccf8.src: ½ cup water, just off the boil

seg.95409b9d346e.src: 2 tbsp filter coffee decoction ⟦1⟧from above; 3 tbsp for a stronger cup⟦/1⟧
seg.95409b9d346e.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯀꯣꯐꯤꯒꯤ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ; ꯀꯟꯕ ꯀꯞꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3⟦/1⟧
seg.95409b9d346e.back: 2 big spoons filter coffee decoction ⟦1⟧from the one made above; 3 big spoons for a strong cup⟦/1⟧

seg.7b8c0f7e922a.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1–2 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.7b8c0f7e922a.back: 1–2 small spoons grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧tasting it⟦/1⟧

seg.95d91fecafcb.src: Make the decoction: put 2 tbsp filter coffee powder in the top chamber of a South Indian coffee filter, set the perforated press on it and pour in ½ cup water just off the boil. Cover and leave it to drip for 10–15 minutes.
seg.95d91fecafcb.t: ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯈꯥ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯥꯒꯤ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯀꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯍꯣꯜ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯇꯤꯛ ꯎꯠꯂꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ½ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯨꯞꯊꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10–15 ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯊꯔꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.95d91fecafcb.back: Make the decoction: put 2 big spoons of filter coffee powder in the upper part of a South India coffee filter, place the press that has many small holes on top, and pour ½ cup of just-boiled water. Cover it and leave it 10–15 minutes to drip slowly.

seg.9024c8716b54.src: While it drips, grate the palm jaggery finely so it dissolves in seconds.
seg.9024c8716b54.t: ꯇꯥꯊꯔꯛꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ, ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.9024c8716b54.back: While it is dripping, grate the palm jaggery finely, so that it will melt in a few seconds.

seg.24689e3dd311.src: Pour the milk into a small saucepan and set it on medium heat.
seg.24689e3dd311.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯁꯣꯁꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.24689e3dd311.back: Pour the milk into a small saucepan and put it on medium fire.

seg.4d8e3042dc81.src: Bring the milk to a boil. As soon as it froths up the sides of the pan, switch off the heat.
seg.4d8e3042dc81.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯣꯁꯄꯦꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯐꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯎꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄꯒꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4d8e3042dc81.back: Boil the milk. When froth rises at the edge of the saucepan, turn off the fire.

seg.a124a0d34983.src: Pour the decoction into a tumbler and add the hot milk. Use 2 tbsp decoction for a mild cup and 3 tbsp for a strong one.
seg.a124a0d34983.t: ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯀꯞꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯀꯞꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a124a0d34983.back: Pour the decoction into a tumbler and add the hot milk. For a mild-taste cup use 2 big spoons of decoction and for a strong cup 3 big spoons.

seg.85570720618b.src: Let it stand for about a minute, so the milk is just off the boil.
seg.85570720618b.t: ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯎꯠꯄꯗꯒꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.85570720618b.back: Leave it about one minute, so that the milk cools a little from boiling.

seg.eacea0d7cf43.src: Stir in the palm jaggery off the heat. Keep stirring for 20–30 seconds, until no grains are left at the bottom of the tumbler.
seg.eacea0d7cf43.t: ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 20–30 ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.eacea0d7cf43.back: Taking it off the fire, add the palm jaggery and stir gently. Stir 20–30 seconds until not even one grain remains at the bottom of the tumbler.

seg.08b600da2ef8.src: Taste, and add a little more jaggery if you like it sweeter.
seg.08b600da2ef8.t: ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.08b600da2ef8.back: Taste it, and if you like it sweeter add a little more jaggery.

seg.878b0d8d7eeb.src: Pour between tumbler and davara to froth. Hold the tumbler high and pour into the davara, then back again, 3–4 times, until a light foam sits on top.
seg.878b0d8d7eeb.t: ꯐꯣꯝ ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕꯥ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯕꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯋꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯠꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯗꯕꯔꯥꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ, ꯃꯇꯝ 3–4, ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯐꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.878b0d8d7eeb.back: To make froth, pour between the tumbler and the davara. Holding the tumbler high, pour into the davara, then once more back, 3–4 times, until there is a thick froth on top.

seg.653390b95f57.src: Serve straight away, in the tumbler set inside the davara.
seg.653390b95f57.t: ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯗꯕꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯂꯕ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔꯗꯥ꯫
seg.653390b95f57.back: Serve immediately, in the tumbler kept inside the davara.

seg.33aca43ebf99.src: Add jaggery after the milk is off the boil so it does not split.
seg.33aca43ebf99.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯎꯠꯄꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯣꯏ꯫
seg.33aca43ebf99.back: Add the jaggery after the milk has cooled from boiling, so that the milk will not break.

seg.60404da43771.src: Grate the jaggery finely: fine shreds dissolve in seconds, while lumps sink and stay at the bottom of the tumbler.
seg.60404da43771.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯃꯤꯟꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯏ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤ꯫
seg.60404da43771.back: Grate the jaggery finely: fine jaggery melts in a few seconds, but big grains sink to the bottom and stay at the bottom of the tumbler.

seg.ca883342300e.src: Palm jaggery has a deep, slightly smoky sweetness, so start with 1 tsp and add more to taste.
seg.ca883342300e.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ca883342300e.back: Palm jaggery gives a strong, slightly smoke-like sweet taste, therefore start with 1 small spoon and add more after tasting.

seg.d7c0084f5cc6.src: A steel tumbler and davara keep the coffee hot and make frothing easy; a mug and a jug work too.
seg.d7c0084f5cc6.t: ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯂꯒꯤ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯕꯔꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯣꯝ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯂꯥꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ; ꯃꯒ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯒꯁꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.d7c0084f5cc6.back: The steel tumbler and davara keep the coffee hot and make frothing easy; a mug and jug can also be used.

seg.1b917ac5fc8c.src: Cane jaggery: use the same amount of grated cane jaggery for a lighter, caramel-like sweetness.
seg.1b917ac5fc8c.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ, ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1b917ac5fc8c.back: Sugarcane jaggery: for a milder, caramel-like sweet taste use the same amount of grated sugarcane jaggery.

seg.0ada954bebfe.src: Palm jaggery tea: make your usual milk tea, switch off the heat, wait a minute, then stir in the palm jaggery the same way.
seg.0ada954bebfe.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥ: ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0ada954bebfe.back: Palm jaggery tea: make the milk tea you always make, turn off the fire, wait one minute, then add palm jaggery in the same way and stir.

seg.6512d133d4c0.src: No coffee filter: dissolve 1 tsp instant coffee in 2 tbsp hot water and use it in place of the decoction.
seg.6512d133d4c0.t: ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯂꯩꯇꯕꯗꯤ: ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2ꯗꯥ ꯏꯟꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯠ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6512d133d4c0.back: If there is no coffee filter: dissolve 1 small spoon of instant coffee in 2 big spoons of hot water and use it instead of the decoction.

seg.e9e80ce83cf6.src: Serve hot after a breakfast of idli, dosa or upma, or in the evening with biscuits or murukulu.
seg.e9e80ce83cf6.t: ꯏꯗꯂꯤ, ꯗꯣꯁꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯎꯄꯃꯥꯒꯤ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡ ꯕꯤꯁ꯭ꯀꯨꯠ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e9e80ce83cf6.back: Serve hot after the morning meal of idli, dosa or upma, or in the afternoon with biscuits or murukulu.

seg.97817ad1f29f.src: Make each cup as you need it; coffee reheated after the jaggery goes in can split. Keep extra decoction covered at room temperature and use it within the day.
seg.97817ad1f29f.t: ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯀꯞ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ꯀꯨꯞꯊꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.97817ad1f29f.back: Make each cup at the time it is needed; coffee heated once more after adding jaggery may break. Cover the remaining decoction and keep it inside the home, without heating or cooling it, and use it within that day.

seg.ea4f4072538a.src: Why did my coffee curdle when I added palm jaggery?
seg.ea4f4072538a.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯗꯥ ꯑꯩꯒꯤ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯏꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.ea4f4072538a.back: Why did my coffee break when I added palm jaggery?

seg.180a2670ead3.src: Jaggery stirred into milk that is still boiling can make it split. Take the milk off the heat, let it stand for about a minute, then stir in the grated jaggery.
seg.180a2670ead3.t: ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.180a2670ead3.back: If jaggery is added and stirred into milk that is still boiling, the milk may break. Take the milk off the fire, leave it about one minute, then add grated jaggery and stir.

seg.2b9449407096.src: Can I use cane jaggery instead of palm jaggery?
seg.2b9449407096.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.2b9449407096.back: Can sugarcane jaggery be used instead of palm jaggery?

seg.890ae3e15593.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery. The coffee tastes lighter and more like caramel, while palm jaggery gives a deeper, slightly smoky cup.
seg.890ae3e15593.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯣꯐꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯞ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.890ae3e15593.back: Yes. Use the same amount of grated sugarcane jaggery. The coffee's taste becomes milder and caramel-like, but palm jaggery gives a stronger, slightly smoke-like cup.

seg.e4c92d1c8a42.src: How much palm jaggery should I add to one cup of coffee?
seg.e4c92d1c8a42.t: ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯀꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.e4c92d1c8a42.back: How much palm jaggery should be added to one cup of coffee?

seg.43a5dfb10340.src: 1 to 2 tsp of grated palm jaggery for 1 cup of milk and 2 tbsp of decoction. Start with 1 tsp, taste, and add more if you like.
seg.43a5dfb10340.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯞ 1 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯗꯒꯤ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.43a5dfb10340.back: For 1 cup of milk and 2 big spoons of decoction, from 1 to 2 small spoons of grated palm jaggery. Start with 1 small spoon, taste it, and if you like add more.

seg.2ba4fb9452bb.src: Can I make palm jaggery coffee without a coffee filter?
seg.2ba4fb9452bb.t: ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.2ba4fb9452bb.back: Can palm jaggery coffee be made without a coffee filter?

seg.23f63da2d908.src: Yes. Dissolve 1 tsp instant coffee in 2 tbsp hot water, use it in place of the decoction and follow the same steps.
seg.23f63da2d908.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2ꯗꯥ ꯏꯟꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯠ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.23f63da2d908.back: Yes. Dissolve 1 small spoon of instant coffee in 2 big spoons of hot water, use it instead of the decoction and do the same steps.

seg.08ada9e6791e.t: తాటి బెల్లం కాఫీ. ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ), ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗꯥ: ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯟ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯂꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ꯫ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ, ꯄꯥꯎꯇꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯍꯪ-ꯄꯥꯎꯈꯨꯝ꯫
seg.08ada9e6791e.back: తాటి బెల్లం కాఫీ. [Telugu: palm jaggery coffee] Palm jaggery coffee (tati bellam coffee), in the Andhra way: filter decoction, hot milk and grated palm jaggery stirred in after taking off the fire. Step-by-step way of making, tips and questions-answers.

seg.03ffde37c28f.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · bellam paramannam · gud wali kheer [Hindi words in Meetei script]

seg.1143d51ba236.src: Paramannam is the rice-and-milk sweet that Telugu homes cook for festivals and pujas: rice simmered slowly in milk until soft and creamy, then sweetened. Bellam paramannam, made with jaggery, is a common naivedyam at Diwali, Sankranti and Varalakshmi Vratham, offered at the puja and then shared at the festive meal.
seg.1143d51ba236.t: ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯝꯍꯩ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯅꯤ: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯟꯏ꯫ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ ꯗꯤꯋꯥꯂꯤ, ꯁꯪꯛꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯔꯂꯛꯁ꯭ꯃꯤ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯠꯄ ꯅꯩꯕꯦꯗ꯭ꯌꯝꯅꯤ, ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯠꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯝꯍꯩꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯈꯥꯌꯗꯣꯛꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫
seg.1143d51ba236.back: Paramannam is a sweet food of rice and milk cooked in Telugu homes for festivals and puja: the rice is cooked slowly in milk until it becomes soft and creamy, then it is sweetened. Bellam paramannam made with jaggery is the naivedyam always offered on Diwali, Sankranti and Varalakshmi Vratam; after being offered in the puja it is distributed and eaten at the festival meal.

seg.360051f42785.src: Cane jaggery turns it a light caramel colour and gives a rounder, toffee-like sweetness. Ghee-fried cashews and a little cardamom finish it. This recipe serves 4.
seg.360051f42785.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯣꯐꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯈꯔꯥꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.360051f42785.back: Sugarcane jaggery gives it a little caramel colour and a toffee-like sweet taste. It is finished with cashews fried in ghee and a little cardamom. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.04a51f6c83e4.src: Total includes the 5-minute rest before the jaggery goes in.
seg.04a51f6c83e4.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯤꯉꯩꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.04a51f6c83e4.back: The total includes the 5 minutes of keeping (resting) before adding the jaggery.

seg.fd8f49fce13b.src: Cook rice in milk till creamy, rest it 5 minutes, then stir in grated cane jaggery. Finish with ghee-fried cashews and cardamom.
seg.fd8f49fce13b.t: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fd8f49fce13b.back: Cook the rice in milk until creamy, leave it 5 minutes, then add grated sugarcane jaggery and stir. Finish with cashews fried in ghee and cardamom.

seg.1c0f194a4451.src: ½ cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masoori or another short-grain rice, about 100 g⟦/1⟧
seg.1c0f194a4451.t: ꯀꯞ ½ ꯆꯦꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯁꯣꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯨꯔꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯇꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯆꯦꯡ, 100 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.1c0f194a4451.back: ½ cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masoori or other short-grain rice, about 100 g⟦/1⟧

seg.8f34922ee281.src: 4 cups milk ⟦1⟧about 1 litre; whole milk gives the creamiest result⟦/1⟧
seg.8f34922ee281.t: ꯀꯞ 4 ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ⟦1⟧1 ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯐꯨꯜ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ⟦/1⟧
seg.8f34922ee281.back: 4 cups milk ⟦1⟧about 1 litre; full-cream milk makes it the most creamy⟦/1⟧

seg.ee0c3b96837f.src: ¾ cup grated cane jaggery ⟦1⟧lightly packed; up to 2 tbsp more if you like it sweeter⟦/1⟧
seg.ee0c3b96837f.t: ꯀꯞ ¾ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯥ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.ee0c3b96837f.back: ¾ cup grated sugarcane jaggery ⟦1⟧to put in without pressing too much; if you like it sweeter, up to 2 big spoons more⟦/1⟧

seg.fa014766d2bf.src: ½ tsp cardamom powder ⟦1⟧or the crushed seeds of 4–5 pods⟦/1⟧
seg.fa014766d2bf.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ 4–5ꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.fa014766d2bf.back: ½ small spoon cardamom powder ⟦1⟧or the ground seeds of 4–5 cardamoms⟦/1⟧

seg.480e0a7d227f.src: Wash the rice in 2–3 changes of water until the water runs almost clear, then drain it well.
seg.480e0a7d227f.t: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ 2–3 ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯌꯦꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯅꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯐꯖꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.480e0a7d227f.back: Wash the rice, changing the water 2–3 times, until the water looks almost clean, then drain the water well.

seg.d5b0fc46818a.src: Pour the milk into a heavy-bottomed pan and bring it to a boil on medium heat, about 8–10 minutes. Stir now and then so it does not catch at the bottom.
seg.d5b0fc46818a.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯈꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 8–10 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯃꯇꯝꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d5b0fc46818a.back: Pour the milk into a heavy-bottomed kadai and boil it on medium fire, about 8–10 minutes. Stir from time to time so it does not stick to the bottom.

seg.b8f9c8c6758b.src: Add the drained rice to the boiling milk and turn the heat to low.
seg.b8f9c8c6758b.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b8f9c8c6758b.back: Add the drained rice to the boiling milk and make the fire low.

seg.9ae9baab76d7.src: Cook the washed rice in the milk on a low flame till soft and creamy, about 30 minutes. Stir often, scraping the bottom and sides of the pan each time.
seg.9ae9baab76d7.t: ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 30 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯤꯕꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9ae9baab76d7.back: Cook the washed rice in the milk on low fire until soft and creamy, about 30 minutes. Stir many times, each time removing with a spoon what has stuck to the bottom and sides of the kadai.

seg.ec1509a08b4c.src: Check the rice: a grain should mash easily between your fingers, and the milk should have thickened slightly. For a creamier paramannam, lightly mash a few grains against the side of the pan.
seg.ec1509a08b4c.t: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯊꯠꯄ ꯌꯥꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ec1509a08b4c.back: Check the rice: a grain should be easily pressed flat between the fingers, and the milk should have thickened a little. For a more creamy paramannam, gently press some grains against the side of the kadai.

seg.d8ba0a82f4ec.src: Switch off and let it rest 5 minutes. This brings the milk below the boil, so the jaggery will not split it.
seg.d8ba0a82f4ec.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯎꯠꯄꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯍꯜꯂꯣꯏ꯫
seg.d8ba0a82f4ec.back: Turn off the fire and leave it 5 minutes. This cools the milk from boiling, therefore the jaggery will not make the milk break.

seg.ca16c98d9b18.src: Stir in the jaggery till it melts, about 1–2 minutes, keeping the pan off the heat.
seg.ca16c98d9b18.t: ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1–2 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫
seg.ca16c98d9b18.back: Taking the kadai off the fire, stir until the jaggery melts, about 1–2 minutes.

seg.74412a8cc141.src: Taste, and stir in a little more grated jaggery if you want it sweeter.
seg.74412a8cc141.t: ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.74412a8cc141.back: Taste it, and if you like it sweeter add a little more grated jaggery and stir.

seg.92b56df40ea6.src: Heat the ghee in a small pan on medium-low heat.
seg.92b56df40ea6.t: ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.92b56df40ea6.back: Heat the ghee in a small kadai on medium-low fire.

seg.1bb1f411e4d0.src: Fry the cashews in ghee; add with the cardamom. Stir the cashews until golden, about 1 minute, adding the raisins for the last few seconds until they puff up. Pour the nuts and ghee into the paramannam, sprinkle in the cardamom powder and stir.
seg.1bb1f411e4d0.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯀꯤꯁꯃꯤꯁ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯆꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1bb1f411e4d0.back: Fry the cashews in the ghee; add them together with the cardamom. Stir the cashews until golden colour, about 1 minute, and in the last few seconds add the raisins until they swell up. Pour the cashews and the ghee into the paramannam, add a little cardamom powder and stir.

seg.e10b7192c157.src: Serve warm. Paramannam thickens as it stands; loosen it with a few spoons of warm milk, off the heat, if needed.
seg.e10b7192c157.t: ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ; ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e10b7192c157.back: Serve warm. If the paramannam is kept it thickens; if needed, take it off the fire, add a few spoons of hot milk and make it less thick.

seg.d30196cf6b28.src: Jaggery goes in off the heat so the milk does not split.
seg.d30196cf6b28.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯏ꯫
seg.d30196cf6b28.back: The jaggery is added after taking off the fire so that the milk does not break.

seg.d4a9c2ee09bf.src: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and scrape the bottom each time you stir; milk catches easily during the long simmer.
seg.d4a9c2ee09bf.t: ꯃꯈꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯤꯕꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫
seg.d4a9c2ee09bf.back: Use a heavy-bottomed kadai and each time you stir remove what has stuck to the bottom; while cooking slowly for a long time, milk easily sticks to the bottom.

seg.a01441abc0b6.src: Cook the rice until fully soft before the jaggery goes in; the grains do not soften further once it is sweetened.
seg.a01441abc0b6.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯤꯉꯩꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯟꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯂꯣꯏ꯫
seg.a01441abc0b6.back: Before adding the jaggery cook the rice until fully soft; after sweetening, the grains will not become any softer.

seg.688b80a32383.src: Grate the jaggery finely so it melts in the hot milk without going back on the stove.
seg.688b80a32383.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯗꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.688b80a32383.back: Grate the jaggery finely, so that it will melt in the hot milk without putting it on the fire once more.

seg.7bf8faca62b8.src: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for a darker colour and a deeper, smoky sweetness.
seg.7bf8faca62b8.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7bf8faca62b8.back: Palm jaggery: for a darker colour and a stronger, smoke-like sweet taste use the same amount of grated palm jaggery.

seg.6672d2210281.src: Pesarapappu paramannam: dry-roast 2 tbsp split moong dal until light golden, wash it and cook it with the rice.
seg.6672d2210281.t: ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ: ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6672d2210281.back: Pesarapappu paramannam: roast 2 big spoons of split moong dal without oil until a little golden, wash it and cook together with the rice.

seg.cd25d9fb2a56.src: Coconut: fry 2 tbsp thin slivers of dry coconut in the ghee along with the cashews.
seg.cd25d9fb2a56.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯄꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.cd25d9fb2a56.back: Coconut: fry 2 big spoons of thinly cut dry coconut in ghee together with the cashews.

seg.988ab75b5ccb.src: Serve warm as naivedyam at the Diwali or Lakshmi puja, then as the sweet at the festive meal. Some like it chilled the next day.
seg.988ab75b5ccb.t: ꯗꯤꯋꯥꯂꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯛꯁ꯭ꯃꯤ ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯗꯥ ꯅꯩꯕꯦꯗ꯭ꯌꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯝꯍꯩꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯈꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯄꯥꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.988ab75b5ccb.back: On Diwali or Lakshmi puja, offer it warm as naivedyam, then serve it as a sweet food at the festival meal. Some like to eat it cooled on the next day.

seg.4a60d211f14d.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. It sets thick when chilled; stir in a little warm milk, off the heat, before serving.
seg.4a60d211f14d.t: ꯂꯦꯃꯍꯧꯔꯤꯕꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯊꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ; ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4a60d211f14d.back: Cover what is left over, keep it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days. When cold it becomes very thick; when serving, take it off the fire, add a little hot milk and stir.

seg.2949774c7efb.src: Why did my paramannam curdle after adding jaggery?
seg.2949774c7efb.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯩꯒꯤ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯏꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.2949774c7efb.back: Why did my paramannam break after adding jaggery?

seg.283626ae50fc.src: Jaggery stirred into milk that is still on the heat or boiling can make it split. Switch off, let the paramannam rest for about 5 minutes, then stir in the grated jaggery.
seg.283626ae50fc.t: ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯕ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.283626ae50fc.back: If jaggery is added and stirred into milk that is still on the fire or boiling, the milk may break. Turn off the fire, leave the paramannam about 5 minutes, then add grated jaggery and stir.

seg.7df6976d1e83.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The paramannam turns darker and tastes deeper and slightly smoky.
seg.7df6976d1e83.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.7df6976d1e83.back: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (tati bellam). The paramannam becomes darker in colour and the taste becomes stronger and a little smoke-like.

seg.6ac2cfc26fb7.src: Which rice is best for paramannam?
seg.6ac2cfc26fb7.back: Which rice is best for paramannam?

seg.ead18bc39c32.src: A short-grain rice such as sona masoori cooks soft and creamy in milk. Long-grain basmati keeps its grains separate and gives a thinner paramannam.
seg.ead18bc39c32.t: ꯁꯣꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯨꯔꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯇꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ꯫ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯁꯥꯡꯕ ꯕꯥꯁꯃꯇꯤꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯕ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.ead18bc39c32.back: Short-grain rice like sona masoori cooks soft and creamy in milk. Long-grain basmati keeps the grains separate and gives a more watery paramannam.

seg.2baf5cc4ec36.src: How do I fix paramannam that has become too thick?
seg.2baf5cc4ec36.back: How to fix a paramannam that has become too thick?

seg.9ffeabf346fa.src: Stir in a few spoons of warm milk, off the heat, until it loosens. It thickens as it cools, so stop when it is a little thinner than you want.
seg.9ffeabf346fa.t: ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯀꯟꯊꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯪꯂꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯤꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9ffeabf346fa.back: Taking it off the fire, add a few spoons of hot milk and stir until it becomes less thick. When it cools it thickens, therefore stop when it is a little more watery than you like.

seg.43e6183ba82c.back: బెల్లం పరమాన్నం [Telugu: bellam paramannam] · Recipe of bellam paramannam | 1acrefarms

seg.8b09026bfd65.t: బెల్లం పరమాన్నం. ꯗꯤꯋꯥꯂꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯦꯡ, ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯜꯂꯕ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ꯫ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ, ꯄꯥꯎꯇꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯍꯪ-ꯄꯥꯎꯈꯨꯝ꯫ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫

seg.cf8cab3618d9.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ

seg.44699ae5fc7d.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · pasupu palu · haldi wala doodh [Hindi words in Meetei script]

seg.5fbc274b0656.src: Pasupu paalu is warm milk simmered with a little turmeric and a pinch of black pepper, then sweetened with jaggery. It is an everyday cup in many Telugu homes, made on cool evenings and often through Karthika masam, the month of Somavaram (Monday) pujas and evening lamps.
seg.5fbc274b0656.t: ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯄꯥꯂꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯅꯤ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯟꯏ꯫ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ, ꯏꯪꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯊꯤꯀ ꯃꯥꯁꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ, ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯣꯃꯕꯥꯔꯝ (ꯅꯤꯡꯊꯧꯀꯥꯕ) ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯗꯤꯌꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯊꯥꯅꯤ꯫
seg.5fbc274b0656.back: Pasupu palu is warm milk cooked slowly with a little turmeric and a little black pepper, then sweetened with jaggery. In many Telugu homes it is an everyday cup, made on cold evenings and made many times in the month of Karthika; it is the month of Somavaram (Monday) pujas and of lighting diyas in the evening.

seg.7d5fe2bc79e0.src: The turmeric turns the milk golden and gives it an earthy, slightly bitter edge, the pepper adds a little heat, and the jaggery rounds it off with a caramel sweetness. This recipe makes one cup in about 5 minutes.
seg.7d5fe2bc79e0.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯒꯨꯝꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯥꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ, ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆꯅꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯔꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯐꯪꯏ꯫
seg.7d5fe2bc79e0.back: Turmeric gives the milk a golden colour and an earth-like, slightly bitter taste, black pepper gives a little pungency (hotness), and jaggery finishes it with a caramel-like sweet taste. This recipe gives one cup in about 5 minutes.

seg.8e4df121a859.src: Simmer milk with turmeric and a pinch of pepper, switch off, then stir in a spoon of jaggery.
seg.8e4df121a859.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8e4df121a859.back: Cook the milk slowly with turmeric and a little black pepper, turn off the fire, then add one spoon of jaggery and stir.

seg.33cd5776caaf.src: ¼ tsp turmeric powder ⟦1⟧Turmeric Powder or Hill Turmeric Powder⟦/1⟧
seg.33cd5776caaf.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ⟦/1⟧
seg.33cd5776caaf.back: ¼ small spoon turmeric powder ⟦1⟧turmeric powder or hill turmeric powder⟦/1⟧

seg.f1056c625241.src: A pinch of black pepper ⟦1⟧powdered or crushed⟦/1⟧
seg.f1056c625241.back: A little black pepper ⟦1⟧powder or ground⟦/1⟧

seg.bc417c4b3691.src: 1 tsp grated palm or cane jaggery ⟦1⟧or to taste⟦/1⟧
seg.bc417c4b3691.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.bc417c4b3691.back: 1 small spoon grated palm jaggery or sugarcane jaggery ⟦1⟧or tasting it⟦/1⟧

seg.12c1bae1db56.back: A little cardamom powder (if you like)

seg.1a51e1f06af0.src: Sweeten it with ⟦1⟧Palm Jaggery⟦/1⟧ or ⟦2⟧Cane Jaggery⟦/2⟧.
seg.1a51e1f06af0.back: Sweeten it with ⟦1⟧palm jaggery⟦/1⟧ or ⟦2⟧sugarcane jaggery⟦/2⟧.

seg.b0b3cf3b3c0d.src: Pour the milk into a small steel saucepan.
seg.b0b3cf3b3c0d.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯂꯒꯤ ꯁꯣꯁꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b0b3cf3b3c0d.back: Pour the milk into a small steel saucepan.

seg.94d57531a741.src: Add the turmeric and pepper (and the cardamom, if using) and stir until no specks of turmeric float on top. They mix in more evenly before the milk is heated.
seg.94d57531a741.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆ (ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ) ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯇꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯆꯞ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯏ꯫
seg.94d57531a741.back: Add the turmeric and black pepper (and cardamom if you like) and stir until not even one grain of turmeric floats on top. While the milk is not yet heated they dissolve more evenly.

seg.9da3932c6508.src: Set the pan on medium-low heat. Warm the milk with the turmeric and pepper; simmer 2 minutes. Once small bubbles appear around the edge, turn the heat to low and let it bubble gently.
seg.9da3932c6508.t: ꯁꯣꯁꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯕꯕꯜ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯔꯛꯄꯒꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯎꯠꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9da3932c6508.back: Keep the saucepan on medium-low fire. Heat the milk with the turmeric and black pepper; cook slowly 2 minutes. When small bubbles appear at the sides, make the fire low and leave it to boil slowly.

seg.c66cb9336ef5.src: Stir now and then and keep an eye on the pan, as milk rises fast once it boils. If it starts to climb, lift the pan off the heat for a few seconds.
seg.c66cb9336ef5.t: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯃꯇꯝꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯣꯁꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯎꯠꯂꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯏ꯫ ꯆꯥꯎꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯍꯧꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯣꯁꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c66cb9336ef5.back: Stir from time to time and keep watching the saucepan, because when it starts boiling the milk rises up quickly. If it starts rising, take the saucepan off the fire for a few seconds.

seg.b567bc0c93c9.src: It is ready when the milk is an even golden yellow and the raw smell of turmeric has gone.
seg.b567bc0c93c9.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯞ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯨꯟꯗꯕ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯔꯦ꯫
seg.b567bc0c93c9.back: When the milk has become evenly golden colour and the raw smell of turmeric is gone, it is ready.

seg.6e16c50d7c2a.src: Switch off and wait a minute. The milk drops just below the boil, so the jaggery will not split it.
seg.6e16c50d7c2a.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯎꯠꯄꯗꯒꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯍꯜꯂꯣꯏ꯫
seg.6e16c50d7c2a.back: Turn off the fire and wait one minute. The milk cools a little from boiling, therefore the jaggery will not make the milk break.

seg.aa0d1bcf6802.src: For a smooth cup, pour the milk through a fine sieve into a tumbler or mug.
seg.aa0d1bcf6802.t: ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯟꯕ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯗꯒꯤ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯒ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.aa0d1bcf6802.back: For a smooth (soft) cup, pour the milk through a fine strainer into a tumbler or a mug.

seg.862cac523844.src: Stir in the jaggery and serve warm. Stir for 20–30 seconds, until it dissolves, and taste for sweetness.
seg.862cac523844.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 20–30 ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.862cac523844.back: Add the jaggery, stir and serve warm. Stir 20–30 seconds until it dissolves, and taste the sweetness.

seg.1d9b9ec736a8.src: Strain through a fine sieve if you like it smooth.
seg.1d9b9ec736a8.back: If you like it smooth, strain through a fine strainer.

seg.018366193ef3.src: Add the jaggery only after switching off; jaggery stirred into boiling milk can split it.
seg.018366193ef3.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.018366193ef3.back: Add the jaggery only after turning off the fire; if jaggery is added and stirred into boiling milk, the milk may break.

seg.0e783ba83473.src: Use a steel pan and spoon; turmeric stains plastic and wood.
seg.0e783ba83473.t: ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯂꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯅꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯎꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯆꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.0e783ba83473.back: Use a steel kadai and spoon; turmeric stains plastic and wood with colour.

seg.dc2a0c79ccd5.src: Making more? Use the same amounts for each cup of milk.
seg.dc2a0c79ccd5.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯒꯗ꯭ꯔꯥ? ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯞ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.dc2a0c79ccd5.back: Making more? Use the same amount for each cup of milk.

seg.485f68415013.src: Hill turmeric: use Hill Turmeric Powder (konda pasupu) in place of turmeric powder, in the same amount.
seg.485f68415013.t: ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ (ꯀꯣꯟꯗꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ) ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.485f68415013.back: Hill turmeric: instead of turmeric powder use the same amount of hill turmeric powder (konda pasupu).

seg.01ec7a142032.src: Palm or cane jaggery: palm jaggery gives a deeper, slightly smoky sweetness; cane jaggery a lighter, caramel one.
seg.01ec7a142032.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ; ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ, ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.01ec7a142032.back: Palm jaggery or sugarcane jaggery: palm jaggery gives a stronger, slightly smoke-like sweet taste; sugarcane jaggery gives a milder, caramel-like taste.

seg.15b67235d087.src: Milder cup: leave out the pepper and add a pinch of cardamom powder instead.
seg.15b67235d087.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯀꯞ: ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.15b67235d087.back: Milder cup: do not add black pepper, and instead add a little cardamom powder.

seg.d80219c8a51f.src: Serve warm in a tumbler or mug, on a cool evening or after the Karthika Somavaram puja.
seg.d80219c8a51f.t: ꯏꯪꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯊꯤꯀ ꯁꯣꯃꯕꯥꯔꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯒꯇꯥ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d80219c8a51f.back: Serve warm in a tumbler or mug on a cold evening or after the Karthika Somavaram puja.

seg.ac04ffd1d51a.src: Make it as you need it and drink it warm. Reheating after the jaggery is in can split the milk.
seg.ac04ffd1d51a.t: ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.ac04ffd1d51a.back: Make it at the time needed and drink it warm. If heated once more after adding jaggery, the milk may break.

seg.c758e61dd102.src: Why did my pasupu paalu curdle?
seg.c758e61dd102.back: Why did my pasupu palu break?

seg.d5f9c6fb2e27.src: Jaggery stirred into milk that is still boiling can make it split. Switch off the heat, wait about a minute, then stir in the grated jaggery.
seg.d5f9c6fb2e27.t: ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯔꯣꯝ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d5f9c6fb2e27.back: If jaggery is added and stirred into milk that is still boiling, the milk may break. Turn off the fire, wait about one minute, then add grated jaggery and stir.

seg.df4dbdd3102b.src: How much turmeric should I use for one cup of milk?
seg.df4dbdd3102b.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.df4dbdd3102b.back: How much turmeric should be used for one cup of milk?

seg.3ec50124bdd7.src: ¼ tsp turmeric powder for 1 cup (about 240 ml) of milk. More than that makes the taste sharp and earthy.
seg.3ec50124bdd7.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯞ 1 (240 ml ꯔꯣꯝ)ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼꯫ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.3ec50124bdd7.back: ¼ small spoon of turmeric powder for 1 cup (about 240 ml) of milk. If more than that, the taste becomes strong and earth-like.

seg.3dc4d1edd4f9.src: Can I skip the black pepper?
seg.3dc4d1edd4f9.back: Is it okay not to add black pepper?

seg.166b3a44e11d.src: Yes. The pepper adds a little heat to the taste; leave it out, or use a pinch of cardamom instead, for a milder cup.
seg.166b3a44e11d.t: ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯇꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.166b3a44e11d.back: It is okay. Black pepper gives a little pungency to the taste; for a milder cup do not add it, or use a little cardamom instead.

seg.2184adfd31b0.src: Should I use palm jaggery or cane jaggery?
seg.2184adfd31b0.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ?
seg.2184adfd31b0.back: Should palm jaggery be used or sugarcane jaggery?

seg.ef65c3a9d015.src: Either works, 1 tsp grated per cup. Palm jaggery tastes deeper and slightly smoky; cane jaggery is lighter and more like caramel.
seg.ef65c3a9d015.t: ꯀꯅꯥꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯃꯛ ꯐꯩ, ꯀꯞ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1꯫ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝ; ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝ꯫
seg.ef65c3a9d015.back: Any one is good, 1 small spoon of grated jaggery per cup. Palm jaggery's taste is stronger and a little smoke-like; sugarcane jaggery is milder and caramel-like.

seg.0f694f995bf8.src: పసుపు పాలు · Pasupu Paalu (Turmeric Milk) Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.0f694f995bf8.t: పసుపు పాలు · ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯄꯥꯂꯨ (ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ)ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ | 1acrefarms
seg.0f694f995bf8.back: పసుపు పాలు [Telugu: turmeric milk] · Recipe of pasupu palu (turmeric milk) | 1acrefarms

seg.bf09ae159f00.src: పసుపు పాలు. Pasupu paalu (haldi doodh): warm milk simmered with turmeric and a pinch of pepper, sweetened with jaggery off the heat. Step-by-step method, tips and FAQs.
seg.bf09ae159f00.t: పసుపు పాలు. ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯄꯥꯂꯨ (ꯍꯜꯗꯤ ꯗꯨꯙ): ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯣꯔꯤꯆ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ, ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯜꯂꯕ꯫ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ, ꯄꯥꯎꯇꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯍꯪ-ꯄꯥꯎꯈꯨꯝ꯫
seg.bf09ae159f00.back: పసుపు పాలు. [Telugu: turmeric milk] Pasupu palu (haldi doodh [Hindi words]): warm milk cooked slowly with turmeric and a little black pepper, sweetened with jaggery after taking off the fire. Step-by-step way of making, tips and questions-answers.

seg.4291e73409f8.src: Warm Pasupu Paalu: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.4291e73409f8.t: ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯄꯥꯂꯨ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ

seg.b0c2f2f3f9c9.src: 1 tsp grated palm or cane jaggery

seg.5094f960d9a4.src: Bellam in a Telugu kitchen usually means one of two things: cheruku bellam, made from sugarcane juice, or thati bellam, made from the sap of the palmyra palm. FSSAI treats them as two separate products, each with its own standard.
seg.5094f960d9a4.t: ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯆꯥꯛꯈꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯅꯤ: ꯆꯦꯔꯨꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ, ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯇꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ, ꯇꯥꯜ ꯎꯄꯥꯜꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯇꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯏ, ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.5094f960d9a4.back: In the Telugu kitchen, when one says bellam, most of the time it means one of two things: cheruku bellam, made from sugarcane juice, or tati bellam, made from the juice (sap) of the palm tree. FSSAI takes these as two different things, and each has its own standard.

seg.13fd9611c493.src: They can look alike in a lump, but they taste different and suit different dishes. Here is how to tell them apart, which to use where, and how to keep them. There is a full Telugu section further down.
seg.13fd9611c493.t: ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯎꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯐꯩ꯫ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯈꯥꯏꯗꯣꯛꯀꯗꯒꯦ, ꯀꯔꯝꯕꯥ ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯒꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯒꯦ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.13fd9611c493.back: When they are in lump (grain) form they may look the same, but the taste is different and they are good in different foods. How to tell them apart, which to use where, and how to keep them, is here. At the bottom there is a full Telugu section.

seg.124d6789cba2.t: ⟦1⟧ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯅꯤ⟦/1⟧ꯑꯣꯏ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯆꯤꯠꯇꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯀꯥꯄꯜꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯆꯨ ꯊꯥꯕ ꯂꯝꯁꯤꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ꯫ ꯌꯦꯠ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯒꯣꯗꯥꯕꯔꯤ ꯗꯦꯜꯇꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ꯫ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯅꯔꯁꯔꯥꯎꯄꯦꯠꯇꯥ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯈꯤꯕ꯫
seg.124d6789cba2.back: ⟦1⟧Our two jaggeries⟦/1⟧On the left: sugarcane jaggery from the sugarcane-growing areas of Chittoor and Anakapalli. On the right: palm jaggery from the Godavari delta. Both were packed at Narasaraopet.

seg.70c115199d4c.src: Cane jaggery (cheruku bellam) is boiled-down sugarcane juice with a mellow, caramel sweetness: the one for payasam, pongal and chimmili. Palm jaggery (thati bellam) is boiled-down palmyra sap, darker and deeper in taste: a favourite in filter coffee and tea. You can swap one for the other gram for gram; start with a little less palm jaggery. Keep both in an airtight jar.
seg.70c115199d4c.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯆꯦꯔꯨꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯅꯤ, ꯅꯦꯝꯕ, ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ: ꯄꯥꯌꯁꯝ, ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯤꯝꯃꯤꯂꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯎꯄꯥꯜꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯅꯤ, ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ: ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯤ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯕ꯫ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯥꯝ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ; ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.70c115199d4c.back: Sugarcane jaggery (cheruku bellam) is sugarcane juice boiled and thickened, with a mild (soft), caramel-like sweet taste: for payasam, pongal and chimmili. Palm jaggery (tati bellam) is palm tree juice boiled and thickened, darker in colour and stronger in taste: liked by many people in filter coffee and tea. One can be used instead of the other gram for gram; start by adding a little less palm jaggery. Keep both in an airtight jar.

seg.db3bddd4a4fc.src: Cane jaggery is made wherever sugarcane grows: the juice is pressed out of the cane and boiled down in open pans. In Andhra Pradesh, Anakapalli has the second largest jaggery market in India.
seg.db3bddd4a4fc.t: ꯆꯨ ꯊꯥꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ: ꯆꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯔꯁ ꯅꯝꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯗꯦꯁꯇꯥ, ꯑꯅꯀꯥꯄꯜꯂꯤꯗꯥ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯥꯒꯤ ꯑꯅꯤꯁꯨꯕꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯎꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯀꯩꯊꯦꯜ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.db3bddd4a4fc.back: In every place where sugarcane grows, sugarcane jaggery is made: juice is squeezed from the sugarcane and boiled in big open kadais and thickened. In Andhra Pradesh, at Anakapalli, there is India's second biggest jaggery market.

seg.31988f9e86fc.src: Palm jaggery is made from the sap of the palmyra palm, thati chettu in Telugu. The sap is called neera, or thati neera, and it is boiled down until it sets.
seg.31988f9e86fc.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯎꯄꯥꯜꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯇꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ, ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯆꯦꯠꯇꯨ꯫ ꯔꯁ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯅꯤꯔꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯅꯤꯔꯥ ꯀꯧꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ꯫
seg.31988f9e86fc.back: Palm jaggery is made from the juice of the palm tree, in Telugu tati chettu. The juice is called neera, or tati neera, and it is boiled until it thickens.

seg.7231a4f0bd69.src: Payasam, sweet pongal and ⟦1⟧bellam paramannam⟦/1⟧: cane jaggery.
seg.7231a4f0bd69.t: ꯄꯥꯌꯁꯝ, ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯔꯃꯥꯟꯅꯝ⟦/1⟧: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ꯫
seg.7231a4f0bd69.back: Payasam, sweet pongal and ⟦1⟧bellam paramannam⟦/1⟧: sugarcane jaggery.

seg.2b10b5036017.src: Filter coffee and tea: palm jaggery. Its deeper taste stands up to the decoction; try our ⟦1⟧palm jaggery coffee⟦/1⟧.
seg.2b10b5036017.t: ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥ: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯅꯥ ꯗꯤꯀꯣꯛꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ; ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯀꯣꯐꯤ⟦/1⟧ ꯁꯦꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2b10b5036017.back: Filter coffee and tea: palm jaggery. Its strong taste matches the taste of the decoction; make our ⟦1⟧palm jaggery coffee⟦/1⟧ and see.

seg.39f0609ee4de.src: ⟦1⟧Pasupu paalu⟦/1⟧: either one, as you like it.
seg.39f0609ee4de.back: ⟦1⟧Pasupu palu⟦/1⟧: any one, as you like.

seg.35b1f8b220a2.back: Using one instead of the other

seg.46fffb385af6.src: Use the same weight. Palm jaggery tastes stronger, so start with a little less and add more to taste.
seg.46fffb385af6.t: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.46fffb385af6.back: Use the same weight. Palm jaggery's taste is stronger, therefore start by adding a little less and add more after tasting.

seg.8a98e07b6f1e.src: In milk, coffee or tea, add either jaggery after the milk is off the boil, so the milk does not split.
seg.8a98e07b6f1e.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ, ꯀꯣꯐꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯗꯥ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯎꯠꯄꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯀꯅꯥꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯃꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯣꯏ꯫
seg.8a98e07b6f1e.back: In milk, coffee or tea, add any jaggery after the milk has cooled from boiling, so that the milk will not break.

seg.6788faade30c.src: Keep jaggery in an airtight jar in a cool, dry place.
seg.6788faade30c.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ, ꯏꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯐꯝꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6788faade30c.back: Keep jaggery in an airtight jar, in a cool and dry place.

seg.5ea00ae441ac.src: Use a dry spoon or knife. Jaggery takes in moisture from the air and turns sticky.
seg.5ea00ae441ac.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯡ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠꯇꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯕ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯀꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.5ea00ae441ac.back: Use a dry spoon or knife. Jaggery takes moisture from the air and becomes sticky.

seg.1d7ae0c59b87.src: If it sets hard, grate it.
seg.1d7ae0c59b87.back: If it has become hard, grate it.

seg.8be6c65e90d5.src: Use it within the best-before date on the pack.
seg.8be6c65e90d5.t: ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯕꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ-ꯕꯤꯐꯣꯔ ꯇꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8be6c65e90d5.back: Use before the best-before date that is on the pack.

seg.cc5783126657.src: Is palm jaggery the same as karupatti?
seg.cc5783126657.back: Are palm jaggery and karupatti the same?

seg.f7071649dddd.src: Yes. Karupatti is the Tamil name for jaggery made from palmyra sap. In Telugu it is thati bellam, and in Hindi taad ka gud.
seg.f7071649dddd.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯀꯔꯨꯄꯠꯇꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯎꯄꯥꯜꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯇꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯇꯥꯃꯤꯜ ꯃꯤꯡꯅꯤ꯫ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯟꯗꯤꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯗ ꯀꯥ ꯒꯨꯗ꯫
seg.f7071649dddd.back: Yes. Karupatti is the Tamil name of jaggery made from the juice of the palm tree. In Telugu it is tati bellam, and in Hindi taad ka gud.

seg.a591ce90fac8.src: Is gud the same as jaggery?
seg.a591ce90fac8.back: Are gud and jaggery the same?

seg.9e04d6270c92.src: Yes. Gud, or gur, is the Hindi word for jaggery, and bellam is the Telugu one. On its own it usually means cane jaggery.
seg.9e04d6270c92.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯒꯨꯗ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ, ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯖꯦꯒꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯍꯤꯟꯗꯤ ꯋꯥꯍꯩꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯋꯥꯍꯩꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.9e04d6270c92.back: Yes. Gud, or gur, is the Hindi word for jaggery, and bellam is the Telugu word. When said by itself, most of the time it means sugarcane jaggery.

seg.e531a25812a8.src: Why has my jaggery gone sticky?
seg.e531a25812a8.back: Why has my jaggery become sticky?

seg.cc79285bfadd.src: It has taken in moisture from the air, which happens faster in humid weather. Move it to an airtight jar and use a dry spoon.

seg.cc79285bfadd.back: It has taken moisture from the air; this happens faster in times of humid air. Put it in an airtight jar and use a dry spoon.

seg.1bdcd09c5ca0.src: Can I use palm jaggery in payasam?
seg.1bdcd09c5ca0.back: Can palm jaggery be used in payasam?

seg.8ba95d799ac9.src: Yes. It gives a darker colour and a deeper taste. Add it off the heat, as you would cane jaggery.

seg.8ba95d799ac9.back: Yes. It gives a darker colour and a stronger taste. Like sugarcane jaggery, add it after taking off the fire.
