seg.2b6b229e651e.src: FSSAI's standard says turmeric powder must be free from added colouring matter, including lead chromate, and from foreign starch. Its testing manual lists what inspectors check turmeric for: added dyes such as metanil yellow, lead salts, and chalk powder.
seg.2b6b229e651e.t: FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ, ꯂꯦꯗ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯃꯦꯠ ꯌꯥꯎꯅꯥ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯣꯠꯀꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯅꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯒꯤ ꯂꯤꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯂꯩ: ꯃꯦꯇꯥꯅꯤꯜ ꯌꯦꯂꯣꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯗꯥꯏ, ꯂꯦꯗꯀꯤ ꯁꯣꯜꯇ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ꯫
seg.2b6b229e651e.back: The FSSAI standard says that colour-giving substances mixed into turmeric powder, including lead chromate, and the starch of other things must not be present. Its testing manual has a list of what checkers check in turmeric: mixed-in dyes like metanil yellow, lead salts, and chalk powder.

seg.b27088069a9d.src: Some of this you can check in your kitchen, and some only a lab can find. This guide covers both, plus two popular tests that do not work for turmeric. Try them on any turmeric you buy, ours included.
seg.b27088069a9d.t: ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯈꯔꯗꯤ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯈꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯗꯤ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯊꯤꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫ ꯒꯥꯏꯗ ꯑꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯂꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯇꯧꯗꯕ, ꯃꯤ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯅꯤꯁꯨ ꯂꯩ꯫ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯅꯥ꯫
seg.b27088069a9d.back: Some of these can be checked in your kitchen, and some only a lab can find. This guide has both, and also two tests that many people use which do not work for turmeric. Do them on every turmeric you buy, ours included.

seg.b74ab3f9bb3e.src: Two glasses of water after the turmeric check. Left: pale yellow water with the powder settled at the bottom. Right: strong yellow water with yellow trails running down from the powder.
seg.b74ab3f9bb3e.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯣꯏ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ, ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕ꯫ ꯌꯦꯠ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ, ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯔꯀꯄ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯁꯤꯡ꯫
seg.b74ab3f9bb3e.back: Two glasses of water after checking turmeric. On the left: water with a little yellow colour, powder sunk to the bottom. On the right: water deep yellow in colour, streaks of yellow colour flowing down from the powder to the bottom.

seg.c8b6eb5f9530.src: ⟦1⟧The water check⟦/1⟧Left: the powder has settled and the water is pale yellow. Right: strong yellow trails ran from the powder as it sank, and the water turned deep yellow. That one is worth a lab test.
seg.c8b6eb5f9530.t: ⟦1⟧ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ⟦/1⟧ꯑꯣꯏ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯦ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯂꯩ꯫ ꯌꯦꯠ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯈꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯈꯤ꯫ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ꯫
seg.c8b6eb5f9530.back: ⟦1⟧Water check⟦/1⟧On the left: the powder has sunk to the bottom and the water has only a little yellow colour. On the right: while the powder was sinking, deep yellow streaks flowed from it, and the water became very deep yellow. For that one a lab test is needed.

seg.a7363cc3fa37.src: Sprinkle a teaspoon of turmeric on a glass of water and let it settle without stirring. Turmeric sinks and leaves the water pale yellow; water that turns strong yellow straight away points to added colour. This check cannot find lead chromate or chalk, so for a sure answer, use a food testing lab. Skip the iodine test: turmeric is starchy to begin with.
seg.a7363cc3fa37.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯊꯃꯖꯤ; ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯂꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ꯫ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯂꯦꯗ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯃꯦꯠ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯣꯛ ꯊꯤꯕ ꯉꯝꯗꯦ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯇꯧꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ꯫
seg.a7363cc3fa37.back: Sprinkle one small spoon of turmeric on top of a glass of water and leave it to sink without stirring. Turmeric sinks to the bottom and gives the water only a little yellow colour; water that becomes deep yellow immediately points to mixed-in colour. This check cannot find lead chromate or chalk, therefore to know for sure use a food testing lab. Leave out (skip) the iodine test: turmeric itself has starch.

seg.34d6f989bfaf.src: Such as metanil yellow, which can make dull turmeric look brighter. FSSAI does not allow added colour in turmeric.
seg.34d6f989bfaf.t: ꯃꯦꯇꯥꯅꯤꯜ ꯌꯦꯂꯣꯒꯨꯝꯕ, ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯗꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯕꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯎꯍꯟꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯌꯥꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫
seg.34d6f989bfaf.back: Like metanil yellow, which can make turmeric with little colour look brighter. FSSAI does not allow mixing colour into turmeric.

seg.042cabe54b01.src: Lead chromate and other lead salts
seg.042cabe54b01.t: ꯂꯦꯗ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯃꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯂꯦꯗꯀꯤ ꯁꯣꯜꯇꯁꯤꯡ
seg.042cabe54b01.back: Lead chromate and other lead salts

seg.8310b11eab8b.src: Lead chromate is a yellow pigment used in paint. Stanford-led studies published in 2019 and 2024 found it in turmeric from parts of South Asia. FSSAI does not allow it in turmeric at all.
seg.8310b11eab8b.t: ꯂꯦꯗ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯃꯦꯠ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯄꯦꯟꯠꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ꯫ 2019 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ 2024ꯗꯥ ꯐꯣꯡꯗꯣꯀꯈꯤꯕ, ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯐꯣꯔꯗꯅꯥ ꯂꯃꯖꯤꯡꯈꯤꯕ ꯊꯤꯖꯤꯟꯕꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯈꯥ ꯑꯦꯁꯤꯌꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯈꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯐꯪꯈꯤ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫
seg.8310b11eab8b.back: Lead chromate is a yellow colour-giving substance used in paint. Studies led by Stanford, published in 2019 and 2024, found it in turmeric from some places in South Asia. FSSAI never allows it in turmeric at all.

seg.4278e7c5416c.src: A cheap white powder that adds weight.
seg.4278e7c5416c.t: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯍꯦꯅꯒꯠꯍꯟꯕ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯄꯥꯝꯕ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯥ꯫
seg.4278e7c5416c.back: A cheap white powder that increases weight.

seg.5a8b446bbce0.src: Flour or starch from other crops. FSSAI's standard rules it out too.
seg.5a8b446bbce0.t: ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯃꯍꯩꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯥꯇꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ꯫ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫
seg.5a8b446bbce0.back: Flour or starch of other crops (fruits). The FSSAI standard does not allow this either.

seg.1b1af7f63ffd.src: Fill a clear glass with water at room temperature.
seg.1b1af7f63ffd.t: ꯃꯌꯦꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯑꯁꯥ-ꯑꯏꯪꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1b1af7f63ffd.back: Fill a clear glass with water at home room temperature (warm-cold).

seg.653731f2ed6f.src: Sprinkle one level teaspoon of turmeric powder on top. Do not stir.
seg.653731f2ed6f.t: ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯊꯛ ꯆꯥꯞ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯒꯅꯨ꯫
seg.653731f2ed6f.back: Sprinkle on top one small spoon of turmeric powder, levelled at the top. Do not stir.

seg.ea5b43cf8436.src: Watch the first minute as the powder sinks. Look for coloured trails running down from it.
seg.ea5b43cf8436.t: ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯤꯉꯩꯒꯤ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯔꯀꯄ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ea5b43cf8436.back: Watch the first minute while the powder sinks. Look for coloured streaks flowing down from it to the bottom.

seg.e37698aaa3fb.src: Leave it for 15 to 20 minutes. Then hold the glass against a white wall or a sheet of paper and look at the water above the settled powder.
seg.e37698aaa3fb.t: ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15ꯗꯒꯤ 20 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯐꯛꯂꯥꯡ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯦ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e37698aaa3fb.back: Keep it for 15 to 20 minutes. Then, holding the glass in front of a white wall or a paper, look at the water above the sunk powder.

seg.e8937cebf136.src: Pale yellow water, powder at the bottom
seg.e8937cebf136.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ, ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ
seg.e8937cebf136.back: Water with a little yellow colour, powder at the bottom

seg.7253b4d90896.back: Not even one sign of mixed-in dye.

seg.256ce5cf303d.src: Strong yellow trails, or deep yellow water within minutes
seg.256ce5cf303d.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯁꯤꯡ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯈꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ
seg.256ce5cf303d.back: Deep yellow streaks, or water that becomes very deep yellow within a few minutes

seg.ce06c8148072.src: Possible added colour. Stop using that batch and get it tested.
seg.ce06c8148072.t: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯈꯤꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ce06c8148072.back: Colour may have been mixed in. Stop using that batch and get it tested.

seg.53d9c5db264d.src: ⟦1⟧Why it works.⟦/1⟧ Turmeric's own yellow, curcumin, hardly dissolves in water, so the powder sinks and only tints the water. Dyes such as metanil yellow dissolve easily and colour the water fast.
seg.53d9c5db264d.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯦ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ, ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯦ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯃꯦꯇꯥꯅꯤꯜ ꯌꯦꯂꯣꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯗꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.53d9c5db264d.back: ⟦1⟧Why this works.⟦/1⟧ Turmeric's own colour, curcumin, does not dissolve much in water, therefore the powder sinks to the bottom and gives the water only a little colour. Dyes like metanil yellow dissolve easily and quickly give colour to the water.

seg.af4442c6e910.src: ⟦1⟧What it misses.⟦/1⟧ Lead chromate and chalk do not dissolve in water either, so turmeric mixed with them can pass this check. Only a lab test can rule them out.
seg.af4442c6e910.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯊꯤꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕꯒꯦ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯂꯦꯗ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯃꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯣꯀꯁꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯦ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯄꯥꯁ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯍꯅꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.af4442c6e910.back: ⟦1⟧What this cannot find.⟦/1⟧ Lead chromate and chalk also do not dissolve in water, therefore turmeric mixed with them can pass this check. Only a lab test can make known that they are not present.

seg.a8b61850b87d.src: Very fine powder can keep the water cloudy for a while. Cloudy is fine; a clear, strong yellow is what to look for.
seg.a8b61850b87d.t: ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯌꯦꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯃꯌꯦꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯕꯁꯨ ꯑꯔꯥꯅꯕ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ; ꯌꯦꯡꯒꯗꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯌꯦꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯕ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯅꯤ꯫
seg.a8b61850b87d.back: Very fine powder can keep the water not clear (cloudy) for some time. Being cloudy is also not bad; what to look for is clear, deep yellow water.

seg.c3455d1f4c96.src: Check 2: if you buy whole turmeric
seg.c3455d1f4c96.t: ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ 2: ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯗꯤ
seg.c3455d1f4c96.back: Check 2: if you buy whole turmeric

seg.3d4e366bb488.src: Snap a finger of dried turmeric in half. Turmeric is yellow-orange right through, so the inside should look much like the outside. A bright yellow skin over a pale or dull core can mean colour was added to the surface. Ask the seller about it, or get it tested.
seg.3d4e366bb488.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯃꯄꯥꯟ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ-ꯀꯃꯂꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯒꯨꯝꯅꯥ ꯎꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯗꯕ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯀꯨꯞ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯈꯤꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯣꯟꯕ ꯃꯤꯗꯥ ꯍꯪꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3d4e366bb488.back: Break one dried turmeric piece into two. Turmeric is turmeric-orange colour all through, inside and outside, therefore the inside should look like the outside. If there is a bright yellow skin over an inside with little colour, colour may have been added on top. Ask the seller about it, or get it tested.

seg.4c4dc95561d2.src: Iodine turns blue-black when it meets starch, and it is often suggested for spotting flour in turmeric. But turmeric is starchy itself, so it turns blue-black either way. That is why FSSAI's own manual uses the iodine test for powdered spices other than turmeric.
seg.4c4dc95561d2.t: ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆꯒꯥ ꯊꯦꯡꯅꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ-ꯑꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯥꯇꯥ ꯊꯤꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯖꯩ꯫ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯝꯕꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕꯁꯨ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ-ꯑꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫ ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯅꯥ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯅꯠꯇꯕ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.4c4dc95561d2.back: Iodine becomes blue-black when it touches starch, and it is often said to be for finding flour in turmeric. But turmeric itself has starch, therefore it becomes blue-black in any case. Therefore FSSAI's own manual uses this iodine test for other powdered spices that are not turmeric.

seg.fc16ff8016e3.src: FSSAI's tests for lead, metanil yellow and chalk in turmeric use concentrated hydrochloric or sulphuric acid. These acids burn skin and eyes. They belong in a lab, not a kitchen.
seg.fc16ff8016e3.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯗ, ꯃꯦꯇꯥꯅꯤꯜ ꯌꯦꯂꯣ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯣꯛ ꯊꯤꯅꯕꯥ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯍꯥꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯣꯛꯂꯣꯔꯤꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯜꯐꯤꯎꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯦꯁꯤꯗ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫ ꯑꯦꯁꯤꯗ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯎꯟ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯠ ꯆꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯂꯦꯕꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯆꯥꯛꯈꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫
seg.fc16ff8016e3.back: FSSAI's tests for finding lead, metanil yellow and chalk in turmeric use strong hydrochloric or sulphuric acid. These acids burn skin and eyes. They should be used in a lab, not in a kitchen.

seg.1dd87aa7bdc7.src: For a sure answer: a food testing lab
seg.1dd87aa7bdc7.t: ꯁꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯅꯕꯥ: ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ
seg.1dd87aa7bdc7.back: To know for sure: a food testing lab

seg.1883beca4d73.src: A NABL-accredited food testing lab can test turmeric for lead and for added colours. Ask the lab how much sample it needs, keep the powder in its sealed pack or a clean sealed bag, and note the batch number printed on the pack. FSSAI publishes a list of notified food testing labs on its website.
seg.1883beca4d73.t: NABL-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯅꯤꯡꯕ ꯄꯤꯔꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯗ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫ ꯂꯦꯕꯇꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯄꯜ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯪꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯁꯤꯜ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯕ, ꯁꯤꯜ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯕꯦꯒ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯝꯕꯔ ꯏꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯋꯦꯕꯁꯥꯏꯠꯇꯥ ꯅꯣꯇꯤꯐꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯂꯤꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯐꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯏ꯫
seg.1883beca4d73.back: A NABL-recognised food testing lab can test turmeric for lead and mixed-in colour. Ask the lab how much sample is needed, keep the powder in its own sealed pack or in a clean, sealed bag, and write down the batch number that is on the pack. FSSAI shows on its website a list of notified food testing labs.

seg.456379c75c24.src: Read the pack before you buy

seg.ff7951e2f36b.src: An FSSAI licence or registration number. You can look it up on FSSAI's FoSCoS website.
seg.ff7951e2f36b.t: FSSAI ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯦꯟꯁ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯔꯦꯖꯤꯁ꯭ꯠꯔꯦꯁꯟ ꯅꯝꯕꯔ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ FoSCoS ꯋꯦꯕꯁꯥꯏꯠꯇꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.ff7951e2f36b.back: FSSAI licence or registration number. This can be checked on FSSAI's FoSCoS website.

seg.476e4849c1d8.src: The name and address of whoever made or packed it.
seg.476e4849c1d8.t: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯃꯤ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯦꯗ꯭ꯔꯦꯁ꯫
seg.476e4849c1d8.back: The name and address of the person who made or packed it.

seg.beee8eda6466.src: Net quantity, MRP, a batch or lot number, and a best-before date.
seg.beee8eda6466.t: ꯅꯦꯠ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ, MRP, ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯠ ꯅꯝꯕꯔ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ-ꯕꯤꯐꯣꯔ ꯇꯥꯡ꯫
seg.beee8eda6466.back: Net quantity, MRP, batch or lot number, and best-before date.

seg.f9270fd96202.src: Where it was grown. Turmeric from different regions differs in colour, so a named region helps you compare like with like.
seg.f9270fd96202.t: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ꯫ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯕ ꯂꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯈꯜ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯡꯗꯝꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯦꯡ ꯄꯥꯡꯏ꯫
seg.f9270fd96202.back: Where it was grown. The colour of turmeric from different regions differs, therefore having the region's name helps in comparing the same kinds.

seg.7cdc58c0c7e8.src: Keep the pack zipped shut, or move the powder to a dry, airtight jar.
seg.7cdc58c0c7e8.t: ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯖꯤꯞ ꯊꯤꯡꯖꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7cdc58c0c7e8.back: Keep the pack with the zip closed, or put the powder into a dry, airtight jar.

seg.bb4d61f86b55.src: Use a dry spoon. A damp spoon is what makes turmeric lumpy.
seg.bb4d61f86b55.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.bb4d61f86b55.back: Use a dry spoon. A wet spoon makes the turmeric lumpy.

seg.a92c022ff52e.src: Keep it out of direct sunlight, which fades the colour.
seg.a92c022ff52e.t: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯀꯤ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯍꯛꯊꯦꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯕ ꯃꯐꯝꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.a92c022ff52e.back: Keep it in a place where sunlight does not fall directly, because that destroys the colour.

seg.6911ce63edde.src: Is very bright yellow turmeric a bad sign?
seg.6911ce63edde.t: ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯐꯠꯇꯕ ꯈꯨꯗꯝꯅꯤ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.6911ce63edde.back: Is turmeric with a very bright yellow colour a sign of bad turmeric?

seg.a0ce62cee740.src: Not by itself. Colour changes with the variety, where it was grown and how it was dried and ground, so turmerics differ a lot. What matters is colour that leaves the powder too easily, as in the water check.
seg.a0ce62cee740.t: ꯃꯁꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯈꯜ, ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯩ꯫ ꯌꯦꯡꯒꯗꯕꯗꯤ: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯎꯕꯒꯨꯝꯅꯥ, ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯤꯕꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.a0ce62cee740.back: Not by itself alone. The colour changes according to the variety, where it was grown and how it was dried and ground, therefore turmerics differ a lot. What to look for is: as seen in the water check, whether the colour comes out very easily from the powder.

seg.e8cc5edbb092.src: Can the water check show that turmeric has no lead?
seg.e8cc5edbb092.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯗ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯛꯄ ꯉꯝꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.e8cc5edbb092.back: Can the water check show that there is no lead in turmeric?

seg.37eb38df9ce8.src: No. Lead chromate does not dissolve in water, so the water check cannot see it. Only a lab test can.
seg.37eb38df9ce8.t: ꯉꯝꯗꯦ꯫ ꯂꯦꯗ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯃꯦꯠ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯦ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯎꯕ ꯉꯝꯗꯦ꯫ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.37eb38df9ce8.back: It cannot. Lead chromate does not dissolve in water, therefore the water check cannot see it. Only a lab test can.

seg.2b76cd3e665b.src: Moisture. A wet spoon or an open pack lets the powder take in water. Break the lumps with a dry spoon and keep the pack sealed.
seg.2b76cd3e665b.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯄꯦꯛꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯂꯧꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯤꯡꯖꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2b76cd3e665b.back: Because of moisture. A wet spoon or an opened pack makes the powder take in water. Break the lumps with a dry spoon and keep the pack closed.

seg.87fe2929801d.src: What should I do if a check looks wrong?
seg.87fe2929801d.t: ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯑꯔꯥꯅꯕ ꯎꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯇꯧꯒꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.87fe2929801d.back: What should be done if something bad shows in a check?

seg.e83aba6cc6df.src: Stop using that batch, keep the pack, and contact the seller with the batch number. You can also report it to FSSAI through its Food Safety Connect app. If it is ours, WhatsApp us a photo of the pack and the glass.
seg.e83aba6cc6df.t: ꯕꯦꯆ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯝꯕꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯣꯟꯕ ꯃꯤꯗꯥ ꯄꯥꯎ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ Food Safety Connect ꯑꯦꯞꯀꯤ ꯈꯨꯠꯊꯥꯡꯗꯥ FSSAI-ꯗꯥ ꯔꯤꯄꯣꯔꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁꯀꯤ ꯐꯣꯇꯣ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯗꯥ WhatsApp-ꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e83aba6cc6df.back: Stop using that batch, keep the pack, and send word to the seller with the batch number. Reporting to FSSAI through FSSAI's Food Safety Connect app is also possible. If it is ours, send a photo of the pack and the glass to us on WhatsApp.

seg.1dd4194330b1.src: Try these checks on ours too. If anything looks off, ⟦1⟧WhatsApp us⟦/1⟧ a photo with the batch number from the pack.
seg.1dd4194330b1.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯁꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯑꯔꯥꯅꯕ ꯎꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯄꯦꯛꯀꯤ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯝꯕꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯐꯣꯇꯣ ꯑꯃꯥ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯗꯥ WhatsApp ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧꯫
seg.1dd4194330b1.back: Do these checks on our turmeric too. If anything at all bad shows, ⟦1⟧WhatsApp us⟦/1⟧ a photo together with the pack's batch number.

seg.2aa376ceaeac.back: Andhra home cooking with our Karam, Pasupu, Bellam and Jeedipappu, from Sunday Kodi Kura to festival Paramannam. Every recipe has a link to the pack that is used.

seg.91bce9460ade.src: Kodi kura is the chicken curry that fills Andhra homes on a Sunday afternoon: bone-in chicken marinated in chilli and turmeric, cooked down in a gravy of deep-golden onions and tomatoes, and finished with garam masala. It goes to the table with hot rice, and the leftovers with dosa or chapati at night.
seg.91bce9460ade.t: ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯅꯣꯡꯃꯥꯏꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯤ: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯑꯍꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯗꯣꯁꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯄꯥꯇꯤꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫
seg.91bce9460ade.back: Kodi kura is the chicken-meat curry cooked in every Andhra house on Sunday afternoon: bone-in chicken marinated in chilli and turmeric, cooked in a gravy of onion turned deep golden colour and tomato, finished with garam masala. It is eaten with hot rice, and the leftover is eaten at night with dosa or chapati.

seg.2422ebb922bc.src: The heat here comes from our Teja chilli powder, the extra-hot Guntur chilli that gives Andhra curries their bite and bright red colour, with our turmeric powder in the marinade. This recipe serves 4 and is properly fiery; the tips say how to scale it down.
seg.2422ebb922bc.t: ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯁꯦꯡꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ; ꯇꯤꯞꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯅꯒꯗꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.2422ebb922bc.back: Its spiciness comes from our Teja chilli powder, the very hot Guntur chilli which gives Andhra curries their fiery spiciness and red colour, and our turmeric powder in the marinade. This recipe is for 4 people and is truly spicy; the tips say how to reduce it.

seg.6037465ed8d2.src: Total includes 30 minutes for the marinade.
seg.6037465ed8d2.back: 30 minutes for marinating is included in the total.

seg.9cb820880217.src: Marinate chicken in curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt, then cook it in a deep-golden onion and tomato gravy. Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.
seg.9cb820880217.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ, ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9cb820880217.back: Marinate the chicken in curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt, then cook in a gravy of onion turned deep golden and tomato. Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.

seg.d35e8cdc661c.src: 750 g chicken ⟦1⟧bone-in, curry-cut pieces, washed and drained well⟦/1⟧
seg.d35e8cdc661c.t: 750 g ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ⟦1⟧ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ, ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ, ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.d35e8cdc661c.back: 750 g chicken ⟦1⟧bone-in, pieces cut for curry, washed and water drained well⟦/1⟧

seg.c84970cf7b6f.t: ꯀꯞ ½ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯊꯨꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯍꯜꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.c84970cf7b6f.back: ½ cup curd ⟦1⟧thick, stirred to make soft⟦/1⟧

seg.9e9cb51b1458.src: 2 tsp Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; use 1 tsp for medium heat⟦/1⟧
seg.9e9cb51b1458.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2 ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ; ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.9e9cb51b1458.back: 2 teaspoons Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very spicy; for medium spiciness use 1 teaspoon⟦/1⟧

seg.9654088d205e.src: 1 tsp salt ⟦1⟧plus more to taste at the end⟦/1⟧
seg.9654088d205e.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯊꯨꯝ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.9654088d205e.back: 1 teaspoon salt ⟦1⟧at the end taste and add more⟦/1⟧

seg.fff6117cc0f5.src: 3 tbsp oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is the usual Andhra choice⟦/1⟧
seg.fff6117cc0f5.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠꯀꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ⟦/1⟧
seg.fff6117cc0f5.back: 3 tablespoons oil ⟦1⟧in Andhra, peanut oil is used most of the time⟦/1⟧

seg.de3654151f5d.t: ꯂꯕꯉ꯭ꯒ 3, ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ 2, 1-ꯏꯟꯆꯒꯤ ꯗꯥꯂꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ⟦/1⟧

seg.3347559a7b17.src: 1 cup hot water ⟦1⟧a little more for a thinner gravy⟦/1⟧
seg.3347559a7b17.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.3347559a7b17.back: 1 cup hot water ⟦1⟧a little more for thin gravy⟦/1⟧

seg.cf5fbb1e5375.back: Also goes very well with ⟦1⟧Sannam chilli powder⟦/1⟧.

seg.b4fe3cc46ec4.src: Rub the chicken with curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Rest 30 minutes. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge if your kitchen is hot.
seg.b4fe3cc46ec4.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ, ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯃꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 30 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯈꯨꯝ ꯁꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b4fe3cc46ec4.back: Mix the chicken with curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Keep it 30 minutes. If your kitchen is hot, cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge.

seg.217eb90c7dac.src: Heat the oil in a heavy pan or kadai on medium heat. Add the cloves, cardamoms and cinnamon and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
seg.217eb90c7dac.t: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯂꯕꯉ꯭ꯒ, ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯂꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯆꯤꯟ ꯆꯤꯟ ꯍꯥꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.217eb90c7dac.back: Heat the oil on medium flame in a heavy pan or kadai. Add cloves, cardamom and cinnamon and let them sizzle a few seconds.

seg.41164e7a534a.src: Add the onions, green chillies and curry leaves.
seg.41164e7a534a.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.41164e7a534a.back: Add onion, green chilli and curry leaves.

seg.127dbd26bc4d.src: Fry the onions in oil till deep golden. This takes 12–15 minutes on medium heat; stir often so they brown evenly without burning.
seg.127dbd26bc4d.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯕꯨ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 12–15 ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯞ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯛꯂꯣꯏ꯫
seg.127dbd26bc4d.back: Fry the onion in the oil until it becomes deep golden colour. On medium flame it takes 12–15 minutes; stir every now and then, then it will become evenly brown and will not burn.

seg.3fa3e9f33095.src: Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomatoes, and cook till soft. Fry the paste for 1 minute until the raw smell goes, then cook the tomatoes for 5–6 minutes, mashing them, until they break down and oil shows at the edges.
seg.3fa3e9f33095.t: ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯅꯣꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯎꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–6 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3fa3e9f33095.back: Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomato, and cook until soft. Fry the paste 1 minute until the uncooked smell goes, then cook the tomatoes 5–6 minutes, pressing them, until they melt and oil comes out at the edges.

seg.24dbd7dfd784.src: Stir in the coriander powder and fry for 30 seconds.
seg.24dbd7dfd784.t: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 30 ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.24dbd7dfd784.back: Add coriander powder, stir and fry 30 seconds.

seg.461e7a0a9c22.src: Add the chicken and cook covered on medium heat till no pink remains near the bone. Fry it uncovered for the first 5 minutes until the pieces turn opaque, then pour in the hot water, cover and cook for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
seg.461e7a0a9c22.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯎꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 20 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯃꯇꯝꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ꯫
seg.461e7a0a9c22.back: Add the chicken and cook covered on medium flame until not even one pink colour appears near the bone. In the first 5 minutes fry uncovered until the pieces cannot be seen through in the middle, then pour the hot water and cook covered about 20 minutes, stirring from time to time.

seg.22f96ed1f76e.src: Check a thick piece: the chicken is cooked when no pink remains near the bone and the juices run clear. Taste the gravy and add salt if needed.
seg.22f96ed1f76e.t: ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯁꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯑꯁꯦꯡꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.22f96ed1f76e.back: Check one big piece: the chicken is done when not even one pink colour appears near the bone and the juice comes out clear. Taste the gravy and add salt if needed.

seg.f10b1f5ae914.src: Stir in garam masala and coriander leaves. Simmer 3 minutes, uncovered, until the gravy is as thick as you like and a red film of oil floats on top.
seg.f10b1f5ae914.t: ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯤꯕꯒꯨꯝ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯒꯤ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯂꯩꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯇꯥꯎꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3 ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f10b1f5ae914.back: Add garam masala and coriander leaves and stir. Boil uncovered 3 minutes on low flame, until the gravy becomes as thick as you like and a red layer of oil floats on top.

seg.a7c73631b2ca.src: Switch off and rest the curry for 10 minutes before serving; the gravy settles and the flavour comes together.
seg.a7c73631b2ca.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯂꯦꯡꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.a7c73631b2ca.back: Turn off the flame and keep the curry 10 minutes before serving; the gravy becomes settled and the taste blends.

seg.0b948e3072fa.src: Brown the onions deep golden; the gravy's colour and body come from them.
seg.0b948e3072fa.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯕꯨ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ꯫
seg.0b948e3072fa.back: Brown the onion to a deep golden colour; the gravy's colour and thickness come from them.

seg.e0365adcf1bf.src: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For a medium curry use 1 tsp, or use Sannam chilli powder for red colour with gentler heat.
seg.e0365adcf1bf.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ꯫ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯐꯪꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e0365adcf1bf.back: Teja chilli powder is very spicy. For a medium-spicy curry use 1 teaspoon, or to get red colour with less spiciness use Sannam chilli powder.

seg.57940a63282d.src: Use bone-in pieces; the bones give the gravy its depth.
seg.57940a63282d.t: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯁꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.57940a63282d.back: Use bone-in pieces; the bones give the gravy a thick (rich) taste.

seg.4f9718c3bc6f.src: Let the oil separate from the tomato masala before the chicken goes in, or the gravy tastes raw.
seg.4f9718c3bc6f.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯨꯝ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.4f9718c3bc6f.back: Before adding the chicken wait until the oil separates from the tomato masala, otherwise the gravy will taste uncooked.

seg.164627c386b7.src: Kobbari kodi kura: grind 3 tbsp grated coconut with 1 tbsp poppy seeds and a little water, and stir the paste in with the garam masala for a richer gravy.
seg.164627c386b7.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.164627c386b7.back: Coconut kodi kura: grind 3 tablespoons grated coconut and 1 tablespoon poppy seed with a little water, and for a thicker gravy add the paste together with the garam masala and stir.

seg.7d79f857440a.src: Ground masala: dry-roast 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp fennel seeds, 3 cloves and a small piece of cinnamon, grind, and use instead of the coriander powder and garam masala.
seg.7d79f857440a.t: ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1, ꯁꯧꯐ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1, ꯂꯕꯉ꯭ꯒ 3 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯂꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7d79f857440a.back: Ground masala: roast without oil 1 tablespoon coriander seed, 1 teaspoon fennel, 3 cloves and a small piece of cinnamon, grind, and use in place of coriander powder and garam masala.

seg.ea1fd7a2c573.src: Pressure cooker: after adding the chicken and water, cook for 2 whistles and let the pressure drop on its own.
seg.ea1fd7a2c573.t: ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔ: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛ ꯇꯥꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ea1fd7a2c573.back: Pressure cooker: after adding chicken and water, cook until 2 whistles and wait until the pressure goes down by itself.

seg.8b4376996905.src: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, the Sunday way. It also goes well with chapati, dosa or ragi sangati.
seg.8b4376996905.t: ꯅꯣꯡꯃꯥꯏꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗꯥ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯄꯥꯇꯤ, ꯗꯣꯁꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯁꯉ꯭ꯒꯇꯤꯒꯥꯁꯨ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.8b4376996905.back: In the Sunday way, serve hot with rice cooked in steam and one spoon of ghee. It also goes very well with chapati, dosa or ragi sangati.

seg.45cb0a9558e6.src: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat until steaming hot all the way through. The curry tastes deeper the next day.
seg.45cb0a9558e6.t: ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯏ꯫
seg.45cb0a9558e6.back: Cover and keep in the fridge up to 2 days; heat thoroughly until steam comes out right to the inside. On the next day the curry's taste becomes thicker (deeper).

seg.bc11ae48bfcf.src: How do I make Andhra chicken curry less spicy?
seg.bc11ae48bfcf.t: ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯅꯒꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.bc11ae48bfcf.back: How to reduce the spiciness of Andhra chicken curry?

seg.aaa9ea580a50.src: Cut the Teja chilli powder to 1 tsp, or use Sannam chilli powder, which gives the same red colour with gentler heat. A spoon of curd stirred in at the end also softens the bite.
seg.aaa9ea580a50.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯄꯤ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ꯫ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯂꯕꯁꯨ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.aaa9ea580a50.back: Reduce the Teja chilli powder to 1 teaspoon, or use Sannam chilli powder, which gives the same red colour but less spicy. Adding one spoon of curd at the end and stirring also reduces the spiciness.

seg.fe399a2a853e.src: Why is Andhra chicken curry so spicy?
seg.fe399a2a853e.t: ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯂꯤꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.fe399a2a853e.back: Why is Andhra chicken fry so very spicy?

seg.ada87f188506.src: Andhra cooking uses Guntur chillies such as Teja, which are much hotter than the chilli powder used in most other regional curries. The heat is part of the dish.
seg.ada87f188506.t: ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ, ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯂꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯒꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ꯫ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥ ꯑꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ꯫
seg.ada87f188506.back: Andhra cooking uses Guntur chillies like Teja, which are much more spicy than the chilli powder used in curries of many other places. The spiciness is one part of this style.

seg.fc940ab96cce.src: How do I know the chicken is cooked through?
seg.fc940ab96cce.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯔꯕꯔꯥ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯒꯅꯤ?
seg.fc940ab96cce.back: How to know the chicken is cooked to the inside?

seg.1445f73d2fc1.src: Cut into the thickest piece near the bone. The chicken is cooked when no pink remains near the bone and the juices run clear.
seg.1445f73d2fc1.t: ꯁꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯑꯁꯦꯡꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.1445f73d2fc1.back: Cut the piece that is biggest of all near the bone and check. The chicken is done when not even one pink colour appears near the bone and the juice comes out clear.

seg.736c9b09bcd3.src: Can I make kodi kura without curd?
seg.736c9b09bcd3.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.736c9b09bcd3.back: Can kodi kura be made without curd?

seg.f9ab2afc44b4.src: Yes. Marinate the chicken with the chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt and 1 tbsp lemon juice, and add one more tomato to the gravy.
seg.f9ab2afc44b4.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f9ab2afc44b4.back: Yes. Marinate the chicken in chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt and 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and add one more tomato to the gravy.

seg.49c9832aa59a.src: ఆంధ్రా కోడి కూర · Andhra Kodi Kura Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.49c9832aa59a.t: ఆంధ్రా కోడి కూర · ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔ ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯀꯨꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ | 1acrefarms
seg.49c9832aa59a.back: ఆంధ్రా కోడి కూర · Recipe of Andhra Kodi Kura | 1acrefarms

seg.dcb6c98b640e.src: ఆంధ్రా కోడి కూర. The Andhra Sunday chicken curry: chicken marinated in Teja chilli powder and turmeric powder, cooked in a deep onion-tomato gravy with garam masala.
seg.dcb6c98b640e.t: ఆంధ్రా కోడి కూర. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯅꯣꯡꯃꯥꯏꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ, ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ-ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ꯫

seg.b79702dac541.src: Bellam pongali is the sweet pongal that Telugu homes cook on Sankranti morning: rice and roasted moong dal cooked very soft, then sweetened with jaggery and enriched with ghee. It is offered as naivedyam before the festive meal, and it is also the prasadam at many temples and Friday pujas.
seg.b79702dac541.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯡꯀ꯭ꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯅꯤ: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯨꯝꯃꯩꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯆꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯩꯕꯦꯗ꯭ꯌꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯠꯊꯣꯀꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯪ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯁꯥꯗꯝꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯏ꯫
seg.b79702dac541.back: Bellam pongali is the sweet pongal cooked in Telugu houses on Sankranti morning: rice and roasted moong dal cooked very soft, then made sweet with jaggery and made richer with ghee. It is offered as naivedyam before eating the festival meal, and it is also prasadam in many temples and Friday pujas.

seg.17053455adbb.src: Cane jaggery gives it a light brown colour and a round, toffee-like sweetness, and ghee-fried whole cashews from our Jeedipappu pack add the crunch. This recipe serves 4.
seg.17053455adbb.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯣꯐꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯦꯀꯇꯒꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.17053455adbb.back: Sugarcane jaggery gives it a slightly brown colour and a full toffee-like sweet taste, and the whole cashews fried in ghee from our Jeedipappu pack give a crunchy (karak-karak) bite. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.50377f017e4e.src: Cook time is for a pressure cooker; allow about 15 minutes more in a pot.
seg.50377f017e4e.t: ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ; ꯄꯣꯠꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫
seg.50377f017e4e.back: This cooking time is for a pressure cooker; if cooked in a pot it takes about 15 minutes more.

seg.b323962ddab1.src: Cook roasted moong dal and rice till very soft, stir in melted cane jaggery and simmer till glossy. Finish with ghee-fried cashews, raisins and cardamom.
seg.b323962ddab1.t: ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ, ꯀꯤꯁꯃꯤꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b323962ddab1.back: Cook the roasted moong dal and rice until very soft, add melted sugarcane jaggery and stir, and boil on low flame until it shines. Finish with cashews, raisins and cardamom fried in ghee.

seg.15ea2f1a2cd2.src: ¼ cup moong dal ⟦1⟧split yellow moong dal (pesarapappu), about 50 g⟦/1⟧
seg.15ea2f1a2cd2.t: ꯀꯞ ¼ ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ (ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯄꯞꯄꯨ), 50 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.15ea2f1a2cd2.back: ¼ cup moong dal ⟦1⟧split yellow-colour moong dal (pesarapappu), about 50 g⟦/1⟧

seg.9f8bf29ce704.src: 1 cup grated cane jaggery ⟦1⟧lightly packed, about 150 g; a little more if you like it sweeter⟦/1⟧
seg.9f8bf29ce704.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯥ, 150 g ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.9f8bf29ce704.back: 1 cup grated sugarcane jaggery ⟦1⟧not pressed very hard, about 150 g; a little more if you like it sweeter⟦/1⟧

seg.8dff8f977372.src: ¼ cup water ⟦1⟧to melt the jaggery⟦/1⟧
seg.8dff8f977372.back: ¼ cup water ⟦1⟧to melt the jaggery⟦/1⟧

seg.c9f89d999d7a.src: a pinch of edible camphor (pacha karpooram) ⟦1⟧optional; a very small pinch⟦/1⟧
seg.c9f89d999d7a.t: ꯆꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯀꯄꯨꯔ (ꯄꯆꯆꯥ ꯀꯔꯄꯨꯔꯝ) ꯈꯔꯥ ⟦1⟧ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ; ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯈꯔꯥꯈꯛ⟦/1⟧
seg.c9f89d999d7a.back: A little edible camphor (pachcha karpooram) ⟦1⟧if you like; a very tiny bit⟦/1⟧

seg.a6184e3e789c.src: Roast the moong dal till light golden, then cook it with the rice till very soft and mushy. Start by dry-roasting the dal in a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot on low heat, stirring, until it smells nutty and turns light golden, about 3–4 minutes.
seg.a6184e3e789c.t: ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯈꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ, ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3–4 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a6184e3e789c.back: Roast the moong dal until a little golden colour, then cook together with the rice until very soft and melted. First, in the pressure cooker or a heavy-bottomed pot on low flame, roast the dal without oil, stirring, until a nut-like smell comes and it becomes a little golden colour, about 3–4 minutes.

seg.03597768c72a.src: Add the rice to the roasted dal, wash both together in 2–3 changes of water, and drain.
seg.03597768c72a.t: ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯗꯥꯂꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ 2–3 ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.03597768c72a.back: Add the rice to the roasted dal, wash both together changing the water 2–3 times, and drain the water.

seg.1c139f802ab6.src: Add the 3 cups water. Pressure cook for 4–5 whistles on medium heat and let the pressure drop on its own, or simmer covered in a pot for 25–30 minutes, adding a splash of hot water if it dries out.
seg.1c139f802ab6.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 3 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 4–5 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛ ꯇꯥꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 25–30 ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ꯫
seg.1c139f802ab6.back: Add 3 cups water. Cook in the pressure cooker on medium flame until 4–5 whistles and wait until the pressure goes down by itself, or cook covered in a pot on low flame 25–30 minutes, adding a little hot water if it becomes dry.

seg.5c9fcb8182ea.src: Open and mash the rice and dal lightly with the back of a ladle. It should be soft and porridge-like, not dry.
seg.5c9fcb8182ea.t: ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯦꯗꯂꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.5c9fcb8182ea.back: Mash the rice and dal a little with the back of the ladle. It should be soft and like porridge, not dry.

seg.41870045e57c.src: Melt the jaggery in ¼ cup water and pour it into the rice. Warm the jaggery and water in a small pan on low heat, stirring, just until it dissolves, about 2–3 minutes; it does not need to boil.
seg.41870045e57c.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ¼ꯗꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2–3 ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯗꯦ꯫
seg.41870045e57c.back: Melt the jaggery in the ¼ cup water and pour it into the rice. In a small pan on low flame heat the jaggery and water, stirring, only until it melts, about 2–3 minutes; there is no need to boil it.

seg.ca9ed938d301.src: Simmer, stirring, till thick and glossy, 5–7 minutes; stir in 2 tbsp ghee. Keep the heat low and stir all the way to the bottom, as the pongali catches easily once the jaggery is in.
seg.ca9ed938d301.t: ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–7; ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.ca9ed938d301.back: Stirring, boil on low flame until it becomes thick and shines, 5–7 minutes; add 2 tablespoons ghee and stir. Keep the flame low and stir to the bottom, because after adding jaggery the pongali sticks to the bottom very quickly.

seg.58e11747230d.src: Taste, and stir in a little more melted jaggery if you want it sweeter.
seg.58e11747230d.t: ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.58e11747230d.back: Taste, and if you want it sweeter add a little more melted jaggery and stir.

seg.9eabfb77c3db.src: Fry the cashews in the rest of the ghee; add with the cardamom. Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan on medium-low heat and stir the cashews until golden, about 1 minute, adding the raisins for the last few seconds until they puff up.
seg.9eabfb77c3db.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯀꯤꯁꯃꯤꯁ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯄꯨꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.9eabfb77c3db.back: Fry the cashews in the remaining ghee; add together with cardamom. In a small pan heat the remaining 2 tablespoons ghee on medium-low flame and stir the cashews until golden colour, about 1 minute, adding the raisins in the last few seconds until they swell.

seg.4f12a8dd8723.src: Pour the cashews, raisins and ghee over the pongali, sprinkle in the cardamom powder and the camphor, if using, and stir well.
seg.4f12a8dd8723.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ, ꯀꯤꯁꯃꯤꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯄꯨꯔ, ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4f12a8dd8723.back: Pour the cashews, raisins and ghee on top of the pongali, sprinkle cardamom powder and camphor, if using, and stir well.

seg.25eb1725b7f2.src: Switch off and serve warm. Pongali thickens as it stands; loosen it with a few spoons of hot water if needed.
seg.25eb1725b7f2.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ; ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.25eb1725b7f2.back: Turn off the flame and serve hot. When the pongali is kept it becomes thick; if needed add a few spoons of hot water to make it thinner.

seg.d8d20508ad3b.src: Cook the rice and dal fully soft; they stop softening once the jaggery goes in.
seg.d8d20508ad3b.t: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯂꯣꯏ꯫
seg.d8d20508ad3b.back: Cook the rice and dal until fully soft; after adding jaggery they will not become soft.

seg.c5408f916731.src: Roasting the moong dal gives pongali its nutty smell; keep the heat low so it turns golden, not brown.
seg.c5408f916731.t: ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯅꯥ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤꯗꯥ ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯄꯤ; ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯅꯤ, ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯣꯏ꯫
seg.c5408f916731.back: Roasting the moong dal gives the pongali a nut-like smell; keep the flame low, then it will become golden colour, not brown.

seg.5ed9375ff107.src: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and keep stirring once the jaggery is in; it catches and burns quickly.
seg.5ed9375ff107.t: ꯃꯈꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯤ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯀꯏ꯫
seg.5ed9375ff107.back: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and keep stirring after adding jaggery; it sticks quickly and burns.

seg.92b31a616baa.src: Take the pongali off the heat while it is still a little loose; it sets as it cools.
seg.92b31a616baa.t: ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯪꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.92b31a616baa.back: Take it off the flame while the pongali is still a little thin; when it cools it becomes thick.

seg.1c14403a599f.src: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for a darker pongali with a deeper, smoky sweetness.
seg.1c14403a599f.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1c14403a599f.back: Palm jaggery: for a darker pongali and a richer, smoke-like sweet taste use the same quantity of grated palm jaggery.

seg.d1a4e19c923c.src: Chakkera pongali: use ¾ cup sugar in place of the jaggery for a pale, sugar-sweet version.
seg.d1a4e19c923c.t: ꯆꯀꯀꯦꯔꯥ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯟꯕ, ꯆꯤꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯀꯞ ¾ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d1a4e19c923c.back: Chakkera pongali: for a pale-coloured pongali with a sugar sweet taste, use ¾ cup sugar instead of jaggery.

seg.44acc6e45d4b.src: Offer it as naivedyam on Sankranti morning, then serve it warm with the festive meal, alongside pulihora and garelu.
seg.44acc6e45d4b.t: ꯁꯡꯀ꯭ꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯩꯕꯦꯗ꯭ꯌꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯠꯊꯣꯀꯎ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯝꯃꯩꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ, ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯥꯔꯦꯂꯨꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.44acc6e45d4b.back: On Sankranti morning offer it as naivedyam, then serve it hot together with the festival meal, pulihora and garelu.

seg.b4e15a70f8c8.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm with a splash of hot water and a little ghee, stirring, before serving.
seg.b4e15a70f8c8.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b4e15a70f8c8.back: Cover the leftover, keep it in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Before serving add a little hot water and a little ghee and heat, stirring.

seg.70c91f153ba8.src: What is the difference between pongali and chakkera pongali?
seg.70c91f153ba8.t: ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯀꯀꯦꯔꯥ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯈꯦꯟꯅꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.70c91f153ba8.back: What is the difference between pongali and chakkera pongali?

seg.75f25d8f552a.src: Pongali on its own often means the savoury version made with pepper and cumin. Chakkera pongali and bellam pongali are the sweet versions, made with sugar or jaggery.
seg.75f25d8f552a.t: ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯒꯣꯜꯃꯔꯤꯆ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯆꯀꯀꯦꯔꯥ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤꯅꯤ, ꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ꯫
seg.75f25d8f552a.back: When only 'pongali' is said, it usually means the salty-taste pongali made with black pepper and cumin. Chakkera pongali and bellam pongali are sweet pongali, made with sugar or jaggery.

seg.94d3b2adcbef.src: Can I make bellam pongali in a pressure cooker?
seg.94d3b2adcbef.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.94d3b2adcbef.back: Can bellam pongali be made in a pressure cooker?

seg.269aace6e2a8.src: Yes. Cook the roasted dal and rice with 3 cups water for 4–5 whistles, let the pressure drop on its own, then add the melted jaggery and simmer in the open cooker.
seg.269aace6e2a8.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 3ꯒꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 4–5 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛ ꯇꯥꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.269aace6e2a8.back: Yes. Cook the roasted dal and rice with 3 cups water until 4–5 whistles, wait until the pressure goes down by itself, then add the melted jaggery and boil on low flame in the opened cooker.

seg.cd439685b7b5.src: Why did my pongali turn hard after cooling?
seg.cd439685b7b5.t: ꯑꯩꯒꯤ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯀꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.cd439685b7b5.back: Why did my pongali become hard after cooling?

seg.696811a7ce7d.src: Pongali sets as it cools, and simmering too long after the jaggery goes in makes it firmer. Take it off while it is still a little loose, and loosen leftovers with hot water.
seg.696811a7ce7d.t: ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯏꯪꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.696811a7ce7d.back: When pongali cools it becomes thick, and if it is boiled a long time after adding jaggery it becomes even harder. Take it off while still a little thin, and make the leftover thinner with hot water.

seg.b0499dbc1bd0.src: Can I use palm jaggery for pongali?
seg.b0499dbc1bd0.back: Can palm jaggery be used for pongali?

seg.7ee832015d30.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The pongali turns darker and tastes deeper and slightly smoky.
seg.7ee832015d30.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.7ee832015d30.back: Yes. Use the same quantity of grated palm jaggery (tati bellam). The pongali becomes darker in colour and the taste becomes richer and a little smoke-like.

seg.d63c3cc4eeac.back: బెల్లం పొంగలి · Recipe of Bellam Pongali | 1acrefarms

seg.978f1b90a63e.src: బెల్లం పొంగలి. Bellam pongali for Sankranti: rice and roasted moong dal cooked soft, sweetened with cane jaggery and finished with ghee-fried cashews. Serves 4.
seg.978f1b90a63e.t: బెల్లం పొంగలి. ꯁꯡꯀ꯭ꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕ꯫ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.978f1b90a63e.back: బెల్లం పొంగలి. Bellam pongali for Sankranti: rice and roasted moong dal cooked soft, sweetened with sugarcane jaggery, and finished with cashews fried in ghee. For 4 people.

seg.ad0644e2314c.src: Bellam Pongali: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.ad0644e2314c.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯣꯡꯒꯂꯤ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.ad0644e2314c.back: Bellam Pongali: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.c5dbb15b1ab8.src: a pinch of edible camphor (pacha karpooram)

seg.79401823a930.src: Andhra Chepala Pulusu ⟦1⟧(Andhra Tamarind Fish Curry)⟦/1⟧
seg.79401823a930.t: ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔ ꯆꯦꯄꯂꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ⟦1⟧(ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯉꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ)⟦/1⟧
seg.79401823a930.back: Andhra Chepala Pulusu ⟦1⟧(Andhra's tamarind fish curry)⟦/1⟧

seg.0fff539adaed.src: Chepala pulusu is the tamarind fish curry of coastal Andhra, made with special care in the Godavari districts: thick fish steaks simmered in a sour, red tamarind gravy with onions, green chillies and curry leaves. It is a Sunday lunch dish, and many homes cook it in a clay pot and keep it for the next day, when the gravy has soaked into the fish.
seg.0fff539adaed.t: ꯆꯦꯄꯂꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯉꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯤ, ꯒꯣꯗꯥꯕꯔꯤ ꯖꯤꯂꯥꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ: ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯉꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ, ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯣꯡꯃꯥꯏꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯉꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯂꯛꯂꯦ꯫
seg.0fff539adaed.back: Chepala pulusu is the tamarind fish curry of Andhra's sea coast, made with great care in the Godavari districts: big fish pieces with onion, green chilli and curry leaves, cooked on low flame in a sour red tamarind gravy. It is the dish of the Sunday afternoon meal, and many houses cook it in an earthen pot and keep it for the next day, when the gravy enters inside the fish.

seg.17fc336d9c12.src: Our turmeric powder goes into the marinade and the gravy. Sannam chilli powder gives the pulusu its deep red colour and a steady heat that balances the tamarind. This recipe serves 4.
seg.17fc336d9c12.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯅꯕ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.17fc336d9c12.back: Our turmeric powder goes into the marinade and the gravy. Sannam chilli powder gives the pulusu a thick red colour and a spiciness that matches the tamarind. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.4ba98eee496a.src: Prep includes the 15-minute marinade. The curry tastes even better after resting a few hours.
seg.4ba98eee496a.t: ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15-ꯒꯤ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯂꯤ꯫
seg.4ba98eee496a.back: The 15-minute marinating is included in preparation. This curry tastes better after keeping a few hours.

seg.aed84f9a20f5.src: Marinate fish with salt, turmeric and chilli powder, fry onions and spices, boil them in tamarind water, then simmer the fish gently in the gravy without stirring.
seg.aed84f9a20f5.t: ꯉꯥꯕꯨ ꯊꯨꯝ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯕꯨ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯉꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.aed84f9a20f5.back: Marinate the fish in salt, turmeric and chilli powder, fry onion and masala, boil them in tamarind water, then without stirring cook the fish in the gravy on low flame.

seg.5ce3c9cccf94.src: 500 g fish pieces ⟦1⟧firm fish cut into thick steaks: rohu (bocha), korameenu (murrel) or seer fish (vanjaram)⟦/1⟧
seg.5ce3c9cccf94.t: 500 g ꯉꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯉꯥ: ꯔꯣꯍꯨ (ꯕꯣꯆꯥ), ꯀꯣꯔꯥꯃꯤꯅꯨ (ꯃꯔꯜ) ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯤꯌꯔ ꯐꯤꯁ (ꯚꯟꯖꯔꯝ)⟦/1⟧
seg.5ce3c9cccf94.back: 500 g fish pieces ⟦1⟧firm-flesh fish cut in big pieces: rohu (bocha), korameenu (maral) or seer fish (vanjaram)⟦/1⟧

seg.23a800982a03.src: 40 g tamarind ⟦1⟧a lemon-sized ball, soaked in 2 cups warm water for 15 minutes⟦/1⟧
seg.23a800982a03.t: 40 g ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯥ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2ꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.23a800982a03.back: 40 g tamarind ⟦1⟧one piece the size of a lemon, soaked 15 minutes in 2 cups hot water⟦/1⟧

seg.f8dec19a56f9.src: ½ tsp turmeric powder ⟦1⟧¼ tsp for the marinade, ¼ tsp for the gravy⟦/1⟧
seg.f8dec19a56f9.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼, ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼⟦/1⟧
seg.f8dec19a56f9.back: ½ teaspoon turmeric powder ⟦1⟧¼ teaspoon for marinating, ¼ teaspoon for the gravy⟦/1⟧

seg.c78341163232.src: 2 tbsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧1 tsp for the marinade, the rest for the gravy⟦/1⟧
seg.c78341163232.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1, ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕꯗꯨ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ⟦/1⟧
seg.c78341163232.back: 2 tablespoons Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧1 teaspoon for marinating, the rest for the gravy⟦/1⟧

seg.bcbd97cd906a.src: 1 tsp salt ⟦1⟧for the gravy, or to taste⟦/1⟧
seg.bcbd97cd906a.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯊꯨꯝ ⟦1⟧ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.bcbd97cd906a.back: 1 teaspoon salt ⟦1⟧for the gravy, or by tasting⟦/1⟧

seg.ba6dcf57651d.back: Also goes very well with ⟦1⟧Teja chilli powder⟦/1⟧.

seg.2fafef6b8781.src: Wash the fish pieces gently in water two or three times and drain them well.
seg.2fafef6b8781.t: ꯉꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2fafef6b8781.back: Wash the fish pieces gently in water two or three times and drain the water well.

seg.cf370c2b1459.src: Rub the fish with salt, turmeric and 1 tsp chilli powder; rest 15 minutes. Use 1 tsp salt and ¼ tsp of the turmeric powder for the marinade.
seg.cf370c2b1459.t: ꯉꯥꯕꯨ ꯊꯨꯝ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.cf370c2b1459.back: Mix the fish with salt, turmeric and 1 teaspoon chilli powder; keep 15 minutes. For marinating use 1 teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder.

seg.0c7defd6c85a.src: Squeeze the soaked tamarind well in its water and strain it. You should have about 2 cups of thin tamarind water.
seg.0c7defd6c85a.t: ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯕ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯀꯞ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.0c7defd6c85a.back: Squeeze the soaked tamarind well in its own water and strain it. You should get about 2 cups of thin tamarind water.

seg.a8777ed4c461.src: Heat the oil in a wide pan or clay pot on medium heat. Add the fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds and cumin seeds and let them splutter, taking care that the fenugreek does not turn dark.
seg.a8777ed4c461.t: ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯇꯅꯕꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ꯫
seg.a8777ed4c461.back: Heat the oil on medium flame in a wide pan or earthen pot. Add fenugreek, mustard seed and cumin and let them crackle, watching that the fenugreek does not turn dark.

seg.e87b5c1bcc02.src: Fry the onions, chillies and curry leaves in oil till soft; add the spice powders. Fry the onions about 6–8 minutes until soft and light golden, add the ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook 2 minutes, then add the remaining turmeric powder, the remaining Sannam chilli powder and the coriander powder and stir for 30 seconds.
seg.e87b5c1bcc02.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 6–8 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 30 ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e87b5c1bcc02.back: Fry the onion, chilli and curry leaves in the oil until soft; add the masala powders. Fry the onion about 6–8 minutes until soft and a little golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook 2 minutes, then add the remaining turmeric powder, remaining Sannam chilli powder and coriander powder and stir 30 seconds.

seg.61e849535fa9.src: Pour in the tamarind water and boil 10 minutes till the oil rises. Add the salt for the gravy; the raw tamarind smell should be gone and the gravy slightly thick.
seg.61e849535fa9.t: ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.61e849535fa9.back: Pour the tamarind water and boil 10 minutes until oil comes up on top. Add the gravy's salt; the uncooked smell of tamarind should go and the gravy should become a little thick.

seg.65cb3d6833cd.src: Taste the gravy. It should be clearly sour, salty and hot, as the fish will take in some of it.
seg.65cb3d6833cd.t: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯃꯌꯦꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ, ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯉꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.65cb3d6833cd.back: Taste the gravy. It should be clearly sour, salty and spicy, because the fish will absorb some of it.

seg.fc6f288cacf9.src: Slide in the fish and simmer covered 10–12 minutes; swirl, do not stir. Lay the pieces in one layer, spoon gravy over them and keep the heat low.
seg.fc6f288cacf9.t: ꯉꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10–12 ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯒꯅꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯛ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fc6f288cacf9.back: Add the fish gently and cook covered 10–12 minutes on low flame; swirl the pan, do not stir. Keep the pieces in a single layer, pour gravy over them with a spoon and keep the flame low.

seg.9fed4db6e81b.src: Check one piece at the thickest part: the fish is cooked when the flesh is white or opaque right through and comes away from the bone easily.
seg.9fed4db6e81b.t: ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯃꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯎꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯔꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯇꯣꯠꯂꯛꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯉꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.9fed4db6e81b.back: Check the biggest part of a piece: the fish is done when the flesh is white to the inside or not see-through in the middle and comes away easily from the bone.

seg.8a5166c34dc3.src: Sprinkle the coriander leaves, switch off and let the pulusu rest at least 30 minutes, covered, before serving.
seg.8a5166c34dc3.t: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯈꯟꯗꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 30 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8a5166c34dc3.back: Sprinkle coriander leaves, turn off the flame and before serving keep the pulusu covered at least 30 minutes.

seg.c6819a9980cc.src: Swirl the pan instead of stirring so the fish stays whole.
seg.c6819a9980cc.t: ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯉꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.c6819a9980cc.back: Swirl the pan instead of stirring, then the fish will stay whole.

seg.1333bb67a0a8.src: Pick a firm fish with thick steaks; thin fillets break up in the long simmer.
seg.1333bb67a0a8.t: ꯃꯁꯥ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯉꯥ ꯈꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯀꯏ꯫
seg.1333bb67a0a8.back: Choose fish with firm flesh and big pieces; thin pieces break when cooked a long time.

seg.dd6f5d867621.src: Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat. Use 1½ tbsp for a milder pulusu, or the full 2 tbsp for the usual Andhra heat.
seg.dd6f5d867621.t: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.dd6f5d867621.back: Sannam chilli powder gives medium spiciness. For a mild pulusu use 1½ tablespoons, or for the usual Andhra spiciness use the whole 2 tablespoons.

seg.6196c7ae078f.src: Boil the tamarind gravy well before the fish goes in; once the fish is in, you cannot cook it much longer without it breaking.
seg.6196c7ae078f.t: ꯉꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯉꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯉꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫
seg.6196c7ae078f.back: Boil the tamarind gravy well before adding the fish; after adding the fish, it cannot be cooked a long time without the fish breaking.

seg.cadf91d0b4a1.src: Teja chilli powder: for a hotter pulusu, use 1 tbsp Teja chilli powder in place of the Sannam in the gravy. Teja is very hot; start with 2 tsp if unsure.
seg.cadf91d0b4a1.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ; ꯁꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯉꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2ꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.cadf91d0b4a1.back: Teja chilli powder: for a spicier pulusu use 1 tablespoon Teja chilli powder in the gravy in place of Sannam. Teja is very spicy; if not sure, start with 2 teaspoons.

seg.1639b09f9df2.src: Royyala pulusu: use 400 g cleaned prawns and simmer only 5–6 minutes, until they turn pink and curl.
seg.1639b09f9df2.t: ꯔꯣꯏꯌꯂꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ: ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ 400 g ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–6 ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1639b09f9df2.back: Royyala pulusu: use 400 g cleaned prawns and cook on low flame only 5–6 minutes until they turn pink and curl.

seg.f5f2c78097e7.src: Mamidikaya pulusu: in summer, Godavari homes add slices of raw mango and use less tamarind.
seg.f5f2c78097e7.t: ꯃꯥꯃꯤꯗꯤꯀꯥꯌ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ: ꯅꯣꯡꯖꯨ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯒꯣꯗꯥꯕꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯗꯕ ꯍꯩꯅꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.f5f2c78097e7.back: Mamidikaya pulusu: in summer Godavari houses add pieces of unripe mango and use less tamarind.

seg.4bb7dd4c2c98.src: Serve with hot steamed rice and sliced onions. Many Godavari homes serve it the next day, when the flavours have settled.
seg.4bb7dd4c2c98.t: ꯁꯥꯕ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒꯣꯗꯥꯕꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯄꯤ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯂꯦ꯫
seg.4bb7dd4c2c98.back: Serve with hot steamed rice and cut onion. Many Godavari houses serve it the next day, when the tastes have blended.

seg.ec67fc31e8d9.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently in the pan without stirring.
seg.ec67fc31e8d9.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ec67fc31e8d9.back: Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Heat thoroughly and gently in a pan without stirring.

seg.3fb4609a3953.src: Which fish is best for chepala pulusu?
seg.3fb4609a3953.t: ꯆꯦꯄꯂꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯔꯝꯕ ꯉꯥꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.3fb4609a3953.back: Which kind of fish is best for chepala pulusu?

seg.81c757cf9b6b.src: Firm river or sea fish cut into thick steaks: rohu (bocha), murrel (korameenu), catla or seer fish. Bony small fish also work but need gentle handling.
seg.81c757cf9b6b.t: ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯇꯨꯔꯦꯜ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯉꯥ: ꯔꯣꯍꯨ (ꯕꯣꯆꯥ), ꯃꯔꯜ (ꯀꯣꯔꯥꯃꯤꯅꯨ), ꯀꯇꯂꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯤꯌꯔ ꯐꯤꯁ꯫ ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯉꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯀꯁꯤꯡꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.81c757cf9b6b.back: Firm-flesh river or sea fish cut in big pieces: rohu (bocha), maral (korameenu), katla or seer fish. Small fish with many bones also work, but must be handled gently.

seg.1d2170a88905.src: Why does chepala pulusu taste better the next day?
seg.1d2170a88905.t: ꯆꯦꯄꯂꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯂꯤꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.1d2170a88905.back: Why is chepala pulusu tastier the next day?

seg.566bd302c316.src: Resting gives the fish time to soak up the tamarind and chilli gravy, and the sourness and heat even out. That is why many homes cook it in the morning for dinner or the next day.
seg.566bd302c316.t: ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯉꯥꯗꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯀꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯆꯨꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯔꯛꯏ꯫ ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.566bd302c316.back: Keeping gives the fish time to absorb the tamarind and chilli gravy, and the sour and the spicy become equal. That is why many houses cook it in the morning and keep it for the afternoon meal or for the next day.

seg.53fa2d1b73d6.src: How do I stop the fish from breaking in the curry?
seg.53fa2d1b73d6.back: How to keep the fish from breaking in the curry?

seg.adc2b712af00.src: Use thick steaks, add them only after the gravy has boiled, keep the heat low and swirl the pan instead of stirring with a spoon.
seg.adc2b712af00.t: ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯎꯠꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.adc2b712af00.back: Use big pieces, add them only after the gravy boils, keep the flame low and swirl the pan instead of stirring with a spoon.

seg.9f483b378e98.src: How much tamarind for 500 g fish?
seg.9f483b378e98.t: 500 g ꯉꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.9f483b378e98.back: How much tamarind is needed for 500 g fish?

seg.f77f33d6b7c5.src: About 40 g, a lemon-sized ball, soaked in 2 cups of warm water. Use a little less if you add tomato or raw mango.
seg.f77f33d6b7c5.t: 40 g ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯥ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2ꯗꯥ ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯕ꯫ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯗꯕ ꯍꯩꯅꯧ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f77f33d6b7c5.back: About 40 g, one piece the size of a lemon, soaked in 2 cups hot water. If you add tomato or unripe mango use a little less.

seg.d9010e0c2ca6.src: చేపల పులుసు · Andhra Fish Curry Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.d9010e0c2ca6.t: చేపల పులుసు · ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯉꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ | 1acrefarms
seg.d9010e0c2ca6.back: చేపల పులుసు · Recipe of Andhra's fish curry | 1acrefarms

seg.03c44db05afe.src: చేపల పులుసు. Godavari-style fish curry: fish simmered in a tangy tamarind gravy with onions, our turmeric and Sannam chilli powder. Serves 4, with tips and FAQs.
seg.03c44db05afe.t: చేపల పులుసు. ꯒꯣꯗꯥꯕꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯤ ꯉꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯉꯥ꯫ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯇꯤꯞꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫
seg.03c44db05afe.back: చేపల పులుసు. Fish curry of the Godavari style: fish cooked on low flame in a sour tamarind gravy with onion, our turmeric and Sannam chilli powder. For 4 people, with tips and questions.
