seg.a6f8caae0640.back: Gongura Mamsam ⟦1⟧(goat meat with roselle leaves)⟦/1⟧

seg.fabe2a976262.src: Gongura mamsam is mutton cooked with gongura, the sour sorrel leaf that Andhra, and Guntur above all, treats as its own. The mutton is cooked soft with chilli and turmeric, then simmered with gongura that has been sauteed down to a dark, tangy paste, until the curry is thick and the oil rises to the top.
seg.fabe2a976262.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯥꯡꯁꯝ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥꯅꯤ, ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯁꯧꯒ꯭ꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯅꯤ, ꯃꯁꯤꯕꯨ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯅꯥ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯅꯥ, ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯏ꯫ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ, ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯣꯇꯦ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ, ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ꯫
seg.fabe2a976262.back: Gongura mamsam is goat meat cooked with gongura; gongura is the sour roselle leaf which Andhra, and above all Guntur, takes as its own. The goat meat is cooked soft with chilli and turmeric, then together with gongura sautéed until it becomes a dark, sour paste, it is cooked on low flame until the curry thickens and oil comes up on top.

seg.a26e996a46c7.src: Gongura's sharp sourness needs strong heat to stand up to it, and that comes from our Teja chilli powder, the extra-hot Guntur chilli, with our turmeric powder alongside. Serves 4 with rice.
seg.a26e996a46c7.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯑꯁꯤꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯅꯅꯕꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.a26e996a46c7.back: To match this strong sourness of gongura a strong spiciness is needed, and that comes from our Teja chilli powder, from the very hot Guntur chilli, together with our turmeric powder. With rice, for 4 people.

seg.18985156497a.src: Pressure-cook mutton with Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and ginger-garlic paste, then simmer it with an onion masala and sauteed gongura leaves till thick and the oil floats on top.
seg.18985156497a.t: ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯀꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯣꯇꯦ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯇꯥꯎꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.18985156497a.back: Cook the goat meat in the pressure cooker with Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and ginger-garlic paste, then with onion masala and sautéed gongura leaves cook on low flame until thick and oil floats on top.

seg.b4cc59b185d3.src: 750 g mutton ⟦1⟧bone-in curry cut, washed and drained⟦/1⟧
seg.b4cc59b185d3.t: 750 g ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ⟦1⟧ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ, ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.b4cc59b185d3.back: 750 g goat meat ⟦1⟧bone-in curry pieces, washed and water drained⟦/1⟧

seg.b66b468c45f7.src: 4 cups gongura leaves ⟦1⟧about 2 bunches (150 g), picked from the stems, washed and drained well⟦/1⟧
seg.b66b468c45f7.t: ꯀꯞ 4 ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯌꯥꯜ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ (150 g), ꯃꯌꯣꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯍꯣꯠꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ, ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.b66b468c45f7.back: 4 cups gongura leaves ⟦1⟧about 2 bunches (150 g), picked from the stems, washed and water drained well⟦/1⟧

seg.9d6372d75a2f.src: 4 tbsp oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is the usual choice⟦/1⟧
seg.9d6372d75a2f.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 4 ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠꯀꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ⟦/1⟧
seg.9d6372d75a2f.back: 4 tablespoons oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is used all the time⟦/1⟧

seg.c89b5d92359a.src: Put the mutton in a pressure cooker with the Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger-garlic paste and salt, mix well and leave for 15 minutes.
seg.c89b5d92359a.t: ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯐꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c89b5d92359a.back: Put the goat meat in the pressure cooker together with Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger-garlic paste and salt, mix well and keep 15 minutes.

seg.d7a27bd7d1d5.src: Pressure-cook the mutton with Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, salt and water. Add the 1½ cups water and cook for 5–6 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure drop on its own.
seg.d7a27bd7d1d5.t: ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ, ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ, ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 1½ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 5–6 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛ ꯇꯥꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d7a27bd7d1d5.back: Cook the goat meat in the pressure cooker with Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, salt and water. Add 1½ cups water and cook on medium flame until 5–6 whistles, then wait until the pressure goes down by itself.

seg.c084351b01db.src: Open the cooker and check a piece: the mutton is done when it is tender and pulls away from the bone easily with a spoon. If not, cook for 1–2 more whistles.
seg.c084351b01db.t: ꯀꯨꯀꯔ ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯕꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯁꯔꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯇꯣꯠꯂꯛꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 1–2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c084351b01db.back: Open the cooker and check a piece: the goat meat is done when it is soft and comes away easily from the bone with a spoon. If not done, cook 1–2 more whistles.

seg.80af0da3b5a1.src: While the mutton cooks, heat the 1 tbsp oil in a pan on medium heat.
seg.80af0da3b5a1.t: ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ, ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.80af0da3b5a1.back: While the goat meat is cooking, heat 1 tablespoon oil on medium flame in a pan.

seg.c59d6a34def2.src: Saute the gongura with green chillies in a little oil till it melts to a dark paste. This takes 8–10 minutes; stir often and mash the leaves with the back of the spoon as they wilt.
seg.c59d6a34def2.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯣꯇꯦ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 8–10 ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c59d6a34def2.back: Sauté the gongura with the green chillies in a little oil until it melts into a dark paste. It takes 8–10 minutes; stir every now and then, and when the leaves wilt mash them with the back of the spoon.

seg.37056d0dd9cf.src: Heat the 4 tbsp oil in a heavy kadai on medium heat and add the cloves, cardamoms and cinnamon.
seg.37056d0dd9cf.t: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 4 ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯕꯉ꯭ꯒ, ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯂꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.37056d0dd9cf.back: In a heavy kadai heat 4 tablespoons oil on medium flame and add cloves, cardamom and cinnamon.

seg.26a945a9fad3.src: Fry the onions with whole spices till golden. Add the curry leaves with the onions, and give them 10–12 minutes, stirring often.
seg.26a945a9fad3.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯕꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10–12 ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.26a945a9fad3.back: Fry the onion with the whole masala until golden colour. Add curry leaves together with the onion, and give it 10–12 minutes, stirring every now and then.

seg.4dd72cc1abd0.src: Stir in the coriander powder and fry for 30 seconds. Add the mutton and its stock, then the gongura.
seg.4dd72cc1abd0.t: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 30 ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ꯫
seg.4dd72cc1abd0.back: Add coriander powder, stir and fry 30 seconds. Add the goat meat and its water (juice), then the gongura.

seg.46f5f6c735ac.src: Simmer till thick and the oil floats on top. Keep the heat low, stir now and then, and allow 12–15 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt now, once the sourness of the gongura is in.
seg.46f5f6c735ac.t: ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯇꯥꯎꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯃꯇꯝꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 12–15 ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯆꯪꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯆꯨꯅꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.46f5f6c735ac.back: Cook on low flame until it thickens and oil floats on top. Keep the flame low, stir from time to time, and give it 12–15 minutes. After the gongura's sourness has gone in, only then taste and adjust the salt.

seg.0abf0f798bd3.src: Stir in garam masala. Cook 2 more minutes, then switch off and rest for 10 minutes before serving.
seg.0abf0f798bd3.t: ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0abf0f798bd3.back: Add garam masala and stir. Cook 2 more minutes, then turn off the flame and keep 10 minutes before serving.

seg.c57eb6bfb001.src: Taste after the gongura goes in; its sourness varies from bunch to bunch.
seg.c57eb6bfb001.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯜ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯩ꯫
seg.c57eb6bfb001.back: Taste after adding gongura; its sourness differs in each bunch.

seg.5544823d42b4.src: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For medium heat use 1 tsp, or Sannam chilli powder; do not cut it out entirely, or the gongura tastes flat and sour.
seg.5544823d42b4.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ꯫ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯀꯅꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.5544823d42b4.back: Teja chilli powder is very spicy. For medium spiciness use 1 teaspoon or Sannam chilli powder; do not remove it completely, otherwise the gongura becomes tasteless and only sour.

seg.62683a58a9fd.src: Do not use an aluminium pan for the gongura; its sourness reacts with the metal and darkens the curry. Use steel or cast iron.
seg.62683a58a9fd.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯑꯦꯂꯨꯃꯤꯅꯤꯌꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯅꯨ; ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯦꯇꯦꯜꯒꯥ ꯊꯧꯗꯣꯛ ꯊꯣꯀꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯜ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯥꯏꯔꯟ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.62683a58a9fd.back: Do not use an aluminium pan for gongura; its sourness reacts with the metal and makes the curry dark. Use steel or cast iron.

seg.d036336075e5.src: If the gongura is very sour, add 1 more onion to the masala to balance it.
seg.d036336075e5.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ 1 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d036336075e5.back: If the gongura is very sour, add 1 more onion to the masala to make it equal.

seg.8faa3986eaa2.src: Gongura chicken: use 750 g bone-in chicken, skip the pressure cooker and cook it covered in the masala for 20–25 minutes, until no pink remains near the bone, before the gongura goes in.
seg.8faa3986eaa2.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ 750 g ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯅꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ, ꯁꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 20–25 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8faa3986eaa2.back: Gongura chicken: use 750 g bone-in chicken, do not use the pressure cooker, and before adding gongura cook covered in the masala 20–25 minutes until not even one pink colour appears near the bone.

seg.2ebce7872a6e.src: Gongura royyalu: use 500 g cleaned prawns, add them after the onions and cook 5–6 minutes, just until they turn pink and curl, then add the gongura.
seg.2ebce7872a6e.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯔꯣꯏꯌꯂꯨ: ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ 500 g ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–6 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2ebce7872a6e.back: Gongura royyalu: use 500 g cleaned prawns, add after the onion and cook only 5–6 minutes until they turn pink and curl, then add the gongura.

seg.7f3c45600b1c.src: Red chilli gongura: fry 6 dried red chillies with the gongura and grind them together for a darker, sharper curry.
seg.7f3c45600b1c.t: ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ 6 ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7f3c45600b1c.back: Red-chilli gongura: for a darker and stronger curry fry 6 dry red chillies with the gongura and grind together.

seg.6fc7d7ad8ce1.src: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, or with jonna rotte. A plain raw onion on the side is the Guntur way.
seg.6fc7d7ad8ce1.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯖꯣꯟꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯠꯇꯦꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯅꯤ꯫
seg.6fc7d7ad8ce1.back: Serve hot with steamed rice and one spoon of ghee, or with jonna rotte. Keeping one uncooked onion at the side is the Guntur way.

seg.a4e072616940.src: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat until steaming hot all the way through. Like most sour curries, it tastes better the next day.
seg.a4e072616940.t: ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 3 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯀꯌꯥꯒꯨꯝꯅꯥ, ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯂꯤ꯫
seg.a4e072616940.back: Cover and keep in the fridge up to 3 days; heat thoroughly until steam comes out right to the inside. Like many sour curries, it is tastier the next day.

seg.056a57b2c0f8.back: What is gongura called in English?

seg.50430ec58f61.src: Gongura is sorrel leaves, also called roselle or red sorrel (ambadi in Marathi, pitwa in Hindi). The leaves are sour and cook down to a dark paste.
seg.50430ec58f61.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯁꯣꯔꯦꯜ ꯃꯅꯥꯅꯤ, ꯃꯁꯤꯕꯨ ꯔꯣꯖꯦꯜ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯔꯦꯗ ꯁꯣꯔꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯁꯨ ꯀꯧꯏ (ꯃꯔꯥꯊꯤꯗꯥ ꯑꯝꯕꯥꯗꯤ, ꯍꯤꯟꯗꯤꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯠꯋꯥ)꯫ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.50430ec58f61.back: Gongura is sorrel leaf, also called roselle or red sorrel (ambadi in Marathi, pitwa in Hindi). The leaves are sour and when cooked become a dark paste.

seg.c813168eb832.src: Can I use gongura pickle instead of gongura leaves?
seg.c813168eb832.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.c813168eb832.back: Can gongura pickle be used in place of gongura leaves?

seg.e1453431b91a.src: Yes, in a pinch. Stir in 3–4 tbsp gongura pickle in place of the sauteed leaves and cut down the salt and chilli powder, since the pickle already has both.
seg.e1453431b91a.t: ꯍꯣꯌ, ꯑꯋꯥꯕꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯁꯣꯇꯦ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3–4 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯑꯆꯥꯔꯗꯥ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯍꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯦ꯫
seg.e1453431b91a.back: Yes, it works when in a fix. In place of sautéed leaves add 3–4 tablespoons gongura pickle and stir, and reduce the salt and chilli powder, because the pickle already has both.

seg.13ee618e3c36.src: How long should I pressure-cook mutton for gongura mamsam?
seg.13ee618e3c36.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯥꯡꯁꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.13ee618e3c36.back: How long should the goat meat be cooked in the pressure cooker for gongura mamsam?

seg.5888ba63831a.src: About 5–6 whistles on medium heat for bone-in curry-cut mutton. It is done when the meat pulls away from the bone easily; older mutton may need 1–2 more whistles.
seg.5888ba63831a.t: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 5–6 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯃꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯔꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯇꯣꯠꯂꯛꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ; ꯑꯍꯜ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 1–2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.5888ba63831a.back: About 5–6 whistles on medium flame for bone-in curry-piece goat meat. The meat is done when it comes away easily from the bone; for meat of an old goat 1–2 more whistles may be needed.

seg.5f47c430018f.src: How do I make gongura mutton less spicy?
seg.5f47c430018f.back: How to reduce the spiciness of gongura mutton?

seg.e4fe5fb9cf48.src: Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder or swap in Sannam chilli powder, and use 2 green chillies. Keep some heat, as it balances the sourness of the gongura.
seg.e4fe5fb9cf48.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯀꯎ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ 2 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.e4fe5fb9cf48.back: Use 1 teaspoon Teja chilli powder or replace it with Sannam chilli powder, and use 2 green chillies. Keep a little spiciness, because it balances the gongura's sourness.

seg.df5186f8f459.src: గోంగూర మాంసం. Gongura mutton, the Guntur way: mutton cooked with Teja chilli powder and turmeric powder, then simmered with sour sorrel leaves till thick.
seg.df5186f8f459.t: గోంగూర మాంసం. ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯇꯟ: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯁꯣꯔꯦꯜ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ꯫
seg.df5186f8f459.back: గోంగూర మాంసం. Gongura mutton in the Guntur way: goat meat cooked with Teja chilli powder and turmeric powder, then cooked on low flame with sour sorrel leaves until thick.

seg.ba26416f3fd1.back: Gongura Mamsam (goat meat with roselle leaves) · 1acrefarms

seg.dffa96c4d761.src: Gongura Mamsam: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.dffa96c4d761.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯥꯡꯁꯝ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.dffa96c4d761.back: Gongura Mamsam: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.a7dd4a4d025c.src: Gongura pachadi is the chutney Andhra is best known for: sour gongura (sorrel) leaves fried down in oil and ground with roasted spices, garlic and red chilli. Around Guntur and Palnadu it is on the table almost every day, mixed into hot rice with a spoon of ghee, with sliced onion on the side.
seg.a7dd4a4d025c.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯕꯨ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯈꯉꯍꯅꯕ ꯆꯠꯅꯤꯅꯤ: ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ (ꯁꯣꯔꯦꯜ) ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕ꯫ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯜꯅꯥꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯩ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫
seg.a7dd4a4d025c.back: Gongura pachadi is the chutney that makes Andhra best known: sour gongura (sorrel) leaves fried in oil and ground with roasted masala, garlic and red chilli. In Guntur and Palnadu it is at nearly every day's meal, mixed into hot rice with one spoon of ghee, together with cut onion at the side.

seg.73ddd8b1df98.src: Teja chilli powder gives it the deep red colour and the sharp heat that stands up to the sourness of the leaves. This recipe makes about 1½ cups, enough for 6.
seg.73ddd8b1df98.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯅꯕ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯀꯞ 1½ ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯏ, ꯃꯤ 6ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫
seg.73ddd8b1df98.back: Teja chilli powder gives it a thick red colour and a strong spiciness that matches the sourness of the leaves. This recipe gives about 1½ cups, enough for 6 people.

seg.1689d390a49e.src: Total includes cooling the leaves and spices before grinding.
seg.1689d390a49e.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.1689d390a49e.back: Cooling the leaves and masala before grinding is included in the total.

seg.b4b21c43d6d9.src: Fry gongura leaves in oil till they turn to a dark mash, then grind them with roasted coriander, fenugreek, garlic, Teja chilli powder and salt. Finish with a mustard and dal tempering.
seg.b4b21c43d6d9.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯅꯣꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ, ꯃꯦꯊꯤ, ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b4b21c43d6d9.back: Fry the gongura leaves in oil until dark and mashed, then grind with roasted coriander, fenugreek, garlic, Teja chilli powder and salt. Finish with a tempering of mustard seed and dal.

seg.bc1f3c96e98a.src: 4 cups gongura leaves ⟦1⟧picked from 2 large bunches, about 200 g⟦/1⟧
seg.bc1f3c96e98a.t: ꯀꯞ 4 ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯌꯥꯜ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2ꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯣꯠꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ, 200 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.bc1f3c96e98a.back: 4 cups gongura leaves ⟦1⟧picked from 2 big bunches, about 200 g⟦/1⟧

seg.e478a092b07c.src: 1 tbsp sesame oil ⟦1⟧gingelly oil, for frying the leaves⟦/1⟧
seg.e478a092b07c.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯖꯤꯟꯖꯦꯂꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ, ꯃꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯅꯕꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.e478a092b07c.back: 1 tablespoon sesame oil ⟦1⟧gingelly oil, to fry the leaves⟦/1⟧

seg.b00132daaabc.src: ¼ tsp fenugreek seeds ⟦1⟧menthulu; no more, or the pachadi turns bitter⟦/1⟧
seg.b00132daaabc.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯦꯟꯊꯨꯂꯨ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯀꯅꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯈꯥꯔꯛꯀꯅꯤ⟦/1⟧
seg.b00132daaabc.back: ¼ teaspoon fenugreek ⟦1⟧menthulu; do not add more, otherwise the pachadi becomes bitter⟦/1⟧

seg.c1657b10781a.src: 2 tsp Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; use 1 tsp for a milder pachadi⟦/1⟧
seg.c1657b10781a.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2 ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ; ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.c1657b10781a.back: 2 teaspoons Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very spicy; for a mild pachadi use 1 teaspoon⟦/1⟧

seg.7e344ce94138.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¾ ꯊꯨꯝ ⟦1⟧ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧

seg.69e8fc35d187.src: Pick the gongura leaves off the stems and wash them in 2–3 changes of water. Spread them on a cloth and pat them completely dry; water left on the leaves splutters in the oil and shortens how long the pachadi keeps.
seg.69e8fc35d187.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯌꯣꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯍꯣꯠꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ 2–3 ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯕꯨ ꯐꯤ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯅꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯟ ꯆꯤꯟ ꯍꯥꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.69e8fc35d187.back: Pick the gongura leaves from the stems and wash, changing the water 2–3 times. Spread them on a cloth and wipe gently until fully dry; water left in the leaves makes it splutter in the oil and reduces the time the pachadi can be kept.

seg.1b214adb5a9c.src: Roast the coriander, cumin and fenugreek till fragrant; let them cool. Use a dry pan on low heat and stir all the time: the fenugreek should turn one shade darker, about 2 minutes, but not brown.
seg.1b214adb5a9c.t: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ, ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯔꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.1b214adb5a9c.back: Roast the coriander, cumin and fenugreek until the smell comes; let cool. In a dry pan on low flame stir all the time: the fenugreek should turn a little dark in about 2 minutes, but should not become brown.

seg.6dd2ecdfbc2f.src: Fry the gongura leaves in 1 tbsp oil till they wilt to a dark mash, 6–8 minutes. Use a wide pan on medium heat and stir often; the leaves shrink fast, turn from green to a dull olive-brown, and almost all their water cooks off.
seg.6dd2ecdfbc2f.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1ꯗꯥ ꯌꯣꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯅꯣꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 6–8꯫ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯁꯪꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯑꯣꯂꯤꯚ-ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.6dd2ecdfbc2f.back: Fry the gongura leaves in 1 tablespoon oil until wilted and dark mashed, 6–8 minutes. Using a wide pan on medium flame, stir every now and then; the leaves shrink quickly, turn from green to a dull olive-brown colour, and almost all their water is lost in the cooking.

seg.adc2540067f6.src: Spread the leaves on a plate and let them cool completely, about 10 minutes.
seg.adc2540067f6.t: ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫
seg.adc2540067f6.back: Spread the leaves on a plate and keep until fully cooled, about 10 minutes.

seg.78d34fa0267e.src: Grind the spices with the garlic, chilli powder and salt, then pulse in the leaves. Grind the roasted spices, the 6 garlic cloves, Teja chilli powder and salt to a coarse powder first.
seg.78d34fa0267e.t: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ 6, ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.78d34fa0267e.back: Grind the masala with garlic, chilli powder and salt, then add the leaves and run (pulse) in short bursts. First grind the roasted masala, 6 garlic cloves, Teja chilli powder and salt into a not-fine (coarse) powder.

seg.e84cadbb2f28.src: Add the cooled leaves and pulse 3–4 times to a coarse paste, without any water. Many Andhra homes pound it in a stone mortar (rolu) instead.
seg.e84cadbb2f28.t: ꯏꯪꯂꯕ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ 3–4 ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯃꯗꯥ (ꯔꯣꯂꯨ) ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏ꯫
seg.e84cadbb2f28.back: Add the cooled leaves and without water pulse 3–4 times in short bursts into a not-fine paste. Many Andhra houses instead grind it in a stone mortar (rolu).

seg.c04597c43292.src: Taste: it should be sour, hot and well salted. Add a pinch more salt if the sourness feels too sharp.
seg.c04597c43292.t: ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ, ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯆꯨꯅꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕꯥ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c04597c43292.back: Taste: it should be sour, spicy and right in salt. If the sourness feels very strong add a little more salt.

seg.317793f8bd6d.src: Temper mustard, dals, red chillies and curry leaves in the rest of the oil; mix it in. Heat the 2 tbsp sesame oil in a small pan, let the mustard seeds crackle, fry the chana dal and urad dal till golden, then add the red chillies, crushed garlic, curry leaves and asafoetida for a few seconds. Pour it over the pachadi and stir well.
seg.317793f8bd6d.t: ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ, ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.317793f8bd6d.back: In the remaining oil make a tempering of mustard seed, dal, red chilli and curry leaves; mix it in. In a small pan heat 2 tablespoons sesame oil, let the mustard seed crackle, fry chana dal and urad dal until golden colour, then add red chilli, crushed garlic, curry leaves and hing for a few seconds. Pour this on top of the pachadi and stir well.

seg.bd6dcf672985.src: Let the pachadi sit for 30 minutes if you can, so the flavours come together, then spoon it into a clean, dry glass jar.
seg.bd6dcf672985.t: ꯌꯥꯕ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 30 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bd6dcf672985.back: If possible keep the pachadi 30 minutes so the tastes blend, then with a spoon put it into a clean, dry glass jar.

seg.e0bb74b2a966.src: Dry the leaves fully before frying so the pachadi keeps longer.
seg.e0bb74b2a966.t: ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.e0bb74b2a966.back: Make the leaves fully dry before frying, then the pachadi can be kept a long time.

seg.29688dc9fded.src: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For a milder pachadi use 1 tsp, or half Teja and half Sannam chilli powder.
seg.29688dc9fded.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ꯫ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ꯫
seg.29688dc9fded.back: Teja chilli powder is very spicy. For a milder pachadi use 1 teaspoon, or half Teja and half Sannam chilli powder.

seg.d1fa39431c01.src: Keep the fenugreek to ¼ tsp and roast it only one shade darker; more, or darker, makes the pachadi bitter.
seg.d1fa39431c01.t: ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯄ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯍꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯈꯥꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.d1fa39431c01.back: Keep the fenugreek at ¼ teaspoon and roast only until it turns a little dark; if more is added, or made darker, the pachadi becomes bitter.

seg.00435dc24e2d.src: Pulse, do not grind smooth: gongura pachadi should be coarse, with bits of leaf you can see.
seg.00435dc24e2d.t: ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯒꯅꯨ: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯎꯕ ꯐꯪꯕ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫
seg.00435dc24e2d.back: Pulse in short bursts, do not grind smooth: gongura pachadi should be not-fine (coarse), with leaf pieces that can be seen.

seg.70ea8f84244b.src: Do not skimp on the oil; the layer of oil on top helps the pachadi keep.
seg.70ea8f84244b.t: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯒꯅꯨ; ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯒꯤ ꯂꯩꯌꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯦꯡ ꯄꯥꯡꯏ꯫
seg.70ea8f84244b.back: Do not reduce the oil; the layer of oil on top helps the pachadi to be kept a long time.

seg.bd2018335c09.src: With onion: stir 1 small onion, finely chopped, into a portion just before serving, and eat it the same day.
seg.bd2018335c09.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ: ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bd2018335c09.back: With onion: only just before serving add 1 small finely chopped onion to one portion and stir, and eat it that same day.

seg.77f8d979d9c5.src: Whole red chillies: in place of the chilli powder, fry 12–15 dried red chillies in a little oil and grind them with the spices.
seg.77f8d979d9c5.t: ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ 12–15 ꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.77f8d979d9c5.back: Whole red chilli: in place of chilli powder fry 12–15 dry red chillies in a little oil and grind with the masala.

seg.98bf90687f81.src: Green chilli gongura: fry 6–8 green chillies with the leaves and cut the chilli powder to 1 tsp, for a sharper, greener heat.
seg.98bf90687f81.t: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕ, ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯀꯤ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ 6–8 ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.98bf90687f81.back: Green-chilli gongura: for a stronger, green-chilli spiciness fry 6–8 green chillies with the leaves and reduce the chilli powder to 1 teaspoon.

seg.3ffc938ce36f.src: Mix a spoon into hot rice with ghee and eat with sliced raw onion on the side. It also goes well with dosa, idli and as a side on any Andhra meal plate.
seg.3ffc938ce36f.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯗꯣꯁꯥ, ꯏꯗꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯊꯥꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.3ffc938ce36f.back: Mix one spoon into hot rice with ghee and eat with uncooked onion cut at the side. It also goes very well at the side of dosa, idli and any Andhra meal thali.

seg.9b58b3a03e55.src: Keep it in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, always using a dry spoon. A thin layer of oil on top helps it keep.
seg.9b58b3a03e55.t: ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ꯫ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯕ ꯂꯩꯌꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯦꯡ ꯄꯥꯡꯏ꯫
seg.9b58b3a03e55.back: Keep in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge up to 2 weeks, always using a dry spoon. The thin layer of oil on top helps it be kept a long time.

seg.5fb383e7c1ab.src: What is gongura called in English?
seg.5fb383e7c1ab.back: What is gongura called in English?

seg.100f275734bd.src: Gongura is the leaf of the roselle plant, often sold as sorrel leaves or red sorrel. In Hindi- and Marathi-speaking areas it is called ambadi.
seg.100f275734bd.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯔꯣꯖꯦꯜ ꯄꯥꯝꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯅꯤ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯁꯣꯔꯦꯜ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯔꯦꯗ ꯁꯣꯔꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯌꯣꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯍꯤꯟꯗꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯥꯊꯤ ꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯐꯃꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯕꯨ ꯑꯝꯕꯥꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯀꯧꯏ꯫
seg.100f275734bd.back: Gongura is the leaf of the roselle plant, often known as sorrel leaf or red sorrel. In Hindi- and Marathi-speaking places it is called ambadi.

seg.7f27f7848f6b.src: How do I make gongura pachadi less sour?
seg.7f27f7848f6b.back: How to reduce the sourness of gongura pachadi?

seg.a8b5b3cafa35.src: Add a little more salt and chilli, or stir in 1 tsp grated jaggery. Frying the leaves down well also mellows their sourness.
seg.a8b5b3cafa35.t: ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯁꯨ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.a8b5b3cafa35.back: Add a little more salt and chilli, or add 1 teaspoon grated jaggery and stir. Frying the leaves well also reduces their sourness.

seg.5bc83cd0bb23.src: Why is my gongura pachadi bitter?
seg.5bc83cd0bb23.back: Why is my gongura pachadi bitter?

seg.bcbd736912c5.src: Usually too much fenugreek, or fenugreek roasted too dark. Keep it to ¼ tsp and stop roasting when it is one shade darker.
seg.bcbd736912c5.t: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯏ꯫ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bcbd736912c5.back: Often because too much fenugreek was added, or the fenugreek was roasted very dark. Keep it at ¼ teaspoon and stop roasting when it turns a little dark.

seg.f5ec54c6b341.src: How long does gongura pachadi last?
seg.f5ec54c6b341.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.f5ec54c6b341.back: How long can gongura pachadi be kept?

seg.693b158b80df.src: About 2 weeks in the fridge in a dry glass jar, if the leaves were dried well and you always use a dry spoon. Outside the fridge, eat it within 2–3 days.
seg.693b158b80df.t: ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯀꯤ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯗꯥ, ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2–3ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.693b158b80df.back: About 2 weeks in the fridge in a dry glass jar, if the leaves were dried well and a dry spoon is always used. Outside the fridge, eat within 2–3 days.

seg.2202d49bd92b.back: గోంగూర పచ్చడి · Recipe of Gongura Pachadi | 1acrefarms

seg.a8b7816171d1.src: గోంగూర పచ్చడి. Gongura pachadi the Guntur way: sorrel leaves fried down, ground with roasted spices, garlic and Teja chilli powder, then tempered. Serves 6.
seg.a8b7816171d1.t: గోంగూర పచ్చడి. ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ: ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯁꯣꯔꯦꯜ ꯃꯅꯥ, ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯕ꯫ ꯃꯤ 6ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.a8b7816171d1.back: గోంగూర పచ్చడి. Gongura pachadi in the Guntur way: fried sorrel leaves ground with roasted masala, garlic and Teja chilli powder, then tempered. For 6 people.

seg.de566b9f7c3e.src: Gongura Pachadi: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.de566b9f7c3e.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.de566b9f7c3e.back: Gongura Pachadi: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.70fd98f238a4.src: Kodi Guddu Pulusu ⟦1⟧(Andhra Egg Curry in Tamarind Gravy)⟦/1⟧
seg.70fd98f238a4.t: ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯒꯨꯗꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ⟦1⟧(ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ)⟦/1⟧
seg.70fd98f238a4.back: Kodi Guddu Pulusu ⟦1⟧(Andhra's egg curry in tamarind gravy)⟦/1⟧

seg.dd0da0936d87.src: Kodi guddu pulusu is the Andhra egg curry that many homes make when there is no meat in the house: hard-boiled eggs simmered in a tangy gravy of tamarind and slow-fried onions. It is thinner and sourer than a North Indian egg curry, made to be mixed into plenty of hot rice.
seg.dd0da0936d87.t: ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯒꯨꯗꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯥ ꯂꯩꯇꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯤ: ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯎꯠꯂꯕ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯣꯡꯄꯣꯛ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯥꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯅꯤ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ꯫
seg.dd0da0936d87.back: Kodi guddu pulusu is Andhra's egg curry that many houses make when there is no meat at home: hard-boiled eggs cooked on low flame in a sour gravy of tamarind and gently fried onion. It is more watery and more sour than north India's egg curry, made to mix with a big heap of hot rice and eat.

seg.27588d5a0d73.src: Our Sannam chilli powder gives the pulusu its red colour and a steady medium heat, and our turmeric powder (Pasupu) gives the golden base. A little jaggery rounds off the sourness.
seg.27588d5a0d73.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨꯗꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ (ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ) ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝꯐꯝ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯈꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.27588d5a0d73.back: Our Sannam chilli powder gives the pulusu red colour and a steady medium spiciness, and our turmeric powder (pasupu) gives a golden-colour base. A little jaggery balances the sourness.

seg.3c683c3f8074.src: Boil and slit the eggs. Fry onions, add turmeric, Sannam chilli powder and tamarind water, simmer, then cook the eggs in the gravy till it thickens.
seg.3c683c3f8074.t: ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ, ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3c683c3f8074.back: Boil the eggs and cut them. Fry onion, add turmeric, Sannam chilli powder and tamarind water, cook on low flame, then cook the eggs in the gravy until the gravy thickens.

seg.8c348975674a.src: a pinch of turmeric powder ⟦1⟧for frying the eggs (optional)⟦/1⟧
seg.8c348975674a.back: A little turmeric powder ⟦1⟧to fry the eggs (if you like)⟦/1⟧

seg.3a31dc522e29.src: 20 g tamarind ⟦1⟧a lemon-sized ball, soaked in 1½ cups warm water⟦/1⟧
seg.3a31dc522e29.t: 20 g ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯥ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 1½ꯗꯥ ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.3a31dc522e29.back: 20 g tamarind ⟦1⟧one piece the size of a lemon, soaked in 1½ cups hot water⟦/1⟧

seg.d56c07ca17af.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ⟦/1⟧

seg.5b3cff6eb38d.src: 2 tsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧medium heat; use 1½ tsp for milder⟦/1⟧
seg.5b3cff6eb38d.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2 ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ; ꯍꯟꯊꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.5b3cff6eb38d.back: 2 teaspoons Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧medium spiciness; for mild use 1½ teaspoons⟦/1⟧

seg.4b88dbe5eb6d.src: Soak the tamarind in the warm water for 15 minutes. Squeeze it well, strain and keep the tamarind water; discard the fibres and seeds.
seg.4b88dbe5eb6d.t: ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯆꯨꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯔꯩ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4b88dbe5eb6d.back: Soak the tamarind in hot water 15 minutes. Squeeze it well and strain, and keep the tamarind water; throw away the fibres and seeds.

seg.e7eefe0a36b0.src: Boil the eggs 10 minutes, peel them and make 3–4 shallow slits on each. Start them in room-temperature water, count 10 minutes from the boil, then cool them in water before peeling. The yolk should be firm and pale yellow right through.
seg.e7eefe0a36b0.t: ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯀꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯃꯗꯕ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ 3–4 ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯠꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯠꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.e7eefe0a36b0.back: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, and after removing the shell [makhu = shell/skin], make 3–4 shallow [literally 'not deep'] slits [kaiba: could be 'cracks/breaks' or 'cuts'] on each one. Put the eggs in room-temperature water [literally 'water of the house's hot-cold', i.e. house temperature] and start boiling; keep [them] for 10 minutes from the time the water boils, and after that, before removing the shell, cool [them] in water [literally 'make cold in water'; the water's temperature is not stated]. The inner 'oraba' part [unclear word: possibly 'yolk', possibly a colour word; I cannot confirm it means yellow] should be fully hard/firm and have a little turmeric colour [yaingang machu = turmeric colour, i.e. a slight yellow].

seg.6747ea35bd7d.src: Optional: heat 1 tsp of the oil with the pinch of turmeric and roll the eggs in it for 2 minutes until lightly blistered. Keep aside.
seg.6747ea35bd7d.t: ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯈꯔꯥ ꯐꯨꯠꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6747ea35bd7d.back: If you like: heat 1 teaspoon oil with a little turmeric and roll the eggs in it about 2 minutes until a little blistered. Keep at the side.

seg.9d3c50e45f8b.src: Heat the rest of the oil in a kadai on medium heat. Add the fenugreek seeds and let them turn light brown; they turn bitter if they go dark.
seg.9d3c50e45f8b.t: ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯥꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.9d3c50e45f8b.back: Heat the remaining oil on medium flame in a kadai. Add fenugreek and let it turn a little brown; if it turns dark it becomes bitter.

seg.c867d4469da7.src: Fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves and onions in the oil till soft and golden. Add the mustard seeds first and let them splutter, then the curry leaves, green chillies and asafoetida, then the onions for about 8 minutes.
seg.c867d4469da7.t: ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 8 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫
seg.c867d4469da7.back: Fry the mustard seed, curry leaves and onion in the oil until soft and golden colour. First add mustard seed and let it crackle, then curry leaves, green chilli and hing, then the onion about 8 minutes.

seg.ae0272dd2475.src: Turn the heat to low. Add the turmeric, Sannam chilli powder and salt, then the tamarind water; simmer 10 minutes. Stir in the coriander powder with the chilli powder so it fries for a few seconds first.
seg.ae0272dd2475.t: ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ, ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ; ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.ae0272dd2475.back: Make the flame low. Add turmeric, Sannam chilli powder and salt, then the tamarind water; cook on low flame 10 minutes. Add the coriander powder together with the chilli powder and stir, so that first it fries a few seconds.

seg.01aeed8b749f.src: The raw tamarind smell should be gone and the gravy should look glossy. Add ½ cup water if it thickens too fast.
seg.01aeed8b749f.t: ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ½ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.01aeed8b749f.back: The uncooked smell of the tamarind should go and the gravy should shine. If it becomes very thick quickly, add ½ cup water.

seg.74f1a1affff6.src: Slide in the eggs and simmer 5 minutes more till the gravy thickens. Spoon the gravy over the eggs now and then.
seg.74f1a1affff6.t: ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯃꯇꯝꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.74f1a1affff6.back: Add the eggs gently and cook on low flame 5 more minutes until the gravy thickens. From time to time pour gravy over the eggs with a spoon.

seg.299781c49104.src: Stir in the jaggery, taste and adjust the salt or sourness, and scatter the coriander leaves.
seg.299781c49104.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯅꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.299781c49104.back: Add jaggery and stir, taste and adjust salt or sourness, and sprinkle coriander leaves.

seg.d0ce3c2b157a.src: Switch off and let the pulusu rest for 10 minutes before serving so the eggs take on the gravy.
seg.d0ce3c2b157a.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯧꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.d0ce3c2b157a.back: Turn off the flame and keep the pulusu 10 minutes before serving, so that the eggs take the taste of the gravy.

seg.feebbb94999b.src: Slits let the tangy gravy into the eggs.
seg.feebbb94999b.t: ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.feebbb94999b.back: The cuts let the sour gravy enter inside the egg.

seg.98394356bb39.src: Cool the boiled eggs in water before peeling; the shells come off cleanly.
seg.98394356bb39.t: ꯎꯠꯂꯕ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯠꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯀꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯦꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯀꯏ꯫
seg.98394356bb39.back: Cool the boiled eggs in water before removing the shell; the shells come off cleanly.

seg.f4306708f8c5.src: Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat; for a hotter pulusu add ½ tsp Teja chilli powder along with it.
seg.f4306708f8c5.t: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f4306708f8c5.back: Sannam chilli powder gives medium spiciness; for a spicier pulusu add ½ teaspoon Teja chilli powder together with it.

seg.fc1643db807e.src: Pulusu tastes better after it rests, and even more the next day, as the eggs soak up the tamarind.
seg.fc1643db807e.t: ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯂꯤ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.fc1643db807e.back: After keeping, the pulusu is tastier, and the next day even tastier, because the eggs absorb the tamarind.

seg.b19fe3919add.src: Tomato: add 1 chopped tomato after the onions for a softer, less sour gravy.
seg.b19fe3919add.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ, ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b19fe3919add.back: Tomato: for a softer, less sour gravy add 1 chopped tomato after the onion.

seg.0d78d434249e.src: Sesame: stir in 1 tbsp roasted sesame powder in the last 5 minutes for a thicker, nutty gravy.
seg.0d78d434249e.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5ꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0d78d434249e.back: Sesame: for a thicker, nut-like gravy add 1 tablespoon roasted sesame powder in the last 5 minutes and stir.

seg.e4adab31c02b.src: Mamidikaya: in summer, replace half the tamarind with a few pieces of raw mango cooked in the gravy.
seg.e4adab31c02b.t: ꯃꯥꯃꯤꯗꯤꯀꯥꯌ: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ, ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕ ꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ½ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯗꯕ ꯍꯩꯅꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e4adab31c02b.back: Mamidikay [not a Manipuri word; looks like the Telugu word for raw/green mango, written in Meetei Mayek]: In the months of hot sun [numit = sun or day; most likely 'summer months'], use only ½ of the amount of tamarind [imli] that should be used, and in its place cook a few pieces of unripe mango [mahei yadaba heinou: literally roughly 'mango whose fruit is not ripe/not ready'; best reading 'unripe/raw mango'] in the gravy.

seg.bbf897873153.src: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, with a crisp fry or appadalu on the side. It also goes with chapati or dosa.
seg.bbf897873153.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ, ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯞꯄꯗꯥꯂꯨꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯄꯥꯇꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯗꯣꯁꯥꯒꯥꯁꯨ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.bbf897873153.back: Serve hot with steamed rice and one spoon of ghee, with a crunchy fry or appadalu at the side. It also goes well with chapati or dosa.

seg.7a5a4bbedfff.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm the pulusu gently in a pan with a splash of water.
seg.7a5a4bbedfff.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7a5a4bbedfff.back: Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Heat the pulusu gently in a pan with a little water.

seg.3dae693db30c.src: How long should I boil eggs for egg curry?
seg.3dae693db30c.t: ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯎꯠꯍꯅꯒꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.3dae693db30c.back: How long should eggs be boiled for egg curry?

seg.2d6d1a298a24.src: About 10 minutes from the time the water boils. The yolk should be firm and pale yellow right through, with no runny centre, before the eggs go into the gravy.
seg.2d6d1a298a24.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯠꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝꯁꯤꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ, ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯕ ꯂꯩꯇꯅꯥ꯫
seg.2d6d1a298a24.back: About 10 minutes from the time the water boils. Before putting the eggs into the gravy, the inner 'oraba' part [same unclear word as L1: possibly 'yolk' or a colour word] should be fully hard/firm and have a little turmeric colour [i.e. slightly yellow], with nothing flowing like water in the middle [i.e. not runny].

seg.4abaae123f39.src: Why do you make slits on eggs for pulusu?
seg.4abaae123f39.back: Why make cuts in the eggs for pulusu?

seg.d3f5992ccd6e.src: Shallow slits let the tamarind gravy soak into the egg white. Without them the gravy stays on the surface and the egg tastes plain.
seg.d3f5992ccd6e.t: ꯑꯔꯨꯃꯗꯕ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯪꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯂꯩꯇꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯂꯩ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯇꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.d3f5992ccd6e.back: Not-deep cuts let the tamarind gravy enter the white part of the egg. Without them the gravy stays only on top and the egg stays tasteless.

seg.7a591bf728ac.src: How do I reduce the sourness of the pulusu?
seg.7a591bf728ac.back: How to reduce the sourness of the pulusu?

seg.0a2bf657f386.src: Simmer it a few minutes longer, add a teaspoon of grated jaggery, or stir in a little water. Use a smaller ball of tamarind next time.
seg.0a2bf657f386.t: ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0a2bf657f386.back: Cook a few more minutes on low flame, add one small spoon of grated jaggery, or add a little water and stir. When making it again use a smaller piece of tamarind.

seg.f9a34864523d.src: What is the difference between egg pulusu and egg curry?
seg.f9a34864523d.t: ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯈꯦꯟꯅꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.f9a34864523d.back: What is the difference between egg pulusu and egg curry?

seg.08bcae4f5075.src: Pulusu is a thinner, tangy tamarind gravy made to mix with rice. A regular egg curry is usually built on onion and tomato, with no tamarind and a thicker masala.
seg.08bcae4f5075.t: ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ, ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯝꯐꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ, ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ꯫
seg.08bcae4f5075.back: Pulusu is a watery, sour tamarind gravy made to mix with rice. The usual egg curry is often made on an onion and tomato base, without tamarind and with a thicker masala.

seg.6977652a1279.src: కోడి గుడ్డు పులుసు · Egg Pulusu Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.6977652a1279.t: కోడి గుడ్డు పులుసు · ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ | 1acrefarms
seg.6977652a1279.back: కోడి గుడ్డు పులుసు · Recipe of egg pulusu | 1acrefarms

seg.4f1d5bbdf5db.src: కోడి గుడ్డు పులుసు. Kodi guddu pulusu, Andhra egg curry: boiled eggs simmered in a tangy tamarind-onion gravy coloured with Sannam chilli powder and turmeric. Serves 4.
seg.4f1d5bbdf5db.t: కోడి గుడ్డు పులుసు. ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯒꯨꯗꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ, ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯔꯕ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ-ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯎꯠꯂꯕ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ꯫ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.4f1d5bbdf5db.back: కోడి గుడ్డు పులుసు. Kodi guddu pulusu, Andhra's egg curry: boiled eggs cooked on low flame in a sour tamarind-onion gravy coloured by Sannam chilli powder and turmeric. For 4 people.

seg.24e368a0d7e4.src: Kodi Guddu Pulusu (Andhra Egg Curry in Tamarind Gravy) · 1acrefarms
seg.24e368a0d7e4.t: ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯒꯨꯗꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ (ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯗꯥ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ) · 1acrefarms
seg.24e368a0d7e4.back: Kodi Guddu Pulusu (Andhra's egg curry in tamarind gravy) · 1acrefarms

seg.722d155a3c4f.src: Gutti Vankaya Kura ⟦1⟧(Andhra Stuffed Brinjal Curry)⟦/1⟧
seg.722d155a3c4f.t: ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ ꯚꯥꯡꯀꯥꯌ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ ⟦1⟧(ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ)⟦/1⟧
seg.722d155a3c4f.back: Gutti Vankaya Kura ⟦1⟧(Andhra's masala-stuffed brinjal curry)⟦/1⟧

seg.00fde8f92a7e.src: Gutti vankaya kura is the stuffed brinjal curry that Andhra homes make for Sunday lunches, weddings and when guests come over. Small, round purple brinjals are slit, packed with a roasted peanut, sesame and coconut masala, and cooked slowly in oil until they turn soft and the masala clings to them.
seg.00fde8f92a7e.t: ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ ꯚꯥꯡꯀꯥꯌ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯡꯃꯥꯏꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ, ꯂꯨꯍꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯇꯤꯊꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯂꯥꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ, ꯑꯀꯣꯌꯕ ꯄꯔꯄꯜ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ, ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯗꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ꯫
seg.00fde8f92a7e.back: Gutti vankaya kura is the masala-stuffed brinjal curry that Andhra houses make for the Sunday afternoon meal, for weddings and when guests come. Small, round, purple-colour brinjals are cut, stuffed with a masala of roasted groundnut, sesame and coconut, and cooked gently in oil until soft and the masala sticks to them.

seg.27fd58488499.src: Our Sannam chilli powder gives the stuffing its red colour and medium heat, and turmeric powder rounds it off. Serve it with hot rice or chapati. This recipe serves 4.
seg.27fd58488499.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯄꯥꯇꯤꯒꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.27fd58488499.back: Our Sannam chilli powder gives the stuffed masala red colour and medium spiciness, and turmeric powder completes it. Serve it with hot rice or chapati. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.dea818e2c052.src: Roast peanuts, sesame, dry coconut and coriander seeds, grind with Sannam chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt, stuff small brinjals and cook them slowly in oil until soft.
seg.dea818e2c052.t: ꯄꯤꯅꯠ, ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.dea818e2c052.back: Roast groundnut, sesame, dry coconut and coriander seed, grind with Sannam chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt, stuff into small brinjals and cook gently in oil until soft.

seg.1ba4509b5345.src: 3 tbsp peanuts ⟦1⟧raw, with or without skins⟦/1⟧
seg.1ba4509b5345.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ⟦1⟧ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯗ꯭ꯔꯕ, ꯃꯀꯨꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.1ba4509b5345.back: 3 tablespoons groundnut ⟦1⟧not roasted, with skin or without skin⟦/1⟧

seg.8be0f88d515d.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯣꯞꯔꯥ⟦/1⟧

seg.b0b877b509dc.src: 2 tsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧up to 1 tbsp for a hotter curry⟦/1⟧
seg.b0b877b509dc.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2 ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.b0b877b509dc.back: 2 teaspoons Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧up to 1 tablespoon for a spicier curry⟦/1⟧

seg.df2079b45203.src: 12 small brinjals ⟦1⟧about 500 g, small round purple ones⟦/1⟧
seg.df2079b45203.t: ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ 12 ⟦1⟧500 g ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯀꯣꯌꯕ ꯄꯔꯄꯜ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ⟦/1⟧
seg.df2079b45203.back: 12 small brinjals ⟦1⟧about 500 g, small, round, purple colour⟦/1⟧

seg.d56e638c12d0.src: Dry-roast the peanuts, sesame, coconut and coriander seeds; grind with the spices. Roast the peanuts first on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, then add the coriander seeds, cumin and sesame for 1 minute, and the coconut for the last 30 seconds, until it is light golden. Let it cool.
seg.d56e638c12d0.t: ꯄꯤꯅꯠ, ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ, ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3–4 ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 30ꯗꯥ, ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d56e638c12d0.back: Roast the groundnut, sesame, coconut and coriander seed without oil; grind with the masala. First roast the groundnut on medium-low flame 3–4 minutes, then add coriander seed, cumin and sesame for 1 minute, and the coconut in the last 30 seconds, until a little golden colour. Let cool.

seg.26e4a965b3f7.src: In a mixer, grind the roasted mix with the garlic, Sannam chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt and tamarind to a coarse powder without water. It should clump when pressed.
seg.26e4a965b3f7.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯅꯝꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.26e4a965b3f7.back: In a mixer grind the roasted things with garlic, Sannam chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt and tamarind into a coarse powder without water. When pressed it should stick together.

seg.5784e45d4bff.src: Wash the brinjals and trim the green cap a little, leaving the stalk on.
seg.5784e45d4bff.t: ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯌꯣꯛ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯀꯣꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5784e45d4bff.back: Wash the brinjals and, keeping the stalk, cut off a little of the green cap.

seg.02665f13e5af.src: Slit each brinjal in a cross from the bottom, keeping the stem on, and pack in the stuffing. Cut about three-quarters of the way up so the four quarters stay joined at the top. Drop each one into a bowl of salted water as you go, then drain.
seg.02665f13e5af.t: ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯣꯛ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯁ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯄꯨꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯃꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯠꯂꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.02665f13e5af.back: Cut each brinjal from the bottom in a cross, keeping the stalk, and stuff the masala. Cut to about three of the four parts so that the four parts stay joined at the top. After cutting put each one into a bowl of salted water, then drain the water.

seg.498fc880430b.src: Press about 1 heaped tsp of stuffing into each brinjal. Keep the leftover stuffing aside.
seg.498fc880430b.t: ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯜꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯅꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.498fc880430b.back: Press about 1 heaped teaspoon of masala into each brinjal. Keep the remaining masala at the side.

seg.3daa0935ccba.src: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan on medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and, when they splutter, the curry leaves and onion, if using. Fry the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
seg.3daa0935ccba.t: ꯄꯥꯛꯄ, ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ, ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫
seg.3daa0935ccba.back: Heat the oil on medium flame in a wide, heavy pan. Add mustard seed and when it crackles add curry leaves and onion, if using. Fry the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.

seg.3a140b72d6a0.src: Place the stuffed brinjals in a single layer in the pan.
seg.3a140b72d6a0.t: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯔꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯦꯟꯗꯥ ꯊꯛ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3a140b72d6a0.back: Place the stuffed brinjals in the pan in a single layer.

seg.1ae98f10b6ed.src: Cook the brinjals in hot oil, covered, on a low flame, turning gently every 4–5 minutes. Use a spoon or tongs so the stuffing stays in, and cook for 15–18 minutes, until the skins wrinkle.
seg.1ae98f10b6ed.t: ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ, ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 4–5 ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯤꯃꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯀꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15–18 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1ae98f10b6ed.back: Cook the brinjals in the hot oil, covered, on low flame, turning gently every 4–5 minutes. Use a spoon or tongs so the masala stays inside, and cook 15–18 minutes until the skins wrinkle.

seg.50530663a626.src: Add the leftover stuffing with ½ cup water; simmer till the brinjals are soft. Cover and cook on low for 8–10 minutes more, until the masala thickens and oil shows at the sides.
seg.50530663a626.t: ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ½ꯒꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯎꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 8–10 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.50530663a626.back: Add the remaining masala with ½ cup water; cook on low flame until the brinjals are soft. Cover and cook 8–10 more minutes on low flame until the masala thickens and oil comes out at the edges.

seg.2a2726cfebd5.src: Check doneness: a knife should slide through the thickest brinjal with no resistance. Sprinkle the coriander leaves and switch off.
seg.2a2726cfebd5.t: ꯆꯤꯟꯔꯕꯔꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯊꯤꯡꯕ ꯂꯩꯇꯅꯥ ꯆꯪꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2a2726cfebd5.back: Check whether done: a knife should go into the biggest brinjal without obstruction. Sprinkle coriander leaves and turn off the flame.

seg.c2e59cef6130.src: Keep the stalks on so the brinjals hold together while they cook and turn.
seg.c2e59cef6130.t: ꯃꯌꯣꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯨꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.c2e59cef6130.back: Keep the stalks, then while cooking and turning the brinjals will stay joined.

seg.15314c3b05cd.src: Pick small, glossy brinjals of the same size, so they cook evenly; large ones stay hard in the centre.
seg.15314c3b05cd.t: ꯆꯥꯎꯕ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ, ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ, ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ ꯈꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯒꯅꯤ; ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯁꯤꯡꯗꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.15314c3b05cd.back: Choose small, shiny brinjals equal in size, then they will cook evenly; big ones stay hard in the middle.

seg.208cff8b9d46.src: Roast the peanuts and sesame on medium-low heat; burnt sesame makes the whole masala bitter.
seg.208cff8b9d46.t: ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯆꯥꯀꯈꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯈꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.208cff8b9d46.back: Roast the groundnut and sesame on medium-low flame; burnt sesame makes the whole masala bitter.

seg.7779355bd06d.src: For a milder curry, use 1½ tsp Sannam chilli powder; for more heat, go up to 1 tbsp.
seg.7779355bd06d.t: ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7779355bd06d.back: For a mild curry use 1½ teaspoons Sannam chilli powder; for more spiciness use up to 1 tablespoon.

seg.742d7eb81437.src: With onion masala: grind 1 small onion into the stuffing for a softer, slightly sweet gravy.
seg.742d7eb81437.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.742d7eb81437.back: With onion masala: for a softer, slightly sweet gravy grind 1 small onion into the stuffing masala.

seg.abde9958c7fa.src: Without coconut: leave out the coconut and use 1 tbsp more peanuts and sesame.
seg.abde9958c7fa.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.abde9958c7fa.back: Without coconut: leave out the coconut and use 1 tablespoon more groundnut and sesame.

seg.b9a6b34c8c73.src: Gravy style: add 1 cup water in place of ½ cup in the last step for a thinner curry to mix into rice.
seg.b9a6b34c8c73.t: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ: ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯒꯤ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞ ½ꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b9a6b34c8c73.back: Gravy style: for a watery curry to mix with rice add 1 cup water in place of ½ cup in the last step.

seg.80faf3a5e4b1.src: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, or with chapati or jonna rotte.
seg.80faf3a5e4b1.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯄꯥꯇꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯖꯣꯟꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯠꯇꯦꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.80faf3a5e4b1.back: Serve hot with steamed rice and one spoon of ghee, or with chapati or jonna rotte.

seg.9adac1f51f99.src: Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm gently with a splash of water.
seg.9adac1f51f99.t: ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9adac1f51f99.back: Cover, keep in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Heat gently with a little water.

seg.83ffeb71bb2a.src: Which brinjals are best for gutti vankaya?
seg.83ffeb71bb2a.t: ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ ꯚꯥꯡꯀꯥꯌꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯔꯝꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.83ffeb71bb2a.back: Which kind of brinjal is best for gutti vankaya?

seg.76c81f4beef2.src: Small, round purple brinjals about the size of an egg, with a glossy skin and green stalk. They cook through in the time the masala takes and hold the stuffing well.
seg.76c81f4beef2.t: ꯌꯦꯔꯨꯝ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ, ꯑꯀꯣꯌꯕ ꯄꯔꯄꯜ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ, ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯌꯣꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅꯥ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯆꯤꯟꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.76c81f4beef2.back: Egg-size small, round, purple-colour brinjals, with shiny skin and a green stalk. They cook in the same time the masala takes to go in and hold the masala well.

seg.71325f387d2a.src: How do I know the brinjals are cooked?
seg.71325f387d2a.back: How to know the brinjals are done?

seg.c65656faa952.src: The skins wrinkle and soften, and a knife slides through the thickest brinjal with no resistance. Undercooked brinjals feel firm and spongy in the centre.
seg.c65656faa952.t: ꯃꯀꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯊꯤꯡꯕ ꯂꯩꯇꯅꯥ ꯆꯪꯊꯣꯀꯏ꯫ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯗꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁ꯭ꯄꯟꯖꯒꯨꯝ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯏ꯫
seg.c65656faa952.back: The skins wrinkle and become soft, and a knife goes into the biggest brinjal without obstruction. Not fully cooked brinjals feel hard and like a sponge in the middle.

seg.297ebd94e89c.src: Can I make gutti vankaya without coconut?
seg.297ebd94e89c.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ ꯚꯥꯡꯀꯥꯌ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.297ebd94e89c.back: Can gutti vankaya be made without coconut?

seg.f9ad1045b4c1.src: Yes. Use 1 tbsp more peanuts and 1 tbsp more sesame seeds in place of the coconut; the masala tastes nuttier.
seg.f9ad1045b4c1.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.f9ad1045b4c1.back: Yes. In place of coconut use 1 tablespoon more groundnut and 1 tablespoon more sesame; the masala taste becomes more nut-like.

seg.534e126ba995.src: Why do my brinjals fall apart?
seg.534e126ba995.back: Why do my brinjals break apart?

seg.96bfe0b8ed06.src: The stalk was removed or the cross was cut all the way through. Keep the stalk on, stop the slit about a quarter from the top and turn them gently.
seg.96bfe0b8ed06.t: ꯃꯌꯣꯛ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯀꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯣꯁ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯃꯌꯣꯛ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯃꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯕꯨ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.96bfe0b8ed06.back: Because the stalk was removed or the cross was cut all the way. Keep the stalk, stop cutting leaving about one of four parts from the top, and turn them gently.

seg.69e1140e9c6e.src: గుత్తి వంకాయ కూర · Gutti Vankaya Kura Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.69e1140e9c6e.t: గుత్తి వంకాయ కూర · ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ ꯚꯥꯡꯀꯥꯌ ꯀꯨꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ | 1acrefarms
seg.69e1140e9c6e.back: గుత్తి వంకాయ కూర · Recipe of Gutti Vankaya Kura | 1acrefarms

seg.d09cc87e5fde.src: గుత్తి వంకాయ కూర. Small brinjals stuffed with roasted peanut, sesame and coconut, ground with Sannam chilli powder and turmeric powder, then slow-cooked in oil.
seg.d09cc87e5fde.t: గుత్తి వంకాయ కూర. ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ, ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯊꯥꯅꯕ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ꯫
seg.d09cc87e5fde.back: గుత్తి వంకాయ కూర. Small brinjals stuffed with roasted groundnut, sesame and coconut ground with Sannam chilli powder and turmeric powder, then cooked gently in oil.

seg.e6d2d516a538.src: Gutti Vankaya Kura (Andhra Stuffed Brinjal Curry) · 1acrefarms
seg.e6d2d516a538.t: ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ ꯚꯥꯡꯀꯥꯌ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ (ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕ ꯈꯥꯃꯦꯟ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ) · 1acrefarms
seg.e6d2d516a538.back: Gutti Vankaya Kura (Andhra's masala-stuffed brinjal curry) · 1acrefarms

seg.edfa611d692c.t: ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ ꯚꯥꯡꯀꯥꯌ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
