seg.6338aa32f352.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ

seg.111c74722b7d.src: Jeedipappu pakodi is the cashew pakoda that Andhra sweet shops and homes fry for tea time, festivals and guests: whole cashews in a thin, spiced coat of besan and rice flour, fried till crisp. Made without onion, it keeps for days in a jar, so many homes fry a batch for Diwali and Sankranti visitors.
seg.111c74722b7d.t: ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯊꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯗꯣꯀꯥꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯥ ꯊꯛꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ, ꯀꯨꯝꯃꯩ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯇꯤꯊꯤꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯥꯅꯤ: ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯕ, ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯗꯤꯋꯥꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯡꯀ꯭ꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯇꯤꯊꯤꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯠꯇꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯏ꯫
seg.111c74722b7d.back: Jeedipappu pakodi is the cashew pakoda that Andhra sweet shops and houses fry for tea time, festivals and guests: whole cashews fried in a thin, spiced coating of besan and rice powder until crunchy. Because it is made without onion it can be kept in a jar many days, so many houses fry one batch for Diwali and Sankranti guests.

seg.b4f22aebea20.src: Whole cashews from our Jeedipappu pack stay crunchy inside the coating, and Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat and a warm red colour. This recipe serves 4.
seg.b4f22aebea20.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯦꯀꯇꯒꯤ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯡꯉꯥꯏꯕ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.b4f22aebea20.back: The whole cashews from our Jeedipappu pack stay crunchy inside the coating, and Sannam chilli powder gives medium spiciness and a pleasant red colour. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.a21c4d5f661e.src: Total includes 5 minutes for the pakodi to cool and crisp.
seg.a21c4d5f661e.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯏꯪꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.a21c4d5f661e.back: 5 minutes for the pakodi to cool and become crunchy is included in the total.

seg.0f4b2d277930.src: Toss whole cashews with besan, rice flour, Sannam chilli powder, salt and a spoon of hot oil, sprinkle in just enough water to coat, and deep fry till golden and crisp.
seg.0f4b2d277930.t: ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯕꯦꯁꯟ, ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯕꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0f4b2d277930.back: Mix the whole cashews with besan, rice powder, Sannam chilli powder, salt and one spoon of hot oil, sprinkle only enough water to coat, and fry in plenty of oil until golden colour and crunchy.

seg.d97defcf6bd2.src: 1 cup whole cashews ⟦1⟧about 150 g; split any very large ones in half⟦/1⟧
seg.d97defcf6bd2.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ⟦1⟧150 g ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯕꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯈꯥꯌꯗꯣꯀꯎ⟦/1⟧
seg.d97defcf6bd2.back: 1 cup whole cashews ⟦1⟧about 150 g; break the very big ones into pieces⟦/1⟧

seg.0fb432c2000d.src: ½ cup besan ⟦1⟧gram flour, about 50 g⟦/1⟧
seg.0fb432c2000d.t: ꯀꯞ ½ ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ⟦1⟧ꯆꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, 50 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.0fb432c2000d.back: ½ cup besan ⟦1⟧chana powder, about 50 g⟦/1⟧

seg.4530b28d3c24.src: 2 tbsp rice flour ⟦1⟧for a crisper coating⟦/1⟧
seg.4530b28d3c24.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ⟦/1⟧
seg.4530b28d3c24.back: 2 tablespoons rice powder ⟦1⟧for a more crunchy coating⟦/1⟧

seg.069bf214d83d.src: 1 tsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧medium heat; add ½ tsp more for a hotter pakodi⟦/1⟧
seg.069bf214d83d.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.069bf214d83d.back: 1 teaspoon Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧medium spiciness; for a spicier pakodi add ½ teaspoon more⟦/1⟧

seg.40a2a51a64aa.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯊꯨꯝ ⟦1⟧ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧

seg.c5de5bb5101e.src: 1 tbsp hot oil ⟦1⟧taken from the frying oil⟦/1⟧
seg.c5de5bb5101e.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯤꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.c5de5bb5101e.back: 1 tablespoon hot oil ⟦1⟧taken from the frying oil⟦/1⟧

seg.a24adfc46507.src: 2–3 tbsp water ⟦1⟧sprinkled in a little at a time⟦/1⟧

seg.9a0fd1249b07.src: oil for deep frying ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is the usual choice⟦/1⟧
seg.9a0fd1249b07.t: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯕꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠꯀꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ⟦/1⟧
seg.9a0fd1249b07.back: Oil for frying in plenty of oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is used all the time⟦/1⟧

seg.8423a6481648.src: Rinse the cashews and drain them well; a slightly damp surface helps the flour stick.
seg.8423a6481648.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯈꯔꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯞꯄ ꯃꯊꯛꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯀꯞꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯦꯡ ꯄꯥꯡꯏ꯫
seg.8423a6481648.back: Wash the cashews in water and drain the water well; a top a little wet with water helps the powder stick.

seg.0d03259dc451.src: Heat the oil for deep frying in a kadai on medium heat.
seg.0d03259dc451.t: ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯅꯕꯒꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0d03259dc451.back: Heat the frying oil on medium flame in a kadai.

seg.c7fa1a156718.src: Mix the besan, rice flour, chilli powder, salt, ginger-garlic paste and curry leaves. Use a wide bowl, and add the green chillies, coriander leaves and asafoetida at the same time.
seg.c7fa1a156718.t: ꯕꯦꯁꯟ, ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯊꯨꯝ, ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ, ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c7fa1a156718.back: Mix besan, rice powder, chilli powder, salt, ginger-garlic paste and curry leaves. Use a wide bowl, and add green chilli, coriander leaves and hing at the same time.

seg.346911fb291b.src: Rub in 1 tbsp hot oil, add the cashews and sprinkle water till the flour just coats them. Spoon the hot oil from the kadai with care and rub it into the flour mix with your fingertips first, then add the cashews and sprinkle the water 1 tbsp at a time, tossing, until the flour clings to every cashew. The mix should look like damp crumbs, not a batter.
seg.346911fb291b.t: ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯕꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯞꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯁꯤꯡꯒꯨꯝ ꯎꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯕꯦꯇꯔꯒꯨꯝ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫
seg.346911fb291b.back: Add 1 tablespoon hot oil and rub, add the cashews and sprinkle water until the powder coats them a little. Carefully take hot oil from the kadai with a spoon and first rub it into the powder with the fingertips, then add the cashews and sprinkle water 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing, until the powder coats each cashew. The mixture should look like small damp lumps, not like a watery batter.

seg.05a50e3b5ae8.src: Check the oil: a pinch of the mix dropped in should rise to the top in 2–3 seconds with steady bubbles. If it browns at once, the oil is too hot.
seg.05a50e3b5ae8.t: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 2–3ꯗꯥ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯏ꯫
seg.05a50e3b5ae8.back: Check the oil: when a little mixture is dropped it should come up to the top with steady bubbles in 2–3 seconds. If it turns brown at once, the oil is very hot.

seg.f3e77b6c0f73.src: Drop small clusters into medium-hot oil. Pick up 3–4 coated cashews at a time with your fingers and let them fall loosely into the oil, without crowding the kadai.
seg.f3e77b6c0f73.t: ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟꯂꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ 3–4 ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯟꯊꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ꯫
seg.f3e77b6c0f73.back: Drop small clusters into medium-hot oil. Take 3–4 coated cashews together with the hand and drop them gently into the oil, without crowding the kadai too much.

seg.5e4bfdad4c05.src: Fry, turning, till golden and crisp, 5–6 minutes; drain on paper. The bubbles around the pakodi get smaller and slow down when they are done.
seg.5e4bfdad4c05.t: ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–6; ꯆꯦꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯆꯤꯟꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯆꯠꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.5e4bfdad4c05.back: Turning, fry until golden colour and crunchy, 5–6 minutes; drain the oil on paper. When done, the bubbles around the pakodi become small and move slowly.

seg.eb1a58e02e89.src: Fry the rest in batches the same way, letting the oil come back to heat between batches.
seg.eb1a58e02e89.t: ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕꯗꯨ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯈꯥꯌꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ꯫
seg.eb1a58e02e89.back: Fry the rest in the same way divided into batches, heating the oil again between each.

seg.8ab193492427.src: Let the pakodi rest for 5 minutes on the paper; they crisp up further as they cool. Sprinkle a pinch of salt or chilli powder over the top, if you like.
seg.8ab193492427.t: ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯦꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯪꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8ab193492427.back: Keep the pakodi on paper 5 minutes; when they cool they become more crunchy. If you like, sprinkle a little salt or chilli powder on top.

seg.c8ded38fad10.src: Keep the batter thick and dry, not runny, or the pakodi turns soft.
seg.c8ded38fad10.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯍꯜꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯅꯠꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.c8ded38fad10.back: Keep the mixture thick and dry, do not add too much water, otherwise the pakodi will become soft.

seg.9670def7c10b.src: Fry on medium heat: cashews brown fast, and on high heat the coating colours before the cashew inside is toasted.
seg.9670def7c10b.t: ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.9670def7c10b.back: Fry on medium flame: cashews turn brown quickly, and on high flame the coating takes colour before the cashew inside is roasted.

seg.76602f605fc8.src: The spoon of hot oil rubbed into the flour makes the pakodi light and crisp.
seg.76602f605fc8.t: ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.76602f605fc8.back: One spoon of hot oil rubbed into the powder makes the pakodi light and crunchy.

seg.2494998e92ed.src: Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat and a good red colour; use ½ tsp for children.
seg.2494998e92ed.t: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯕ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ; ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2494998e92ed.back: Sannam chilli powder gives medium spiciness and a good red colour; for children use ½ teaspoon.

seg.7f70d313349e.src: Hotter: replace half the Sannam chilli powder with Teja chilli powder, which is much hotter.
seg.7f70d313349e.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯅꯕꯥ: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ꯫
seg.7f70d313349e.back: To make it spicier: use Teja chilli powder instead of the Sannam chilli powder portion; it is much spicier.

seg.2b2be3846a1d.src: With onion: add 1 small onion, thinly sliced, with the cashews for a softer, sweeter pakodi, and eat it the same day.
seg.2b2be3846a1d.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ, ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2b2be3846a1d.back: With onion: for a softer, sweeter pakodi add 1 thinly cut small onion together with the cashews, and eat it that same day.

seg.7f852eddc8b5.src: Mint: add 2 tbsp chopped mint leaves along with the coriander leaves.
seg.7f852eddc8b5.t: ꯄꯨꯗꯤꯅꯥ: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯄꯨꯗꯤꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7f852eddc8b5.back: Mint: add 2 tablespoons chopped mint leaves together with the coriander leaves.

seg.cd47edc05460.src: Serve warm with evening tea or filter coffee. They also go into lunch boxes or onto the side of a rice-and-pappu meal.
seg.cd47edc05460.t: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯋꯥꯏꯔꯃꯒꯤ ꯆꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯐꯤꯜꯇꯔ ꯀꯣꯐꯤꯒꯥ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯂꯟꯆ ꯕꯣꯛꯁꯇꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ-ꯄꯞꯄꯨꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯁꯨ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫
seg.cd47edc05460.back: Serve hot with evening tea or filter coffee. They also go into the lunch box or at the side of a rice-pappu meal.

seg.e2777b4dabb7.src: Once fully cooled, keep them in an airtight jar at room temperature and eat within 4–5 days. If they soften, warm them in a dry pan on low heat for 2–3 minutes.
seg.e2777b4dabb7.t: ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 4–5ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2–3 ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e2777b4dabb7.back: After fully cooling, keep in an airtight jar at home room temperature and eat within 4–5 days. If they become soft, heat in a dry pan on low flame 2–3 minutes.

seg.f8c9120f7f67.src: Why did my cashew pakodi turn soft?
seg.f8c9120f7f67.back: Why did my cashew pakodi become soft?

seg.346050614d3a.src: Too much water in the flour, or frying on low heat. Keep the mix like damp crumbs and fry on medium heat until the bubbles slow down.
seg.346050614d3a.t: ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯞꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯁꯤꯡꯒꯨꯝ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯆꯠꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.346050614d3a.back: Because too much water was in the powder, or it was fried on low flame. Keep the mixture like small damp lumps and fry on medium flame until the bubbles move slowly.

seg.921421ebf2c6.src: Should I soak cashews before making pakodi?
seg.921421ebf2c6.back: Should the cashews be soaked in water before making pakodi?

seg.e6e487728264.src: No soak is needed. A quick rinse is enough to help the flour stick; cashews soaked for long lose some of their crunch.
seg.e6e487728264.t: ꯆꯨꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯗꯦ꯫ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯀꯞꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯏ; ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯥꯡꯏ꯫
seg.e6e487728264.back: There is no need to soak. One quick wash is enough for the powder to stick; cashews soaked a long time lose a little of their crunch.

seg.905443e515e2.src: Can I make cashew pakodi without rice flour?
seg.905443e515e2.t: ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.905443e515e2.back: Can cashew pakodi be made without rice powder?

seg.72a2c55cca9c.src: Yes. Use 2 tbsp more besan, or 1 tbsp cornflour. Rice flour gives the crispest coating, so the pakodi will be a little softer without it.
seg.72a2c55cca9c.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯣꯔꯟꯐ꯭ꯂꯥꯋꯥꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟ ꯄꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.72a2c55cca9c.back: Yes. Use 2 tablespoons more besan, or 1 tablespoon cornflour. Rice powder gives the most crunchy coating, so without it the pakodi will be a little softer.

seg.f129edc737b1.src: How long does cashew pakodi stay crisp?
seg.f129edc737b1.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.f129edc737b1.back: How long does cashew pakodi stay crunchy?

seg.d73ef4b28b6d.src: About 4–5 days in an airtight jar, as long as it cools completely before it goes in.
seg.d73ef4b28b6d.t: ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 4–5 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯗꯤ꯫
seg.d73ef4b28b6d.back: About 4–5 days in an airtight jar, if it was fully cooled before putting in the jar.

seg.60df05d4b9d3.back: జీడిపప్పు పకోడీ · Recipe of cashew pakodi | 1acrefarms

seg.62c3aa71c55a.src: జీడిపప్పు పకోడీ. Crisp cashew pakodi with whole cashews from our Jeedipappu pack, besan, rice flour and Sannam chilli powder. Step-by-step method, tips and FAQs.
seg.62c3aa71c55a.t: జీడిపప్పు పకోడీ. ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯦꯀꯇꯒꯤ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ, ꯕꯦꯁꯟ, ꯆꯦꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ꯫ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ, ꯇꯤꯞꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯁꯤꯡ꯫
seg.62c3aa71c55a.back: జీడిపప్పు పకోడీ. Crunchy cashew pakodi with whole cashews from our Jeedipappu pack, besan, rice powder and Sannam chilli powder. Step-by-step way, tips and questions.

seg.f560ff3badb6.src: Jeedipappu Pakodi: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.f560ff3badb6.t: ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯀꯣꯗꯤ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.f560ff3badb6.back: Jeedipappu Pakodi: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.7d26dc20462c.t: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯕꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ
seg.7d26dc20462c.back: Oil for frying in plenty of oil

seg.a64f3158d8da.src: Upma is the everyday Andhra tiffin: semolina cooked soft in a seasoned water with onion, green chillies and curry leaves. Jeedipappu upma is the dressed-up version, with a good handful of cashews fried golden in ghee, the way it is made for guests, for festival mornings and at weddings, often served next to pesarattu or with a spoon of sugar.
seg.a64f3158d8da.t: ꯎꯞꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯇꯤꯐꯤꯟꯅꯤ: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯁꯨꯖꯤ꯫ ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯎꯞꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯁꯖꯦꯠ ꯁꯖꯦꯠꯄ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯅꯤ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ, ꯑꯇꯤꯊꯤꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯀꯨꯝꯃꯩꯒꯤ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯨꯍꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯨꯝ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯠꯇꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.a64f3158d8da.back: Upma is Andhra's everyday tiffin: semolina cooked soft in water tempered with onion, green chilli and curry leaves. Jeedipappu upma is the decorated form, with plenty of cashews fried golden colour in ghee, as made for guests, festival mornings and weddings, often served at the side of pesarattu or with one spoon of sugar.

seg.f9bc03f64077.src: Our Jeedipappu cashews are whole and plain, so they fry evenly and stay crunchy against the soft rava. It is on the table in about 25 minutes. This recipe serves 3.
seg.f9bc03f64077.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯟꯅꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯔꯋꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 25 ꯔꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯏ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 3ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.f9bc03f64077.back: Our Jeedipappu cashews are whole and plain, so they fry evenly and stay crunchy in the soft rava. It is ready for the meal in about 25 minutes. This recipe is for 3 people.

seg.5ef4d1713249.src: Roast rava, fry cashews in ghee, then temper and soften onion and chillies. Boil water with salt, stir in the rava, cover and finish with the cashews.
seg.5ef4d1713249.t: ꯔꯋꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯅꯦꯝꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯔꯋꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5ef4d1713249.back: Roast the rava, fry the cashews in ghee, then temper and soften the onion and chilli. Boil water with salt, add the rava and stir, cover and finish with the cashews.

seg.5f9c9ea52cc5.src: 1 cup bombay rava ⟦1⟧medium semolina (sooji), about 170 g⟦/1⟧
seg.5f9c9ea52cc5.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯕꯣꯝꯕꯦ ꯔꯋꯥ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯁꯨꯖꯤ, 170 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.5f9c9ea52cc5.back: 1 cup Bombay rava ⟦1⟧medium semolina, about 170 g⟦/1⟧

seg.30102cb3f08b.src: 2½ cups water ⟦1⟧use 2 cups for a firmer upma⟦/1⟧
seg.30102cb3f08b.t: ꯀꯞ 2½ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯞ 2 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.30102cb3f08b.back: 2½ cups water ⟦1⟧for a firmer upma use 2 cups⟦/1⟧

seg.be0ebf4a6ec1.src: ¼ cup cashews ⟦1⟧whole or halved, about 35 g⟦/1⟧
seg.be0ebf4a6ec1.t: ꯀꯞ ¼ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ, 35 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.be0ebf4a6ec1.back: ¼ cup cashews ⟦1⟧whole or split into halves, about 35 g⟦/1⟧

seg.0e1b40869004.src: 3 tbsp ghee ⟦1⟧or 2 tbsp oil plus 1 tbsp ghee⟦/1⟧
seg.0e1b40869004.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1⟦/1⟧
seg.0e1b40869004.back: 3 tablespoons ghee ⟦1⟧or 2 tablespoons oil and 1 tablespoon ghee⟦/1⟧

seg.07a870690b21.src: 2 green chillies ⟦1⟧slit; use 3 for a hotter upma⟦/1⟧
seg.07a870690b21.t: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ 2 ⟦1⟧ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ 3 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.07a870690b21.back: 2 green chillies ⟦1⟧cut; for a spicier upma use 3⟦/1⟧

seg.46ba774a4c39.back: 2 tablespoons coriander leaves ⟦1⟧chopped, if you like⟦/1⟧

seg.5fe03b6066ae.src: Chop the onion, ginger and coriander leaves, slit the green chillies, and measure out the water.
seg.5fe03b6066ae.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯀꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5fe03b6066ae.back: Chop the onion, ginger and coriander leaves, cut the green chillies, and get ready by measuring the water.

seg.015e5d6ef88c.src: Roast the rava in a dry pan till it smells toasty, about 5 minutes. Keep it pale. Stir all the time on medium-low heat, then tip it onto a plate.
seg.015e5d6ef88c.t: ꯔꯋꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.015e5d6ef88c.back: Roast the rava in a dry pan until a roasted smell comes out, about 5 minutes. Keep it a pale colour. Stir all the time on medium-low fire, then pour it out onto a plate.

seg.2ccb9bbfe373.src: Heat the ghee in a wide, heavy pan on medium-low heat.
seg.2ccb9bbfe373.t: ꯄꯥꯛꯄ, ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2ccb9bbfe373.back: Heat the ghee on medium-low flame in a wide, heavy pan.

seg.827cce77ebf1.src: Fry the cashews in the ghee till golden; lift them out. This takes about 1–2 minutes; keep the ghee in the pan.
seg.827cce77ebf1.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯕꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1–2 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯄꯦꯅꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.827cce77ebf1.back: Fry the cashews in the ghee until golden colour; take them out. This takes about 1–2 minutes; keep the ghee in the pan.

seg.57b61920de4c.src: Temper mustard, dals and curry leaves. Soften the onion and chillies, add water and salt, and boil. Let the mustard seeds splutter and the dals turn light golden before the curry leaves go in, then add the ginger with the onion and cook for 3–4 minutes till the onion is soft.
seg.57b61920de4c.t: ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯅꯦꯝꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3–4 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.57b61920de4c.back: Make a tempering of mustard seed, dal and curry leaves. Soften the onion and chilli, add water and salt and boil. Before adding curry leaves let the mustard seed crackle and the dals turn a little golden, then add ginger together with the onion and cook 3–4 minutes until the onion is soft.

seg.be01d433ae80.src: Taste the water once it boils; it should taste a little salty, as the rava will take up the salt.
seg.be01d433ae80.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯠꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯈꯔꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯔꯋꯥꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.be01d433ae80.back: Taste after the water boils; it should be a little salty, because the rava will absorb the salt.

seg.b99b11495ead.src: Turn the heat to low. Pour in the rava in a thin stream, stirring. Cover on low for 3 minutes; top with the cashews.
seg.b99b11495ead.t: ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3 ꯀꯨꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b99b11495ead.back: Make the flame low. Pour the rava in a thin stream while stirring. Cover 3 minutes on low flame; put the cashews on top.

seg.fbf1f55f7751.src: Before adding the cashews, check the upma: the rava should be soft with no hard grains, and the upma should leave the sides of the pan. If it is still grainy, sprinkle in 2 tbsp hot water, cover and cook 1 minute more.
seg.fbf1f55f7751.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯎꯞꯃꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯔꯋꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯂꯩꯇꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯅꯥ ꯄꯦꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯇꯣꯠꯂꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fbf1f55f7751.back: Before adding the cashews check the upma: the rava should be soft without hard grains, and the upma should come away from the side of the pan. If it still feels grainy, sprinkle 2 tablespoons hot water, cover and cook 1 more minute.

seg.28e90add4ba6.src: Stir in the extra spoon of ghee and the coriander leaves, if using, along with most of the cashews.
seg.28e90add4ba6.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ, ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.28e90add4ba6.back: Add the extra spoon of ghee and coriander leaves, if using, together with most of the cashews and stir.

seg.351e9512c914.src: Serve hot, with the rest of the cashews on top.
seg.351e9512c914.t: ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.351e9512c914.back: Serve hot with the remaining cashews kept on top.

seg.4643e12d303d.src: Pour the rava in a thin stream while stirring so no lumps form.
seg.4643e12d303d.t: ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯁꯦꯃꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4643e12d303d.back: Pour the rava in a thin stream while stirring so it does not form lumps.

seg.3c98bb62770b.src: Roasting the rava first keeps each grain separate; skip it and the upma turns sticky.
seg.3c98bb62770b.t: ꯔꯋꯥ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ; ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯎꯞꯃꯥ ꯆꯦꯜꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.3c98bb62770b.back: If the rava is roasted first, each grain stays separate; if not roasted the upma becomes sticky.

seg.fc5bc0e0bf4e.src: Fry the cashews on medium-low heat and lift them out as soon as they turn golden; they keep darkening in the hot ghee.
seg.fc5bc0e0bf4e.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤ꯫
seg.fc5bc0e0bf4e.back: Fry the cashews on medium-low flame and take them out just when golden colour; in hot ghee they keep on darkening.

seg.975560a8a158.src: Upma firms up as it stands, so take it off the heat when it is a little softer than you want.
seg.975560a8a158.t: ꯎꯞꯃꯥ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯤꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.975560a8a158.back: When upma is kept it becomes firm, so take it off the flame when it is a little softer than you want.

seg.508f0ab3992d.src: Vegetable upma: add ½ cup chopped carrot, beans and green peas with the onion and cook them for 3–4 minutes before the water goes in.
seg.508f0ab3992d.t: ꯃꯅꯥ-ꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯎꯞꯃꯥ: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯒꯥꯖꯔ, ꯕꯤꯟ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯔ ꯀꯞ ½ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3–4 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.508f0ab3992d.back: Vegetable upma: add ½ cup chopped carrot, beans and peas together with the onion and cook 3–4 minutes before adding water.

seg.1742d7bd0e23.src: Tomato upma: add 1 chopped tomato after the onion and cook till soft before adding the water.
seg.1742d7bd0e23.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯎꯞꯃꯥ: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1742d7bd0e23.back: Tomato upma: add 1 chopped tomato after the onion and cook until soft before adding water.

seg.1981c7f3fc60.src: Godhuma rava upma: use the same amount of wheat rava with 3 cups water and cook it covered for 5–6 minutes.
seg.1981c7f3fc60.t: ꯒꯣꯙꯨꯃꯥ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯎꯞꯃꯥ: ꯒꯦꯍꯨꯒꯤ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 3ꯒꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–6 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1981c7f3fc60.back: Godhuma rava upma: use the same quantity of wheat rava with 3 cups water and cook covered 5–6 minutes.

seg.01300d94ad36.src: Serve hot as a breakfast tiffin with coconut chutney, allam pachadi or a spoon of sugar, or next to pesarattu for pesarattu upma.
seg.01300d94ad36.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯆꯠꯅꯤ, ꯑꯜꯂꯝ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯇꯤꯐꯤꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯠꯇꯨ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯠꯇꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ꯫
seg.01300d94ad36.back: Serve hot as the morning tiffin with coconut chutney, allam pachadi or one spoon of sugar, or at the side of pesarattu for pesarattu upma.

seg.3316a3d82f44.src: Upma is best eaten hot, soon after it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and sprinkle with water before reheating.
seg.3316a3d82f44.t: ꯎꯞꯃꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯩ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3316a3d82f44.back: Upma is best eaten hot right after making. Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge up to 1 day and sprinkle water before heating it again.

seg.b53646711bf0.src: How do I make upma without lumps?
seg.b53646711bf0.back: How to make upma without lumps?

seg.429b54b4ab3a.src: Keep the water at a boil, turn the heat to low and pour in the rava in a thin stream with one hand while you stir with the other.
seg.429b54b4ab3a.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.429b54b4ab3a.back: Keep the water boiling, make the flame low, and stirring with one hand, pour the rava in a thin stream with the other hand.

seg.0c2874233201.src: What is the right rava to water ratio for upma?
seg.0c2874233201.t: ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯆꯨꯅꯕ ꯆꯥꯡ ꯀꯔꯤꯅꯣ?
seg.0c2874233201.back: What is the right quantity of rava and water for upma?

seg.91a8fe1a38a5.src: For a soft Andhra-style upma, use 2½ cups water to 1 cup bombay rava. Use 2 cups for a firmer, more separate upma.
seg.91a8fe1a38a5.t: ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯤ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯕꯣꯝꯕꯦ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯀꯞ 1ꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯃꯔꯨ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯞ 2 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.91a8fe1a38a5.back: For a soft Andhra-style upma, use 2½ cups water for 1 cup Bombay rava. For a firmer upma with separate grains use 2 cups.

seg.bd11a83d27d8.src: The rava was not roasted, or too much water went in. Roast the rava till it smells toasty, and stay close to 2½ cups water per cup.
seg.bd11a83d27d8.t: ꯔꯋꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯈꯤꯗꯕꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯔꯋꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯞ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2½ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯂꯩꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bd11a83d27d8.back: Because the rava was not roasted, or too much water was added. Roast the rava until the roasted smell comes, and stay near 2½ cups water for each cup.

seg.247181e411d9.src: When should I add cashews to upma?
seg.247181e411d9.back: At what time should the cashews be added to the upma?

seg.83f262d9c56e.src: Fry them in the ghee first and lift them out, then stir them in at the end. Added early, they turn soft in the upma.
seg.83f262d9c56e.t: ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.83f262d9c56e.back: First fry them in ghee and take them out, then add at the end and stir. If added at the beginning, they become soft in the upma.

seg.6cb14eaca16a.back: జీడిపప్పు ఉప్మా · Recipe of Jeedipappu Upma | 1acrefarms

seg.8b57b24af158.back: జీడిపప్పు ఉప్మా. Andhra rava upma with Jeedipappu cashews fried golden colour in ghee, a soft and quick-to-make morning tiffin. Step-by-step way, tips and questions. For 3 people.

seg.661f01591624.src: Jeedipappu Upma: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.661f01591624.t: ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯎꯞꯃꯥ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.661f01591624.back: Jeedipappu Upma: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.992a8475993f.src: Kodi vepudu is the dry Andhra chicken fry: small pieces of chicken cooked in their own juices, then fried hard in oil with curry leaves, green chillies and a just-roasted masala until dark and sticky with spice. It is the starter at Andhra weddings and the side that sits next to rasam rice or pappu at home.
seg.992a8475993f.t: ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯅꯤ: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯇꯤꯛ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯜꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯂꯨꯍꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯔꯁꯝ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥꯅꯤ꯫
seg.992a8475993f.back: Kodi vepudu is Andhra's dry chicken fry: small pieces of chicken cooked in their own juice, then fried hard in oil with curry leaves, green chilli and just-now roasted masala until they darken and are coated in masala. It is the dish eaten first at Andhra weddings and the dish kept at home at the side of rasam rice or pappu.

seg.db90598234ea.src: Our Teja chilli powder gives it the deep red colour and the heat Andhra fries are known for, our turmeric powder goes into the marinade, and our whole cashew kernels, fried golden, go in at the end. Serves 4 as a side.
seg.db90598234ea.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ, ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ, ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.db90598234ea.back: Our Teja chilli powder gives it a thick red colour and the famous spiciness of Andhra fries, our turmeric powder goes into the marinade, and our whole cashews, fried golden colour, go in at the end. As a side dish, for 4 people.

seg.22b3994cc48a.src: Marinate chicken in Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger-garlic paste and lemon, cook it in its own juices, then fry it dry with curry leaves, green chillies, a roasted masala and cashews.
seg.22b3994cc48a.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ, ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.22b3994cc48a.back: Marinate the chicken in Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger-garlic paste and lemon, cook in its own juice, then fry dry with curry leaves, green chilli, roasted masala and cashews.

seg.4cb33a348eb8.src: 500 g boneless chicken ⟦1⟧cut into 1-inch pieces; or 600 g small bone-in pieces⟦/1⟧
seg.4cb33a348eb8.t: 500 g ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ⟦1⟧1-ꯏꯟꯆꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ; ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ 600 g⟦/1⟧
seg.4cb33a348eb8.back: 500 g boneless chicken ⟦1⟧cut in 1-inch pieces; or 600 g small bone-in pieces⟦/1⟧

seg.57789012bc80.src: 15 cashews ⟦1⟧whole cashew kernels; halve any large ones⟦/1⟧
seg.57789012bc80.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ 15 ⟦1⟧ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ; ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯈꯥꯌꯗꯣꯀꯎ⟦/1⟧
seg.57789012bc80.back: 15 cashews ⟦1⟧whole cashews; break the big ones into pieces⟦/1⟧

seg.8df3bc4567e3.src: Pat the chicken dry with a cloth so the marinade sticks.
seg.8df3bc4567e3.t: ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯞꯅꯕꯥ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯐꯤ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8df3bc4567e3.back: Wipe the chicken gently with a cloth and dry it so the marinade sticks.

seg.075327f4deca.src: Marinate the chicken in Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt, 30 minutes. Mix well with your hands so every piece is coated.
seg.075327f4deca.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ, ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ, ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 30 ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯞꯅꯕꯥ ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.075327f4deca.back: Marinate the chicken in Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt 30 minutes. Mix well with the hand so it coats each piece.

seg.63af904bba96.src: Meanwhile, dry-roast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, cloves and cinnamon in a small pan on low heat until fragrant and a shade darker, about 2 minutes. Cool and grind to a coarse powder. This is the fry masala.
seg.63af904bba96.t: ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ, ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯖꯤꯔꯥ, ꯁꯧꯐ, ꯂꯕꯉ꯭ꯒ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯂꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅꯤ꯫
seg.63af904bba96.back: Meanwhile, in a small pan on low flame roast without oil the coriander seed, cumin, fennel, cloves and cinnamon until the smell comes and they darken a little, about 2 minutes. Let cool and grind into a coarse powder. This is the fry masala.

seg.4406ac2e72fe.src: Put the chicken in a heavy kadai with no water, cover and set it on medium heat.
seg.4406ac2e72fe.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4406ac2e72fe.back: Put the chicken in a heavy kadai without water, cover and keep on medium flame.

seg.93ccca0c5178.src: Cook it covered in its own juices till no pink remains, about 12 minutes. Stir once or twice; the chicken releases water as it cooks.
seg.93ccca0c5178.t: ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 12 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯣꯀꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.93ccca0c5178.back: Cook covered in its own juice until not even one pink colour appears, about 12 minutes. Stir once or twice; while cooking the chicken lets out water.

seg.32f3a3f56679.src: Uncover and cook on high, stirring, until the liquid has almost dried up, 3–4 minutes. Tip the chicken out onto a plate and wipe the kadai.
seg.32f3a3f56679.t: ꯀꯨꯞꯄꯥ ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3–4꯫ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯨꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.32f3a3f56679.back: Open the lid and cook on high flame, stirring, until the water is almost dry, 3–4 minutes. Pour the chicken onto a plate and wipe the kadai.

seg.f3e846aa4edd.src: Heat the oil in the kadai on medium heat.
seg.f3e846aa4edd.t: ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f3e846aa4edd.back: Heat oil on medium flame in the kadai.

seg.e210c9534a07.src: Fry the cashews in oil till golden; lift out. They take under a minute, so stir them all the time and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
seg.e210c9534a07.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯜ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e210c9534a07.back: Fry the cashews in the oil until golden colour; take them out. They are done within one minute, so stir all the time and take them out with a spoon with holes.

seg.09e282d2e36f.src: Add the onion, if using, and fry until golden. Fry the green chillies and curry leaves. Stand back; the leaves crackle and spit.
seg.09e282d2e36f.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ, ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯂꯥꯞꯅꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯀꯏ꯫
seg.09e282d2e36f.back: Add the onion, if using, and fry until golden colour. Fry the green chillies and curry leaves. Stay far away; the leaves crackle and throw out oil.

seg.1fae224eb27a.src: Add the chicken and fry masala. Fry on high till dry and dark, then toss in the cashews. Keep tossing for 6–8 minutes, until the masala clings to the pieces and the edges turn dark and crisp.
seg.1fae224eb27a.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 6–8 ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1fae224eb27a.back: Add the chicken and the fry masala. Fry on high flame until dry and dark, then add the cashews and toss. Keep tossing 6–8 minutes until the masala sticks to the pieces and the edges darken and become crunchy.

seg.0b62f402945c.src: Taste, add salt if needed, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot.
seg.0b62f402945c.t: ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0b62f402945c.back: Taste, add salt if needed, sprinkle coriander leaves and serve hot.

seg.349c72ce839a.src: Fry it on high heat at the end so the masala clings to every piece.
seg.349c72ce839a.t: ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.349c72ce839a.back: At the end fry on high flame, so the masala will stick to every piece.

seg.d287ba2c2c11.src: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For medium heat use 1 tsp, or swap in Sannam chilli powder for the red colour with less fire.
seg.d287ba2c2c11.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ꯫ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫
seg.d287ba2c2c11.back: Teja chilli powder is very spicy. For medium spiciness use 1 teaspoon, or for red colour with less spiciness replace it with Sannam chilli powder.

seg.a0ef9b138cd4.src: Cut the pieces small and even so they cook through at the same time and crisp up well in the fry.
seg.a0ef9b138cd4.t: ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯒꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.a0ef9b138cd4.back: Cut the pieces small and equal, so they cook to the inside in the same time and become well crunchy in the fry.

seg.d72b3c1c529a.src: Grind the fry masala just before you cook; the roasted spice smell is the soul of a good vepudu.
seg.d72b3c1c529a.t: ꯊꯣꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯐꯕ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯊꯋꯥꯏꯅꯤ꯫
seg.d72b3c1c529a.back: Grind the fry masala only just before cooking; the smell of roasted masala is the soul of a good vepudu.

seg.62d6684e446e.src: Bone-in: use 600 g small bone-in pieces and cook them in their juices for 18–20 minutes, until no pink remains near the bone.
seg.62d6684e446e.t: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ 600 g ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 18–20 ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.62d6684e446e.back: Bone-in: use 600 g small bone-in pieces and cook in their juice 18–20 minutes until not even one pink colour appears near the bone.

seg.6960fe7f3ff8.src: Kobbari vepudu: add 3 tbsp grated dry coconut to the fry with the masala and toss until it browns.
seg.6960fe7f3ff8.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ: ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6960fe7f3ff8.back: Coconut vepudu: add 3 tablespoons grated dry coconut to the fry together with the masala and toss until brown.

seg.afd92118eb80.src: Mutton vepudu: pressure-cook 500 g boneless mutton with the marinade and ½ cup water for 5–6 whistles, then fry it the same way.
seg.afd92118eb80.t: ꯃꯇꯟ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ 500 g ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ½ꯒꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 5–6 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.afd92118eb80.back: Mutton vepudu: cook 500 g boneless goat meat in the pressure cooker with the marinade masala and ½ cup water until 5–6 whistles, then fry in the same way.

seg.2c4ab1a1a5de.src: Serve hot as a side with rasam rice, pappu and rice or sambar rice, or on its own as a starter with sliced onion and lemon wedges.
seg.2c4ab1a1a5de.t: ꯔꯁꯝ ꯆꯥꯛ, ꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯝꯕꯔ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ꯫
seg.2c4ab1a1a5de.back: Serve hot at the side of rasam rice, pappu and rice or sambar rice, or as a first-eaten dish with cut onion and lemon pieces.

seg.b7598301bd86.src: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan with a few drops of oil until steaming hot all the way through; it crisps up again.
seg.b7598301bd86.t: ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯤ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.b7598301bd86.back: Cover and keep in the fridge up to 2 days. Heat again in a hot pan with a little oil until steam comes out right to the inside; it becomes crunchy again.

seg.551573b4b443.src: What is the difference between chicken fry and chicken curry in Andhra?
seg.551573b4b443.t: ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯈꯦꯟꯅꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.551573b4b443.back: In Andhra, what is the difference between chicken fry and chicken curry?

seg.dbeff7335e31.src: Vepudu is dry: the chicken is cooked in its own juices, then fried until the masala coats it with no gravy. Kodi kura is a curry with an onion-tomato gravy for rice.
seg.dbeff7335e31.t: ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯡꯕꯅꯤ: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯏ꯫ ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯀꯨꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ-ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.dbeff7335e31.back: Vepudu is dry: the chicken is cooked in its own juice, then fried without gravy until coated with masala. Kodi kura is a curry with onion-tomato gravy for rice.

seg.439aacfe8e34.src: Should I use boneless or bone-in chicken for vepudu?
seg.439aacfe8e34.t: ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗ꯭ꯔꯥ?
seg.439aacfe8e34.back: Should boneless or bone-in chicken be used for vepudu?

seg.982f470b118d.src: Both work. Boneless cooks faster and crisps more; small bone-in pieces have more flavour but need about 8 minutes longer in their juices.
seg.982f470b118d.t: ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏ; ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 8 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ꯫
seg.982f470b118d.back: Both work. Boneless cooks quickly and becomes more crunchy; small bone-in pieces have more taste but need about 8 minutes more in their juice.

seg.ade697e78f9b.src: Cut open the thickest piece. The chicken is cooked when no pink remains in the middle (or near the bone) and the juices run clear.
seg.ade697e78f9b.t: ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ (ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ) ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯑꯁꯦꯡꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.ade697e78f9b.back: Cut the biggest piece and check. The chicken is done when not even one pink colour appears in the middle (or near the bone) and the juice comes out clear.

seg.eddd3046275b.src: How do I make kodi vepudu less spicy?
seg.eddd3046275b.back: How to reduce the spiciness of kodi vepudu?

seg.9b5459aec9d6.src: Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder, or swap in Sannam chilli powder, and slit only 2 green chillies. The cashews and curry leaves keep the flavour full.
seg.9b5459aec9d6.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯀꯎ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ 2 ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯀꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.9b5459aec9d6.back: Use 1 teaspoon Teja chilli powder, or replace it with Sannam chilli powder, and cut only 2 green chillies. The cashews and curry leaves keep the taste complete.

seg.a00af5cf9954.src: కోడి వేపుడు · Kodi Vepudu (Andhra Chicken Fry) | 1acrefarms
seg.a00af5cf9954.t: కోడి వేపుడు · ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ (ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ) | 1acrefarms
seg.a00af5cf9954.back: కోడి వేపుడు · Kodi Vepudu (Andhra's chicken fry) | 1acrefarms

seg.1af4fbb646e3.src: కోడి వేపుడు. Andhra chicken fry: chicken in Teja chilli powder and turmeric powder, fried dry with curry leaves, green chillies, a roasted masala and our cashews.
seg.1af4fbb646e3.t: కోడి వేపుడు. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥ, ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ, ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕ꯫
seg.1af4fbb646e3.back: కోడి వేపుడు. Andhra's chicken fry: chicken marinated in Teja chilli powder and turmeric powder, fried dry with curry leaves, green chilli, roasted masala and our cashews.

seg.917dba1166ab.src: Kodi Vepudu: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.917dba1166ab.t: ꯀꯣꯗꯤ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.917dba1166ab.back: Kodi Vepudu: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.f9771e2222df.src: Nimmakaya pulihora is the bright yellow lemon rice of Andhra homes: cooked rice tossed with a crackling tempering of peanuts, chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds, green chillies and curry leaves, then soured with lemon juice. It is the rice packed for train journeys, school tiffin boxes and temple days, and it is made in big batches for festivals and pujas.
seg.f9771e2222df.t: ꯅꯤꯝꯃꯀꯥꯌ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯤ: ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯍꯟꯕ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯔꯦꯜ ꯆꯠꯄꯥ, ꯁ꯭ꯀꯨꯂꯒꯤ ꯇꯤꯐꯤꯟ ꯕꯣꯛꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯨꯝꯃꯩ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.f9771e2222df.back: Nimmakaya pulihora is the bright yellow lemon rice of Andhra houses: cooked rice mixed with a crackling tempering of groundnut, chana dal, urad dal, mustard seed, green chilli and curry leaves, then made sour with lemon juice. It is the rice packed for train journeys, school tiffin boxes and temple days, and it is made a lot for festivals and pujas.

seg.ac569e0882d5.src: Our turmeric powder goes into the hot oil for a few seconds, which turns every grain an even golden yellow and takes away its raw edge. This recipe serves 4.
seg.ac569e0882d5.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯪꯏ, ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯀꯏ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.ac569e0882d5.back: Our turmeric powder goes into the hot oil for a few seconds, which makes every grain an even golden-yellow colour and removes its uncooked taste. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.d194bee0cc5e.src: Total includes cooking the rice and a 15-minute rest so the flavours settle.
seg.d194bee0cc5e.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯊꯝꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.d194bee0cc5e.back: Cooking the rice and keeping it 15 minutes for the tastes to blend are included in the total.

seg.1cfa4342f462.src: Fry peanuts, dals, mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric powder and hing, then toss with cooled rice, salt and lemon juice.
seg.1cfa4342f462.t: ꯄꯤꯅꯠ, ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ, ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1cfa4342f462.back: Fry groundnut, dal, mustard seed, chilli and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric powder and hing, then mix with cooled rice, salt and lemon juice.

seg.2561142fed2c.src: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masoori, about 200 g; gives about 3 cups cooked⟦/1⟧
seg.2561142fed2c.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯆꯦꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯁꯣꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯨꯔꯤ, 200 g ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞ 3 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯏ⟦/1⟧
seg.2561142fed2c.back: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masuri, about 200 g; after cooking it gives about 3 cups⟦/1⟧

seg.06ba75699134.src: 3 cups cooked rice ⟦1⟧cooked a little firm, grains separate⟦/1⟧
seg.06ba75699134.t: ꯀꯞ 3 ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ⟦1⟧ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ, ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.06ba75699134.back: 3 cups cooked rice ⟦1⟧cooked a little firm, grains separate⟦/1⟧

seg.fbba93c11bc9.src: 3 tbsp lemon juice ⟦1⟧from about 2 lemons; add more to taste⟦/1⟧
seg.fbba93c11bc9.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ 2 ꯔꯣꯃꯗꯒꯤ; ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.fbba93c11bc9.back: 3 tablespoons lemon juice ⟦1⟧from about 2 lemons; add more by tasting⟦/1⟧

seg.e254f20f8f14.src: 3 tbsp oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is the usual choice⟦/1⟧
seg.e254f20f8f14.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠꯀꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ⟦/1⟧
seg.e254f20f8f14.back: 3 tablespoons oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is used all the time⟦/1⟧

seg.ad3af06df4e4.t: ꯀꯞ ¼ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ⟦1⟧ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯗ꯭ꯔꯕ, ꯃꯀꯨꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.ad3af06df4e4.back: ¼ cup groundnuts ⟦1⟧not roasted, with skin⟦/1⟧

seg.bc63d9715c03.src: Wash the rice and cook it with 2 cups of water until just done, so the grains stay separate. You need about 3 cups of cooked rice.
seg.bc63d9715c03.t: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2ꯒꯥ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛ ꯆꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯤ꯫ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯀꯞ 3 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ꯫
seg.bc63d9715c03.back: Wash the rice and cook with 2 cups water only until just done, so the grains stay separate. About 3 cups of cooked rice is needed.

seg.adb2b75edafc.src: Spread the cooked rice on a plate to cool; add the salt. Fluff it with a fork and let it sit about 10 minutes until warm, not hot, so the grains do not break when mixed.
seg.adb2b75edafc.t: ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ; ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯐꯣꯔꯀꯅꯥ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯣꯏ꯫
seg.adb2b75edafc.back: Spread the cooked rice on a plate to cool; add salt. Loosen it with a fork and keep it about 10 minutes until a little warm, not too hot, so the grains do not break when mixing.

seg.e05322a3ed24.src: Heat the oil; fry the peanuts, dals, mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves. Start with the peanuts on medium heat and fry them about 2 minutes until they crackle and the skins darken.
seg.e05322a3ed24.t: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯄꯤꯅꯠ, ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯀꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e05322a3ed24.back: Heat the oil; fry the groundnut, dal, mustard seed, chilli and curry leaves. Start with the groundnuts on medium flame and fry about 2 minutes until they crackle and the skins darken.

seg.542a4fea7b18.src: Add the chana dal and urad dal and fry until light golden, about 1 minute.
seg.542a4fea7b18.t: ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫
seg.542a4fea7b18.back: Add chana dal and urad dal and fry until a little golden colour, about 1 minute.

seg.502483d7a042.src: Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add the dry red chillies, green chillies, ginger and curry leaves and fry a few seconds until the leaves turn crisp.
seg.502483d7a042.t: ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ, ꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.502483d7a042.back: Add mustard seed and let it crackle, then add dry red chilli, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves and fry a few seconds until the leaves become crunchy.

seg.6e856356980b.src: Stir in the turmeric powder and hing; switch off. Stir for 5–10 seconds only so the turmeric cooks in the hot oil without burning.
seg.6e856356980b.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯀꯇꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 5–10 ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6e856356980b.back: Add turmeric powder and hing and stir; turn off the flame. Stir only 5–10 seconds so the turmeric cooks in the hot oil without burning.

seg.dd6ccaf923d8.src: Pour over the rice, add the lemon juice and mix gently. Use your fingers or a flat spatula and lift the rice from below so every grain turns yellow without turning mushy.
seg.dd6ccaf923d8.t: ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯁ꯭ꯄꯦꯆꯨꯂꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.dd6ccaf923d8.back: Pour it over the rice, add the lemon juice and mix gently. Using the fingers or a flat spatula, lift the rice from the bottom, so every grain becomes yellow without becoming mushy.

seg.1bfc2c04d40e.src: Taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed. The rice should taste clearly sour and salty, as the flavour softens on standing.
seg.1bfc2c04d40e.t: ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯃꯌꯦꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.1bfc2c04d40e.back: Taste and if needed add more salt or lemon juice. The rice should be clearly sour and salty, because after keeping the taste reduces.

seg.8cea6688d0fb.src: Cover and rest the pulihora for 15 minutes before serving so the rice takes in the lemon and tempering.
seg.8cea6688d0fb.t: ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯧꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.8cea6688d0fb.back: Before serving keep the pulihora covered 15 minutes, so the rice takes the taste of the lemon and tempering.

seg.c1a7043ce357.src: Add the lemon juice off the heat so it stays sharp. Cooked lemon juice turns bitter.
seg.c1a7043ce357.t: ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯤ꯫ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯈꯥꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.c1a7043ce357.back: Add the lemon juice after taking it off the flame, then the taste stays strong. Cooked lemon juice becomes bitter.

seg.b634a4257b6c.src: Cook the rice slightly firm and let it cool before mixing; hot, soft rice turns pasty.
seg.b634a4257b6c.t: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯁꯥꯕ, ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.b634a4257b6c.back: Cook the rice a little firm and cool it before mixing; hot, soft rice becomes like paste.

seg.a1d93274ea3f.src: Keep the turmeric powder in the oil for just a few seconds; burnt turmeric gives a dark colour and a bitter taste.
seg.a1d93274ea3f.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯆꯥꯀꯈꯔꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯥꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.a1d93274ea3f.back: Keep the turmeric powder in the oil only a few seconds; burnt turmeric gives a dark colour and bitter taste.

seg.747474140bbf.src: Leftover rice from the morning works well, as the grains are already firm and separate.
seg.747474140bbf.t: ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯦ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯦ꯫
seg.747474140bbf.back: Leftover rice from the morning works well, because the grains are already firm and separate.

seg.7a379d805448.src: Cashews: fry 10 cashew halves with the peanuts for a festive pulihora.
seg.7a379d805448.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ: ꯀꯨꯝꯃꯩꯒꯤ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯤꯅꯠꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯤ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ 10 ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7a379d805448.back: Cashew: for festival pulihora, fry 10 cashew halves/pieces together with the peanuts.

seg.be93899ec308.src: Mamidikaya pulihora: in place of lemon juice, mix in 1 cup grated raw mango with the tempering.
seg.be93899ec308.t: ꯃꯥꯃꯤꯗꯤꯀꯥꯌ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ: ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ, ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯗꯕ ꯍꯩꯅꯧ ꯀꯞ 1 ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.be93899ec308.back: Mamidikaya pulihora: in place of lemon juice, mix 1 cup grated unripe mango together with the tempering.

seg.867dba923c04.src: Grated coconut: add 2 tbsp grated coconut along with the lemon juice for a milder rice.
seg.867dba923c04.t: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.867dba923c04.back: Grated coconut: for a milder rice add 2 tablespoons grated coconut together with the lemon juice.

seg.88b87529b506.src: Serve at room temperature with curd, a pickle or appadams. It is a classic tiffin-box and travel rice.
seg.88b87529b506.t: ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ, ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯞꯄꯗꯃꯒꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯇꯤꯐꯤꯟ ꯕꯣꯛꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯠꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.88b87529b506.back: Serve at home room temperature with curd, pickle or appadam. It is the famous rice of the tiffin box and journeys.

seg.9791f1c7a8e4.src: It keeps well at room temperature for about 6 hours, which is why it travels. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within a day.
seg.9791f1c7a8e4.t: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯡ 6 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯠꯄꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯊꯣꯀꯏ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9791f1c7a8e4.back: It stays well about 6 hours at home room temperature, that is why it is taken on journeys. Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge and eat within one day.

seg.c12ab7274709.src: Why does my lemon rice taste bitter?
seg.c12ab7274709.back: Why is my lemon rice bitter?

seg.44b56d19b9fb.src: Either the lemon juice was cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Switch off the stove before the turmeric goes in, and add the lemon juice only to the rice, off the heat.
seg.44b56d19b9fb.t: ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯀꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.44b56d19b9fb.back: Because the lemon juice was cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Turn off the flame before adding turmeric, and add the lemon juice only to the rice after taking it off the flame.

seg.69e4bfb93ba8.src: What is the difference between pulihora and lemon rice?
seg.69e4bfb93ba8.t: ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯈꯦꯟꯅꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.69e4bfb93ba8.back: What is the difference between pulihora and lemon rice?

seg.f2f993f1b94b.src: Pulihora is the Telugu name for soured rice. Chintapandu pulihora is soured with tamarind paste; nimmakaya pulihora is the lemon version, quicker to make and lighter in colour.
seg.f2f993f1b94b.t: ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯃꯃꯤꯡꯅꯤ꯫ ꯆꯤꯟꯇꯥꯄꯟꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯍꯜꯂꯤ; ꯅꯤꯝꯃꯀꯥꯌ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯅꯤ, ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯪꯏ꯫
seg.f2f993f1b94b.back: Pulihora is the Telugu name of soured rice. Chintapandu pulihora is soured with tamarind paste; nimmakaya pulihora is the lemon way, quick to make and its colour is more [ꯁꯪꯏ: reads 'green', meant pale/light].

seg.1ab5dcf1d80a.src: How do I stop lemon rice from getting mushy?
seg.1ab5dcf1d80a.back: How to keep lemon rice from becoming mushy?

seg.8a0fad2d4bfd.src: Cook the rice a little firm with less water, cool it on a plate, and mix gently by lifting from below instead of pressing.
seg.8a0fad2d4bfd.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8a0fad2d4bfd.back: Cook the rice a little firm with less water, cool it on a plate, and instead of pressing, mix gently by lifting from the bottom.

seg.dd00224f5f94.src: How much lemon juice for 3 cups of rice?
seg.dd00224f5f94.t: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯀꯞ 3ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.dd00224f5f94.back: How much lemon juice is needed for 3 cups rice?

seg.50f8efabb87e.src: About 3 tbsp, the juice of 2 medium lemons. Add it slowly and taste, because lemons vary in sourness.
seg.50f8efabb87e.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ 2ꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ꯫ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯩ꯫
seg.50f8efabb87e.back: About 3 tablespoons, the juice of 2 medium lemons. Add slowly and taste, because the sourness of lemons differs.

seg.0251508f9c8b.back: నిమ్మకాయ పులిహోర · Recipe of lemon rice | 1acrefarms

seg.2d3c4d5f7608.src: నిమ్మకాయ పులిహోర. Andhra lemon rice: cooled rice tossed with a peanut and dal tempering, our turmeric powder and lemon juice. Step-by-step method, tips and FAQs.
seg.2d3c4d5f7608.t: నిమ్మకాయ పులిహోర. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ: ꯏꯪꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ, ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ꯫ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ, ꯇꯤꯞꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯁꯤꯡ꯫
seg.2d3c4d5f7608.back: నిమ్మకాయ పులిహోర. Andhra's lemon rice: cooled rice mixed with a tempering of groundnut and dal, our turmeric powder and lemon juice. Step-by-step way, tips and questions.

seg.5f0282fcd0a8.src: Nimmakaya Pulihora: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.5f0282fcd0a8.t: ꯅꯤꯝꯃꯀꯥꯌ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.5f0282fcd0a8.back: Nimmakaya Pulihora: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.8922ef1e3767.src: Pasupu annam is plain rice turned bright yellow with turmeric and tossed in a crackling tempering of mustard seeds, chana dal, curry leaves and green chillies, with fried cashews on top. Andhra homes make it for lunch boxes, for quick weekday meals and as a prasadam on puja days, often with the morning's leftover rice.
seg.8922ef1e3767.t: ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯑꯟꯅꯝ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯟ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯤ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯇꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ, ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯂꯟꯆ ꯕꯣꯛꯁ, ꯊꯕꯛꯀꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯀꯤ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯖꯥꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯁꯥꯗꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ꯫
seg.8922ef1e3767.back: Pasupu annam is plain rice made bright yellow with turmeric, mixed with a crackling tempering of mustard seed, chana dal, curry leaves and green chilli, together with fried cashews on top. Andhra houses make it for the lunch box, the quickly made meal of a workday, and as prasadam on puja day, often with leftover rice from the morning.

seg.510252086556.src: Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) gives the rice its deep yellow colour and an earthy turmeric smell, so half a teaspoon is enough for 4. Whole cashews (Jeedipappu) fried in the same oil add the crunch.
seg.510252086556.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ (ꯀꯣꯟꯗꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ) ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯄꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯅꯥ (ꯖꯤꯗꯤꯄꯞꯄꯨ) ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.510252086556.back: Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) gives the rice a deep yellow colour and an earthy turmeric smell, so for 4 people only half a teaspoon is needed. Whole cashews (Jeedipappu) fried in that same oil give a crunch.

seg.38badedc8d11.src: Total includes about 15 minutes for the cooked rice to cool.
seg.38badedc8d11.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.38badedc8d11.back: About 15 minutes to cool the cooked rice is included in the total.

seg.8ad70ebff643.src: Cook rice and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seeds, chana dal, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add hill turmeric powder and toss in the rice.
seg.8ad70ebff643.t: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8ad70ebff643.back: Cook the rice and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seed, chana dal, chilli and curry leaves in oil, add hill turmeric powder and mix with the rice.

seg.bc286f12f1ba.src: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masoori, about 200 g; makes about 3 cups cooked⟦/1⟧
seg.bc286f12f1ba.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯆꯦꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯁꯣꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯨꯔꯤ, 200 g ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞ 3 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯏ⟦/1⟧
seg.bc286f12f1ba.back: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masuri, about 200 g; after cooking it gives about 3 cups⟦/1⟧

seg.06cd9d581aec.src: ½ tsp hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧Konda Pasupu⟦/1⟧
seg.06cd9d581aec.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯣꯟꯗꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.06cd9d581aec.back: ½ teaspoon hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧konda pasupu⟦/1⟧

seg.399f19de4e13.src: 1 tbsp ghee (optional) ⟦1⟧stirred in at the end⟦/1⟧
seg.399f19de4e13.back: 1 tablespoon ghee (if you like) ⟦1⟧added at the end and stirred⟦/1⟧

seg.afe3b0737680.back: Also goes very well with ⟦1⟧turmeric powder⟦/1⟧.

seg.53fcfe53b909.src: Wash the rice in 2–3 changes of water and drain it.
seg.53fcfe53b909.t: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ 2–3 ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.53fcfe53b909.back: Wash the rice changing the water 2–3 times and drain the water.

seg.cdcf37be99e8.src: Cook the rice so the grains stay separate, then spread it on a plate to cool. Use 2 cups water to 1 cup rice in a pot or pressure cooker (2 whistles), and fluff it with a fork before spreading it out.
seg.cdcf37be99e8.t: ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯡ ꯀꯞ 1ꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ (ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 2), ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯛꯠꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯐꯣꯔꯀꯅꯥ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.cdcf37be99e8.back: Cook the rice so the grains stay separate, then spread it on a plate to cool. In a pot or pressure cooker use 2 cups water for 1 cup rice (2 whistles), and loosen with a fork before spreading.

seg.296995189451.src: Let the rice cool for about 15 minutes until it is just warm. Sprinkle the salt over it.
seg.296995189451.t: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.296995189451.back: Cool the rice about 15 minutes until it is only a little warm. Sprinkle salt on top.

seg.48839bd22983.src: Heat the oil in a wide kadai on medium heat.
seg.48839bd22983.t: ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.48839bd22983.back: Heat oil on medium flame in a wide kadai.

seg.bdc1a0df8ffc.src: Fry the cashews in the oil till golden; lift out. Add mustard seeds and chana dal. Keep the cashews on a plate; they turn golden in about 1 minute.
seg.bdc1a0df8ffc.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯔꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.bdc1a0df8ffc.back: Fry the cashews in the oil until golden colour; take them out. Add mustard seed and chana dal. Keep the cashews on a plate; they become golden colour in about 1 minute.

seg.0729c6efc94a.src: Once the mustard seeds splutter, add the urad dal and the dried red chillies and stir.
seg.0729c6efc94a.t: ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ, ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0729c6efc94a.back: When the mustard seed crackles, add urad dal and dry red chilli and stir.

seg.2688182af66a.src: When the dal turns golden, add the chillies and curry leaves, then the turmeric on low heat. Add the ginger and asafoetida with the curry leaves, and stir the turmeric for only 5–10 seconds.
seg.2688182af66a.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ꯫ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ 5–10 ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2688182af66a.back: When the dal becomes golden colour, add chilli and curry leaves, then the turmeric on low flame. Add ginger and hing together with the curry leaves, and stir the turmeric only 5–10 seconds.

seg.59fd9b87153d.src: Switch off the heat straight away so the turmeric does not burn.
seg.59fd9b87153d.back: Turn off the flame at once so the turmeric does not burn.

seg.15dc85e42ca1.src: Tip in the rice, cashews and salt and toss gently till evenly yellow. Use a flat spatula and lift and fold rather than pressing down, so the grains stay whole.
seg.15dc85e42ca1.t: ꯆꯥꯛ, ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯁ꯭ꯄꯦꯆꯨꯂꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.15dc85e42ca1.back: Add the rice, cashews and salt and mix gently until evenly yellow. Using a flat spatula, lift and turn instead of pressing, so the grains stay whole.

seg.b005e5771235.src: Taste for salt, stir in the ghee if using, cover and leave for 5 minutes before serving so the rice takes on the tempering.
seg.b005e5771235.t: ꯊꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯧꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.b005e5771235.back: Taste the salt, add ghee if using and stir, cover and keep 5 minutes before serving, so the rice takes the taste of the tempering.

seg.9bce1ed4dbee.src: Spread the rice to cool first so the grains do not break.
seg.9bce1ed4dbee.t: ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫
seg.9bce1ed4dbee.back: First spread the rice to cool so the grains do not break.

seg.1f9a348f8750.src: Add the turmeric on low heat and stir for only a few seconds; burnt turmeric turns the rice bitter.
seg.1f9a348f8750.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯆꯥꯀꯈꯔꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯈꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.1f9a348f8750.back: Add the turmeric on low flame and stir only a few seconds; burnt turmeric makes the rice bitter.

seg.394d01a50207.src: Hill turmeric powder colours strongly; start with ½ tsp for 1 cup of rice and add a pinch more only if you want a deeper yellow.
seg.394d01a50207.t: ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯄꯤ; ꯆꯦꯡ ꯀꯞ 1ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.394d01a50207.back: Hill turmeric powder gives a thick colour; start with ½ teaspoon for 1 cup rice and add a little more only if you want a thicker yellow.

seg.505872469eb9.src: Leftover rice from the morning works well, as long as the grains are separate.
seg.505872469eb9.t: ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ, ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯗꯤ꯫
seg.505872469eb9.back: Leftover rice from the morning works well, if the grains are separate.

seg.ab1b24f9cf3d.src: Turmeric powder: our everyday Pasupu turmeric powder works the same way; use the same ½ tsp.
seg.ab1b24f9cf3d.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯁꯨ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ; ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ab1b24f9cf3d.back: Turmeric powder: our everyday pasupu turmeric powder also works the same way; use the same ½ teaspoon.

seg.302f50dc74c9.src: Peanuts: fry 2 tbsp raw peanuts in the oil before the cashews for extra crunch.
seg.302f50dc74c9.t: ꯄꯤꯅꯠ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯅꯕꯥ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯗ꯭ꯔꯕ ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.302f50dc74c9.back: Groundnut: for more crunch fry 2 tablespoons unroasted groundnuts in the oil before the cashews.

seg.551f49339b3d.src: Lemon: squeeze in the juice of half a lemon with the rice for a tangy, pulihora-style rice.
seg.551f49339b3d.t: ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ: ꯁꯨꯔꯕ, ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ½ ꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.551f49339b3d.back: Lemon [champra]: For a sour [or: lighter/milder?], pulihora-like rice, squeeze out the juice of ½ lemon and add it to that rice.

seg.6b9e9c07efba.src: Coconut: toss in 2 tbsp grated coconut along with the rice.
seg.6b9e9c07efba.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ: ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6b9e9c07efba.back: Coconut: add 2 tablespoons grated coconut together with the rice and mix.

seg.d541a1d237fc.src: Serve warm or at room temperature with curd, appadalu or a dry potato fry. It also packs well for lunch boxes and travel.
seg.d541a1d237fc.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ, ꯑꯞꯄꯗꯥꯂꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯂꯨ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯒꯥ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯂꯟꯆ ꯕꯣꯛꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯁꯨ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.d541a1d237fc.back: Serve hot or at home room temperature with curd, appadalu or dry potato fry. It can also be packed well for the lunch box and journeys.

seg.db97e1ae49fa.src: Best eaten the same day. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and warm them with a sprinkle of water.
seg.db97e1ae49fa.t: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯩ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.db97e1ae49fa.back: It is best eaten the same day. Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge up to 1 day and heat after sprinkling a little water.

seg.54acb7b11b4c.src: How do you make pasupu annam?

seg.d99d12f26e71.src: Cook rice so the grains stay separate and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seeds, chana dal, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric on low heat for a few seconds, then toss in the rice with salt.
seg.d99d12f26e71.t: ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ, ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d99d12f26e71.back: Cook rice so the grains stay separate and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seed, chana dal, chilli and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric on low flame for a few seconds, then add the rice with salt and mix.

seg.a4a87b4f7d63.src: How much turmeric powder goes into turmeric rice?
seg.a4a87b4f7d63.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯀꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.a4a87b4f7d63.back: How much turmeric powder should be added to turmeric rice?

seg.aa37527cdcfb.src: About ½ tsp for 1 cup of raw rice (about 3 cups cooked). Hill turmeric powder colours strongly, so start with less and add a pinch more if needed.
seg.aa37527cdcfb.t: ꯆꯦꯡ ꯀꯞ 1ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ (ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞ 3 ꯔꯣꯝ) ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯄꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.aa37527cdcfb.back: About ½ teaspoon for 1 cup rice (about 3 cups after cooking). Hill turmeric powder gives a thick colour, so start with less and add a little more if needed.

seg.3d200fb0e6fc.src: Why is my turmeric rice bitter?
seg.3d200fb0e6fc.back: Why is my turmeric rice bitter?

seg.2c9da3559a42.src: The turmeric burnt in the hot oil, or too much went in. Add it on low heat, stir for only a few seconds and switch off before tipping in the rice.
seg.2c9da3559a42.t: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯀꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2c9da3559a42.back: Because the turmeric burnt in hot oil, or too much was added. Add it on low flame, stir only a few seconds and turn off the flame before adding the rice.

seg.36ca370ac0d9.src: Can I make pasupu annam with leftover rice?
seg.36ca370ac0d9.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯑꯟꯅꯝ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.36ca370ac0d9.back: Can pasupu annam be made with leftover rice?

seg.71df75edcd26.src: Yes. Leftover rice with separate grains works well. Break up any lumps with your fingers before tossing it in the tempering.
seg.71df75edcd26.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ꯫ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.71df75edcd26.back: Yes. Leftover rice with separate grains works well. Before mixing into the tempering, break the lumps with the fingers.

seg.42238d687a8f.back: పసుపు అన్నం · Recipe of Pasupu Annam | 1acrefarms

seg.720281a9dc26.src: పసుపు అన్నం. Pasupu annam, Andhra turmeric rice: cooked rice tossed in a mustard, chana dal and curry leaf tempering with hill turmeric powder and fried cashews. Serves 4.
seg.720281a9dc26.t: పసుపు అన్నం. ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯑꯟꯅꯝ, ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯆꯥꯛ: ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ, ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ꯫ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.720281a9dc26.back: పసుపు అన్నం. Pasupu annam, Andhra's turmeric rice: cooked rice mixed with a tempering of mustard seed, chana dal and curry leaves, hill turmeric powder and fried cashews. For 4 people.

seg.a5bf108c0e27.src: Pasupu Annam: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.a5bf108c0e27.t: ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯑꯟꯅꯝ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.a5bf108c0e27.back: Pasupu Annam: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.ed1a4a430aee.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ

seg.cc1333072822.src: Ragi java is a pourable porridge of ragi flour cooked in water, a daily drink in many Andhra and Rayalaseema homes. The salted version is made with buttermilk; this sweet one is loosened with milk and sweetened with jaggery, and it is drunk warm from a steel tumbler at breakfast or in the evening.
seg.cc1333072822.t: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯅꯤ, ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯥꯌꯂꯁꯤꯃꯥꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯊꯛꯄꯅꯤ꯫ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯕꯇꯔꯃꯤꯜꯛꯀꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ; ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯋꯥꯏꯔꯃꯗꯥ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯜꯒꯤ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯛꯏ꯫
seg.cc1333072822.back: Ragi java is a pourable porridge of ragi powder cooked in water, the everyday drink in many houses of Andhra and Rayalaseema. The salty form is made with buttermilk; this sweet form is thinned with milk and sweetened with jaggery, and drunk hot from a steel tumbler at the morning meal or in the evening.

seg.b29ec96bcd5c.src: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery suits the earthy taste of ragi and gives the java a toffee-brown colour. It takes about 15 minutes from start to finish. This recipe serves 2.
seg.b29ec96bcd5c.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯔꯥꯒꯤꯒꯤ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯥ ꯆꯨꯅꯩ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯥꯋꯥꯗꯥ ꯇꯣꯐꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯍꯧꯔꯀꯄꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 2ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.b29ec96bcd5c.back: Our tati bellam palm jaggery matches ragi's earth-like taste and gives the java a toffee-like brown colour. From start to finish it takes about 15 minutes. This recipe is for 2 people.

seg.f65620e4f5c4.src: Total includes the 2-minute rest before the jaggery goes in.
seg.f65620e4f5c4.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯊꯝꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.f65620e4f5c4.back: Keeping 2 minutes before adding jaggery is included in the total.

seg.f0a8282433d4.src: Whisk ragi flour into water, cook it in boiling water till thick and glossy, then add milk. Off the heat, stir in palm jaggery and cardamom.
seg.f0a8282433d4.t: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f0a8282433d4.back: Mix the ragi powder in water by whisking, cook in boiling water until thick and shiny, then add milk. After taking off the flame add palm jaggery and cardamom and stir.

seg.41bd564147d7.src: ¼ cup ragi flour ⟦1⟧finger millet flour, about 35 g⟦/1⟧
seg.41bd564147d7.t: ꯀꯞ ¼ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯐꯤꯉ꯭ꯒꯔ ꯃꯤꯂꯦꯠꯀꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, 35 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.41bd564147d7.back: ¼ cup ragi powder ⟦1⟧finger millet powder, about 35 g⟦/1⟧

seg.d9504b3b8592.src: 2 cups water ⟦1⟧1 cup to mix the flour, 1 cup to boil⟦/1⟧
seg.d9504b3b8592.t: ꯀꯞ 2 ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯀꯞ 1, ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯀꯞ 1⟦/1⟧
seg.d9504b3b8592.back: 2 cups water ⟦1⟧1 cup to mix the powder, 1 cup to boil⟦/1⟧

seg.0570314748ee.src: 3 tbsp grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 30 g; add a spoon more if you like it sweeter⟦/1⟧
seg.0570314748ee.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧30 g ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.0570314748ee.back: 3 tablespoons grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 30 g; if you like it sweeter add one more spoon⟦/1⟧

seg.2b7de8d37fd0.src: Put the ragi flour in a bowl.
seg.2b7de8d37fd0.back: Put the ragi powder in a bowl.

seg.fce6db4082ef.src: Whisk the ragi flour into 1 cup water till smooth, with no lumps. Use a whisk or a fork and break up any lumps against the side of the bowl.
seg.fce6db4082ef.t: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 1ꯗꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯂꯩꯇꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯨꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯨꯏꯁ꯭ꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯐꯣꯔꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯕꯣꯂꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯅꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fce6db4082ef.back: Mix the ragi powder in 1 cup water by whisking until soft without lumps. Using a whisk or fork, if there are lumps press them against the side of the bowl and break them.

seg.ac6b0e0e7003.src: Pour the remaining 1 cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan and set it on medium heat.
seg.ac6b0e0e7003.t: ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 1 ꯃꯈꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ac6b0e0e7003.back: Put the remaining 1 cup water in a heavy-bottomed pan and keep on medium flame.

seg.ec55acf2b96a.src: Boil the other cup of water, pour in the ragi and stir on low heat till thick and glossy, 6–8 minutes. Stir the mix once more before pouring, as the flour settles at the bottom of the bowl.
seg.ec55acf2b96a.t: ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯀꯞ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 6–8꯫ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯠꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯕꯣꯂꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯡꯏ꯫
seg.ec55acf2b96a.back: Boil the other cup of water, pour in the ragi and stir on low flame until thick and shiny, 6–8 minutes. Stir the mixture once more while pouring, because the powder settles at the bottom of the bowl.

seg.d0f8efa78d43.src: Keep stirring all the time. The java is cooked when it turns from dull pinkish-brown to a darker, glossy brown and coats the back of the spoon.
seg.d0f8efa78d43.t: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯌꯨ꯫ ꯖꯥꯋꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ-ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ, ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
