seg.d0f8efa78d43.back: Keep stirring all the time. The java is done when it turns from a dull pinkish-brown colour to a darker, shiny brown and coats the back of the spoon.

seg.e7ef07a808c5.src: Add the milk and simmer 2 minutes. Switch off and rest 2 minutes. Stir once or twice while it simmers so it does not catch.
seg.e7ef07a808c5.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯊꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e7ef07a808c5.back: Add the milk and boil on low flame 2 minutes. Turn off the flame and keep 2 minutes. While boiling stir once or twice so it does not stick at the bottom.

seg.8f86db3a6d08.src: Grate the palm jaggery finely while the java rests, so it melts quickly.
seg.8f86db3a6d08.t: ꯖꯥꯋꯥ ꯊꯃꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.8f86db3a6d08.back: While the java is resting grate the palm jaggery fine, so it melts quickly.

seg.9cad3a0176bc.src: Stir in the palm jaggery and cardamom. Serve warm. Stir till the jaggery has fully melted, then taste and add a little more if needed.
seg.9cad3a0176bc.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9cad3a0176bc.back: Add palm jaggery and cardamom and stir. Serve hot. Stir until the jaggery fully melts, then taste and if needed add a little more.

seg.a8de8fe6382d.src: Pour into tumblers or bowls. If it is too thick to drink, stir in a few spoons of warm milk.
seg.a8de8fe6382d.t: ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯕꯣꯂꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯊꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a8de8fe6382d.back: Pour into a tumbler or bowl. If too thick to drink, add a few spoons of hot milk and stir.

seg.c3916a972329.src: Always mix the ragi flour in water first; flour added straight to boiling water forms lumps that do not break up.
seg.c3916a972329.t: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕ ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.c3916a972329.back: Always mix the ragi powder first in water; powder added straight into boiling water forms lumps that cannot be broken.

seg.966098732312.src: Do not rush the cooking; undercooked ragi tastes raw and floury.
seg.966098732312.t: ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯅꯨ; ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯗꯕ ꯔꯥꯒꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯨꯝ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.966098732312.back: Do not cook in a hurry; not fully cooked ragi tastes uncooked and like powder.

seg.7c0f350f3691.src: For a thinner java to drink from a tumbler, use 2 tbsp ragi flour; for a spoonable porridge, use ⅓ cup.
seg.7c0f350f3691.t: ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯊꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯖꯥꯋꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯞ ⅓ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7c0f350f3691.back: For a more watery java to drink from a tumbler use 2 tablespoons ragi powder; for a porridge that can be eaten with a spoon use ⅓ cup.

seg.146636ba6c2e.src: With dry fruit: stir in a few chopped cashews or almonds and a spoon of raisins at the end.
seg.146636ba6c2e.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯍꯩꯒꯥ: ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯕꯥꯗꯥꯝ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯤꯁꯃꯤꯁ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.146636ba6c2e.back: With dry fruits: at the end add a few chopped cashews or almonds and one spoon of raisins and stir.

seg.6fc3ada569ad.src: Without milk: cook the ragi in 2½ cups water and stir in the jaggery once it has stopped bubbling, for a thinner, darker java.
seg.6fc3ada569ad.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ, ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯖꯥꯋꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2½ꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯨꯠ ꯊꯣꯀꯄꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6fc3ada569ad.back: Without milk: for a more watery, darker java cook the ragi in 2½ cups water and add jaggery after it stops bubbling, and stir.

seg.639ea388ead3.src: Serve warm in a steel tumbler or bowl for breakfast, or as an evening drink with a few biscuits or murukulu. Some like it chilled in summer.
seg.639ea388ead3.t: ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯜꯒꯤ ꯇꯝꯕ꯭ꯂꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯕꯣꯂꯗꯥ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯋꯥꯏꯔꯃꯒꯤ ꯊꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯕꯤꯁ꯭ꯀꯨꯠ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨꯒꯥ꯫ ꯈꯔꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯡꯖꯨ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.639ea388ead3.back: Serve hot in a steel tumbler or bowl for the morning meal, or as the evening drink with a few biscuits or murukulu. Some like it cooled in summer.

seg.e770a9eec01e.src: Best drunk the day it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and stir in a little warm milk, off the heat, when reheating.
seg.e770a9eec01e.t: ꯁꯦꯝꯂꯕꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯛꯄꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯩ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ, ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e770a9eec01e.back: It is best drunk the same day it is made. Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge up to 1 day, and when heating again, take it off the flame and add a little hot milk and stir.

seg.a10b6147a5ac.src: How do I make ragi java without lumps?
seg.a10b6147a5ac.t: ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯒꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.a10b6147a5ac.back: How to make ragi java without lumps?

seg.ca8628b7e082.src: Whisk the ragi flour into room-temperature water first until smooth, then pour this into boiling water while stirring all the time.
seg.ca8628b7e082.t: ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯨꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ca8628b7e082.back: First mix the ragi powder in water at home room temperature by whisking until soft, then pour it into boiling water while stirring all the time.

seg.8bd78affc52d.src: How do I know ragi java is cooked?
seg.8bd78affc52d.back: How to know ragi java is done?

seg.9b05db7490cb.src: It turns darker and glossy, thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, and no longer tastes floury. This takes about 6–8 minutes on low heat.
seg.9b05db7490cb.t: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯊꯣꯀꯏ, ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯔꯔꯣꯏ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 6–8 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫
seg.9b05db7490cb.back: Its colour darkens and it shines, it thickens until it coats the back of the spoon, and it no longer tastes of powder. On low flame it takes about 6–8 minutes.

seg.6d748d67adfb.src: Can I use palm jaggery in ragi java?
seg.6d748d67adfb.t: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.6d748d67adfb.back: Can palm jaggery be used in ragi java?

seg.06e768643767.src: Yes. Grate the palm jaggery (thati bellam) finely and stir it in after switching off the stove, so the milk does not split. It gives a deeper colour and a slightly smoky sweetness.
seg.06e768643767.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯣꯏ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.06e768643767.back: Yes. Grate the palm jaggery (tati bellam) fine and add and stir after turning off the flame, so the milk does not break (curdle). It gives a thicker colour and a slightly smoke-like sweet taste.

seg.9a71713417de.src: What is the difference between ragi java and ragi malt?
seg.9a71713417de.t: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯜꯠꯀꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯈꯦꯟꯅꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.9a71713417de.back: What is the difference between ragi java and ragi malt?

seg.c2632b6d0b4f.src: They are the same drink with different names. Ragi java is the Telugu name; ragi malt is what it is often called in shops and on menus.
seg.c2632b6d0b4f.t: ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯕ ꯊꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯤꯡꯅꯤ; ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯜꯠ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯗꯣꯀꯥꯟ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯧꯕ ꯃꯃꯤꯡꯅꯤ꯫
seg.c2632b6d0b4f.back: They are one drink with different names. Ragi java is the Telugu name; ragi malt is the name often used in shops and menus.

seg.6134777fbfa8.src: రాగి జావ · Sweet Ragi Java Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.6134777fbfa8.t: రాగి జావ · ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ | 1acrefarms
seg.6134777fbfa8.back: రాగి జావ · Recipe of sweet ragi java | 1acrefarms

seg.708e3c523d72.src: రాగి జావ. Sweet ragi java, the Andhra way: ragi flour cooked in water till glossy, loosened with milk and sweetened with Thati Bellam palm jaggery. Method and tips.
seg.708e3c523d72.t: రాగి జావ. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥ: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯍꯜꯂꯕ꯫ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯤꯞꯁꯁꯤꯡ꯫
seg.708e3c523d72.back: రాగి జావ. Sweet ragi java in the Andhra way: ragi powder cooked in water until shiny, thinned with milk and sweetened with tati bellam palm jaggery. Method and tips.

seg.2889ed2cf93b.src: Ragi Java: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.2889ed2cf93b.t: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.2889ed2cf93b.back: Ragi Java: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.8ee2205b2e8b.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ

seg.671d48882eed.src: Iguru is the Andhra way of cooking meat or prawns down in a thick onion masala until almost dry, so the spices cling to every piece. Royyala iguru comes from the coastal districts, from Nellore to Godavari to Srikakulam, where prawns from the backwaters and the sea are a Sunday lunch with rice.
seg.671d48882eed.t: ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯁꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯅꯤ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯏ꯫ ꯔꯣꯏꯌꯂꯥ ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯖꯤꯂꯥꯁꯤꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯀꯏ, ꯅꯦꯜꯂꯣꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯒꯣꯗꯥꯕꯔꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁ꯭ꯔꯤꯀꯥꯀꯨꯂꯝ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯄꯥꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯡꯃꯥꯏꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.671d48882eed.back: Iguru is the Andhra way of cooking meat or prawns in a thick onion masala until almost dry, so the masala sticks to each piece. Royyala iguru comes from the sea-coast districts, from Nellore to Godavari and Srikakulam, where pond and sea prawns with rice are the Sunday afternoon meal.

seg.ff39877dbdbd.src: Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) goes on the prawns first and into the masala. Teja chilli powder brings the deep red colour and strong heat coastal homes like, so scale it to your table.
seg.ff39877dbdbd.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ (ꯀꯣꯟꯗꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ) ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯕ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯨꯔꯛꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯆꯥꯕ ꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯡ ꯆꯨꯅꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ff39877dbdbd.back: Our hill turmeric powder (konda pasupu) goes first into the prawns and into the masala. Teja chilli powder brings the thick red colour and strong spiciness that sea-coast houses like, so adjust the quantity looking at the people eating your meal.

seg.885826f68de3.src: Prep includes cleaning the prawns and the 10-minute rest with turmeric.
seg.885826f68de3.t: ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯕꯗꯥ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10-ꯒꯤ ꯊꯝꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.885826f68de3.back: Washing the prawns and the 10-minute keeping with turmeric are included in preparation.

seg.cff5bbd725a6.src: Rub prawns with turmeric and salt. Fry onions and ginger-garlic paste, add Teja chilli powder and coriander powder, then cook the prawns in the masala till it coats them.
seg.cff5bbd725a6.t: ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯕꯨ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯃꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.cff5bbd725a6.back: Rub the prawns with turmeric and salt. Fry onion and ginger-garlic paste, add Teja chilli powder and coriander powder, then cook the prawns in the masala until the masala coats them.

seg.cf489166a3fd.src: 500 g prawns ⟦1⟧medium size, shelled and deveined, weighed after cleaning⟦/1⟧
seg.cf489166a3fd.t: 500 g ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯆꯥꯏ, ꯃꯀꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ, ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.cf489166a3fd.back: 500 g prawns ⟦1⟧medium size, shell and the dark vein inside removed, weighed after washing⟦/1⟧

seg.141eb60cb009.src: ¾ tsp salt ⟦1⟧divided, or to taste⟦/1⟧
seg.141eb60cb009.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¾ ꯊꯨꯝ ⟦1⟧ꯈꯥꯌꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.141eb60cb009.back: ¾ teaspoon salt ⟦1⟧divided, or by tasting⟦/1⟧

seg.8c4c1b789de7.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯅꯠꯀꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ⟦/1⟧
seg.8c4c1b789de7.back: 3 tablespoons oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil all the time⟦/1⟧

seg.716dc45cf0b3.src: ½ tsp hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧Konda Pasupu; ¼ tsp for the prawns, ¼ tsp for the masala⟦/1⟧
seg.716dc45cf0b3.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯣꯟꯗꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ; ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼, ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼⟦/1⟧
seg.716dc45cf0b3.back: ½ teaspoon hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧konda pasupu; ¼ teaspoon for the prawns, ¼ teaspoon for the masala⟦/1⟧

seg.f7ec1e72abc0.src: 1½ tsp Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; use 1 tsp for medium heat, ½ tsp for mild⟦/1⟧
seg.f7ec1e72abc0.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1½ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ; ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1, ꯍꯟꯊꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.f7ec1e72abc0.back: 1½ teaspoons Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very spicy; for medium spiciness use 1 teaspoon, for mild ½ teaspoon⟦/1⟧

seg.fce641038ff4.src: Shell and devein the prawns, rinse them well and drain in a colander.
seg.fce641038ff4.t: ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯐꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯠꯅꯤꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fce641038ff4.back: Remove the prawns' shell and the vein inside, wash well and drain the water in a strainer.

seg.152d1d89f6a5.src: Rub the prawns with half the turmeric and a little salt; set aside 10 minutes. Use ¼ tsp turmeric and ¼ tsp of the salt.
seg.152d1d89f6a5.t: ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯕꯨ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯈꯔꯥꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.152d1d89f6a5.back: Rub the prawns with the turmeric portion and a little salt; keep about 10 minutes. Use ¼ teaspoon turmeric and ¼ teaspoon salt.

seg.9e027c56020d.src: Heat the oil in a heavy kadai on medium heat and add the mustard seeds. When they splutter, add the green chillies and curry leaves.
seg.9e027c56020d.t: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9e027c56020d.back: Heat oil on medium flame in a heavy kadai and add mustard seed. When it crackles, add green chilli and curry leaves.

seg.5d608fabeb97.src: Fry the onions in the oil till golden, then the ginger-garlic paste till it smells cooked. The onions take about 8–10 minutes; the paste about 1 minute, until the raw smell goes.
seg.5d608fabeb97.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯡ-ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 8–10 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯇꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.5d608fabeb97.back: Fry the onion in the oil until golden colour, then the ginger-garlic paste until the cooked smell comes. The onion takes about 8–10 minutes; the paste about 1 minute, until the uncooked smell goes.

seg.7677bdc79559.src: If using the tomato, add it now and cook until soft and pulpy, about 4 minutes.
seg.7677bdc79559.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 4 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫
seg.7677bdc79559.back: If using tomato, add it now and cook until soft and melted, about 4 minutes.

seg.5aff56b73c8a.src: Turn the heat to low. Add the rest of the turmeric, Teja chilli powder and coriander powder; fry 1 minute. Add the remaining salt and stir so the spices do not catch.
seg.5aff56b73c8a.t: ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ, ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1 ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯊꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5aff56b73c8a.back: Make the flame low. Add the remaining turmeric, Teja chilli powder and coriander powder; fry 1 minute. Add the remaining salt and stir so the masala does not stick at the bottom.

seg.ba25fbb9cf98.src: Pour in the water and cook the masala on medium heat until the oil starts to separate at the edges, about 3–4 minutes.
seg.ba25fbb9cf98.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯍꯧꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 3–4 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫
seg.ba25fbb9cf98.back: Pour water and cook the masala on medium flame until oil starts to come out separately at the edges, about 3–4 minutes.

seg.e60a6389cdf2.src: Add the prawns and cook till they curl and turn pink, 5–6 minutes. Finish with garam masala. Stir often on medium-high heat so the masala dries and coats the prawns.
seg.e60a6389cdf2.t: ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–6꯫ ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e60a6389cdf2.back: Add the prawns and cook until they curl and turn pink colour, 5–6 minutes. Finish with garam masala. Stir from time to time on medium-high flame so the masala dries and coats the prawns.

seg.af87e48d1429.src: Check doneness: prawns are cooked when they are pink and opaque all the way through and curled into a loose C. Cut one open if unsure; there should be no grey, see-through centre.
seg.af87e48d1429.t: ꯆꯤꯟꯔꯕꯔꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯎꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ C ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯁꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯉꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ-ꯑꯉꯧꯕ, ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯎꯕ ꯉꯝꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯂꯩꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.af87e48d1429.back: Check whether done: the prawns are done when pink colour to the inside and not see-through in the middle and curled in a soft C shape. If not sure, cut one and check; there should be no grey-white, see-through part in the middle.

seg.32e58c09609e.src: Taste for salt, scatter the coriander leaves and switch off. Do not keep cooking once the prawns are done, or they turn rubbery.
seg.32e58c09609e.t: ꯊꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯆꯤꯟꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯔꯕꯔꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.32e58c09609e.back: Taste the salt, sprinkle coriander leaves and turn off the flame. Do not keep cooking the prawns after they are done, otherwise they will become like rubber.

seg.89a9cb293875.src: Teja is very hot: 1½ tsp makes a fiery iguru the way coastal homes like it; use 1 tsp for medium heat, or ½ tsp for mild.
seg.89a9cb293875.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1½ꯅꯥ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯕꯒꯨꯝ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ; ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.89a9cb293875.back: Teja is very spicy: 1½ teaspoons makes a very spicy iguru as sea-coast houses like; for medium spiciness use 1 teaspoon, or for mild ½ teaspoon.

seg.095c6105ce36.src: Fry the onions until properly golden; the colour and body of an iguru come from well-browned onions.
seg.095c6105ce36.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯀꯏ꯫
seg.095c6105ce36.back: Fry the onion well until golden colour; the colour and thickness of the iguru come from well-browned onion.

seg.04fb6307d058.src: Prawns cook fast. A loose C shape means done; a tight O means overcooked and chewy.
seg.04fb6307d058.t: ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯏ꯫ ꯂꯥꯏꯕ C ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯔꯦ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯅꯤ; ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯕ O ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯈ꯭ꯔꯦ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯕꯥ ꯀꯟꯈ꯭ꯔꯦ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.04fb6307d058.back: Prawns cook quickly. A soft C shape means done; a tightly curled O shape means cooked too much and hard to eat.

seg.a5e6a832090a.src: Pat the prawns dry after rinsing so they fry in the masala instead of stewing in water.
seg.a5e6a832090a.t: ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯎꯠꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.a5e6a832090a.back: After washing, wipe the prawns gently and dry them, so they fry in the masala instead of boiling in water.

seg.4145e1ca56b5.src: Gongura royyalu: stir in ½ cup gongura leaves, wilted in a little oil and mashed, with the prawns.
seg.4145e1ca56b5.t: ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯔꯣꯏꯌꯂꯨ: ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ, ꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯌꯣꯏꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯂꯕ ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯀꯞ ½ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4145e1ca56b5.back: Gongura royyalu: together with the prawns, add ½ cup gongura leaves wilted and mashed in a little oil and stir.

seg.e52b316e5c51.src: Coconut: add 2 tbsp grated coconut or 3 tbsp thick coconut milk in the last 2 minutes for a softer, richer masala.
seg.e52b316e5c51.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ, ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2ꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜꯒꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e52b316e5c51.back: Coconut: for a softer, thicker masala add 2 tablespoons grated coconut or 3 tablespoons thick coconut milk in the last 2 minutes.

seg.fc55c7b1a788.src: Gravy style: add ¾ cup water after the prawns for a thinner royyala kura to pour over rice.
seg.fc55c7b1a788.t: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ: ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯔꯣꯏꯌꯂꯥ ꯀꯨꯔꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ¾ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fc55c7b1a788.back: Gravy style: for a watery royyala kura to pour over rice add ¾ cup water after the prawns.

seg.8ccb6d545dd0.src: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, or with rasam or sambar rice. It also goes well with chapati.
seg.8ccb6d545dd0.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯔꯁꯝ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯝꯕꯔ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯄꯥꯇꯤꯒꯥꯁꯨ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.8ccb6d545dd0.back: Serve hot with steamed rice and one spoon of ghee, or with rasam or sambar rice. It also goes very well with chapati.

seg.d51021b311d0.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Warm gently in a pan; long reheating makes the prawns tough.
seg.d51021b311d0.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 1ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.d51021b311d0.back: Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Heat gently in a pan; if reheated a long time the prawns become hard.

seg.8381d6ac4e4f.src: How do I know when prawns are cooked?
seg.8381d6ac4e4f.back: How to know the prawns are done?

seg.45cd36ecb77b.src: They turn pink and opaque all the way through and curl into a loose C shape, usually in 5–6 minutes in the hot masala. A grey, see-through centre means they need a little longer.
seg.45cd36ecb77b.t: ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯄꯤꯉ꯭ꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯎꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ C ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5–6ꯗꯥ꯫ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ-ꯑꯉꯧꯕ, ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯎꯕ ꯉꯝꯕ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.45cd36ecb77b.back: They become pink colour to the inside and not see-through in the middle, and curl in a soft C shape, often in 5–6 minutes in hot masala. If there is a grey-white, see-through part in the middle, they should be cooked a little more.

seg.2e4c4a4632d7.src: What is the difference between iguru and vepudu?
seg.2e4c4a4632d7.t: ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯈꯦꯟꯅꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.2e4c4a4632d7.back: What is the difference between iguru and vepudu?

seg.1ee73f38a967.src: Iguru is cooked down in an onion masala until thick and almost dry, with the masala clinging to the prawns. Vepudu is a fry, with less or no onion gravy, cooked until the prawns are crisp at the edges.
seg.1ee73f38a967.t: ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ, ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ꯫ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯅꯤ, ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯕꯤ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ, ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ꯫
seg.1ee73f38a967.back: Iguru is cooked in onion masala until thick and almost dry, the masala coating the prawns. Vepudu is a fry, with less or no onion gravy, cooked until the prawn edges become crunchy.

seg.d248a2970455.src: How can I make royyala iguru less spicy?
seg.d248a2970455.back: How to reduce the spiciness of royyala iguru?

seg.8c9c12b68361.src: Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder for medium heat or ½ tsp for mild, and skip the green chillies. A tablespoon of curd or coconut milk at the end also softens the heat.
seg.8c9c12b68361.t: ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯍꯥꯞꯀꯅꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜꯒꯤ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯑꯃꯅꯥꯁꯨ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.8c9c12b68361.back: For medium spiciness use 1 teaspoon Teja chilli powder or for mild ½ teaspoon, and do not add green chilli. At the end one tablespoon of curd or coconut milk also reduces the spiciness.

seg.9cd9740c2604.src: Yes. Thaw them in the fridge, drain them well and pat them dry before rubbing with turmeric and salt. Frozen prawns release more water, so cook the masala a little longer.
seg.9cd9740c2604.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯃꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯣꯖꯟ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯀꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9cd9740c2604.back: Yes. Thaw them in the fridge, drain the water well and wipe gently dry before rubbing with turmeric and salt. Frozen prawns let out more water, so cook the masala a little more.

seg.3120e29b987a.back: రొయ్యల ఇగురు · Recipe of Royyala Iguru | 1acrefarms

seg.0484ea984ed7.src: రొయ్యల ఇగురు. Royyala iguru, the coastal Andhra prawn roast: prawns cooked down in onion masala with hill turmeric powder and fiery Teja chilli powder. Serves 4.
seg.0484ea984ed7.t: రొయ్యల ఇగురు. ꯔꯣꯏꯌꯂꯥ ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨ, ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ: ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ꯫ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.0484ea984ed7.back: రొయ్యల ఇగురు. Royyala iguru, Andhra's sea-coast prawn roast: prawns cooked in onion masala with hill turmeric powder and very spicy Teja chilli powder. For 4 people.

seg.1b1d6a89c215.src: Royyala Iguru: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.1b1d6a89c215.t: ꯔꯣꯏꯌꯂꯥ ꯏꯒꯨꯔꯨ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.1b1d6a89c215.back: Royyala Iguru: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.965a1e93fb08.src: Sunnundalu are the urad dal laddus of Andhra: split urad dal roasted till nutty, ground fine with jaggery and pressed together with hot ghee. There is no cooking of syrup, so they come together in about half an hour. Andhra homes make a tin for Sankranti and Diwali, pack them for relatives travelling abroad, and keep them for an evening sweet with tea.
seg.965a1e93fb08.t: ꯁꯨꯟꯅꯨꯟꯗꯥꯂꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯅꯤ: ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯒꯥ ꯅꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯕ꯫ ꯁꯤꯔꯞ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯗꯦ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯔꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯏ꯫ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯁꯡꯀ꯭ꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯤꯋꯥꯂꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯇꯤꯟ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ, ꯂꯃꯗꯝ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄꯗꯥ ꯆꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯂꯩꯅꯕꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯋꯥꯏꯔꯃꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.965a1e93fb08.back: Sunnundalu is Andhra's urad dal laddu: roasted urad dal, roasted until a nut-like smell comes out, ground fine with jaggery, mixed with hot ghee and bound together. There is no need to make syrup, so it is made in about half an hour. Andhra homes make a tin for Sankranti and Diwali, pack it for relatives travelling to other countries, and keep it as a sweet afternoon bite with tea.

seg.e564344550cd.src: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery gives sunnundalu a deep brown colour and a rich, slightly smoky sweetness that suits the roasted dal. This recipe makes about 15 laddus.
seg.e564344550cd.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯟꯅꯨꯟꯗꯥꯂꯨꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯅꯕ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ 15 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯏ꯫
seg.e564344550cd.back: Our tati bellam palm jaggery gives sunnundalu a thick brown colour and a thick, slightly smoke-like sweet taste that matches the roasted dal. This recipe gives about 15 laddus.

seg.b1400f429b2f.src: Total includes cooling the roasted dal before grinding.
seg.b1400f429b2f.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.b1400f429b2f.back: Cooling the roasted dal before grinding is included in the total.

seg.6c6369238635.src: Roast urad dal till golden, cool and grind fine, then grind in palm jaggery and cardamom. Mix with hot ghee and shape into laddus.
seg.6c6369238635.t: ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6c6369238635.back: Roast the urad dal until golden colour, cool and grind fine, then grind the palm jaggery and cardamom. Mix with hot ghee and make laddus.

seg.890ddaaca185.src: 1 cup white urad dal ⟦1⟧split, skinless (minapappu), about 200 g⟦/1⟧
seg.890ddaaca185.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ, ꯃꯀꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ (ꯃꯤꯅꯄꯞꯄꯨ), 200 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.890ddaaca185.back: 1 cup white urad dal ⟦1⟧split, skinless (minapappu), about 200 g⟦/1⟧

seg.06c2723f717d.src: 1 cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 180 g, lightly packed; pound or grate the pieces first⟦/1⟧
seg.06c2723f717d.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧180 g ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯥ; ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.06c2723f717d.back: 1 cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 180 g, not pressed very hard; first crush or grate the pieces⟦/1⟧

seg.25c886ef1375.src: ½ cup ghee ⟦1⟧melted and hot; keep 1–2 tbsp extra on hand⟦/1⟧
seg.25c886ef1375.t: ꯀꯞ ½ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ; ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1–2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.25c886ef1375.back: ½ cup ghee ⟦1⟧melted and hot; keep 1–2 tablespoons more at the side⟦/1⟧

seg.99983266b588.src: Pick through the urad dal for any small stones. Do not wash it; it must stay dry for roasting.
seg.99983266b588.t: ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯂꯗꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯡ ꯑꯄꯤꯀꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯀꯅꯨ; ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯅꯕꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.99983266b588.back: Pick out the small stones from the urad dal and remove them. Do not wash; for roasting it must stay dry.

seg.2f2807ce216b.src: Put the dal in a heavy pan on a low flame.
seg.2f2807ce216b.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2f2807ce216b.back: Keep the dal in a heavy pan on low flame.

seg.65588a76c883.src: Dry-roast the urad dal on a low flame till golden and nutty, about 10 minutes. Stir all the time so every grain colours evenly; it should smell toasty and snap when you bite a grain.
seg.65588a76c883.t: ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.65588a76c883.back: Roast the urad dal without oil on low flame until golden colour and a nut-like smell comes, about 10 minutes. Stir all the time so every grain colours evenly; the roasted smell should come and one grain should break with a 'karak' when eaten.

seg.9e8dc23d38fa.src: Tip the dal onto a plate and spread it out. Cool it, then grind to a fine powder. Grind in short bursts so the mixer does not heat up, and sieve out any coarse bits to grind again.
seg.9e8dc23d38fa.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔ ꯁꯥꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯦꯠꯅꯤꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9e8dc23d38fa.back: Pour the dal onto a plate and spread it. Let it cool, then grind fine. Grind in short bursts so the mixer does not get hot, and take out the not-fine pieces with a strainer and grind again.

seg.edfa5bb66e59.src: Grate the palm jaggery finely, or pound the pieces in a mortar, breaking up any hard lumps.
seg.edfa5bb66e59.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ꯫
seg.edfa5bb66e59.back: Grate the palm jaggery fine, or crush the pieces in a mortar, breaking the hard lumps.

seg.fcf7bce21bc5.src: Add the jaggery and cardamom powder to the dal powder in the mixer jar. Grind in the jaggery and cardamom till evenly mixed. A few pulses are enough; tip it all into a wide bowl.
seg.fcf7bce21bc5.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯏ; ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯄꯥꯛꯄ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fcf7bce21bc5.back: In the mixer jar add the jaggery and cardamom powder to the dal powder. Grind until the jaggery and cardamom mix evenly. A few runs are enough; pour it all into a wide bowl.

seg.1cd01dc31b1a.src: Melt the ghee in a small pan until it is hot but not smoking.
seg.1cd01dc31b1a.t: ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯃꯩꯈꯨ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.1cd01dc31b1a.back: In a small pan melt the ghee until hot, but it should not smoke.

seg.0b0ec921a239.src: Pour in the hot ghee, mix well and press into small balls. Start with most of the ghee, mix with a spoon, then use your hands once it is cool enough to touch.
seg.0b0ec921a239.t: ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯐꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯁꯣꯛꯄ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯪꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0b0ec921a239.back: Pour the hot ghee, mix well and make small laddus by pressing. Start with almost all the ghee, mix with a spoon, then when it has cooled enough for the hand to bear, use the hands.

seg.0c005163369c.src: Take a small handful and squeeze it firmly in your fist, then roll it round between your palms. If it crumbles, add a spoon more hot ghee to the bowl and mix.
seg.0c005163369c.t: ꯈꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯂꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯕꯣꯂꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0c005163369c.back: Take a small handful in the hand and press hard, then roll gently between the two hands. If it breaks apart, add one more spoon of hot ghee to the bowl and mix.

seg.7ac27bb5fb12.src: Set the laddus on a plate to firm up for 15–20 minutes before storing.
seg.7ac27bb5fb12.t: ꯊꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15–20 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7ac27bb5fb12.back: Before storing keep the laddus on a plate 15–20 minutes to become firm.

seg.591b2b7e4ef4.src: Roast the dal on a low flame so it cooks through without burning.
seg.591b2b7e4ef4.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯀꯇꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.591b2b7e4ef4.back: Roast the dal on low flame so it cooks to the inside without burning.

seg.07daa833e53a.src: Grind the dal only after it has cooled completely; warm dal turns pasty in the mixer.
seg.07daa833e53a.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯁꯥꯕ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔꯗꯥ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.07daa833e53a.back: Grind only after the dal has fully cooled; hot dal becomes like paste in the mixer.

seg.33701abc66f0.src: Shape the laddus while the mixture is still warm; it binds best with the heat of the ghee.
seg.33701abc66f0.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.33701abc66f0.back: Make the laddus while the mixture is still hot; the heat of the ghee binds them best.

seg.b6fb58b6b287.src: Palm jaggery pieces vary in hardness, so grate or pound them small before they go into the mixer.
seg.b6fb58b6b287.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯩ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b6fb58b6b287.back: Palm jaggery pieces differ in hardness, so grate or crush them small before adding to the mixer.

seg.1797acff16a2.src: Cane jaggery: use the same amount of grated cane jaggery for a lighter colour and a caramel-like sweetness.
seg.1797acff16a2.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1797acff16a2.back: Sugarcane jaggery: for a lighter [ꯁꯪꯕ: reads 'greener'] colour and caramel-like sweet taste use the same quantity of grated sugarcane jaggery.

seg.f95b0650add7.src: With skin: use black split urad dal with its skin for darker, grainier sunnundalu, the way some village homes make them.
seg.f95b0650add7.t: ꯃꯀꯨꯒꯥ: ꯈꯨꯡꯒꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯈꯔꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯨꯝ, ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯁꯨꯟꯅꯨꯟꯗꯥꯂꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f95b0650add7.back: With skin: as some village houses make it, for darker and grainier sunnundalu use split black urad dal with skin.

seg.07498f6166e4.src: With sugar: use ¾ cup powdered sugar in place of the jaggery for pale, crisp-melting laddus.
seg.07498f6166e4.t: ꯆꯤꯅꯤꯒꯥ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯟꯕ, ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯆꯤꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯀꯞ ¾ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.07498f6166e4.back: With sugar: for a pale-coloured, crunchy-melting laddu, use ¾ cup sugar powder instead of jaggery.

seg.8fea3a4a695f.src: Serve as an evening sweet with tea or coffee, or as part of the Sankranti and Diwali sweet plate.
seg.8fea3a4a695f.t: ꯆꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯣꯐꯤꯒꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯋꯥꯏꯔꯃꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯡꯀ꯭ꯔꯥꯟꯇꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯤꯋꯥꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯊꯥꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8fea3a4a695f.back: Serve as the evening sweet with tea or coffee, or as one part of the Sankranti and Diwali sweet plate.

seg.83b4edc5c69d.src: Keep in an airtight steel tin at room temperature and eat within 2 weeks. In warm weather they keep longer in the fridge; let them come to room temperature before eating.
seg.83b4edc5c69d.t: ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯤꯜꯒꯤ ꯇꯤꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ; ꯆꯥꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.83b4edc5c69d.back: Keep in an airtight steel tin at home room temperature and eat within 2 weeks. In hot weather they can be kept longer in the fridge; before eating let them come to home room temperature.

seg.c0ae9315eb0e.src: Why are my sunnundalu not holding shape?
seg.c0ae9315eb0e.back: Why do my sunnundalu not hold shape?

seg.03c64235659e.src: The mixture needs more hot ghee, or it has cooled down. Warm a spoon or two of ghee, mix it in and shape the laddus while the mixture is still warm.
seg.03c64235659e.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯛꯂꯦ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.03c64235659e.back: The mixture needs more hot ghee, or it has cooled. Heat one or two spoons of ghee, mix, and make laddus while the mixture is still hot.

seg.c125d749f215.src: Can I make sunnundalu with palm jaggery?
seg.c125d749f215.back: Can sunnundalu be made with palm jaggery?

seg.7b13a91f65e1.src: Yes. Grate or pound the palm jaggery (thati bellam) finely and use the same amount as cane jaggery. The laddus turn darker and taste deeper and slightly smoky.
seg.7b13a91f65e1.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.7b13a91f65e1.back: Yes. Grate or crush the palm jaggery (tati bellam) fine and use the same quantity as sugarcane jaggery. The laddus become darker in colour and the taste becomes thicker and a little smoke-like.

seg.946f64207639.back: How long can sunnundalu be kept?

seg.b2aed25ebff6.src: About 2 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature, and longer in the fridge. Use a dry spoon or dry hands to take them out.
seg.b2aed25ebff6.t: ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯇꯤꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ꯫ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b2aed25ebff6.back: About 2 weeks in an airtight tin at home room temperature, and longer in the fridge. Use a dry spoon or a dry hand to take them out.

seg.e750875c4912.src: Should I use urad dal with or without skin?
seg.e750875c4912.t: ꯃꯀꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗ꯭ꯔꯥ?
seg.e750875c4912.back: Should urad dal with skin or without skin be used?

seg.b12320430e22.src: Both are made in Andhra. White skinless urad dal gives smooth, light brown laddus; black urad dal with skin gives darker, grainier ones.
seg.b12320430e22.t: ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯗꯥ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯂꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯄꯤ; ꯃꯀꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯂꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.b12320430e22.back: In Andhra both are made. White skinless urad dal gives a soft, slightly brown laddu; dark urad dal with skin gives a darker and grainier laddu.

seg.d8e8e5770555.src: సున్నుండలు. Andhra sunnundalu: roasted urad dal ground with Thati Bellam palm jaggery and bound with hot ghee into laddus. Step-by-step method, tips and FAQs.
seg.d8e8e5770555.t: సున్నుండలు. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯟꯅꯨꯟꯗꯥꯂꯨ: ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ꯫ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯊꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ, ꯇꯤꯞꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯁꯤꯡ꯫
seg.d8e8e5770555.back: సున్నుండలు. Andhra's sunnundalu: laddus made by grinding roasted urad dal with tati bellam palm jaggery and binding with hot ghee. Step-by-step way, tips and questions.

seg.c61b125404d0.src: Sunnundalu: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.c61b125404d0.t: ꯁꯨꯟꯅꯨꯟꯗꯥꯂꯨ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.c61b125404d0.back: Sunnundalu: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.02d0a5789a02.src: Tomato pachadi is the everyday chutney of Andhra kitchens: ripe tomatoes cooked down in oil with roasted dals, then ground coarse with chilli, garlic and a little tamarind. Many homes still grind it in the stone roti for a rough, spoonable texture, though a mixer in short pulses does the job. It goes with hot rice and ghee, dosa, idli and pesarattu.
seg.02d0a5789a02.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯈꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯆꯠꯅꯤꯅꯤ: ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯔꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕ꯫ ꯌꯨꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯔꯣꯇꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏ, ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ, ꯆꯥꯃꯆꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔꯅꯥꯁꯨ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯧꯏ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ, ꯗꯣꯁꯥ, ꯏꯗꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯠꯇꯨꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫
seg.02d0a5789a02.back: Tomato pachadi is the everyday chutney of Andhra kitchens: ripe tomatoes cooked in oil with roasted dal, then ground not-fine with chilli, garlic and a little tamarind. Many houses still grind it on a stone grinder, for a not-fine, spoon-eatable texture, but a mixer run in short bursts also does the work. It goes with hot rice and ghee, dosa, idli and pesarattu.

seg.7735dff0ccd2.src: Our Sannam chilli powder gives it a deep red colour and steady, medium heat, and a little turmeric powder goes in with the tomatoes. This recipe makes about 1½ cups.
seg.7735dff0ccd2.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ, ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯀꯞ 1½ ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯏ꯫
seg.7735dff0ccd2.back: Our Sannam chilli powder gives it a thick red colour and a steady, medium spiciness, and a little turmeric powder goes in with the tomato. This recipe gives about 1½ cups.

seg.44c4d82a4524.src: Total includes 5 minutes for the tomatoes to cool before grinding.
seg.44c4d82a4524.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.44c4d82a4524.back: 5 minutes to cool the tomato before grinding is included in the total.

seg.827e4421a48d.src: Fry dals and methi in oil, cook tomatoes down with turmeric and salt, then grind coarsely with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. Finish with a mustard and curry-leaf tempering.
seg.827e4421a48d.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.827e4421a48d.back: Fry dal and fenugreek in oil, cook the tomato with turmeric and salt, then grind not-fine with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. Finish with a tempering of mustard seed and curry leaves.

seg.4171dd59d18a.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯄꯤꯅꯠ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ⟦/1⟧

seg.826b52ef9f19.src: ¼ tsp methi seeds ⟦1⟧fenugreek seeds; no more, or the pachadi turns bitter⟦/1⟧
seg.826b52ef9f19.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯃꯔꯨ ⟦1⟧ꯐꯦꯅꯨꯒ꯭ꯔꯤꯛ ꯃꯔꯨ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯀꯅꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯈꯥꯔꯛꯀꯅꯤ⟦/1⟧
seg.826b52ef9f19.back: ¼ teaspoon fenugreek seed ⟦1⟧fenugreek seed; do not add more, otherwise the pachadi becomes bitter⟦/1⟧

seg.6cd60f9cc4c2.src: 5 medium tomatoes ⟦1⟧about 500 g, ripe and red, chopped⟦/1⟧
seg.6cd60f9cc4c2.t: ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ 5 ⟦1⟧500 g ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯔꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ, ꯀꯛꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.6cd60f9cc4c2.back: 5 medium tomatoes ⟦1⟧about 500 g, ripe and red, chopped⟦/1⟧

seg.29558a247c61.src: 2 tsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧up to 1 tbsp for a hotter pachadi⟦/1⟧
seg.29558a247c61.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2 ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.29558a247c61.back: 2 teaspoons Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧up to 1 tablespoon for a spicier pachadi⟦/1⟧

seg.f7c3bb463ff4.t: ꯒꯨꯂꯤ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ⟦1⟧5 g ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯃꯔꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧

seg.2f8f5bd3f25f.back: ¼ cup coriander leaves (if you like) ⟦1⟧not finely chopped⟦/1⟧

seg.2c1074e3a23e.src: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a kadai on medium-low heat.
seg.2c1074e3a23e.t: ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2c1074e3a23e.back: Heat 2 tablespoons oil on medium-low flame in a kadai.

seg.9d0674551be0.src: Fry the urad dal, chana dal and methi in oil till golden; lift them out. This takes 2–3 minutes; stir all the time, as methi burns fast and turns bitter.
seg.9d0674551be0.t: ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2–3 ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯀꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯥꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.9d0674551be0.back: Fry the urad dal, chana dal and fenugreek in the oil until golden colour; take them out. It takes 2–3 minutes; stir all the time, because fenugreek burns quickly and becomes bitter.

seg.4727da6f2a95.src: In the same oil, add the chopped tomatoes and stir for a minute on medium heat.
seg.4727da6f2a95.t: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4727da6f2a95.back: In the same oil add the chopped tomatoes and stir one minute on medium flame.

seg.8032f2a2778c.src: Cook the tomatoes with turmeric and salt till soft and the juice dries up. Cover for the first 5 minutes, then cook uncovered, stirring now and then, about 12–15 minutes in all, until the tomatoes are pulpy and oil shows at the edges.
seg.8032f2a2778c.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯀꯨꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯅꯥ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯃꯇꯝꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 12–15 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯌꯧꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯎꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.8032f2a2778c.back: Cook the tomato with turmeric and salt until soft and the juice is dry. Cover the first 5 minutes, then uncovered, stirring from time to time, cook about 12–15 minutes in all, until the tomato melts and oil comes out at the edges.

seg.d606b6ac13a2.src: Switch off, stir in the tamarind so it softens in the heat, and let everything cool for about 5 minutes.
seg.d606b6ac13a2.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯁꯥꯕꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯕꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d606b6ac13a2.back: Turn off the flame, add the tamarind to soften in the heat and stir, and cool everything about 5 minutes.

seg.c1820dcae462.src: In the stone roti or a mixer jar, first grind the fried dals and methi to a coarse powder.
seg.c1820dcae462.t: ꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯔꯣꯇꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯔꯗꯥ, ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c1820dcae462.back: In a stone grinder or mixer jar, first grind the fried dal and fenugreek into a not-fine powder.

seg.f07d8b97d1db.src: Grind the dals, garlic, tamarind, chilli powder and tomatoes coarsely. In a mixer, add the garlic, chilli powder and cooked tomatoes to the dal powder and pulse 4–5 times without water; stop while it still has texture. Stir in the coriander leaves, if using.
seg.f07d8b97d1db.t: ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯏꯃꯂꯤ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔꯗꯥ, ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ 4–5 ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ, ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.f07d8b97d1db.back: Grind the dal, garlic, tamarind, chilli powder and tomato not-fine. In the mixer, add garlic, chilli powder and cooked tomato to the dal powder and pulse 4–5 times in short bursts without water; stop while it still has texture. Add coriander leaves, if using, and stir.

seg.6675d75425f6.src: Taste and adjust: a pinch more salt, or a little more chilli powder pulsed in, if you want it hotter.
seg.6675d75425f6.t: ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯨꯅꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯊꯨꯝ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6675d75425f6.back: Taste and adjust: a little more salt, or if you want it spicier add a little more chilli powder and pulse.

seg.27426b7ca3c6.src: Spoon the pachadi into a bowl. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds; when they splutter, add the urad dal and fry until golden.
seg.27426b7ca3c6.t: ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ, ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.27426b7ca3c6.back: Put the pachadi in a bowl. In a small pan heat 1 tablespoon oil and add mustard seed; when it crackles, add urad dal and fry until golden colour.

seg.77131f9506c3.src: Add the red chillies, asafoetida and curry leaves and stir for a few seconds.
seg.77131f9506c3.t: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ, ꯍꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.77131f9506c3.back: Add red chilli, hing and curry leaves and stir a few seconds.

seg.d4a4b9439500.src: Temper with mustard, red chillies and curry leaves; pour over. Mix it in just before serving.
seg.d4a4b9439500.t: ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d4a4b9439500.back: Temper with mustard seed, red chilli and curry leaves; pour on top. Mix only just before serving.

seg.0f23e6b9231e.src: Cook the tomatoes till the juice dries up so the pachadi keeps longer and does not taste raw.
seg.0f23e6b9231e.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯒꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯔꯣꯏ꯫
seg.0f23e6b9231e.back: Cook until the tomato juice is dry, then the pachadi can be kept a long time and has no uncooked taste.

seg.bad083b47507.src: Ripe, deep-red tomatoes give the best colour; if yours are sour, cut the tamarind to half.
seg.bad083b47507.t: ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯔꯕ, ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ; ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bad083b47507.back: Ripe, deep red tomatoes give the best colour; if your tomatoes are sour, reduce the tamarind to half.

seg.99bd4830d431.src: Pulse, do not run the mixer: a coarse pachadi is how Andhra homes like it, and a smooth paste loses that texture.
seg.99bd4830d431.t: ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯒꯅꯨ: ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤꯕꯨ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯃꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯅꯥ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.99bd4830d431.back: Pulse in short bursts, do not run the mixer a long time: Andhra houses like not-fine pachadi, and a soft paste loses that texture.

seg.27f2aaa2d25d.src: Sannam chilli powder gives medium heat. Start at 2 tsp and add more after tasting; the heat settles a little as the pachadi rests.
seg.27f2aaa2d25d.t: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2ꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.27f2aaa2d25d.back: Sannam chilli powder gives medium spiciness. Start with 2 teaspoons and add more after tasting; when the pachadi is kept the spiciness reduces a little.

seg.5e0bf03c1b36.src: Green chilli: replace the chilli powder with 4–5 green chillies, fried with the dals.
seg.5e0bf03c1b36.t: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ 4–5 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5e0bf03c1b36.back: Green chilli: in place of chilli powder use 4–5 green chillies fried with the dal.

seg.d7301a50c407.src: Onion-tomato: fry 1 sliced onion until soft before the tomatoes go in.
seg.d7301a50c407.t: ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ-ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ 1 ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d7301a50c407.back: Onion-tomato: before adding tomato fry 1 cut onion until soft.

seg.bc90e2638112.src: Hotter: use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder in place of 1 tsp of the Sannam; Teja is very hot, so go slowly.
seg.bc90e2638112.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯅꯕꯥ: ꯁꯟꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bc90e2638112.back: For more spiciness: in place of 1 teaspoon Sannam use 1 teaspoon Teja chilli powder; Teja is very spicy, so add slowly.

seg.aab608a427a9.src: Without garlic: leave out the garlic and add a pinch more asafoetida to the tempering.
seg.aab608a427a9.t: ꯆꯅꯝ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ: ꯆꯅꯝ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.aab608a427a9.back: Without garlic: leave out the garlic and add a little more hing in the tempering.

seg.62d9491c4e58.src: Mix a spoonful into hot rice with a little ghee, or serve alongside dosa, idli, pesarattu or upma.
seg.62d9491c4e58.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯗꯣꯁꯥ, ꯏꯗꯂꯤ, ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯠꯇꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯎꯞꯃꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.62d9491c4e58.back: Mix one spoon with a little ghee into hot rice, or serve at the side of dosa, idli, pesarattu or upma.

seg.3f0b892d2728.src: Keep it in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge and eat within 4 days. Always use a dry spoon.
seg.3f0b892d2728.t: ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 4ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3f0b892d2728.back: Keep in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge and eat within 4 days. Always use a dry spoon.

seg.20425f76c6e2.src: How do you make Andhra tomato pachadi?
seg.20425f76c6e2.back: How is Andhra tomato pachadi made?

seg.32ae9ac6b03c.src: Fry urad dal, chana dal and methi in oil, cook chopped tomatoes with turmeric and salt until the juice dries up, then grind everything coarsely with chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. Finish with a mustard, red chilli and curry-leaf tempering.
seg.32ae9ac6b03c.t: ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.32ae9ac6b03c.back: Fry urad dal, chana dal and fenugreek in oil, cook chopped tomato with turmeric and salt until the juice is dry, then grind it all not-fine with chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. Finish with a tempering of mustard seed, red chilli and curry leaves.

seg.2e87824684cb.src: Why is my tomato pachadi bitter?
seg.2e87824684cb.back: Why is my tomato pachadi bitter?

seg.b367557bedfc.src: Usually the methi seeds burnt or there were too many. Use only ¼ tsp for 500 g tomatoes and fry them on medium-low heat, lifting them out as soon as they turn golden.
seg.b367557bedfc.t: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ 500 gꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b367557bedfc.back: Often because the fenugreek burnt or too much was added. For 500 g tomato use only ¼ teaspoon and fry on medium-low flame, taking it out as soon as it is golden colour.

seg.acdf33e5cc6d.src: Can I make tomato pachadi without tamarind?
seg.acdf33e5cc6d.t: ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.acdf33e5cc6d.back: Can tomato pachadi be made without tamarind?

seg.53fbd8949e0b.src: Yes, if your tomatoes are sour enough. Taste after cooking; ripe, sweet tomatoes need the small piece of tamarind for balance.
seg.53fbd8949e0b.t: ꯍꯣꯌ, ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯗꯤ꯫ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯔꯕ, ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯗꯤ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ꯫
seg.53fbd8949e0b.back: Yes, if your tomatoes are sour enough. Taste after cooking; ripe, sweet tomatoes need that small piece of tamarind to balance.

seg.2938c7a0249e.src: How long does tomato pachadi last?
seg.2938c7a0249e.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.2938c7a0249e.back: How long can tomato pachadi be kept?

seg.a35105e3a4af.src: About 4 days in the fridge in a clean, dry jar, as long as the tomatoes were cooked down well and you use a dry spoon.
seg.a35105e3a4af.t: ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 4 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ꯫
seg.a35105e3a4af.back: About 4 days in the fridge in a clean, dry jar, if the tomatoes were cooked well and a dry spoon was used.

seg.4dbd4103e7fb.back: టమాటా పచ్చడి · Recipe of tomato pachadi | 1acrefarms

seg.de4e2a65c3ae.src: టమాటా పచ్చడి. Andhra tomato pachadi: tomatoes cooked down with turmeric powder, ground coarse with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind, then tempered.
seg.de4e2a65c3ae.t: టమాటా పచ్చడి. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ: ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ, ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯕ꯫
seg.de4e2a65c3ae.back: టమాటా పచ్చడి. Andhra's tomato pachadi: tomato cooked with turmeric powder, ground not-fine with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind, then tempered.

seg.03de1ac75259.src: Tomato Pachadi: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.03de1ac75259.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.03de1ac75259.back: Tomato Pachadi: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.6357099a14e8.back: ¼ cup coriander leaves (if you like)

seg.3d323a4b41cc.src: Tomato pappu is the everyday dal of Andhra homes: toor dal (kandi pappu) cooked soft with tomatoes and green chillies, mashed smooth and finished with a garlic tempering. It is cooked most days of the week and eaten with hot rice, a spoon of ghee and an appadam or a pickle on the side.
seg.3d323a4b41cc.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯗꯥꯂꯅꯤ: ꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯥꯜ (ꯀꯟꯗꯤ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ) ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕꯒꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯍꯞꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯃꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯑꯞꯄꯗꯝ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯆꯥꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫
seg.3d323a4b41cc.back: Tomato pappu is the everyday dal of Andhra houses: toor dal (kandi pappu) cooked soft with tomato and green chilli, mashed soft and finished with a garlic tempering. It is cooked on almost all days of the week and eaten with hot rice, one spoon of ghee and appadam or pickle at the side.

seg.734276af9399.src: Our turmeric powder goes into the cooker with the dal and gives it a deep yellow colour. Sannam chilli powder adds a red tinge and a steady, medium heat that sits behind the sour tomato. This recipe serves 4.
seg.734276af9399.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ, ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.734276af9399.back: Our turmeric powder goes into the cooker together with the dal and gives it a thick yellow colour. Sannam chilli powder gives a little red colour and a steady, medium spiciness that remains after the sour tomato. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.8c5a5da215b1.src: Total includes letting the cooker release its steam.
seg.8c5a5da215b1.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯜ ꯊꯣꯀꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.8c5a5da215b1.back: Letting the cooker release its steam is included in the total.

seg.2c1a760b1cf8.src: Pressure-cook toor dal with tomatoes, green chillies and turmeric powder, mash it with Sannam chilli powder and salt, and finish with a garlic and mustard tempering.
seg.2c1a760b1cf8.t: ꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2c1a760b1cf8.back: Cook toor dal in the pressure cooker with tomato, green chilli and turmeric powder, mash with Sannam chilli powder and salt, and finish with a tempering of garlic and mustard seed.

seg.d102a6fa5887.src: ¾ cup toor dal ⟦1⟧kandi pappu, about 150 g⟦/1⟧
seg.d102a6fa5887.t: ꯀꯞ ¾ ꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯥꯜ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯟꯗꯤ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ, 150 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.d102a6fa5887.back: ¾ cup toor dal ⟦1⟧kandi pappu, about 150 g⟦/1⟧

seg.258b0303a820.src: ½ tsp turmeric powder ⟦1⟧goes in the cooker⟦/1⟧
seg.258b0303a820.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ⟦/1⟧
seg.258b0303a820.back: ½ teaspoon turmeric powder ⟦1⟧goes into the cooker⟦/1⟧

seg.25c2493b65be.src: 1 tsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧goes in after mashing; up to 2 tsp for more heat⟦/1⟧
seg.25c2493b65be.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯅꯣꯟꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.25c2493b65be.back: 1 teaspoon Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧goes in after mashing; up to 2 teaspoons for more spiciness⟦/1⟧

seg.f4f5c6c6e2d3.src: 2½ cups water ⟦1⟧plus ½ cup to adjust⟦/1⟧
seg.f4f5c6c6e2d3.back: 2½ cups water ⟦1⟧and ½ cup to adjust⟦/1⟧

seg.5f7d589d9776.src: 1 tbsp tamarind water (optional) ⟦1⟧if the tomatoes are not very sour⟦/1⟧
seg.5f7d589d9776.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ (ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ) ⟦1⟧ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯗꯔꯕꯗꯤ⟦/1⟧
seg.5f7d589d9776.back: 1 tablespoon tamarind water (if you like) ⟦1⟧if the tomatoes are not very sour⟦/1⟧

seg.4efa92e0ce99.src: Wash the toor dal in 2–3 changes of water and drain it.
seg.4efa92e0ce99.t: ꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ 2–3 ꯍꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4efa92e0ce99.back: Wash the toor dal changing the water 2–3 times and drain the water.

seg.3f536116a096.src: Put the dal in a pressure cooker with the tomatoes, green chillies, onion and 2½ cups of water.
seg.3f536116a096.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ, ꯇꯤꯜꯍꯧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2½ꯒꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3f536116a096.back: Put the dal in the pressure cooker with tomato, green chilli, onion and 2½ cups water.

seg.7d012f63f2a2.src: Pressure-cook the dal with the tomatoes, green chillies and turmeric powder for 4 whistles. Stir the turmeric powder into the water before closing the lid, then cook on medium heat.
seg.7d012f63f2a2.t: ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 4 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯀꯣꯛ ꯊꯨꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7d012f63f2a2.back: Cook the dal with tomato, green chilli and turmeric powder in the pressure cooker until 4 whistles. Before closing the lid mix the turmeric powder into the water, then cook on medium flame.

seg.5dccba018dbc.src: Let the pressure drop on its own, about 10 minutes. The dal is done when a grain mashes completely between two fingers.
seg.5dccba018dbc.t: ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛ ꯇꯥꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯔꯣꯝ꯫ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥ ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯂꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯆꯤꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.5dccba018dbc.back: Wait until the pressure goes down by itself, about 10 minutes. The dal is done when one grain mashes fully between two fingers.

seg.da76f4c700ad.src: Mash well; add the chilli powder and salt. Use a wooden masher (pappu gutti) or the back of a ladle and mash while the dal is still hot, until the tomatoes and dal turn into one smooth mix.
seg.da76f4c700ad.t: ꯐꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯎꯒꯤ ꯅꯣꯟꯅꯕ (ꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯒꯨꯠꯇꯤ) ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯦꯗꯂꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.da76f4c700ad.back: Mash well; add chilli powder and salt. Using a wooden masher (pappu gutti) or the back of the ladle, mash while the dal is still hot, until the tomato and dal become one soft blend.

seg.c1cb2443fbeb.src: Simmer 5 minutes with a splash of water. Add up to ½ cup water for a pouring consistency, and the tamarind water if using, and keep the heat on low so it does not catch.
seg.c1cb2443fbeb.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ½ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯊꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c1cb2443fbeb.back: Cook 5 minutes on low flame with a little water. For a pourable form add up to ½ cup water, and tamarind water if using, and keep the flame low so it does not stick at the bottom.

seg.b24472a45a67.src: Taste for salt and sourness, then stir in the coriander leaves and switch off.
seg.b24472a45a67.t: ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯔꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b24472a45a67.back: Taste the salt and sourness, then add coriander leaves, stir and turn off the flame.

seg.6f90b7e4f66a.src: Heat the ghee in a small pan on medium heat and add the mustard seeds; let them splutter.
seg.6f90b7e4f66a.t: ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯈꯣꯟꯖꯦꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6f90b7e4f66a.back: In a small pan heat ghee on medium flame and add mustard seed; let it crackle.

seg.0d1dd3c84a64.src: Fry mustard, cumin, garlic and curry leaves in the ghee; pour over. Add the cumin, garlic and dry red chillies after the mustard and fry until the garlic turns golden, then add the curry leaves and hing, and pour the sizzling tempering over the dal.
seg.0d1dd3c84a64.t: ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ, ꯖꯤꯔꯥ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯪꯒꯝ ꯃꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ, ꯆꯅꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯆꯤꯟ ꯆꯤꯟ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯤꯕ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0d1dd3c84a64.back: Fry mustard seed, cumin, garlic and curry leaves in ghee; pour on top. After the mustard seed add cumin, garlic and dry red chilli and fry until the garlic is golden colour, then add curry leaves and hing, and pour the sizzling tempering over the dal.

seg.81a1668adc10.src: Cover for 2 minutes so the tempering flavours the dal, then stir and serve hot.
seg.81a1668adc10.t: ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯂꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯀꯨꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.81a1668adc10.back: Cover 2 minutes so the tempering gives taste to the dal, then stir and serve hot.

seg.f904a5f14a1b.src: Mash the dal while it is hot for a smooth pappu. Once it cools, the grains set and stay lumpy.
seg.f904a5f14a1b.t: ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯄꯞꯄꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯃꯄꯨꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤ꯫
seg.f904a5f14a1b.back: For a soft pappu mash the dal while hot. When it cools the grains harden and stay as lumps.

seg.1a8211877e00.src: Sannam chilli powder is medium-hot. Start with 1 tsp; go up to 2 tsp for a spicier pappu.
seg.1a8211877e00.t: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ꯫ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯞꯄꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1a8211877e00.back: Sannam chilli powder is medium spicy. Start with 1 teaspoon; for a spicier pappu add up to 2 teaspoons.

seg.d85da2ea2cf7.src: Ripe, sour country tomatoes (natu tomatoes) give the best flavour; with mild hybrid tomatoes add the tamarind water.
seg.d85da2ea2cf7.t: ꯃꯍꯩ ꯌꯥꯔꯕ, ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯅꯥ (ꯅꯥꯇꯨ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ) ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ; ꯁꯨꯔꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯍꯥꯏꯕ꯭ꯔꯤꯗ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥꯒꯥ ꯏꯃꯂꯤꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d85da2ea2cf7.back: Ripe, sour local tomatoes (natu tomato) give the best taste; with less sour hybrid tomatoes add tamarind water.

seg.37f3ad1bf7b9.src: Let the garlic turn golden in the tempering before the curry leaves go in; pale garlic tastes raw.
seg.37f3ad1bf7b9.t: ꯀꯔꯤ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯟꯕ ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯆꯤꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯕꯒꯨꯝ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.37f3ad1bf7b9.back: Before adding curry leaves, let the garlic in the tempering become golden colour; pale-coloured garlic has a taste like it is uncooked.

seg.dfd3706fe457.src: Teja chilli powder: for a hotter pappu, use ½ tsp Teja chilli powder in place of the Sannam. Teja is very hot, so do not go over 1 tsp.
seg.dfd3706fe457.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯄꯞꯄꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯟꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ½ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯀꯅꯨ꯫
seg.dfd3706fe457.back: Teja chilli powder: for a spicier pappu use ½ teaspoon Teja chilli powder in place of Sannam. Teja is very spicy, so do not add more than 1 teaspoon.

seg.434f1a510bbb.src: Palakura tomato pappu: add 2 cups chopped spinach to the dal after mashing and simmer 5 minutes.
seg.434f1a510bbb.t: ꯄꯥꯂꯀꯨꯔꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ: ꯅꯣꯟꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯗꯥꯂꯗꯥ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯄꯥꯂꯪ ꯀꯞ 2 ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.434f1a510bbb.back: Palakura tomato pappu: after mashing add 2 cups chopped spinach to the dal and cook 5 minutes on low flame.

seg.8d7a932afdbe.src: Pesarapappu: make it with yellow moong dal and cook for 2 whistles only.
seg.8d7a932afdbe.t: ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯄꯞꯄꯨ: ꯑꯣꯔꯥꯕ ꯃꯨꯡ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 2 ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8d7a932afdbe.back: Pesarapappu: make it with yellow moong dal and cook only 2 whistles.

seg.94f44314ecbb.src: Serve hot with steamed rice, a spoon of ghee and an appadam or avakaya on the side. It also goes well with chapati.
seg.94f44314ecbb.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯑꯞꯄꯗꯝ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯥꯚꯀꯥꯌꯥꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯄꯥꯇꯤꯒꯥꯁꯨ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.94f44314ecbb.back: Serve hot with steamed rice, one spoon of ghee and appadam or avakaya at the side. It also goes very well with chapati.

seg.29a23e2fa864.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. The dal thickens when chilled; add a little hot water and heat through before serving.
seg.29a23e2fa864.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ; ꯄꯤꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.29a23e2fa864.back: Cover the leftover, keep in the fridge and eat within 2 days. When it cools the dal thickens; before serving add a little hot water and heat right to the inside.

seg.8e56f1d7c871.src: How many whistles for toor dal in a pressure cooker?
seg.8e56f1d7c871.t: ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ ꯀꯌꯥ?
seg.8e56f1d7c871.back: How many whistles for toor dal in the pressure cooker?

seg.562abdd39933.src: About 4 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure drop on its own. Older dal or dal that was not washed well may need 5.
seg.562abdd39933.t: ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 4 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯃꯛ ꯇꯥꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯉꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯤꯕ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯇꯕ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ 5 ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.562abdd39933.back: About 4 whistles on medium flame, then wait until the pressure goes down by itself. For old dal or dal not washed well 5 may be needed.

seg.6a800f643cf1.src: What is the difference between tomato pappu and sambar?
seg.6a800f643cf1.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯝꯕꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯈꯦꯟꯅꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.6a800f643cf1.back: What is the difference between tomato pappu and sambar?

seg.05135ac52968.src: Tomato pappu is a thick, mashed dal with a simple tempering and no sambar powder or vegetables. Sambar is thinner, uses tamarind, vegetables and a roasted spice powder.
seg.05135ac52968.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯕ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯅꯣꯟꯂꯕ ꯗꯥꯂꯅꯤ, ꯁꯥꯝꯕꯔ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯅꯥ-ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ꯫ ꯁꯥꯝꯕꯔꯗꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯕꯅꯤ, ꯏꯃꯂꯤ, ꯃꯅꯥ-ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫
seg.05135ac52968.back: Tomato pappu is a thick, mashed dal with a simple tempering, without sambar powder or vegetables. Sambar is more watery, and uses tamarind, vegetables and roasted masala powder.

seg.19117f898a31.src: Can I make tomato pappu without a pressure cooker?
seg.19117f898a31.t: ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.19117f898a31.back: Can tomato pappu be made without a pressure cooker?

seg.631df239c7a7.src: Yes. Soak the dal for 30 minutes and cook it in a covered pot with 3½ cups of water for about 40–45 minutes, stirring now and then, until it mashes easily.
seg.631df239c7a7.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 30 ꯆꯨꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯨꯞꯄꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 3½ꯒꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 40–45 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯃꯇꯝꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯌꯥꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.631df239c7a7.back: Yes. Soak the dal 30 minutes and cook in a pot with a lid with 3½ cups water about 40–45 minutes, stirring from time to time, until it can be mashed easily.

seg.b1140d6c02b4.src: Why is my tomato pappu too sour?
seg.b1140d6c02b4.t: ꯑꯩꯒꯤ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯤꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.b1140d6c02b4.back: Why is my tomato pappu very sour?

seg.6fb0505bf751.src: Some tomatoes are very sour. Simmer the dal a few more minutes and stir in a pinch of jaggery or a spoon of extra mashed dal to balance it.
seg.6fb0505bf751.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯈꯔꯗꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯔꯏ꯫ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯣꯟꯂꯕ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6fb0505bf751.back: Some tomatoes are very sour. Cook the dal a few more minutes on low flame and to balance add a little jaggery or one more spoon of mashed dal and stir.

seg.80a51a64344d.src: టమాటో పప్పు · Andhra Tomato Dal Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.80a51a64344d.t: టమాటో పప్పు · ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ | 1acrefarms
seg.80a51a64344d.back: టమాటో పప్పు · Recipe of Andhra's tomato dal | 1acrefarms

seg.7b91fd1a3bc3.src: టమాటో పప్పు. Andhra tomato dal: toor dal cooked soft with tomatoes and green chillies, our turmeric and Sannam chilli powder, and a garlic tempering. Serves 4.
seg.7b91fd1a3bc3.t: టమాటో పప్పు. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ, ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯝꯄꯔꯤꯡ꯫ ꯃꯤ 4ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ꯫
seg.7b91fd1a3bc3.back: టమాటో పప్పు. Andhra's tomato dal: toor dal cooked soft with tomato and green chilli, our turmeric and Sannam chilli powder, and a garlic tempering. For 4 people.

seg.bf96bcd14023.src: Tomato Pappu: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.bf96bcd14023.t: ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.bf96bcd14023.back: Tomato Pappu: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.9078b361da10.src: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Vellulli Kaaram · Lahsun Ki Sookhi Chutney
seg.9078b361da10.t: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · ꯚꯦꯜꯂꯨꯜꯂꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯝ · ꯂꯍꯁꯨꯟ ꯀꯤ ꯁꯨꯈꯤ ꯆꯠꯅꯤ
seg.9078b361da10.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Vellulli Karam · lahsun ki sukhi chutney [Hindi]

seg.464f01dcf4e8.src: Vellulli kaaram is the garlic chilli podi kept on Andhra dining tables: red chilli powder pounded with plenty of garlic, roasted coriander and cumin, and salt. Mixed into the first handful of hot rice with ghee, or sprinkled over idli and dosa with a little oil, it is a quick meal on busy days and a staple in tiffin boxes.
seg.464f01dcf4e8.t: ꯚꯦꯜꯂꯨꯜꯂꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯝ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯆꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯕꯜꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯆꯅꯝ-ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯀꯤ ꯄꯣꯗꯤꯅꯤ: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ, ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯈꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯏꯗꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯣꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯁꯤ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯤꯐꯤꯟ ꯕꯣꯛꯁꯇꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯅꯤ꯫
seg.464f01dcf4e8.back: Vellulli karam is the garlic-chilli podi kept on Andhra dining tables: red chilli powder ground with plenty of garlic, roasted coriander and cumin, and salt. Mixed into the first handful of hot rice with ghee, or sprinkled with a little oil on top of idli and dosa, it is the quickly eaten meal on busy days and an always-present item in the tiffin box.

seg.a9654adade5e.src: Our Teja chilli powder makes it deep red and very hot, the way Guntur homes like it. For less heat, use half Sannam chilli powder.
seg.a9654adade5e.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯟꯅꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯝꯕꯒꯨꯝ꯫ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯍꯟꯊꯅꯕꯥ, ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a9654adade5e.back: Our Teja chilli powder makes this deep red and very spicy, as Guntur homes like. To reduce the spiciness, use Sannam chilli powder for part.

seg.b43a6fdf4164.src: Total includes cooling the seeds and garlic before grinding.
seg.b43a6fdf4164.t: ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.b43a6fdf4164.back: Cooling the seeds and garlic before grinding is included in the total.

seg.501bcac1011e.src: Roast coriander and cumin, grind them, then pulse with Teja chilli powder, salt and lightly warmed garlic into a coarse podi. Eat it with hot rice and ghee, idli or dosa.
seg.501bcac1011e.t: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ ꯄꯣꯗꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ, ꯏꯗꯂꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯗꯣꯁꯥꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.501bcac1011e.back: Roast the coriander and cumin, grind, then with Teja chilli powder, salt and lightly heated garlic pulse in short bursts into a not-fine podi. Eat with hot rice and ghee, idli or dosa.

seg.e9ce857fe180.src: 25 garlic cloves ⟦1⟧about ½ cup, peeled; the thin inner skin can stay⟦/1⟧
seg.e9ce857fe180.t: ꯆꯅꯝ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ 25 ⟦1⟧ꯀꯞ ½ ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯃꯀꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ; ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯗꯥꯏꯕ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯏ⟦/1⟧
seg.e9ce857fe180.back: 25 garlic cloves ⟦1⟧about ½ cup, skin removed; the thin inner skin may stay⟦/1⟧

seg.47382aff4c0b.src: ¼ cup Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; see the tips to make it milder⟦/1⟧
seg.47382aff4c0b.t: ꯀꯞ ¼ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ; ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯇꯤꯞꯁꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.47382aff4c0b.back: ¼ cup Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very spicy; see the tips to reduce⟦/1⟧

seg.33ac26ca8201.t: ꯒꯨꯂꯤ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ 1 (ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ) ⟦1⟧ꯀꯥꯡꯕ, ꯃꯔꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.33ac26ca8201.back: 1 small marble-size tamarind (if you like) ⟦1⟧dry, seeds removed⟦/1⟧

seg.7bca54595a6a.src: Ghee or oil ⟦1⟧1 tsp per serving⟦/1⟧
seg.7bca54595a6a.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯆꯥꯕ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1⟦/1⟧
seg.7bca54595a6a.back: Ghee or oil ⟦1⟧1 teaspoon for each meal⟦/1⟧

seg.074d39a3f8b1.src: Peel the garlic and pat the cloves completely dry with a cloth; any water shortens how long the podi keeps.
seg.074d39a3f8b1.t: ꯆꯅꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯐꯤ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯁꯨ ꯄꯣꯗꯤ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.074d39a3f8b1.back: Remove the garlic skin and wipe the cloves gently with a cloth until fully dry; even a little water reduces the time the podi can be kept.

seg.33bb0e9eea87.src: Dry-roast the coriander and cumin seeds till fragrant; let them cool. Use a small pan on medium-low heat; this takes 1–2 minutes, and the coriander should turn a shade darker, not brown.
seg.33bb0e9eea87.t: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1–2 ꯆꯪꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.33bb0e9eea87.back: Roast the coriander and cumin seeds without oil until the smell comes; let cool. Use a small pan on medium-low flame; it takes 1–2 minutes, and the coriander should darken a little but should not become brown.

seg.a2f7a86fc993.src: Warm the garlic in 1 tsp oil for 2 minutes. Keep the heat low and stir; the cloves should soften slightly at the edges without browning. Let it cool.
seg.a2f7a86fc993.t: ꯆꯅꯝ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1ꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a2f7a86fc993.back: Heat the garlic in 1 teaspoon oil 2 minutes. Keep the flame low and stir; the cloves should become a little soft at the edges without browning. Let cool.

seg.a4d0f7c87bd5.src: Grind the seeds to a powder, then pulse with the chilli powder and salt. Add the tamarind with the seeds, if using, so it breaks down evenly.
seg.a4d0f7c87bd5.t: ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.a4d0f7c87bd5.back: Grind the seeds into powder, then pulse in short bursts with chilli powder and salt. If using tamarind add it together with the seeds, so it grinds evenly.

seg.c12763cab28c.src: Add the garlic and pulse in short bursts to a coarse, moist powder. Stop and scrape down the jar after every 2–3 pulses, as garlic sticks to the sides.
seg.c12763cab28c.t: ꯆꯅꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯞꯄ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ 2–3 ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯖꯥꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛ ꯈꯨꯠꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯤ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯞꯂꯤ꯫
seg.c12763cab28c.back: Add the garlic and pulse in short bursts until a not-fine, damp powder. After every 2–3 runs stop and scrape the side of the jar, because garlic sticks at the side.

seg.31358182425b.src: In a stone mortar, pound the seeds first, then the garlic with the salt, and work in the chilli powder last.
seg.31358182425b.t: ꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯃꯗꯥ, ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯝꯒꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.31358182425b.back: In a stone mortar, first pound the seeds, then the garlic with salt, and at the end mix in the chilli powder.

seg.29ac6dd20660.src: Taste a pinch with a little rice and ghee, and add salt if needed.
seg.29ac6dd20660.t: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.29ac6dd20660.back: Taste a little with a little rice and ghee, and add salt if needed.

seg.b4ccc3b591dd.src: Spread the podi on a plate for 10 minutes so the steam escapes, then pack it into a clean, dry jar.
seg.b4ccc3b591dd.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯣꯜ ꯊꯣꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯄꯣꯗꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10 ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b4ccc3b591dd.back: Spread the podi on a plate 10 minutes for the steam to go out, then put into a clean, dry jar.

seg.23d348ffe051.src: Teja is very hot; use half Sannam for a milder podi, or cut the chilli powder to 3 tbsp for the same garlic.
seg.23d348ffe051.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯏ; ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯄꯣꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.23d348ffe051.back: Teja is very spicy; for a milder podi use Sannam for part, or keeping the garlic the same, reduce the chilli powder to 3 tablespoons.

seg.948075d5f572.src: Dry the garlic well and warm it in oil; damp garlic makes the podi go off quickly.
seg.948075d5f572.t: ꯆꯅꯝ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯞꯄ ꯆꯅꯃꯅꯥ ꯄꯣꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.948075d5f572.back: Dry the garlic well and heat it in oil; damp garlic spoils the podi quickly.

seg.1a71c64c8c74.src: Pulse, do not run the mixer: run it long and the garlic turns into a paste.
seg.1a71c64c8c74.t: ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯔ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯒꯅꯨ: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯄꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.1a71c64c8c74.back: Pulse in short bursts, do not run the mixer a long time: if run a long time the garlic becomes paste.

seg.d1432fb9a627.src: Mix 1 tsp podi with 1 tsp ghee into a cup of hot rice; adjust to taste.
seg.d1432fb9a627.t: ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯄꯣꯗꯤ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ 1 ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯨꯅꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d1432fb9a627.back: In one cup of hot rice mix 1 teaspoon podi and 1 teaspoon ghee; adjust by tasting.

seg.bdc5e9728b98.src: With dals: dry-roast 1 tbsp chana dal and 1 tbsp urad dal with the seeds for a nuttier, slightly milder podi.
seg.bdc5e9728b98.t: ꯗꯥꯂꯒꯥ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯥꯠꯁ꯭ꯒꯨꯝꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯄꯣꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯎꯔꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
