seg.bdc5e9728b98.back: With dal: for a more nut-like, slightly milder podi roast 1 tablespoon chana dal and 1 tablespoon urad dal without oil together with the seeds.

seg.4d03eacf7428.src: Raw garlic: skip warming the garlic for a sharper taste, and eat it within a week.
seg.4d03eacf7428.t: ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯕ ꯆꯅꯝ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4d03eacf7428.back: Unheated garlic: for a stronger taste skip heating the garlic, and eat within one week.

seg.21139bdcd961.src: Medium heat: use 2 tbsp Teja and 2 tbsp Sannam chilli powder.
seg.21139bdcd961.t: ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.21139bdcd961.back: Medium spiciness: use 2 tablespoons Teja and 2 tablespoons Sannam chilli powder.

seg.bceea7c8cb4f.src: Mix with the first handful of hot rice and ghee, or sprinkle over idli, dosa or pesarattu with a little oil or ghee.
seg.bceea7c8cb4f.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯈꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯏꯗꯂꯤ, ꯗꯣꯁꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯦꯁꯔꯠꯇꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bceea7c8cb4f.back: Mix into the first handful of hot rice with ghee, or sprinkle with a little oil or ghee on top of idli, dosa or pesarattu.

seg.5fd9cf1554fd.src: Keep in a clean, dry, airtight jar for about 2 weeks at room temperature, or a month in the fridge. Always use a dry spoon.
seg.5fd9cf1554fd.t: ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5fd9cf1554fd.back: About 2 weeks in a clean, dry, airtight jar at home room temperature, or keep one month in the fridge. Always use a dry spoon.

seg.c58bc6538b2f.src: How do you make vellulli kaaram?

seg.0ecd3203de93.src: Roast coriander and cumin seeds, grind them, add chilli powder and salt, then pulse in peeled garlic cloves to a coarse, moist powder. Andhra homes often pound it in a stone mortar.
seg.0ecd3203de93.t: ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯀꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯕ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯞꯄ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯂꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏ꯫
seg.0ecd3203de93.back: Roast coriander and cumin seeds, grind, add chilli powder and salt, then add peeled garlic cloves and pulse in short bursts into a not-fine, damp powder. Andhra houses often grind it in a stone mortar.

seg.727d415cb888.src: How do I make garlic podi less spicy?
seg.727d415cb888.back: How to reduce the spiciness of garlic podi?

seg.e4231ea5cf7a.src: Use half Sannam chilli powder in place of half the Teja, or use 3 tbsp chilli powder in all. Eating it with plenty of ghee also takes the edge off.
seg.e4231ea5cf7a.t: ꯇꯦꯖꯥꯒꯤ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 3 ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯅꯥꯁꯨ ꯍꯥꯒꯠꯄ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.e4231ea5cf7a.back: Use Sannam chilli powder instead of the Teja portion, or use 3 tablespoons chilli powder in all. Eating it mixed with plenty of ghee also reduces the spiciness.

seg.982e854e4417.src: How long does vellulli kaaram last?
seg.982e854e4417.t: ꯚꯦꯜꯂꯨꯜꯂꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯝ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.982e854e4417.back: How long can vellulli karam be kept?

seg.a620f29950c0.src: About 2 weeks at room temperature in a dry, airtight jar, or a month in the fridge. Dry the garlic well and warm it in oil first so it lasts longer.
seg.a620f29950c0.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯕ-ꯏꯪꯕꯗꯥ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2 ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃꯥ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯕꯥ ꯌꯥꯅꯕꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a620f29950c0.back: About 2 weeks in a dry, airtight jar at home room temperature, or one month in the fridge. To keep it long, dry the garlic well and first heat it in oil.

seg.4c626acd1bdd.src: Can I use whole dried red chillies instead of chilli powder?
seg.4c626acd1bdd.t: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.4c626acd1bdd.back: Can whole dry red chillies be used in place of chilli powder?

seg.c796942589c3.src: Yes. Dry-roast about 20 dried red chillies with a few drops of oil until crisp, cool and grind them before adding the garlic.
seg.c796942589c3.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ 20 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c796942589c3.back: Yes. Roast about 20 dry red chillies in a little oil until crunchy, cool, and grind before adding garlic.

seg.a2202c094baa.back: వెల్లుల్లి కారం · Recipe of Vellulli Karam | 1acrefarms

seg.c5afa85ab56d.src: వెల్లుల్లి కారం. Andhra garlic chilli podi: roasted coriander and cumin pounded with garlic, salt and Teja chilli powder. Mix with hot rice and ghee, or idli and dosa.
seg.c5afa85ab56d.t: వెల్లుల్లి కారం. ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯅꯝ-ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯀꯤ ꯄꯣꯗꯤ: ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯐꯗꯤꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ, ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯗꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯣꯁꯥꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c5afa85ab56d.back: వెల్లుల్లి కారం. Andhra's garlic-chilli podi: roasted coriander and cumin ground with garlic, salt and Teja chilli powder. Mix with hot rice and ghee, or with idli and dosa.

seg.eff09f5a48ed.src: Vellulli Kaaram: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.eff09f5a48ed.t: ꯚꯦꯜꯂꯨꯜꯂꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯝ: 1acrefarms-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯗ, ꯁꯦꯝꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ
seg.eff09f5a48ed.back: Vellulli Karam: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and the way of making

seg.3b01a30ec3ce.src: Rub the chicken with curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Rest 30 minutes. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge while it rests.
seg.3b01a30ec3ce.t: ꯌꯦꯟꯁꯥꯕꯨ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯈꯥꯔ, ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯃꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 30 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3b01a30ec3ce.back: Rub the chicken with curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Keep 30 minutes. During that time keep the bowl covered in the fridge.

seg.6cceb77cd01b.src: 500 g fish pieces ⟦1⟧firm fish cut into thick steaks: rohu, catla (bochcha), korameenu (murrel) or seer fish (vanjaram)⟦/1⟧
seg.6cceb77cd01b.t: 500 g ꯉꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯉꯥ: ꯔꯣꯍꯨ, ꯀꯇꯂꯥ (ꯕꯣꯆꯥ), ꯀꯣꯔꯥꯃꯤꯅꯨ (ꯃꯔꯜ) ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯤꯌꯔ ꯐꯤꯁ (ꯚꯟꯖꯔꯝ)⟦/1⟧
seg.6cceb77cd01b.back: 500 g fish pieces ⟦1⟧firm-fleshed fish cut into big pieces: rohu, katla (bocha), korameenu (maral) or seer fish (vanjaram)⟦/1⟧

seg.3248f0a2bb4b.src: 40 g tamarind ⟦1⟧about two lemon-sized balls, soaked in 2 cups warm water for 15 minutes⟦/1⟧
seg.3248f0a2bb4b.t: 40 g ꯏꯃꯂꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯔꯣꯝ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ 2ꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯆꯨꯞꯂꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.3248f0a2bb4b.back: 40 g tamarind ⟦1⟧about two lemon-sizes, soaked 15 minutes in 2 cups hot water⟦/1⟧

seg.6efbfa504170.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently in the pan without stirring, until steaming hot all the way through.
seg.6efbfa504170.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯁꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯃꯩꯈꯨ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.6efbfa504170.back: Keep the leftover covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Without stirring in the pan, heat slowly until hot, until everything right to the inside is hot and steam comes out.

seg.379b410c6994.src: Firm river or sea fish cut into thick steaks: rohu, catla (bochcha), murrel (korameenu) or seer fish. Bony small fish also work but need gentle handling.
seg.379b410c6994.t: ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯁꯥ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯇꯨꯔꯦꯜ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯃꯨꯗ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯉꯥ: ꯔꯣꯍꯨ, ꯀꯇꯂꯥ (ꯕꯣꯆꯥ), ꯃꯔꯜ (ꯀꯣꯔꯥꯃꯤꯅꯨ) ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯤꯌꯔ ꯐꯤꯁ꯫ ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯉꯥ ꯑꯄꯤꯀꯁꯤꯡꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.379b410c6994.back: Firm-fleshed river or sea fish cut into big pieces: rohu, katla (bocha), maral (korameenu) or seer fish. Small fish with many bones also work, but must be used carefully.

seg.3af5b68fc2e1.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm the pulusu in a pan with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.
seg.3af5b68fc2e1.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 2 ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯨꯂꯨꯁꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯥꯒꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯁꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯃꯩꯈꯨ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫
seg.3af5b68fc2e1.back: Keep the leftover covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Heat the pulusu in a pan with a little water until everything right to the inside is hot and steam comes out.

seg.b4d28033bb05.src: Mutton vepudu: pressure-cook 500 g boneless mutton with the marinade and ½ cup water for 5–6 whistles, until tender, then fry it the same way.
seg.b4d28033bb05.t: ꯃꯇꯟ ꯚꯦꯄꯨꯗꯨ: ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕ ꯍꯃꯦꯡꯁꯥ 500 g ꯊꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ½ꯒꯥ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯀꯨꯀꯔꯗꯥ ꯍꯨꯏꯁꯜ 5–6 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b4d28033bb05.back: Mutton vepudu: cook 500 g boneless goat meat with ground masala and ½ cup water in a pressure cooker until 5–6 whistles, until soft, then fry it the same way.

seg.04112853a660.src: Both work. Boneless cooks faster and crisps more; small bone-in pieces have more flavour but need 6–8 minutes longer in their juices.
seg.04112853a660.t: ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯗꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏ; ꯁꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯩ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 6–8 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ꯫
seg.04112853a660.back: Both work. Boneless cooks quickly and becomes crunchier; small bone-in pieces have more flavour but need 6–8 more minutes in their juice.

seg.d20a641bec03.src: Pack it for a lunch box or a short journey and eat it within about 4 hours. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat them within a day.
seg.d20a641bec03.t: ꯂꯟꯆ ꯕꯣꯛꯁ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯞꯗꯕ ꯆꯠꯄꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯨꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯨꯡ 4 ꯔꯣꯝꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d20a641bec03.back: If packed for a lunch box or a long journey, eat within about 4 hours. Keep the leftover covered in the fridge and eat within one day.

seg.bc9078e02646.src: Either the lemon juice was cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Add the turmeric last, switch off the stove right after and stir for only 5–10 seconds; add the lemon juice to the rice, off the heat.
seg.bc9078e02646.t: ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯀꯈꯤꯕꯅꯥ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟꯗ 5–10 ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯆꯥꯝꯄ꯭ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bc9078e02646.back: Because the lemon juice was boiled or the turmeric burnt in oil. Add the turmeric at the end, then immediately turn off the fire and stir only 5–10 seconds; add the lemon juice to the rice after taking it off the fire.

seg.c288f67fcabb.src: Pour the other cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan; a thin pan lets the ragi catch.
seg.c288f67fcabb.t: ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯞ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯈꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯈꯥ ꯄꯥꯗꯕ ꯄꯦꯟꯗꯥ ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.c288f67fcabb.back: Put the remaining cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan; in a thin-bottomed pan the ragi sticks/burns at the bottom.

seg.e87c26125f87.src: Can I use cane jaggery in ragi java?
seg.e87c26125f87.t: ꯔꯥꯒꯤ ꯖꯥꯋꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.e87c26125f87.back: Can sugarcane jaggery be used in ragi java?

seg.a9a06390a945.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery (cheruku bellam) and stir it in after switching off the stove, so the milk does not split. It gives a lighter colour and a milder, caramel-like sweetness.
seg.a9a06390a945.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯆꯦꯔꯨꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯠꯊꯠꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯣꯏ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯍꯜꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯄ, ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.a9a06390a945.back: Yes. Use an equal amount of grated sugarcane jaggery (cheruku bellam) and stir it in after turning off the fire, so the milk does not split. This makes the colour lighter and gives a gentler, caramel-like sweet taste.

seg.e7cb15cc47e2.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Reheat in a pan only until steaming hot all the way through; longer reheating makes the prawns tough.
seg.e7cb15cc47e2.t: ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 1ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯁꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯃꯩꯈꯨ ꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯥꯖꯤꯡ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.e7cb15cc47e2.back: Keep the leftover covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Heat in a pan only until everything right to the inside is hot and steam comes out; if heated longer than that the prawns become hard.

seg.ea5408ec0853.src: Can I make sunnundalu with cane jaggery?
seg.ea5408ec0853.back: Can sunnundalu be made with sugarcane jaggery?

seg.ec48010dffbe.src: Yes. Grate the cane jaggery (cheruku bellam) finely and use the same amount as palm jaggery. The laddus turn lighter in colour, with a milder, caramel-like sweetness.
seg.ec48010dffbe.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯆꯦꯔꯨꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯇꯞꯄ, ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.ec48010dffbe.back: Yes. Grate the sugarcane jaggery (cheruku bellam) finely and use it equal to palm jaggery. The laddus' colour becomes lighter and the taste becomes a gentler, caramel-like sweet.

seg.767f9e16fa95.src: Raw garlic: skip warming the garlic for a sharper taste; keep it in the fridge and eat it within 3 days.
seg.767f9e16fa95.t: ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯕ ꯆꯅꯝ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 3ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.767f9e16fa95.back: Unroasted garlic: for a stronger taste skip roasting the garlic; keep it in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

seg.8665687f81ce.src: Keep in a clean, dry, airtight jar in the fridge and use it within 2 weeks. Always use a dry spoon.
seg.8665687f81ce.t: ꯁꯦꯡꯂꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8665687f81ce.back: Keep in a clean, dry, airtight jar in the fridge and use within 2 weeks. Always use a dry spoon.

seg.367798df40e3.src: Up to 2 weeks in a dry, airtight jar in the fridge. Dry the garlic well and warm it in oil first, and always use a dry spoon.
seg.367798df40e3.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ 2 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.367798df40e3.back: Can be kept in a dry, airtight jar in the fridge up to 2 weeks. Dry the garlic well and first cook it in oil, and always use a dry spoon.

seg.1d41be2d17f9.src: Yes. Roast about 20 dried red chillies in a few drops of oil until crisp, cool and grind them before adding the garlic.
seg.1d41be2d17f9.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ 20 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯥꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯛ-ꯀꯔꯛ ꯍꯥꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯅꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1d41be2d17f9.back: Yes. Roast about 20 dry red chillies in a little oil until crisp, let cool and grind before adding the garlic.

seg.c473a3556357.back: Sweet dish of Andhra · for 2 people · 10 minutes

seg.7099f7c35107.src: Bellam Atukulu ⟦1⟧(Sweet Poha with Palm Jaggery)⟦/1⟧
seg.7099f7c35107.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯑꯇꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨ ⟦1⟧(ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ)⟦/1⟧
seg.7099f7c35107.back: Bellam Atukulu ⟦1⟧(sweet poha made with palm jaggery)⟦/1⟧

seg.b6b19d4f12bb.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Bellam Atukulu · gur wale pohe (Hindi words in Meetei script)

seg.c9c11f5b43da.src: Bellam atukulu is the 10-minute sweet of Telugu homes. It is the poha offered to Krishna on Krishnashtami, recalling Kuchela's gift, and it is also a quick sweet for children after school. The poha is only rinsed, never cooked in water, and then tossed in warm jaggery syrup.
seg.c9c11f5b43da.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯑꯇꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 10ꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯁ꯭ꯅꯥꯁ꯭ꯇꯃꯤꯗꯥ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯁ꯭ꯅꯗꯥ ꯀꯠꯄ ꯄꯣꯍꯥꯅꯤ, ꯀꯨꯆꯦꯂꯥꯒꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯣꯜ ꯅꯤꯡꯁꯤꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁ꯭ꯀꯨꯂꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯏ꯫ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯦ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.c9c11f5b43da.back: This bellam atukulu is a 10-minute sweet dish of Telugu homes. It is the poha offered to Krishna on Krishnashtami, it makes one remember Kuchela's gift, and it is also a sweet dish that can be made quickly for children after they come back from school. The poha is only washed in water, it is not cooked in water at all, after that it is mixed into warm jaggery syrup.

seg.8594fedb25dc.src: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery gives it a deep brown colour and a rich, slightly smoky sweetness. This recipe serves 2.
seg.8594fedb25dc.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯟꯕ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯤ 2ꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ꯫
seg.8594fedb25dc.back: Our thati bellam palm jaggery gives it a deep brown colour and a deep, slightly smoke-like sweet taste. This recipe is for 2 people.

seg.25e28614accb.src: Prep includes 5 minutes for the rinsed poha to soften.
seg.25e28614accb.t: ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.25e28614accb.back: Preparation includes 5 minutes for softening the washed poha.

seg.b9dedcd705aa.src: Soften thick poha, toss it in warm palm jaggery syrup with coconut and cardamom, and finish with ghee.
seg.b9dedcd705aa.t: ꯃꯣꯇꯥ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯔꯁꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b9dedcd705aa.back: Soften the thick poha, mix it into warm palm-jaggery syrup together with coconut and cardamom, and finish with ghee.

seg.e13864ccb71f.src: ½ cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 90 g⟦/1⟧
seg.e13864ccb71f.t: ꯀꯞ ½ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧90 g ꯔꯣꯝ⟦/1⟧
seg.e13864ccb71f.back: ½ cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 90 g⟦/1⟧

seg.b78c520dca8d.src: ½ cup grated coconut ⟦1⟧white part only⟦/1⟧
seg.b78c520dca8d.t: ꯀꯞ ½ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ⟦/1⟧
seg.b78c520dca8d.back: ½ cup grated coconut ⟦1⟧white part only⟦/1⟧

seg.2d6d2ff14f71.src: ¼ tsp cardamom powder ⟦1⟧or the crushed seeds of 2–3 pods⟦/1⟧
seg.2d6d2ff14f71.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ¼ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ⟦1⟧ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ 2–3ꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.2d6d2ff14f71.back: ¼ small spoon cardamom powder ⟦1⟧or the crushed seeds of 2–3 cardamoms⟦/1⟧

seg.5f1854fd1277.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ 6–8, ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.5f1854fd1277.back: 6–8 cashews, if wanted ⟦1⟧fried in ghee until gold colour⟦/1⟧

seg.fbe7b4b8afbc.src: Put the poha in a sieve and pick out any bits of husk.
seg.fbe7b4b8afbc.t: ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯀꯣꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯁꯛ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯅꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fbe7b4b8afbc.back: Put the poha in a strainer and, if there are pieces of husk, pick them out.

seg.b0f730c0b062.src: Rinse the poha in a sieve under running water for a few seconds, drain, and leave it for 5 minutes to soften. It should feel soft when pressed, but not wet.
seg.b0f730c0b062.t: ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯜꯂꯤꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯊꯣꯛꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 5 ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯅꯝꯂꯕꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯨꯔꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫
seg.b0f730c0b062.back: Keeping the poha in the strainer, wash it a few seconds under running water, let the water drain, and keep it 5 minutes to soften. When pressed it should be soft, but it should not be soaked with water.

seg.0a3e2261d7bc.src: Grate the palm jaggery finely, breaking up any hard lumps.
seg.0a3e2261d7bc.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯆꯧꯕꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ꯫
seg.0a3e2261d7bc.back: Grate the palm jaggery finely, crushing the hard big lumps.

seg.d2b892bf70af.src: Melt the palm jaggery with 2 tbsp water on a low flame, then strain it. Wipe the pan and pour the syrup back in.
seg.d2b892bf70af.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2ꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯡꯅꯥ ꯍꯨꯠꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯁ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d2b892bf70af.back: Melt the palm jaggery together with 2 big spoons of water on low fire, then strain. Wipe the kadai clean and pour the syrup back into that place.

seg.d073ead78aef.src: If you are using cashews, fry them in a little ghee till golden.
seg.d073ead78aef.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d073ead78aef.back: If using cashews, fry them in a little ghee until gold colour.

seg.62c17a0f01a5.src: Add the poha, coconut and cardamom to the warm syrup and toss gently on a low flame for 1–2 minutes, until every flake is coated. Use a light hand so the flakes do not break.
seg.62c17a0f01a5.t: ꯁꯥꯕ ꯔꯁ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ, ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 1–2 ꯇꯞꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯔꯁ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.62c17a0f01a5.back: Add the poha, coconut and cardamom to the warm syrup and mix gently on low fire for 1–2 minutes, until syrup coats each poha. Mix with a gentle hand so the poha does not break.

seg.d1abe3d7557d.src: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the flakes are coated; longer cooking makes them chewy.
seg.d1abe3d7557d.t: ꯄꯣꯍꯥꯗꯥ ꯔꯁ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯄꯒꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ; ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯆꯥꯕꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.d1abe3d7557d.back: As soon as the syrup coats the poha, take the kadai off the fire; if cooked too long it becomes hard to eat.

seg.c91ffab6359d.src: Finish with the ghee and cashews. Serve warm or at room temperature.
seg.c91ffab6359d.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯖꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯕ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c91ffab6359d.back: Finish with ghee and cashews. Serve warm, or at room temperature (not heated, not cooled).

seg.544ea222a497.src: Use thick poha. Thin poha turns mushy in the syrup.
seg.544ea222a497.t: ꯃꯣꯇꯥ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯥꯟꯕ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯔꯁꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.544ea222a497.back: Use thick poha. Thin poha becomes too soft in the syrup and breaks apart.

seg.0f56d718ca89.src: Do not soak the poha in a bowl of water; a quick rinse is enough, or it turns soft and sticky.
seg.0f56d718ca89.t: ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯕꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯆꯨꯍꯟꯒꯅꯨ; ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯏ, ꯅꯠꯇ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯅꯦꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.0f56d718ca89.back: Do not soak the poha in a bowl of water at all; only a quick wash is enough, otherwise it becomes soft and sticks together.

seg.972f174730fe.src: Keep the syrup warm, not bubbling, when the poha goes in, so the flakes coat evenly.
seg.972f174730fe.t: ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯔꯁ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯎꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯞ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯔꯁ ꯀꯞꯀꯅꯤ꯫
seg.972f174730fe.back: When adding the poha keep the syrup warm, it should not be boiling, then the syrup will coat each poha equally.

seg.8496cfe4aa1d.src: With milk: pour 2–3 tbsp warm milk over the finished poha for a softer sweet.
seg.8496cfe4aa1d.t: ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯃꯒꯥ: ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯔꯕ ꯄꯣꯍꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2–3 ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.8496cfe4aa1d.back: With milk: for a softer sweet dish, pour 2–3 big spoons of warm milk over the prepared poha.

seg.bb5e4ee879e6.src: With sesame: add 1 tbsp roasted sesame seeds along with the coconut.
seg.bb5e4ee879e6.t: ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡꯒꯥ: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯔꯣꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bb5e4ee879e6.back: With sesame: add 1 big spoon of roasted sesame together with the coconut.

seg.25d7247d3c7b.src: Serve it as naivedyam on Krishnashtami, or as a quick sweet for children after school.
seg.25d7247d3c7b.t: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯁ꯭ꯅꯥꯁ꯭ꯇꯃꯤꯗꯥ ꯅꯩꯕꯦꯗ꯭ꯌꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁ꯭ꯀꯨꯂꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.25d7247d3c7b.back: Offer it as naivedyam on Krishnashtami, or give it to children after they come back from school as a sweet dish that can be made quickly.

seg.1170385c1b79.src: Best eaten the day it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat them the next day; the poha firms up as it stands.
seg.1170385c1b79.t: ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯩ꯫ ꯂꯦꯃꯍꯧꯔꯤꯕꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯞꯊꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.1170385c1b79.back: Eating it the same day it is made is best. Cover what is left, keep it in the fridge and eat it the next day; if kept, the poha becomes hard.

seg.6acb206e9df4.src: Which poha is best for bellam atukulu?
seg.6acb206e9df4.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯑꯇꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯀꯔꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯍꯥꯅꯥ ꯈ꯭ꯕꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯩ?
seg.6acb206e9df4.back: What kind of poha is best for bellam atukulu?

seg.7cb97f8423cf.src: Thick poha (atukulu). It holds its shape in the warm syrup; thin poha turns mushy.
seg.7cb97f8423cf.t: ꯃꯣꯇꯥ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ (ꯑꯇꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨ)꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯔꯁꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ; ꯄꯥꯟꯕ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯏ꯫
seg.7cb97f8423cf.back: Thick poha (atukulu). It keeps its shape in warm syrup; thin poha becomes too soft and breaks apart.

seg.ba8eb1721096.src: Can I make bellam atukulu with cane jaggery?
seg.ba8eb1721096.t: ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯑꯇꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.ba8eb1721096.back: Can bellam atukulu be made with sugarcane jaggery?

seg.2a1aa941db07.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery (cheruku bellam). It turns lighter in colour, with a caramel-like sweetness.
seg.2a1aa941db07.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯆꯦꯔꯨꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯛꯏ, ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫
seg.2a1aa941db07.back: Yes. Use grated sugarcane jaggery (cheruku bellam) in the same amount. The colour becomes a bit lighter, with a caramel-like sweet taste.

seg.88008fa2d0e6.src: Why is my bellam atukulu sticky?
seg.88008fa2d0e6.t: ꯑꯩꯒꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ ꯑꯇꯨꯀꯨꯂꯨ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯥ ꯊꯨꯡꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯂꯤꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.88008fa2d0e6.back: Why did my bellam atukulu stick together?

seg.a6945e480c9a.src: The poha was soaked or cooked too long. Rinse it for only a few seconds, and take the pan off the heat as soon as every flake is coated.
seg.a6945e480c9a.t: ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯨꯍꯅꯈꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯈꯤ꯫ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯁꯦꯡꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯔꯁ ꯀꯞꯂꯛꯄꯒꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a6945e480c9a.back: The poha was soaked in water or cooked too long. Wash it only a few seconds, and take the kadai off the fire as soon as syrup coats each poha.

seg.d4c0fab65bf7.src: Why is it made on Krishnashtami?
seg.d4c0fab65bf7.back: Why is it made on Krishnashtami?

seg.51ab1914ac8d.src: It recalls the story of Kuchela, who brought a handful of poha to his friend Krishna as his only gift.
seg.51ab1914ac8d.t: ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯀꯨꯆꯦꯂꯥꯒꯤ ꯋꯥꯔꯤ ꯅꯤꯡꯁꯤꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯃꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯔꯨꯞ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯁ꯭ꯅꯗꯥ ꯃꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯣꯍꯥ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯄꯨꯔꯛꯈꯤ꯫
seg.51ab1914ac8d.back: It recalls the story of Kuchela; he brought a handful of poha as his only gift to his friend Krishna.

seg.aa55b9fd31e8.back: Kobbari Undalu ⟦1⟧(laddu of coconut and jaggery)⟦/1⟧

seg.753ec27036d4.src: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Kobbari Undalu · Nariyal Gud Ke Laddu
seg.753ec27036d4.t: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · ꯀꯣꯕ꯭ꯕꯔꯤ ꯎꯟꯗꯂꯨ · ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯌꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯀꯦ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ
seg.753ec27036d4.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Kobbari Undalu · nariyal gur ke laddu (Hindi words in Meetei script)

seg.de7ddbad7bf0.src: Kobbari undalu are the coconut laddus Andhra homes make for festivals, naivedyam and an everyday sweet. They need only coconut, jaggery, cardamom and a spoon of ghee. The jaggery is melted and strained, the coconut is cooked in it on a low flame until the mix holds together, and the laddus are rolled by hand while still warm.
seg.de7ddbad7bf0.t: ꯀꯣꯕ꯭ꯕꯔꯤ ꯎꯟꯗꯂꯨ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯁꯤ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯨꯝꯍꯩ, ꯅꯩꯕꯦꯗ꯭ꯌꯝ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ, ꯒꯨꯔ, ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ꯫ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯟꯂꯤ, ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯁꯥꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯂꯤ꯫
seg.de7ddbad7bf0.back: Kobbari undalu is a coconut laddu made in Andhra homes for festivals, naivedyam and an every-day sweet dish. It needs only coconut, jaggery, cardamom and one spoon of ghee. The jaggery is melted and strained, the coconut is cooked in it on low fire until the mixture binds, and the laddus are made by hand while it is still hot.

seg.089fb020d00e.src: Our Cheruku Bellam gives them a light golden colour and a mellow caramel taste. This recipe makes about 14 laddus.
seg.089fb020d00e.t: ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯆꯦꯔꯨꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯃꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯗꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ, ꯀꯦꯔꯥꯃꯦꯜꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤ꯫ ꯔꯦꯁꯤꯄꯤ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ 14 ꯔꯣꯝ ꯐꯪꯏ꯫
seg.089fb020d00e.back: Our cheruku bellam gives them a little gold colour and a mild, caramel-like taste. This recipe gives about 14 laddus.

seg.d9e7175cce3e.src: Allow another 15 minutes for the laddus to cool before you store them.
seg.d9e7175cce3e.t: ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯝꯃꯤꯟꯅꯔꯤꯉꯩꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 15 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d9e7175cce3e.back: Give 15 more minutes for cooling before storing the laddus.

seg.80b59063a128.src: Melt cane jaggery, cook it with grated coconut till it comes together, add cardamom and ghee, and roll into laddus.
seg.80b59063a128.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜꯒꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.80b59063a128.back: Melt the sugarcane jaggery, cook with grated coconut until it binds, add cardamom and ghee, and make laddus.

seg.9dbfabbc7bd0.src: 2 cups grated coconut ⟦1⟧1 medium coconut; grate only the white part⟦/1⟧
seg.9dbfabbc7bd0.t: ꯀꯞ 2 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ⟦1⟧ꯃꯌꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ 1; ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.9dbfabbc7bd0.back: 2 cups grated coconut ⟦1⟧1 medium coconut; grate the white part only⟦/1⟧

seg.fa687abb7dd1.src: 1 cup grated cane jaggery ⟦1⟧about 180 g; pound or grate the pieces first⟦/1⟧
seg.fa687abb7dd1.t: ꯀꯞ 1 ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ⟦1⟧180 g ꯔꯣꯝ; ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ⟦/1⟧
seg.fa687abb7dd1.back: 1 cup grated sugarcane jaggery ⟦1⟧about 180 g; first crush the pieces or grate⟦/1⟧

seg.1ca2ce946869.src: 1 tbsp ghee ⟦1⟧plus a little for greasing your palms⟦/1⟧
seg.1ca2ce946869.t: ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 1 ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯅꯕꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ⟦/1⟧
seg.1ca2ce946869.back: 1 big spoon ghee ⟦1⟧and a little more for applying on the hands⟦/1⟧

seg.ccf1a746b971.src: 10 cashews, optional ⟦1⟧broken and fried golden in ghee⟦/1⟧
seg.ccf1a746b971.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ 10, ꯄꯥꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ⟦/1⟧
seg.ccf1a746b971.back: 10 cashews, if wanted ⟦1⟧broken and fried in ghee until gold colour⟦/1⟧

seg.15ef8686cc9e.src: Grate the coconut, leaving out the brown skin so the laddus stay light in colour.
seg.15ef8686cc9e.t: ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯨ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.15ef8686cc9e.back: Grate the coconut, removing the brown-coloured skin, so that the laddu's colour stays light.

seg.00b442d7f507.src: Pound or grate the cane jaggery into small pieces so it melts evenly.
seg.00b442d7f507.t: ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯁꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯞ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯒꯅꯤ꯫
seg.00b442d7f507.back: Crush the sugarcane jaggery into small pieces or grate it, so that it will melt equally.

seg.c25e0610c714.src: Melt the jaggery with 2 tbsp water on a low flame, then strain it through a fine sieve. This catches any grit or bits of cane from the block.
seg.c25e0610c714.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ 2ꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯤꯟꯕ ꯆꯥꯟꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯛ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯁꯤꯡ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯤ꯫
seg.c25e0610c714.back: Melt the jaggery together with 2 big spoons of water on low fire, then strain through a fine strainer. This removes the small hard grains that come from the jaggery pieces or the small pieces of sugarcane.

seg.3eb20f2a7136.src: Return it to the pan, add the coconut and cook on medium-low, stirring, until the mix leaves the sides of the pan and holds together, 12–15 minutes. Keep stirring so it does not catch at the bottom.
seg.3eb20f2a7136.t: ꯃꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 12–15꯫ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯂꯦꯞꯇꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3eb20f2a7136.back: Pour it back into the kadai, add the coconut and cook while mixing on medium-low fire, until the mixture comes away from the sides of the kadai and binds, 12–15 minutes. Mix without stopping so it does not stick/burn at the bottom.

seg.e1985b8e5f9c.src: If you are using cashews, fry them in a little ghee till golden while the mix cooks.
seg.e1985b8e5f9c.t: ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯁꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯥꯏ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e1985b8e5f9c.back: If using cashews, while the mixture is cooking fry them in a little ghee until gold colour.

seg.1dc27e2d9b3e.src: Stir in the cardamom, ghee and cashews. Take the pan off the heat.
seg.1dc27e2d9b3e.t: ꯏꯂꯥꯏꯆꯤ, ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯖꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1dc27e2d9b3e.back: Add the cardamom, ghee and cashews and mix. Take the kadai off the fire.

seg.d4ee96780aba.src: Let it cool till you can handle it, grease your palms with ghee and roll it into small balls. Press each one firmly so it holds together.
seg.d4ee96780aba.t: ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯁꯣꯛꯄ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯈꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯑꯃꯃꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯄꯥꯉ꯭ꯒꯜ ꯀꯅꯕꯥ ꯅꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.d4ee96780aba.back: Let it cool until the hand can touch it, apply ghee on the hands and make small laddus. Press each one firmly so it binds.

seg.3753ea8bc7d0.src: Set the laddus on a greased plate and let them cool completely before you store them.
seg.3753ea8bc7d0.t: ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯝꯃꯤꯟꯅꯔꯤꯉꯩꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.3753ea8bc7d0.back: Put the laddus on a plate with ghee applied and let them cool completely before storing.

seg.fb3de84de9f6.src: If the mix won't hold a shape, cook it 2 minutes more. If it sets too hard, sprinkle in a spoon of warm milk and press again.
seg.fb3de84de9f6.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔꯅꯥ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯉꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ, ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯂꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ, ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.fb3de84de9f6.back: If the mixture cannot keep its shape, cook 2 more minutes. If it has become too hard, add a spoon of warm milk little by little and press again.

seg.71475e1a7345.src: Keep the flame at medium-low; on a high flame the jaggery darkens and the laddus turn hard.
seg.71475e1a7345.t: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯌꯥꯏ-ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯩ ꯆꯥꯎꯕꯗꯥ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯀꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.71475e1a7345.back: Keep it on medium-low fire; on high fire the jaggery's colour becomes dark and the laddus become hard.

seg.46a2e2b2d323.src: Roll the laddus while the mix is still warm; once it cools completely it will not bind.
seg.46a2e2b2d323.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯁꯥꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅꯥ ꯏꯪꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯣꯏ꯫
seg.46a2e2b2d323.back: Make the laddus while the mixture is still hot; after it has completely cooled it does not bind.

seg.b277c024adad.src: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for darker laddus with a slightly smoky sweetness.
seg.b277c024adad.t: ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b277c024adad.back: Palm jaggery: for laddus with a darker colour and a slight smoke-like sweet taste, use grated palm jaggery in the same amount.

seg.7b597df04222.src: Dry coconut: use the same amount of grated dry coconut (kopra); the mix comes together faster, so watch it closely.
seg.7b597df04222.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯅꯥꯔꯤꯀꯦꯜ (ꯀꯣꯞꯔꯥ) ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ; ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯐꯖꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7b597df04222.back: Dry coconut: use grated dry coconut (kopra) in the same amount; the mixture binds quickly, therefore watch carefully.

seg.676bca051e10.src: Kobbari burfi: spread the cooked mix on a greased plate, let it set a little and cut it into squares instead of rolling laddus.
seg.676bca051e10.t: ꯀꯣꯕ꯭ꯕꯔꯤ ꯕꯔꯐꯤ: ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ, ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯕ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯟꯗꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯀꯟꯊꯍꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯥꯛ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯁꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.676bca051e10.back: Kobbari burfi: instead of making laddus, spread the cooked mixture on a plate with ghee applied, let it harden a little, and cut into four-sided pieces.

seg.80538d77ab41.src: Serve as an everyday sweet, offer them as naivedyam, or add them to the festival sweet plate.
seg.80538d77ab41.t: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯤꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯩꯕꯦꯗ꯭ꯌꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯀꯠꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯨꯝꯍꯩꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯄ꯭ꯂꯦꯇꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.80538d77ab41.back: Give as an every-day sweet dish, offer as naivedyam, or add to a festival sweet plate.

seg.6f3252f28ef8.src: Keep in an airtight container and eat within 3 days at room temperature, or within a week if kept in the fridge.
seg.6f3252f28ef8.t: ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯁꯥꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯏꯪꯍꯟꯗꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 3ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯐ꯭ꯔꯤꯖꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯞꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.6f3252f28ef8.back: Keep in an air-tight box and, if kept inside the house not heated or cooled, eat within 3 days, or if kept in the fridge eat within a week.

seg.f232fb960e89.src: Why are my kobbari undalu not holding shape?
seg.f232fb960e89.t: ꯑꯩꯒꯤ ꯀꯣꯕ꯭ꯕꯔꯤ ꯎꯟꯗꯂꯨ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯊꯝꯗꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.f232fb960e89.back: Why does my kobbari undalu not keep its shape?

seg.1cf59b528a13.src: The mix needs a little more cooking. Put it back on a low flame for 2 minutes, stirring, until it leaves the sides of the pan, then roll it while it is still warm.
seg.1cf59b528a13.t: ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 2 ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯂꯥꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛꯁꯨ ꯁꯥꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯥꯗꯨ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1cf59b528a13.back: The mixture must cook a little more. Keeping it back on low fire, cook while mixing for 2 minutes, until it comes away from the sides of the kadai, then make laddus while it is still hot.

seg.9371fa8705cd.src: Why did my laddus turn hard?
seg.9371fa8705cd.back: Why did my laddus become hard?

seg.ee988ba3472f.src: The jaggery was cooked too long or on too high a flame. Sprinkle in a spoon of warm milk, mix and press again. Next time, take the pan off the heat as soon as the mix holds together.
seg.ee988ba3472f.t: ꯒꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯕ ꯃꯩꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯈꯤ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯁꯉꯒꯣꯝ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ, ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅꯥ ꯅꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯃꯊꯪꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ, ꯃꯤꯛꯁꯆꯔ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯂꯛꯄꯒꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ee988ba3472f.back: The jaggery was cooked too long or on too high a fire. Add a spoon of warm milk little by little, mix and press again. Next time, take the kadai off the fire as soon as the mixture binds.

seg.d830316a6adb.src: Can I make kobbari undalu with palm jaggery?
seg.d830316a6adb.t: ꯀꯣꯕ꯭ꯕꯔꯤ ꯎꯟꯗꯂꯨ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.d830316a6adb.back: Can kobbari undalu be made with palm jaggery?

seg.813bf680c8a8.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The laddus turn darker, with a slightly smoky sweetness.
seg.813bf680c8a8.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯦꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯥꯜ ꯒꯨꯔ (ꯇꯥꯇꯤ ꯕꯦꯜꯂꯝ) ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯂꯥꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯨꯔꯛꯏ, ꯈꯔꯥ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯊꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯍꯤꯛꯀꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ꯫
seg.813bf680c8a8.back: Yes. Use grated palm jaggery (thati bellam) in the same amount. The laddu's colour becomes darker, with a slight smoke-like sweet taste.

seg.ea6121eb3993.src: How long do kobbari undalu keep?
seg.ea6121eb3993.t: ꯀꯣꯕ꯭ꯕꯔꯤ ꯎꯟꯗꯂꯨ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯕꯒꯦ?
seg.ea6121eb3993.back: How long does kobbari undalu stay good?

seg.26aba27412dc.src: About 3 days in an airtight container at room temperature, and up to a week in the fridge.

seg.13ab70df1ad4.src: How to check chilli powder at home
seg.13ab70df1ad4.back: How to check chilli powder at home

seg.1841c397898f.src: FSSAI's standard says chilli powder must be dry and free from dirt, added colouring matter, flavouring matter and mineral oil. Its testing manual has methods for finding brick powder, added starch, added colour, colours that dissolve in oil, and the dyes Sudan III and Rhodamine B.
seg.1841c397898f.t: FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯇꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯑꯃꯣꯠ, ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ, ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯅꯔꯦꯜ ꯑꯣꯏꯜ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯗꯥ ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ, ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ, ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ III ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯣꯗꯥꯃꯤꯟ B ꯗꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯁꯤꯡ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.1841c397898f.back: According to FSSAI's standard, chilli powder must be dry, and it says it must not contain dirt, added colouring matter, flavour-giving [or: taste-giving; unsure] matter and mineral oil. Its testing manual has methods for detecting brick powder, added starch, added colour, oil-soluble colours, and Sudan III and Rhodamine B dyes.

seg.a0af610174e4.src: Some of this you can check in your kitchen with a glass of water, your fingers and a few drops of iodine. Some, like Sudan dyes, only a lab can find. This guide covers both. Try the checks on any chilli powder you buy.
seg.a0af610174e4.t: ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯈꯔꯗꯤ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯈꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯃꯥ, ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯃꯔꯤꯛ ꯈꯔꯥꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯈꯔꯗꯤ, ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ ꯗꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯨꯝꯕ, ꯂꯦꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯊꯤꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫ ꯒꯥꯏꯗ ꯑꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯂꯩ꯫ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯕꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a0af610174e4.back: Some of these you can check in your kitchen with a glass of water, your hands and a few drops of iodine. Some, like Sudan dyes, only a lab can detect. This guide has both. Please do these checks on every chilli powder you have.

seg.b356a193952e.src: ⟦1⟧Our two chilli powders⟦/1⟧Left: Sannam chilli powder. Right: Teja chilli powder. Both from chillies grown in Palnadu and Guntur, sun-dried and packed in Narasaraopet.
seg.b356a193952e.t: ⟦1⟧ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯅꯤ⟦/1⟧ꯑꯣꯏ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯁꯟꯅꯝ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ꯫ ꯌꯦꯠ ꯊꯪꯕꯗꯥ: ꯇꯦꯖꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ꯫ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯄꯜꯅꯥꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯔꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯅꯤ, ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯅꯔꯁꯔꯥꯎꯄꯦꯠꯇꯥ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯈꯤꯕ꯫
seg.b356a193952e.back: ⟦1⟧Our two chilli powders⟦/1⟧On the left side: Sannam chilli powder. On the right side: Teja chilli powder. Both are made from chillies grown in Palnadu and Guntur, dried in the sun and packed in Narasaraopet.

seg.a574ced14407.src: Sprinkle a teaspoon of chilli powder on a glass of water and do not stir. Colour streaks running down at once point to added colour, and bits still floating after the powder sinks point to sawdust or bran. Rub the sediment: grit points to brick powder or sand, a soapy feel to soapstone. Iodine turning the powder blue points to added starch. Dyes such as Sudan I do not show in water; for those, use a lab.
seg.a574ced14407.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯒꯅꯨ꯫ ꯈꯨꯗꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯔꯀꯄ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯁꯨ ꯇꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯎꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯦꯟ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ꯫ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯐꯥꯎꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯕꯥꯂꯨ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ, ꯁꯥꯕꯣꯟꯒꯨꯝ ꯐꯥꯎꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯣꯞꯁ꯭ꯇꯣꯟ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ꯫ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯕ꯭ꯂꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ꯫ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ I ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯗꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯎꯕ ꯐꯪꯗꯦ; ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.a574ced14407.back: Sprinkle a small spoonful of chilli powder little by little over the top of a glass of water and do not mix. Right away, streaks of colour going down to the bottom show added colour, and particles still floating after the powder has sunk show wood powder or bran. Rub the matter that sank to the bottom: if you feel hard particles it shows brick powder or sand, if it feels soapy it shows soapstone. If iodine turns the powder blue, it shows added starch. Dyes like Sudan I do not show in water; for them use a lab.

seg.11caa5f871e4.src: What FSSAI checks chilli powder for
seg.11caa5f871e4.back: What FSSAI checks in chilli powder

seg.7d346e39c41e.src: FSSAI's chilli powder standard does not allow added colouring matter. FSSAI's tests look for colours that dissolve in water, colours that dissolve in oil, and the dyes Sudan III and Rhodamine B.
seg.7d346e39c41e.t: FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯌꯥꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡ, ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ III ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯣꯗꯥꯃꯤꯟ B ꯗꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯤꯔꯤ꯫
seg.7d346e39c41e.back: FSSAI's chilli powder standard does not allow colouring matter to be added. FSSAI's tests detect water-soluble colours, oil-soluble colours, and Sudan III and Rhodamine B dyes.

seg.dab0f1b06607.src: Sudan I is used to colour oils, fats, waxes, and shoe and floor polish. The Indian Standard on quick tests for adulterants says Sudan III, much used in wax polishes, has been used to make chilli pods shine, and so finds its way into chilli powder.
seg.dab0f1b06607.t: ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ I ꯑꯁꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ, ꯐꯦꯠ, ꯋꯦꯛꯁ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯣꯡꯎꯞ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐ꯭ꯂꯣꯔꯒꯤ ꯄꯣꯂꯤꯁꯇꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯟ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ, ꯋꯦꯛꯁ ꯄꯣꯂꯤꯁꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ III ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯃꯍꯩꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯈꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯌꯧꯔꯀꯏ꯫
seg.dab0f1b06607.back: Sudan I is used to colour oil, fat, wax, and shoe and floor polish. The Indian standard on tests for detecting adulteration says that Sudan III, which is used a lot in wax polish, was used to make chilli fruits [pods] bright, and for that reason it reaches chilli powder.

seg.65d2132b3a71.src: Brick powder, sand, salt, talc and soapstone
seg.65d2132b3a71.t: ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯕꯥꯂꯨ, ꯊꯨꯝ, ꯇꯥꯜꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯣꯞꯁ꯭ꯇꯣꯟ
seg.65d2132b3a71.back: Brick powder, sand, salt, talc and soapstone

seg.eaaa28049f76.src: FSSAI's household tests list these for chilli powder. The Indian Standard says brick powder is mixed in to increase bulk.
seg.eaaa28049f76.t: FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯁꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯟ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯦꯅꯒꯠꯍꯟꯅꯕꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.eaaa28049f76.back: These are included in FSSAI's home tests for chilli powder. The Indian standard says brick powder is added to increase weight.

seg.591f55c64be8.src: FSSAI's manual tests powdered spices other than turmeric for added starch. The Indian Standard notes that colour is also added to chilli powder to hide added starch.
seg.591f55c64be8.t: FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯅꯠꯇꯕ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯊꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯏ꯫ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯟ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯅꯥ ꯐꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯂꯣꯠꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.591f55c64be8.back: FSSAI's manual tests for detecting added starch in other powder spices that are not turmeric. The Indian standard reveals that colour is also added to chilli powder to hide [ꯂꯣꯠꯅꯕꯥ] added starch.

seg.6cdabb4ac9cc.src: Both float on water, which is how FSSAI's household tests spot them.
seg.6cdabb4ac9cc.t: ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯎꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯌꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯕꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯊꯤꯗꯣꯛꯏ꯫
seg.6cdabb4ac9cc.back: Both float on water, and FSSAI's home tests detect them by this.

seg.2ad2a1900226.t: ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ 1: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯕꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ
seg.2ad2a1900226.back: Check 1: Glass of water and rubbing test

seg.5ebb4d43f1c6.src: Sprinkle one teaspoon of chilli powder on top. Do not stir.
seg.5ebb4d43f1c6.t: ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯒꯅꯨ꯫
seg.5ebb4d43f1c6.back: Sprinkle a small spoonful of chilli powder little by little on top. Do not mix.

seg.e11be0844965.src: Watch the first minute. Look for coloured streaks running down from the powder.
seg.e11be0844965.t: ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯔꯀꯄ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e11be0844965.back: Watch the first minute. Look for streaks of colour going down from the powder to the bottom.

seg.14ad43586f91.src: Leave it until most of the powder has sunk. Look at the surface for bits still floating.
seg.14ad43586f91.t: ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯀꯁꯨ ꯇꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.14ad43586f91.back: Let most of the powder sink. Look for particles still floating on top of the water.

seg.379262f468f1.src: Pour off most of the water and rub the sediment at the bottom between your fingers.
seg.379262f468f1.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕ ꯍꯨꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.379262f468f1.back: Pour off most of the water and rub the matter that sank to the bottom between your fingers.

seg.9d20132af7ae.src: Colour streaks running down at once
seg.9d20132af7ae.back: Streaks of colour going down to the bottom right away

seg.4dd6d7d4418f.src: Added colour that dissolves in water
seg.4dd6d7d4418f.back: Added colour that dissolves in water

seg.99d03e1725f4.src: Bits still floating after the powder sinks
seg.99d03e1725f4.back: Particles floating even after the powder has sunk

seg.f211ed47d57c.t: ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯂꯩꯕꯒꯨꯝ ꯐꯥꯎꯕ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ
seg.f211ed47d57c.back: Sunk matter that feels like it has hard particles

seg.0778aeb79734.src: White sediment that feels soapy and smooth
seg.0778aeb79734.t: ꯁꯥꯕꯣꯟꯒꯨꯝ ꯐꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ
seg.0778aeb79734.back: Sunk matter that feels soapy and smooth [or: soft] white

seg.92ba3085667d.src: No sign of what this check can find.
seg.92ba3085667d.t: ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯊꯤꯕ ꯉꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯀꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯝ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯥ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫
seg.92ba3085667d.back: There is no sign of anything this check can detect.

seg.e4f5d2924afa.src: Possible adulteration. Stop using that batch and get it tested.
seg.e4f5d2924afa.t: ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯈꯤꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.e4f5d2924afa.back: Other matter may have been added. Set aside the batch you used and get it tested.

seg.e5e493d4cb12.src: ⟦1⟧Why it works.⟦/1⟧ Colours that dissolve in water leave the powder and run down as streaks. Brick powder is heavy and settles to the bottom, while sawdust and bran float.
seg.e5e493d4cb12.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯦ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯔꯛꯏ꯫ ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯛꯏ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯎꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯦꯟ ꯇꯥꯎꯏ꯫
seg.e5e493d4cb12.back: ⟦1⟧What this does.⟦/1⟧ Water-soluble colours separate from the powder and sink to the bottom as streaks. Brick powder sinks to the bottom because it is heavy, but wood powder and bran float.

seg.551c97147aa3.src: ⟦1⟧What it misses.⟦/1⟧ Dyes that do not dissolve in water stay in the powder. Sudan I is one: it does not dissolve in water, and it is used to colour oils, fats and waxes. Chilli powder coloured with such dyes can pass this check. Only a lab test can rule them out.
seg.551c97147aa3.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯊꯤꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕꯒꯦ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯕ ꯗꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯊꯣꯀꯊꯗꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥꯛ ꯂꯦꯡꯗꯅꯥ ꯂꯩꯔꯤ꯫ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ I ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ, ꯐꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯦꯛꯁꯇꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯅꯕꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫ ꯑꯁꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯗꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯔꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯄꯥꯁ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯍꯅꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.551c97147aa3.back: ⟦1⟧What it cannot detect.⟦/1⟧ Dyes that do not dissolve in water stay in the powder without moving, not coming out of the powder. Sudan I is one of them: it does not dissolve in water, and is used to give colour to oil, fat and wax. A chilli powder that looks good [or: bright] because it was coloured by such a dye can pass this. Only a lab test can show that they are not there.

seg.5bbec3bc6fbf.src: Wash your hands after the rub test, before you touch your eyes.
seg.5bbec3bc6fbf.t: ꯁꯨꯕꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯃꯤꯠ ꯁꯣꯛꯠꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯁꯦꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5bbec3bc6fbf.back: After doing the rubbing test, wash your hands before touching your eyes.

seg.36726998b551.src: Check 2: the iodine test for starch

seg.3d76d0b2a476.src: FSSAI's manual uses the iodine test for powdered spices other than turmeric, so chilli powder can take it. ⟦1⟧Our turmeric guide⟦/1⟧ explains why turmeric is left out.
seg.3d76d0b2a476.t: FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯅꯥ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯅꯠꯇꯕ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯁꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯒꯥꯏꯗ⟦/1⟧ꯗꯥ ꯇꯥꯀꯄꯤꯔꯤ꯫
seg.3d76d0b2a476.back: FSSAI's manual uses this iodine test for other powder spices that are not turmeric, therefore it can be done on chilli powder. Why turmeric was left out is shown in ⟦1⟧our turmeric guide⟦/1⟧.

seg.c7d23b036696.src: Put half a teaspoon of chilli powder on a white saucer.
seg.c7d23b036696.t: ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯁꯣꯁꯔ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯇꯪꯈꯥꯏ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.c7d23b036696.back: Put half a small spoonful of chilli powder on a white saucer.

seg.9b2fb67a0f9a.src: Add a few drops of tincture of iodine from a chemist.
seg.9b2fb67a0f9a.t: ꯀꯦꯃꯤꯁ꯭ꯠꯀꯤ ꯗꯨꯀꯥꯅꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯔꯕ ꯇꯤꯉꯆꯔ ꯑꯣꯐ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯃꯔꯤꯛ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9b2fb67a0f9a.back: Add a few drops of tincture of iodine bought from a chemist's shop.

seg.2d93dfc80312.src: Look at the colour where the drops land.
seg.2d93dfc80312.t: ꯃꯔꯤꯛꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯥꯔꯀꯄ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.2d93dfc80312.back: Look at the colour at the place where the drops fell.

seg.c698ff17efbf.back: After that, throw the powder away.

seg.0db85a4ff58c.src: Points to added starch. Stop using that batch and get it tested. On red powder a faint change is hard to judge, so if you are not sure, let a lab decide.
seg.0db85a4ff58c.t: ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ꯫ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯍꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯍꯣꯡꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯪꯕ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯟꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯗꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯂꯦꯕꯅꯥ ꯋꯥꯔꯦꯞ ꯂꯧꯍꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.0db85a4ff58c.back: Shows added starch. Set aside the batch and get it tested. In red powder, if it changes only a little it is very hard to see, so if you are not sure, let a lab decide.

seg.ed4a959013d8.src: ⟦1⟧Why it works.⟦/1⟧ Iodine turns blue when it meets starch.
seg.ed4a959013d8.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯇꯧꯕꯒꯦ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆꯒꯥ ꯊꯦꯡꯅꯔꯀꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯂꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫
seg.ed4a959013d8.back: ⟦1⟧What this does.⟦/1⟧ Iodine turns blue when it meets starch.

seg.5adf326d0b8f.back: Get these done by a lab

seg.9e0f62706054.src: Acid and solvent tests at home
seg.9e0f62706054.back: Acid and solvent tests at home

seg.f5e28e97055b.src: The methods in FSSAI's manual for brick powder, added colour, oil-soluble colours, Sudan III and Rhodamine B in chilli powder use strong acids and solvents such as chloroform, petroleum ether, hexane and acetone. The acids can cause burns, and several of the solvents catch fire easily. They belong in a lab, not a kitchen.
seg.f5e28e97055b.t: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ, ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ, ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡ, ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ III ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯣꯗꯥꯃꯤꯟ B ꯊꯤꯅꯕꯥ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯟꯕ ꯑꯦꯁꯤꯗꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀ꯭ꯂꯣꯔꯣꯐꯣꯔꯝ, ꯄꯦꯠꯔꯣꯂꯤꯌꯝ ꯏꯊꯔ, ꯍꯦꯛꯁꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯦꯁꯤꯇꯣꯟꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯁꯣꯜꯕꯦꯟꯇꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫ ꯑꯦꯁꯤꯗꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯍꯟꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯣꯜꯕꯦꯟꯇ ꯈꯔꯗꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯀꯏ꯫ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯂꯦꯕꯇꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯆꯥꯛꯈꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫
seg.f5e28e97055b.back: The methods in FSSAI's manual for detecting brick powder, added colour, oil-soluble colours, Sudan III and Rhodamine B in chilli powder use strong acids and solvents such as chloroform, petroleum ether, hexane and acetone. Acids can burn, and some solvents catch fire easily. They should be used in a lab, not in the kitchen.

seg.1e30ce9ef855.src: For a sure answer, send a sample to a NABL-accredited food testing lab. Ask it to test for added colours, including Sudan dyes, and against FSSAI's chilli powder standard. Its limits include moisture up to 11%, total ash up to 8%, and ash insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid up to 1.3%, all by weight, with both ash limits on a dry basis. Keep the powder in its sealed pack or a clean sealed bag, and note the batch number printed on the pack.
seg.1e30ce9ef855.t: ꯁꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯅꯕꯥ, NABL-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯅꯤꯡꯕ ꯄꯤꯔꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯄꯜ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ ꯗꯥꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗꯀꯥ ꯆꯥꯡꯗꯝꯅꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯅꯕꯥ ꯍꯪꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯂꯤꯃꯤꯠꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ 11% ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯃꯩꯐꯨ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ 8% ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯍꯥꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯣꯛꯂꯣꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯦꯁꯤꯗꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯕ ꯃꯩꯐꯨ 1.3% ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ, ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅꯥ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩꯐꯨꯒꯤ ꯂꯤꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯕ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅꯥ꯫ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯁꯤꯜ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯦꯡꯕ, ꯁꯤꯜ ꯇꯧꯔꯕ ꯕꯦꯒ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯝꯕꯔ ꯏꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.1e30ce9ef855.back: To confirm, send a sample to a food testing lab accredited by NABL. Ask for testing for added colours including Sudan dyes, and against FSSAI's chilli powder standard. The standard's limits include moisture not more than 11%, total ash not more than 8%, and ash insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid not more than 1.3%, all by weight, and both ash limits by dried weight. Keep the powder in its own sealed pack or a clean, sealed bag, and write down the batch number on the pack.

seg.8ef59aeeebe4.src: An FSSAI licence or registration number.

seg.f90b0f258a47.src: Net quantity, a batch or lot number, and a best-before date.
seg.f90b0f258a47.t: ꯅꯦꯠ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ, ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯠ ꯅꯝꯕꯔ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ-ꯕꯤꯐꯣꯔ ꯇꯥꯡ꯫
seg.f90b0f258a47.back: Net weight, batch or lot number, and best-before date.

seg.fa3907160dbb.src: The ingredients. FSSAI allows up to 2% edible vegetable oil by weight in chilli powder, but only if the label says which oil and how much.
seg.fa3907160dbb.t: ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯕ ꯄꯥꯝꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯥꯎ 2% ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯂꯦꯕꯦꯂꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯤ ꯊꯥꯎꯅꯣ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫
seg.fa3907160dbb.back: Ingredients included. FSSAI allows up to 2% edible vegetable oil by weight in chilli powder, but only if the label says what oil and how much is included.

seg.616cb55edf33.src: Where it was grown, and the chilli variety if named. Our ⟦1⟧Sannam⟦/1⟧ and ⟦2⟧Teja⟦/2⟧ packs say Palnadu and Guntur.
seg.616cb55edf33.t: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯈꯜ꯫ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ⟦1⟧ꯁꯟꯅꯝ⟦/1⟧ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ⟦2⟧ꯇꯦꯖꯥ⟦/2⟧ ꯄꯦꯛꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯄꯜꯅꯥꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ꯫
seg.616cb55edf33.back: Where it was grown, and if the name is included, the chilli variety. Our ⟦1⟧Sannam⟦/1⟧ and ⟦2⟧Teja⟦/2⟧ packs say Palnadu and Guntur.

seg.5766b566dbba.src: Use a dry spoon, and keep the jar away from steam from the stove.
seg.5766b566dbba.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯨꯂꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯀꯄ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯩꯈꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯞꯅꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.5766b566dbba.back: Use a dry spoon, and keep the jar away from steam coming from the stove.

seg.ae76fa3c0a37.src: Keep it in a cool, dry place, out of direct sunlight.
seg.ae76fa3c0a37.t: ꯏꯪꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯀꯤ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯍꯛꯊꯦꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.ae76fa3c0a37.back: Keep in a cool [or: cold], dry place that direct sunlight does not fall on.

seg.cee32139c40b.src: Use it within the best-before date on the pack, in dishes such as ⟦1⟧vellulli kaaram⟦/1⟧, ⟦2⟧gongura pachadi⟦/2⟧ or ⟦3⟧tomato pachadi⟦/3⟧.
seg.cee32139c40b.t: ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯕꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ-ꯕꯤꯐꯣꯔ ꯇꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗꯥ, ⟦1⟧ꯚꯦꯜꯂꯨꯜꯂꯤ ꯀꯥꯔꯝ⟦/1⟧, ⟦2⟧ꯒꯣꯡꯒꯨꯔꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ⟦/2⟧ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ⟦3⟧ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯆꯆꯗꯤ⟦/3⟧ꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.cee32139c40b.back: Before the best-before date on the pack, use it in dishes like ⟦1⟧Vellulli Karam⟦/1⟧, ⟦2⟧Gongura Pachadi⟦/2⟧ or ⟦3⟧Tomato Pachadi⟦/3⟧.

seg.13c76694dc1e.src: How do I check chilli powder for brick powder at home?
seg.13c76694dc1e.t: ꯌꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯂꯩꯕꯔꯥ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯅꯒꯗꯒꯦ?
seg.13c76694dc1e.back: How to check at home whether chilli powder has brick powder?

seg.3e87e1d30613.src: Put a teaspoon of chilli powder in a glass of water and let it settle. Pour off most of the water and rub the sediment between your fingers: grit points to brick powder or sand, and a white residue that feels soapy and smooth points to soapstone.
seg.3e87e1d30613.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯆꯥꯃꯆ ꯑꯄꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯛꯅꯕꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕ ꯍꯨꯟꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯨꯝꯂꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇꯥ ꯁꯨꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯀꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯦꯛ ꯐꯥꯎꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯏꯠꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯕꯥꯂꯨ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯕꯣꯟꯒꯨꯝ ꯐꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯦꯝꯕ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯃꯍꯧꯔꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯅꯥ ꯁꯣꯞꯁ꯭ꯇꯣꯟ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ꯫
seg.3e87e1d30613.back: Sprinkle a small spoonful of chilli powder into a glass of water and leave it to sink. Pour off most of the water and rub what sank between your fingers: if you feel hard particles it shows brick powder or sand, and soapy-feeling, smooth white leftover matter shows soapstone.

seg.f609f5773557.src: Can the water test detect Sudan dye in chilli powder?
seg.f609f5773557.t: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯅꯥ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ ꯗꯥꯏ ꯊꯤꯕ ꯉꯝꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.f609f5773557.back: Can the water test detect Sudan dye in chilli powder?

seg.7bd8af24de2f.src: No. Sudan I does not dissolve in water, so it cannot run out as streaks. FSSAI's manual tests for Sudan III and for oil-soluble colours with solvents such as hexane and petroleum ether, so those tests need a lab.
seg.7bd8af24de2f.t: ꯉꯝꯗꯦ꯫ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ I ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯗꯦ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯅꯥ ꯁꯨꯗꯥꯟ III ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯍꯦꯛꯁꯦꯟ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯦꯠꯔꯣꯂꯤꯌꯝ ꯏꯊꯔꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯁꯣꯜꯕꯦꯟꯇꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯃꯊꯧ ꯇꯥꯏ꯫
seg.7bd8af24de2f.back: It cannot. Sudan I does not dissolve in water, therefore it cannot come out as streaks. FSSAI's manual tests for Sudan III and oil-soluble colours with solvents like hexane and petroleum ether, therefore a lab is needed for those tests.

seg.d63c02ec2e5c.src: Does the iodine test work on chilli powder?
seg.d63c02ec2e5c.t: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠꯅꯥ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯇꯧꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.d63c02ec2e5c.back: Does the iodine test work on chilli powder?

seg.01e86c518d41.src: Yes. FSSAI's manual uses the iodine test for powdered spices other than turmeric, and chilli powder is one of them. A blue colour points to added starch.
seg.01e86c518d41.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ FSSAI-ꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯌꯦꯂꯅꯥ ꯑꯥꯏꯑꯣꯗꯤꯟ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯅꯠꯇꯕ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ꯫ ꯕ꯭ꯂꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯥꯔꯆ ꯇꯥꯛꯂꯤ꯫
seg.01e86c518d41.back: Yes. FSSAI's manual uses this iodine test for other powder spices that are not turmeric, and chilli powder is one of them. If it turns blue, it shows added starch.

seg.75e20911cd47.src: Is bright red chilli powder a sign of adulteration?
seg.75e20911cd47.t: ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯕ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯈꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯝꯅꯤ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.75e20911cd47.back: Does very bright red chilli powder mean it is a sign that other matter was added?

seg.dcfec3eff0b8.src: Colour alone does not tell you. The water check looks for colour that leaves the powder and runs down as streaks, not for how red the powder looks, and a lab can test for added colours.
seg.dcfec3eff0b8.t: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯂꯤꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯊꯣꯛꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯦꯟꯊꯔꯀꯄ ꯃꯆꯨꯅꯤ, ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯎꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯗꯨ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.dcfec3eff0b8.back: Colour alone does not prove it. What the water check looks at is colour that comes out of the powder and goes down to the bottom as streaks, not how red the powder looks, and a lab can test for added colours.

seg.54f85d34859f.src: Stop using that batch and keep the pack. Contact the seller with the batch number, or send a sample to a NABL-accredited food testing lab for a sure answer.
seg.54f85d34859f.t: ꯕꯦꯆ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯝꯕꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅꯥ ꯌꯣꯟꯕ ꯃꯤꯗꯥ ꯄꯥꯎ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯁꯣꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯅꯕꯥ NABL-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯅꯤꯡꯕ ꯄꯤꯔꯕ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝꯄꯜ ꯊꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.54f85d34859f.back: Set aside the batch and keep the pack. Inform the seller together with the batch number, or to confirm, send a sample to a food testing lab accredited by NABL.

seg.a7d8a3890045.src: Both are grown in Palnadu and Guntur and packed in Narasaraopet.
seg.a7d8a3890045.t: ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯄꯜꯅꯥꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯔꯁꯔꯥꯎꯄꯦꯠꯇꯥ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯏ꯫
seg.a7d8a3890045.back: Both are grown in Palnadu and Guntur and packed in Narasaraopet.

seg.3ed867d1961c.t: కారం కల్తీ · ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯟꯕꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ | 1acrefarms

seg.8b7a90a6aed6.src: Konda pasupu means hill turmeric: turmeric grown in hill country. Plains turmeric grows on farmland in districts such as Guntur.

seg.8b7a90a6aed6.back: Konda pasupu is hill turmeric: turmeric grown in hill areas. In Andhra Pradesh this includes the agency hills of the Eastern Ghats around Araku Valley, Chintapalle and Paderu, where mostly tribal farmers grow turmeric. Plains turmeric is grown in the fields of districts like Guntur.

seg.404d008584f4.src: FSSAI's standard for turmeric powder is the same wherever it grew. What changes is the place, the variety, and how it is grown and dried. This guide covers each of those, what curcumin is, how to cook with each and how to compare two turmerics fairly. There is a Telugu section further down.

seg.404d008584f4.back: The FSSAI standard for turmeric powder applies wherever it is grown. What changes is the place, the variety, and how it is grown and dried. This guide has each of them, what curcumin is, how each should be cooked, and how to compare the two turmerics properly. Below there is a Telugu section.

seg.10eec083bb3d.src: Hill turmeric (konda pasupu) grows in hill country, such as the Eastern Ghats around Araku, where most tribal farmers grow it. Plains turmeric grows on farmland in districts such as Guntur. Both are boiled, dried and ground, and FSSAI holds both to the same standard. Curcumin, the yellow pigment in turmeric, changes with variety, soil, climate and processing, so the word hill or plains does not tell you how much a turmeric has. Cook with both the same way.
seg.10eec083bb3d.t: ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ (ꯀꯣꯟꯗꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ) ꯑꯔꯀꯨꯒꯤ ꯑꯀꯣꯕꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯁ꯭ꯇꯔꯟ ꯘꯥꯠꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯂꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯏ, ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯕꯦꯜ ꯂꯧꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯊꯥꯏ꯫ ꯇꯃꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯤ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯗꯤꯁ꯭ꯠꯔꯤꯛꯇꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯕꯨꯛꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯏ꯫ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯂꯧꯏ꯫ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ, ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ, ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯈꯜ, ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ-ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯃꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯏ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯡ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯝ ꯍꯥꯌꯕ ꯋꯥꯍꯩꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯂꯩꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕ ꯈꯪꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯗꯥ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.10eec083bb3d.back: Hill turmeric (konda pasupu) is grown in hill areas like the Eastern Ghats around Araku, where mostly tribal farmers grow it. Plains turmeric is grown in the fields of districts like Guntur. Both are boiled, dried and ground, and FSSAI applies one and the same standard for both. Curcumin, the colour-giving substance in turmeric, changes according to the variety, soil, weather and the way of processing, so the word hill or plains does not show how much curcumin is in a turmeric. Please use both the same way in cooking.

seg.a9e5b44e1be6.src: ⟦1⟧Hill turmeric.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR's report on the Paderu agency, the tribal hill country of the Eastern Ghats that takes in Araku Valley, Chintapalle and Paderu, says turmeric is grown there by most tribal farmers.
seg.a9e5b44e1be6.t: ⟦1⟧ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯑꯔꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯂꯤ, ꯆꯤꯟꯇꯥꯄꯜꯂꯦ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯗꯦꯔꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯏꯁ꯭ꯇꯔꯟ ꯘꯥꯠꯀꯤ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯕꯦꯜ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯂꯝ, ꯄꯥꯗꯦꯔꯨ ꯑꯦꯖꯦꯟꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯥ ICAR-IISR-ꯒꯤ ꯔꯤꯄꯣꯔꯠꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯕꯦꯜ ꯂꯧꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯊꯥꯏ꯫
seg.a9e5b44e1be6.back: ⟦1⟧Hill turmeric.⟦/1⟧ The tribal hill areas of the Eastern Ghats that include Araku Valley, Chintapalle and Paderu; the ICAR-IISR report on the Paderu agency says that there mostly tribal farmers grow turmeric.

seg.736e66a0b5de.src: ⟦1⟧Plains turmeric.⟦/1⟧ Guntur district lists turmeric among its commercial crops, with cotton, chillies and tobacco. Duggirala, in Guntur, has a turmeric processing cluster that makes processed turmeric and turmeric powder. In 2022, Guntur district was divided into three districts: Guntur, Palnadu and Bapatla.
seg.736e66a0b5de.t: ⟦1⟧ꯇꯃꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯤꯁ꯭ꯠꯔꯤꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯀꯩꯊꯦꯂꯗꯥ ꯌꯣꯟꯅꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯥꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯩꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ, ꯀꯣꯇꯟ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯥꯈꯨꯒꯨꯝꯅꯥ, ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯗꯨꯒ꯭ꯒꯤꯔꯥꯂꯥꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯁꯦꯃꯒꯠꯄꯒꯤ ꯀ꯭ꯂꯁ꯭ꯇꯔ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯂꯩ, ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯃꯒꯠꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫ 2022ꯗꯥ, ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔ ꯗꯤꯁ꯭ꯠꯔꯤꯛꯇ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯗꯤꯁ꯭ꯠꯔꯤꯛꯇ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯈꯥꯌꯈꯤ: ꯒꯨꯟꯇꯨꯔ, ꯄꯜꯅꯥꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯥꯄꯠꯂꯥ꯫
seg.736e66a0b5de.back: ⟦1⟧Plains turmeric.⟦/1⟧ Guntur district includes turmeric among its crops grown for selling in the market, like cotton, chilli and tobacco. Duggirala in Guntur has a turmeric processing cluster, where processed turmeric and turmeric powder are made. In 2022, Guntur district was divided into three districts: Guntur, Palnadu and Bapatla.

seg.0f26c0785ed1.src: Turmeric can be grown either way: ICAR-IISR says it can be grown rain-fed or irrigated, from sea level up to 1,500 m.

seg.0f26c0785ed1.back: Turmeric can be grown both ways: ICAR-IISR says it can be grown depending on rain water or by irrigating [lit: giving water], up to 1,500 metres above sea level.
