seg.e641ce21ee35.src: ⟦1⟧In the hills.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR's Paderu report says tribal farmers there have grown a local variety called Chayapasupu, or Chintapalle Local, for ages. It has been common practice to leave it in the ground for two or three seasons, up to 18 to 24 months, before digging. From 2011-12, ICAR-IISR and the Horticultural Research Station at Chintapalle tested varieties for the hill zone and brought in Roma and IISR Pragati, which are dug after one season. The report says tribal farmers boil and dry their turmeric by hand, which takes a lot of labour and firewood; the project gave four farmer producer organisations turmeric boilers and polishers.
seg.e641ce21ee35.t: ⟦1⟧ꯆꯤꯡꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ꯫⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR-ꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯗꯦꯔꯨ ꯔꯤꯄꯣꯔꯠꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯕꯦꯜ ꯂꯧꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯌꯥꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ (ꯆꯤꯟꯇꯥꯄꯜꯂꯦ ꯂꯣꯀꯦꯜ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯁꯨ ꯀꯧꯏ) ꯀꯧꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯜ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯇꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯔꯛꯂꯤ꯫ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯠꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗꯥ ꯂꯧ ꯊꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯁꯤꯖꯟ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ, ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯗꯤ ꯊꯥ 18ꯗꯒꯤ 24 ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯥ ꯃꯤ ꯀꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯅꯤ꯫ 2011-12ꯗꯒꯤ, ICAR-IISR ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯤꯟꯇꯥꯄꯜꯂꯦꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯍꯣꯔꯇꯤꯀꯂꯆꯔꯦꯜ ꯔꯤꯁꯔꯆ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯁꯟꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯂꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯈꯜꯁꯤꯡ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯈꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯧ ꯊꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯁꯤꯖꯟ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯔꯣꯃꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ IISR ꯄ꯭ꯔꯒꯇꯤ ꯄꯨꯔꯀꯈꯤ꯫ ꯔꯤꯄꯣꯔꯠꯇꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯕꯦꯜ ꯂꯧꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯎꯃꯩ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯄ꯭ꯔꯣꯖꯦꯛꯇ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯂꯧꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯣꯗ꯭ꯌꯨꯁꯔ ꯑꯣꯔꯒꯥꯅꯥꯏꯖꯦꯁꯟꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯏꯂꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯣꯂꯤꯁꯔꯁꯤꯡ ꯄꯤꯈꯤ꯫
seg.e641ce21ee35.back: ⟦1⟧In the hills.⟦/1⟧ The ICAR-IISR Paderu report says that the tribal farmers there have been growing for many years a variety of that place called Chayapasupu (also called Chintapalle local). Keeping it in the soil for two or three harvest seasons before taking it out, that is up to 18 to 24 months, is the way many people do it. From 2011-12, ICAR-IISR and the Horticultural Research Station at Chintapalle tested varieties for the hill area and brought in Roma and IISR Pragati, which are taken out after one harvest season. The report says that tribal farmers boil and dry their turmeric by hand, which needs much work and time [unsure: 'ꯎꯃꯩ']; the project gave turmeric boilers and polishers to the farmer producer organisations that had become members [or: were connected].

seg.f93b2805162b.src: ⟦1⟧The usual steps.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR's turmeric guide describes how the crop is handled after it is dug:
seg.f93b2805162b.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯈꯣꯉꯊꯥꯡꯁꯤꯡ꯫⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR-ꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯒꯥꯏꯗꯅꯥ ꯃꯍꯩ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯅꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯗꯨ ꯇꯥꯀꯏ:
seg.f93b2805162b.back: ⟦1⟧Usual steps.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR's turmeric guide tells how to handle [lit: check] the crop after taking it out of the soil:

seg.675a9ec4355c.src: Dig it when the leaves dry and turn light brown to yellowish. A well-managed crop is ready seven to nine months after planting, usually between January and March.
seg.675a9ec4355c.t: ꯃꯅꯥꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯥꯎꯟ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄꯥ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯐꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯃꯍꯩ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯊꯥꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯥ ꯇꯔꯦꯠꯇꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯄꯟ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯁꯦꯝ ꯁꯥꯏ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯗꯥ ꯖꯅꯨꯋꯥꯔꯤꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯔꯆꯀꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ꯫
seg.675a9ec4355c.back: Take it out of the soil when the leaves dry and turn from somewhat brown to somewhat yellow. After a good-looking crop is planted, it gets ready in about seven to nine months, mostly around January to March.

seg.763940881dcd.src: Separate the fingers from the bulbs and boil them within 3 or 4 days of digging, in water until soft: 45 to 60 minutes for fingers and 90 minutes for bulbs. Boiling takes away the raw smell, cuts the drying time and gives an even colour.
seg.763940881dcd.t: ꯐꯤꯉ꯭ꯒꯔꯁꯤꯡ ꯕꯜꯕꯁꯤꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯅꯥ ꯊꯃꯗꯨꯅꯥ, ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 3 ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ 4ꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯂꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯐꯤꯉ꯭ꯒꯔꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 45ꯗꯒꯤ 60 ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯜꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ 90꯫ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯗꯕ ꯃꯅꯥꯝ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯏ, ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.763940881dcd.back: Keeping the fingers separate from the bulbs, boil them in water until soft, within 3 or 4 days of taking out of the soil: 45 to 60 minutes for fingers and 90 minutes for bulbs. Boiling removes the raw smell, shortens the drying time and gives even colour.

seg.a52a5947071a.src: Dry them in the sun in layers 5 to 7 cm deep, heaped and covered at night. It may take 10 to 12 days for the moisture to fall below 12%.
seg.a52a5947071a.t: ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯕꯨ 5ꯗꯒꯤ 7 cm ꯂꯨꯕ ꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯨ, ꯑꯍꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯨꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ 12%ꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯅꯕꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ 10ꯗꯒꯤ 12 ꯆꯪꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫
seg.a52a5947071a.back: Dry them in the sun in a layer 5 to 7 cm thick, gather them together and cover them at night. Bringing moisture below 12% can take 10 to 12 days.

seg.69d24ab1420a.src: Polish off the rough, dull, scaly skin by rubbing, by hand or in a turning drum.
seg.69d24ab1420a.t: ꯅꯦꯝꯗꯕ, ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ, ꯊꯛ ꯊꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯒꯤ ꯃꯀꯨꯞ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯀꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯆꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯗ꯭ꯔꯝ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯁꯨꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯣꯂꯤꯁ ꯇꯧꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫
seg.69d24ab1420a.back: Remove the rough, dull, layered outer skin by polishing by hand or by rubbing in a rotating drum.

seg.1b7d7df8b7fa.src: Grind the dried turmeric into powder. FSSAI allows turmeric powder up to 10% moisture.
seg.1b7d7df8b7fa.t: ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯨ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ 10% ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫
seg.1b7d7df8b7fa.back: Grind the dried turmeric into powder. FSSAI allows moisture up to 10% in turmeric powder.

seg.1668650874a7.src: Fingers are the side branches of the turmeric rhizome, usually 2.5 to 7.5 cm long; bulbs are the shorter, thicker central rhizome. Our hill turmeric pack says whole hill turmeric fingers, packed as fine powder. Our turmeric pack says sun-dried and stone-ground.
seg.1668650874a7.t: ꯐꯤꯉ꯭ꯒꯔꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨ (ꯔꯥꯏꯖꯣꯝ) ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ ꯂꯥꯛꯄ ꯃꯆꯥꯁꯤꯡꯅꯤ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯗꯥ 2.5ꯗꯒꯤ 7.5 cm ꯁꯥꯡꯕ; ꯕꯜꯕꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ, ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯆꯥꯎꯕ ꯃꯔꯨꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯐꯤꯉ꯭ꯒꯔꯁꯤꯡ, ꯐꯥꯏꯟ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯇꯧꯈꯤꯕ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ꯫ ꯑꯩꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯦꯛꯇꯥ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯊꯨꯒꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ꯫
seg.1668650874a7.back: Fingers are the branches coming out beside the main root (rhizome) of turmeric, usually 2.5 to 7.5 cm long; bulbs are the main root in the middle, shorter and fatter. Our hill turmeric pack says whole hill turmeric fingers, packed as fine powder. Our turmeric pack says dried in the sun and ground on stone.

seg.4a08c0de8660.back: Curcumin, and how they are seen [or: how they compare]

seg.7ef4d7667b4e.src: Curcumin is the yellow pigment in turmeric, ICAR-IISR says. FSSAI measures a turmeric powder's colouring power as its curcuminoid content, and asks for at least 2% on a dry basis. That standard is the same for hill and plains turmeric.
seg.7ef4d7667b4e.t: ICAR-IISR-ꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯅꯤ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕꯒꯤ ꯁꯛꯇꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯅꯣꯌꯗꯀꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯃꯥꯞ ꯂꯧꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯕ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯥ 2% ꯍꯥꯏ꯫ ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫
seg.7ef4d7667b4e.back: ICAR-IISR says that curcumin is the colour-giving substance in turmeric. FSSAI measures the colour-giving power of a turmeric powder as the amount of curcuminoids it contains, and it is at least 2% according to the dried [unsure: 'ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ', perhaps 'basis/weight']. The standard is one and the same, applying to both hill and plains turmeric.

seg.fec370db2315.src: Curcumin changes from one turmeric to the next:
seg.fec370db2315.t: ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯏ:
seg.fec370db2315.back: Curcumin changes from one turmeric to another:

seg.bf314e75200d.src: ⟦1⟧Variety.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR's 2022 turmeric guide lists its own varieties from 4.3% curcumin (Suvarna) to 6.5% (IISR Prabha).
seg.bf314e75200d.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯈꯜ꯫⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR-ꯒꯤ 2022ꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯒꯥꯏꯗꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯜꯁꯤꯡ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ 4.3% (ꯁꯨꯕꯔ꯭ꯅꯥ)ꯗꯒꯤ 6.5% (IISR ꯄ꯭ꯔꯚꯥ) ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤ꯫
seg.bf314e75200d.back: ⟦1⟧Variety.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR's 2022 turmeric guide includes its own varieties from curcumin 4.3% (Suvarna) to 6.5% (IISR Prabha).

seg.cee7632d2998.src: ⟦1⟧Soil and climate.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR notes that turmeric from different regions differs in quality because of soil, climate and farming practice. Its Paderu report calls curcumin content highly sensitive to changes in the growing environment.
seg.cee7632d2998.t: ⟦1⟧ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ-ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ꯫⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR-ꯅꯥ ꯐꯣꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯕ ꯂꯃꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ-ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯧ ꯊꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀ꯭ꯕꯥꯂꯤꯇꯤ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯩ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯄꯥꯗꯦꯔꯨ ꯔꯤꯄꯣꯔꯠꯇꯥ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯊꯥꯕ ꯃꯐꯃꯒꯤ ꯐꯤꯕꯝ ꯍꯣꯡꯕꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯕ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯀꯧꯏ꯫
seg.cee7632d2998.back: ⟦1⟧Soil and weather.⟦/1⟧ ICAR-IISR reveals that turmeric from different lands differs in quality because of soil, weather and farming methods. Its Paderu report calls the amount of curcumin something that changes a lot with change of growing place.

seg.70b529fe0f69.src: ⟦1⟧Processing.⟦/1⟧ Handling and processing after harvest add to the differences, and boiling too long or too short affects the quality of the dried turmeric.
seg.70b529fe0f69.t: ⟦1⟧ꯁꯦꯃꯒꯠꯄ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯃꯍꯩ ꯂꯧꯔꯕꯥ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯅꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯦꯃꯒꯠꯄꯅꯥ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯕꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯦꯅꯒꯠꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯁꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯡꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯀ꯭ꯕꯥꯂꯤꯇꯤꯗꯥ ꯁꯥꯐꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫
seg.70b529fe0f69.back: ⟦1⟧Processing.⟦/1⟧ Care and processing after harvest increase the differences, and boiling for too long or too short affects the quality of dried turmeric.

seg.493187b22749.src: So the word hill or plains on a pack does not tell you a turmeric's curcumin content. A food testing lab can measure the curcuminoid content of a batch.
seg.493187b22749.t: ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯆꯤꯡ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯇꯝ ꯍꯥꯌꯕ ꯋꯥꯍꯩꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯪꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯅꯣꯌꯗꯀꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯞ ꯂꯧꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.493187b22749.back: Therefore the word hill or plains written on a pack does not tell the amount of curcumin of a turmeric. A food testing lab can measure the amount of curcuminoids of a batch.

seg.53dc21b97510.src: ⟦1⟧How they look.⟦/1⟧ Colour varies too. ICAR-IISR describes its varieties' rhizomes as ranging from reddish yellow to deep orange. Processing counts as well: boiling evens out the colour, drying in too thin a layer can spoil it, and polishing by hand leaves a rough, dull surface.
seg.53dc21b97510.t: ⟦1⟧ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯎꯕꯒꯦ꯫⟦/1⟧ ꯃꯆꯨꯁꯨ ꯍꯣꯡꯏ꯫ ICAR-IISR-ꯅꯥ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯜꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯌꯥꯎꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯀꯃꯂꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯩ ꯍꯥꯌꯅꯥ ꯇꯥꯀꯏ꯫ ꯁꯦꯃꯒꯠꯄꯁꯨ ꯃꯔꯨꯑꯣꯏ: ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯂꯨꯕ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯍꯟꯊꯕ ꯊꯛꯇꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯁꯣꯀꯍꯟꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯨꯠꯅꯥ ꯄꯣꯂꯤꯁ ꯇꯧꯕꯅꯥ ꯅꯦꯝꯗꯕ, ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯃꯊꯛ ꯊꯃꯖꯤ꯫

seg.d8ece11f902a.src: Cooking with each, and keeping it

seg.276f633c7a1f.src: Use either one wherever you use turmeric: dal, sambar, rasam, curries and pulihora.
seg.276f633c7a1f.t: ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯀꯅꯥꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯗꯥꯜ, ꯁꯥꯝꯕꯔ, ꯔꯁꯝ, ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ꯫
seg.276f633c7a1f.back: Use either one in every place where you use turmeric: dal, sambar, rasam, curries [lit: ꯊꯣꯡꯕ 'cooking/boiled dish'; unsure] and pulihora.

seg.ca5e9b6340f2.src: Add it on a low flame so it does not burn.
seg.ca5e9b6340f2.back: To keep it from burning, add it on low heat [lit: small fire].

seg.7e910d4ad2a1.src: To swap one for the other, start with the amount you usually use and adjust to taste.
seg.7e910d4ad2a1.t: ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯅꯕꯥ, ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯥ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯌꯦꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯁꯦꯃꯖꯤꯟꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.7e910d4ad2a1.back: To use one in place of the other, start by putting in the same amount you always use, and then look at [check] the taste and adjust.

seg.731001f6177d.src: Try either one in ⟦1⟧pasupu annam⟦/1⟧, ⟦2⟧nimmakaya pulihora⟦/2⟧, ⟦3⟧tomato pappu⟦/3⟧ or ⟦4⟧pasupu paalu⟦/4⟧.
seg.731001f6177d.t: ⟦1⟧ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯑꯟꯅꯝ⟦/1⟧, ⟦2⟧ꯅꯤꯝꯃꯀꯥꯌ ꯄꯨꯂꯤꯍꯣꯔꯥ⟦/2⟧, ⟦3⟧ꯇꯃꯥꯇꯥ ꯄꯞꯄꯨ⟦/3⟧ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ⟦4⟧ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯄꯥꯂꯨ⟦/4⟧ꯗꯥ ꯀꯅꯥꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯃꯛ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.731001f6177d.back: Try using either one in ⟦1⟧Pasupu Annam⟦/1⟧, ⟦2⟧Nimmakaya Pulihora⟦/2⟧, ⟦3⟧Tomato Pappu⟦/3⟧ or ⟦4⟧Pasupu Palu⟦/4⟧.

seg.073f63fe23e0.src: Use a dry spoon every time.
seg.073f63fe23e0.back: Use a dry spoon every time.

seg.b334ade49a15.src: Store it in a cool, dry place, away from light.
seg.b334ade49a15.t: ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯞꯅꯥ, ꯏꯪꯕ, ꯀꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.b334ade49a15.back: Keep in a cool [or: cold], dry place, away from light.

seg.ea935ed7c1aa.src: How to compare two turmerics fairly
seg.ea935ed7c1aa.back: How to compare two turmerics properly

seg.dcebc75ff722.src: Compare powder with powder. FSSAI allows whole turmeric up to 12% moisture and powder up to 10%, so the two are held to different limits.
seg.dcebc75ff722.t: ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯕꯨ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯒꯥ ꯆꯥꯡꯗꯝꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ 12% ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔꯗꯥ 10% ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯌꯥꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛꯀꯤ ꯂꯤꯃꯤꯠ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯟꯏ꯫
seg.dcebc75ff722.back: Compare powder with powder. FSSAI allows moisture up to 12% in whole turmeric and up to 10% in powder, therefore the limits of the two are different.

seg.9d14be920107.src: Read both packs: where it was grown, the batch or lot number, the best-before date and the FSSAI licence or registration number. Note the batch numbers, so you know which lots you compared.
seg.9d14be920107.t: ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯄꯥꯕꯤꯌꯨ: ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ, ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯂꯣꯠ ꯅꯝꯕꯔ, ꯕꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ-ꯕꯤꯐꯣꯔ ꯇꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ FSSAI ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯦꯟꯁ ꯅꯠꯔꯒꯥ ꯔꯦꯖꯤꯁ꯭ꯠꯔꯦꯁꯟ ꯅꯝꯕꯔ꯫ ꯀꯔꯝꯕꯥ ꯂꯣꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯥꯡꯗꯝꯅꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ ꯈꯪꯅꯕꯥ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯅꯝꯕꯔꯁꯤꯡ ꯏꯊꯝꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.9d14be920107.back: Read both packs: where it was grown, batch or lot number, best-before date and FSSAI licence or registration number. Write down the batch numbers to know which lots were compared.

seg.fbb64b2b32b0.src: Do the water check on both, side by side, with the same amount in the same kind of glass. The steps are in ⟦1⟧how to check turmeric powder at home⟦/1⟧.
seg.fbb64b2b32b0.t: ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯟꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯥꯛ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇꯥ, ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯈꯂꯒꯤ ꯒ꯭ꯂꯥꯁꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯇꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫ ꯈꯣꯉꯊꯥꯡꯁꯤꯡ ⟦1⟧ꯌꯨꯃꯗꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯅꯒꯗꯒꯦ⟦/1⟧ꯗꯥ ꯂꯩ꯫
seg.fbb64b2b32b0.back: Do the water check on both side by side, with the same amount in the same kind of glass. The steps are in ⟦1⟧How to check turmeric powder at home⟦/1⟧.

seg.bd82039194f2.src: Cook the same dish with each, with the same amount, and compare the colour and taste.
seg.bd82039194f2.t: ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯅꯥ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯃꯈꯜ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯆꯥꯡꯗꯝꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.bd82039194f2.back: Using the same amount, cook just one same dish with each, and compare the colour and taste.

seg.8949107c3ad8.src: Do not judge curcumin by colour alone. A brighter yellow is not a measurement; a food testing lab can measure curcuminoid content.
seg.8949107c3ad8.t: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ ꯋꯥꯌꯦꯜ ꯇꯧꯒꯅꯨ꯫ ꯍꯦꯟꯅꯥ ꯃꯉꯥꯜꯂꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯥꯞ ꯂꯧꯕ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ; ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯅꯣꯌꯗꯀꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯞ ꯂꯧꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.8949107c3ad8.back: Do not judge curcumin by colour alone. A brighter turmeric colour is not a measurement; a food testing lab can measure the amount of curcuminoids.

seg.1810d213ce3f.src: Konda pasupu is Telugu for hill turmeric: turmeric grown in hill country. In Andhra Pradesh it grows in the Eastern Ghats, for example in the Paderu agency around Araku Valley and Chintapalle, where most tribal farmers grow turmeric.
seg.1810d213ce3f.t: ꯀꯣꯟꯗꯥ ꯄꯁꯨꯄꯨ ꯍꯥꯏꯕꯁꯤ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯇꯦꯂꯨꯒꯨ ꯃꯤꯡꯅꯤ: ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯂꯃꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ꯫ ꯑꯥꯟꯙ꯭ꯔ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯗꯦꯁꯇꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯏꯁ꯭ꯇꯔꯟ ꯘꯥꯠꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯏ, ꯈꯨꯗꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ ꯑꯔꯀꯨ ꯕꯦꯂꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯤꯟꯇꯥꯄꯜꯂꯦꯒꯤ ꯑꯀꯣꯕꯗꯥ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯄꯥꯗꯦꯔꯨ ꯑꯦꯖꯦꯟꯁꯤꯗꯥ, ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯥ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯕꯦꯜ ꯂꯧꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯊꯥꯏ꯫
seg.1810d213ce3f.back: Konda pasupu is the Telugu name of hill turmeric: turmeric grown in hill areas. In Andhra Pradesh it is grown in the Eastern Ghats, for example in the Paderu agency around Araku Valley and Chintapalle, where mostly tribal farmers grow turmeric.

seg.15730f8cc6b8.src: Is hill turmeric different from regular turmeric?
seg.15730f8cc6b8.t: ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.15730f8cc6b8.back: Is hill turmeric different from the turmeric always used?

seg.47cf644d0819.src: FSSAI holds all turmeric powder to the same standard, wherever it grew. Hill and plains turmeric can differ in where they grow, the varieties grown, and how they are grown and dried. In the Paderu hills, for example, an old local variety has often been left in the ground for up to two years.
seg.47cf644d0819.t: FSSAI-ꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯄꯥꯎꯗꯔ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ, ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯔꯕꯁꯨ, ꯁ꯭ꯇꯦꯟꯗꯔꯗ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯂꯧꯏ꯫ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯃꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯕꯒꯦ, ꯊꯥꯔꯤꯕ ꯃꯈꯜꯁꯤꯡ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯗꯥ ꯈꯦꯠꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯈꯨꯗꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅꯥ, ꯄꯥꯗꯦꯔꯨ ꯆꯤꯡꯁꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯑꯔꯤꯕ ꯂꯣꯀꯦꯜ ꯃꯈꯜ ꯑꯃꯥ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯌꯥꯝꯅꯥ ꯀꯌꯥꯗꯥ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯃꯖꯤ꯫
seg.47cf644d0819.back: FSSAI applies one and the same standard to all turmeric powder, wherever it is grown. Hill and plains turmeric can differ in where they are grown, the varieties grown, and how they are planted [or: put] and dried. For example, an old local variety in the Paderu hills is often kept in the soil for about two years.

seg.925655ca4b05.src: Does hill turmeric have more curcumin?
seg.925655ca4b05.back: Does hill turmeric have more curcumin?

seg.0d1b42a32899.src: The word hill alone does not tell you. Curcumin changes with the variety, the soil and climate, and how the turmeric was boiled and dried. A food testing lab can measure the curcuminoid content of a batch.
seg.0d1b42a32899.t: ꯆꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯌꯕ ꯋꯥꯍꯩ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯍꯟꯗꯦ꯫ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯟ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯈꯜ, ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠ-ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯔꯝꯅꯥ ꯊꯣꯡꯗꯨꯅꯥ ꯀꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅꯥ ꯍꯣꯡꯏ꯫ ꯆꯤꯟꯖꯥꯛ ꯇꯦꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯇꯧꯕ ꯂꯦꯕ ꯑꯃꯅꯥ ꯕꯦꯆ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯀꯔꯀꯨꯃꯤꯅꯣꯌꯗꯀꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯥꯞ ꯂꯧꯕ ꯉꯝꯃꯤ꯫
seg.0d1b42a32899.back: The word hill alone does not prove it. Curcumin changes according to variety, soil and weather, and how the turmeric was boiled and dried. A food testing lab can measure the amount of curcuminoids of a batch.

seg.4bce9a44c11e.src: What are the types of turmeric (haldi) in India?
seg.4bce9a44c11e.back: What are the varieties of turmeric (haldi) in India?

seg.4e6e7201dae6.src: ICAR-IISR says India grows many turmeric cultivars, mostly known by the name of the place where they are grown, such as Duggirala, Mydukur, Tekkurpet and Amalapuram. It has also released improved varieties such as IISR Prabha, IISR Prathibha and IISR Pragati.
seg.4e6e7201dae6.t: ICAR-IISR-ꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯌꯔꯤ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯥꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯜ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯊꯥꯏ, ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯌꯥꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯕ ꯊꯥꯕ ꯃꯐꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯤꯡꯅꯥ ꯈꯪꯅꯩ, ꯗꯨꯒ꯭ꯒꯤꯔꯥꯂꯥ, ꯃꯥꯏꯗꯨꯀꯨꯔ, ꯇꯦꯛꯀꯨꯔꯄꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯂꯥꯄꯨꯔꯃꯒꯨꯝꯕ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯥ IISR ꯄ꯭ꯔꯚꯥ, IISR ꯄ꯭ꯔꯇꯤꯚꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ IISR ꯄ꯭ꯔꯒꯇꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯐꯒꯠꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯈꯜꯁꯤꯡꯁꯨ ꯊꯣꯀꯍꯜꯂꯦ꯫
seg.4e6e7201dae6.back: ICAR-IISR says India grows many varieties of turmeric, many of them known by the name of the place where they are grown, like Duggirala, Mydukur, Tekkurpet and Amalapuram. It has also brought out improved varieties like IISR Prabha, IISR Prathibha and IISR Pragati.

seg.7f1a5999ea66.src: Can I use hill turmeric instead of regular turmeric?
seg.7f1a5999ea66.t: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇꯥ ꯆꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯌꯥꯕꯔꯥ?
seg.7f1a5999ea66.back: Can hill turmeric be used in place of the turmeric always used?

seg.4ed419c2136a.src: Yes. Use it wherever you use turmeric, start with the amount you usually use, and add it on a low flame so it does not burn.
seg.4ed419c2136a.t: ꯍꯣꯌ꯫ ꯅꯍꯥꯛꯅꯥ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗꯥ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯕꯗꯥ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯇꯨꯅꯥ ꯍꯧꯕꯤꯌꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯆꯥꯗꯅꯕꯥ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄꯗꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯤꯌꯨ꯫
seg.4ed419c2136a.back: Yes. Use it in every place where you use turmeric, start by putting in the same amount you always use, and put it in on a low fire so it does not burn.

seg.1a441b0df6de.src: Both packs list one ingredient, turmeric (Curcuma longa), and name where it was grown.
seg.1a441b0df6de.t: ꯄꯦꯛ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛꯇꯥ ꯌꯥꯎꯔꯤꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯃꯈꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ, ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯤ ꯌꯥꯏꯉꯡ (Curcuma longa), ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗꯥ ꯊꯥꯈꯤꯕꯒꯦ ꯍꯥꯌꯕ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯏ꯫
